sops.title: SOP CL-01: Routine House Cleaning
sops.sourceFile: Standard Of Operations/sop Routine Cleaning Checklist.md

lines: - The customer provides entry by key, lockbox code or in person, as the agreement records (source: agreement "Access" clause).
- Evidence: note
- Every visit re-confirms access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions (source: spec CX-005).

- PROPOSED for the preparation checklist (not yet in the agreement): pets secured or kept away from the rooms being cleaned; excluded rooms or items named; fragile or high-value items named or put away; product preferences and allergies, with consent before any fragranced product is used; priority areas; surfaces to be cleaned cleared of clutter, since the pricing file's clutter fee has no defined threshold (source: 04 CL-01 "customer preparation requirements"; spec CL-01.INT; X-11; C-CL01-05).
- HandyHub's own pre-start checks are never moved onto the customer (source: 30 section 4.1 clause 5).
*Dispatch and Start Job gates for this service (source: spec APXA-001, APXA-003; 31 section 3.1 row 3). Every item is pending review.*
- Intake complete: rooms, occupancy and pets, surfaces and materials, priority areas, excluded rooms or items, and product preferences or allergies if volunteered (source: spec CL-01.INT).
- An approved estimate version covers the rooms and tasks of the visit; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec CX-003; APXA-003).
- Evidence: note
- Every visit re-confirms access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions, also for a repeat customer (source: spec CX-005).

- Access by key, lockbox code or in-person entry as recorded for the property. Codes are revealed only in the app's secured fields, and keys are custody items with an issue and return log; the key and code custody, return and rotation procedure is not yet written (source: agreement "Access" clause; 27 AUTH-009; spec COM-002; 02 G-065, G-115).
- Evidence: note

- Every cleaning product is on an approved product list with a reviewed SDS; a chemical product without a reviewed SDS is not carried to the job. No product is approved yet: TBD - requires qualified safety reviewer review (source: 29 section 8.3 interim rule, PROPOSED; spec CL-01.SAF).
- A means to sign or control wet floors is loaded (source: spec CL-01.SAF "signage/control wet floors"); no wet-floor sign is stocked yet (inventory file, proposed additions).
- Customer-provided products, where a preference or allergy requires them: product and condition are recorded before use (source: spec START-009; 29 section 9.1).
- Evidence: note

- Before this SOP can be activated, the named reviewers approve: the chemical, SDS and wet-floor controls (C-CL01-06); the sharps, biohazard and mold boundary (X-06); the fan and disposal holds (section 12); the arrangement for a cleaner working alone (02 G-065) (source: 31 section 10 CL-01; owner facts L20).

- Before leaving: confirm the job, customer, address and time; read the latest changes; verify access; review scope and exclusions; review hazards and safety; load critical tools and materials, including the means to sign wet floors; check customer-supplied items; confirm required documents and approvals (source: spec APXA-001).

- On arrival: confirm address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants; inspect the actual site against the briefing; capture required existing-condition photos; protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo

- Entry: use the key, lockbox code or in-person entry recorded for the property; reveal codes only in the app; never write down, photograph or message a code (source: agreement "Access" clause; 27 AUTH-009; spec COM-002; Do not perform 7).
- Evidence: note
- Ventilation adequate for the approved products, as their SDSs require: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003; START-004).
- Evidence: note
- The original "Phase 1: High-Level Dusting & Preparation" heading names preparation but holds only dusting tasks; setup is this section (source: 31 section 6.2 matrix, Setup partial).

*The original procedure lines below are unchanged and in their original order; the five original phase headings are demoted one level, text unchanged. Lines starting with "HOLD" or "FLAG" were added on 2026-10-03; they are pending review and never replace the step text.*

> HOLD (precondition; X-11; spec CL-01.SAF): before "Cobwebs" and every step below - occupants, children and pets are kept away from the rooms being worked, as confirmed on arrival (spec CX-005). An unsafe animal or an aggressive occupant or situation means stop, leave the area and escalate (section 19). Pending review.
- [ ] **Cobwebs:** Scan with an extension duster along all ceiling corners, crown moldings, and upper door frames.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: High-Level Dusting & Preparation"

lines: > HOLD (precondition; RISK; 31 section 10 CL-01): before "Ceiling Fans" - the fan is stopped and switched off before its blades are dusted. If it cannot be switched off, or its blades cannot be reached from the floor, do not dust it; record it and report it (section 17). No ladder or step stool unless the approved height and access policy allows it (section 2, Do not perform 10). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: High-Level Dusting & Preparation"

lines: - [ ] **Ceiling Fans:** Dust top and bottom of fan blades using a slip-on microfiber sleeve (no dust dropping on floors).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: High-Level Dusting & Preparation"

lines: - [ ] **Light Fixtures:** Dust the exterior of hanging pendants and wall sconces; wipe bulb tops if cool.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: High-Level Dusting & Preparation"

lines: - [ ] **Air Vents:** Dust the exterior slats of supply and return air vents.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: High-Level Dusting & Preparation"

lines: - [ ] **Horizontal Surfaces:** Dust nightstands, dressers, coffee tables, and desks; lift minor objects (remotes, books) to dust underneath—do not dust around them.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛋️ Phase 2: Bedrooms & Living Areas Detailing"

lines: - [ ] **Electronics:** Dry-wipe TV screens with a clean anti-static microfiber cloth; dust the tops of soundbars and gaming consoles.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛋️ Phase 2: Bedrooms & Living Areas Detailing"

lines: - [ ] **Decor:** Dust picture frames, mirrors, lampshades (using a lint roller if fabric), and decorative items.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛋️ Phase 2: Bedrooms & Living Areas Detailing"

lines: - [ ] **Beds:** Strip blankets, pull sheets tight, tuck corners, fluff pillows, and lay the comforter/duvet perfectly flat without wrinkles.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛋️ Phase 2: Bedrooms & Living Areas Detailing"

lines: > HOLD (precondition; C-CL01-06; spec CL-01.SAF): before "High-Touch Wiping" and every later step that uses a cleaning product ("Large Appliances", "Counters & Backsplash", "Sink Area", the Phase 4 steps and "Mopping") - use only products on the approved product list with a reviewed SDS, exactly as their labels direct, and never mix incompatible chemicals or mix or sequence products in a way the approved step and the SDSs do not allow ("never mix incompatible chemicals"; 31 section 3.3 entry 6). No product is approved and no SDS is reviewed yet, so a chemical product is not carried to the job until the qualified safety professional approves it (29 section 8.3 interim rule, PROPOSED). Ventilation as each SDS requires. Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛋️ Phase 2: Bedrooms & Living Areas Detailing"

lines: - [ ] **High-Touch Wiping:** Wipe down all room light switches and main door handles with a disinfectant wipe.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛋️ Phase 2: Bedrooms & Living Areas Detailing"

lines: - [ ] **Microwave:** Wipe down the rotating glass plate, roller ring, interior walls, ceiling, and exterior control pad.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🍳 Phase 3: Kitchen Surface Care"

lines: - [ ] **Large Appliances:** Wipe down the front faces, handles, and touchscreens of the refrigerator, oven, and dishwasher using material-specific cleaner (e.g., stainless steel polish).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🍳 Phase 3: Kitchen Surface Care"

lines: - [ ] **Stovetop:** Wipe down the stovetop surface, removing minor spills around burner caps.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🍳 Phase 3: Kitchen Surface Care"

lines: - [ ] **Counters & Backsplash:** Clear counters, spray with multi-surface sanitizer, wipe completely, and wipe down the backsplash tiles.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🍳 Phase 3: Kitchen Surface Care"

lines: > HOLD (precondition; RISK; 31 section 10 CL-01): before "Sink Area" - hands never go inside the garbage disposal, and the disposal is not run while the rim, drain basket or sink is cleaned (PROPOSED). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🍳 Phase 3: Kitchen Surface Care"

lines: - [ ] **Sink Area:** Scrub the sink basin, clear the drain basket, sanitize the garbage disposal rim, and polish the faucet fixture until streak-free.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🍳 Phase 3: Kitchen Surface Care"

lines: > HOLD (precondition; C-CL01-06, X-06; spec CL-01.SAF): before "Toilet" and the other Phase 4 steps - if a biohazard (the agreement's "Exclusions" clause names feces), sharps or suspected mold growth is found, do not clean, disturb or handle it; stop and escalate ("stop and escalate on sharps/biohazard"). Where routine bathroom cleaning ends and the excluded biohazards and mold begin is undefined until the company mold and biohazard rule exists (X-06; Q-31-10); when in doubt, stop and escalate (owner facts 2026-10-02 "Unknown is not safe"). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛁 Phase 4: Bathroom Sanitization"

lines: - [ ] **Toilet:** Scrub the interior bowl with a brush; wipe down the flush handle, toilet lid, seat (both sides), porcelain base, and behind the toilet tank.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛁 Phase 4: Bathroom Sanitization"

lines: - [ ] **Shower & Tub:** Wipe down shower walls, glass panels, and the bathtub rim to remove daily water spots.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛁 Phase 4: Bathroom Sanitization"

lines: - [ ] **Vanity:** Scrub the sink basin, wipe down the countertop, and polish the mirror with glass cleaner and a waffle-weave cloth.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛁 Phase 4: Bathroom Sanitization"

lines: - [ ] **Fixtures:** Wipe and polish all metal faucets, shower heads, and towel racks to remove water smudges.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛁 Phase 4: Bathroom Sanitization"

lines: > FLAG (C-CL01-V01): SCOPE CONFLICT - disinfection promised for showers/tubs/mirrors but not proceduralised. The main plan promises "Cleaning and disinfecting essential fixtures such as toilets, sinks, showers, tubs, and mirrors.", but the Phase 4 steps above wipe, scrub or polish and name no disinfectant, and the stocked bathroom disinfectant is designated only for sinks, counters and toilet seats (inventory file). Adding a reviewed disinfecting step with an approved product and its label directions, or narrowing the copy, is an owner decision. Until then, do not tell the customer that fixtures were disinfected or sanitized (section 17). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛁 Phase 4: Bathroom Sanitization"

lines: > HOLD (precondition; C-CL01-06; spec CL-01.HAZ, CL-01.SAF): before "Trash Bins" and "Upholstery" - hidden sharps or biohazards can be in bins, bags and under cushions ("sharps/biohazard surprises"). Do not reach into bins or press trash down by hand, and look before reaching under cushions (PROPOSED; RISK). If sharps or a biohazard are seen or suspected, do not handle them; stop and escalate. Whether workers ever contain found sharps, and with what container and PPE, is for the qualified safety professional (inventory file, proposed additions). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧹 Phase 5: Waste Management & Floor Care (Exit)"

lines: - [ ] **Trash Bins:** Gather trash from all rooms, tie bags, wipe down exterior bin lids if sticky, and place fresh liners.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧹 Phase 5: Waste Management & Floor Care (Exit)"

lines: - [ ] **Upholstery:** Vacuum the surfaces of fabric sofas, armchairs, and remove cushions to vacuum underneath if accessible.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧹 Phase 5: Waste Management & Floor Care (Exit)"

lines: - [ ] **Vacuuming:** Vacuum all carpets and rugs using overlapping straight lines; vacuum hard floors to remove loose crumbs and hair before mopping.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧹 Phase 5: Waste Management & Floor Care (Exit)"

lines: > HOLD (precondition; C-CL01-06; spec CL-01.SAF): before "Mopping" - place wet-floor signage or otherwise keep people and pets off the wet floor until it is dry ("signage/control wet floors"); the step's own "working backward out of each room" stays. No wet-floor sign is stocked yet (inventory file, proposed additions). If a wet floor cannot be signed or controlled, for example because occupants or pets cannot be kept away, do not mop that area; escalate. The bathroom floor cleaner is used only as an approved product with a reviewed SDS (chemical hold before "High-Touch Wiping"). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧹 Phase 5: Waste Management & Floor Care (Exit)"

lines: - [ ] **Mopping:** Mop all hard floors with a damp microfiber mop, working backward out of each room (use disinfectant floor cleaner for bathrooms).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧹 Phase 5: Waste Management & Floor Care (Exit)"

lines: - [ ] **Final Look:** Stand at the doorway of each room to verify visual symmetry, straight lines, and zero missed spots.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧹 Phase 5: Waste Management & Floor Care (Exit)"

lines: > FLAG: outcome claim - owner and attorney review (31 section 10 CL-01). "zero missed spots" in the step above is the worker's inspection aim, not a promise to the customer, and it is not repeated in customer communication (section 17; 31 section 3.5 rule 5).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧹 Phase 5: Waste Management & Floor Care (Exit)"

lines: > HOLD (C-CL01-06; spec CL-01.QAC): the visual check in the step above does not cover the card's "no damage" and "rooms secured as found" checks; answer both in section 13 before the job is marked complete. Damage found or caused is reported as an incident (section 20). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧹 Phase 5: Waste Management & Floor Care (Exit)"

lines: *From spec CL-01.QAC. The worker cannot mark the job complete without answering the required checks or recording an exception (source: spec QA-001). Which checks need a second person rather than a self-check is open (Q-31-15).*
| Check | Source | Inspector | Evidence |

| Specified surfaces cleaned: the rooms and surfaces in the approved visit scope, with excluded rooms and items left untouched | spec CL-01.QAC; CL-01.INT | Worker; supervisor where policy requires (Q-31-15) | After photos mapped to rooms or areas (QA-003) |
| Floors complete | spec CL-01.QAC; steps "Vacuuming" and "Mopping" | Worker | After photos |
| Bathrooms and kitchen standard met: the Phase 3 and Phase 4 steps done; no disinfection result is claimed (C-CL01-V01) | spec CL-01.QAC | Worker | After photos |
| Trash handled | spec CL-01.QAC; step "Trash Bins" | Worker | Checklist answer |
| No damage | spec CL-01.QAC | Worker; damage found or caused is reported as an incident (section 20) | Checklist answer; internal photos of any damage |

| Rooms secured as found, including the entry used (lock, key or lockbox returned to its recorded state) | spec CL-01.QAC; agreement "Access" clause | Worker | Checklist answer; key return logged (27 AUTH-009) |
| Visual check from each doorway | step "Final Look" | Worker | Inspection aim only; "zero missed spots" is not a customer promise (FLAG in section 12) |

- A customer signature or acknowledgement does not clear an unresolved safety hold, and missing evidence is recorded as unknown, not as a pass (source: quality-assistant playbook "A signed customer form does not clear an unresolved safety hold." and "Missing photos are unknown evidence, not proof of defective work.").
- Evidence: note
*For a cleaning service, cleanup means the exit sequence and the crew's own equipment (source: 31 section 6.1).*
- Remove the wet-floor sign once the floor is dry; account for tools and materials; put back anything moved within scope (source: spec APXA-005; QA-002).

- Used cloths and mop pads: bagging and laundering method TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve. Keeping toilet cloths apart is part of the open colour-system question (section 7).
- Return unused materials (source: spec APXA-007).
- Secure the property as found before leaving (section 13).

- Household trash ("Trash Bins"): the step ties the bags, but where they go (the customer's outdoor bin or removal by the crew) is not stated; TBD - owner decision (source: section 12; 31 section 3.1 row 15).

- Dirty mop water, chemical residues, used wipes and empty product containers: disposal per each product's SDS and the municipality's rules; no method is approved yet (source: 29 section 8.2 item 10; Q-29-10).

- Sharps and biohazards are not handled by the worker under this SOP: stop and escalate (section 10); their disposal method is decided by the reviewer and the local authority (source: spec CL-01.SAF; Q-29-10).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: existing-condition photos where the briefing requires them, including damage found on arrival, which matters for the agreement's "Breakage" clause (source: spec APXA-002; START-008).
- Evidence: photo
- During: unexpected conditions such as sharps, a biohazard, suspected mold or damage, recorded with photos and severity without touching the item (source: spec JOB-004; UXE-006).
- Evidence: note
- After: photos mapped to rooms or areas (source: spec QA-003; 04 CL-01 "completion evidence").
- Evidence: photo

- Privacy in an occupied home: every photo is internal-only by default; avoid people, documents, valuables and personal items not needed for the work; never photograph keys or access codes; marketing use needs separate consent (source: spec REC-002, REC-003; 31 section 3.5 rule 7; Do not perform 7).
- Arrival and completion updates are drafts; the worker or admin controls the send (source: spec UXE-008).

- Record the walkthrough outcome: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed; on unattended recurring visits "unavailable" is the expected outcome (source: spec QA-004; 04 CL-01 "completion evidence").
- Evidence: note

- Report what was left undone and why, in approved wording: areas not reachable from the floor, fans that could not be switched off, heavy objects not moved, excluded biohazards or suspected mold, damage found (source: sections 10 and 12). Wording TBD - owner.
- Evidence: note
- Requests for extra work, such as organizing clutter, appliance interiors or deep grease, are recorded as change requests; no price is agreed on site (source: spec JOB-005, FIN-008; C-CL01-05).
- Evidence: note
- Blocked work: only the approved "work blocked" message; no incident details or access codes by text or email (source: spec NTF-007, COM-002).

- What not to say: that fixtures were disinfected or sanitized (C-CL01-V01); "zero missed spots" or any other outcome promise (31 section 10 CL-01); "Eco-Friendly" or other product claims (29 section 8.2 item 12); that the company is insured (C-CL01-02; 32 section 4.1 rule 5).
- Required QA checks answered or an exception recorded (source: spec QA-001; section 13).
- Evidence: note
- After photos mapped to rooms or areas (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup and waste handling done as approved (source: spec QA-002; sections 14 and 15).
- Tools and materials accounted for (source: spec APXA-005).
- Property secured as found, and the key or lockbox code returned to its recorded state (source: spec CL-01.QAC; 27 AUTH-009).
- Evidence: note
- Open holds, items left undone, damage and punch items recorded; walkthrough outcome recorded (source: spec QA-004; APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- The job closes only when the required operational and financial steps are complete (source: spec APXA-007).
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:

*Standard block copied verbatim from 31 SOP standard section 8.5 (PROPOSED wording; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional; attorney licensed in KY and/or IN for the "right to stop work" sentence; bilingual reviewer for Spanish).*

**Service stop triggers and holds (CL-01).** Card stop guidance (spec CL-01.SAF): "never mix incompatible chemicals; signage/control wet floors; stop and escalate on sharps/biohazard/unsafe animal/aggressive situation".
| Trigger or hold | Action | Cleared by (evidence) | Source |
| Product without a reviewed SDS, or a mix or sequence the SDSs do not allow | Do not use; escalate | Reviewed SDS and approved product | spec CL-01.SAF; 29 section 8.3; C-CL01-06 |

| A wet floor cannot be signed or controlled, for example because occupants or pets cannot be kept away | Do not mop that area; escalate | Signage or access control in place | spec CL-01.SAF; C-CL01-06 |

| Sharps or a biohazard seen or suspected, including in trash, under cushions or around the toilet | Stop; do not handle; escalate | Owner, with the qualified safety reviewer's approved method | spec CL-01.SAF; X-06 |
| Suspected mold growth | Stop; do not clean or disturb; escalate | Company mold rule (Q-31-10); qualified mold assessor | agreement "Exclusions" clause; X-06; 31 section 8.4 rule 2 |
| Unsafe animal | Stop; leave the area; escalate | Owner; the customer secures the animal | spec CL-01.SAF |
| Aggressive occupant or situation | Stop; leave; escalate; emergency services if anyone is in danger | Owner | spec CL-01.SAF; START-011 |
| Ceiling fan cannot be stopped and switched off | Do not dust the fan; report it | Fan off | 31 section 10 CL-01 (RISK) |
| Area not reachable from the floor | Do not use a ladder, step stool or furniture; leave and report | Approved height and access policy (Q-31-09) | 31 section 10 CL-01; 02 G-005 |
| Heavy object in the way | Do not lift; leave and report | Manual-handling rule | agreement "Exclusions" clause |
| Gas odor | Emergency (section 19, step 2) | Emergency services | spec START-011; 31 section 8.5 |

Critical holds cannot be overridden by any role; they clear only with a recorded qualified assessment (source: 31 section 8.3 rule 2). Under the PROPOSED classification rule of 31 section 8.4, the chemical compatibility and SDS hold behaves as a critical hold until the chemicals module is approved (rule 4), and suspected mold growth is treated as critical until the company mold definition exists (rule 2).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
*Standard block copied verbatim from 31 section 8.5 (PROPOSED wording; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional).*

**CL-01 escalation routes (owner decisions pending, Q-31-05):** sharps, a biohazard or suspected mold go to the owner, who decides with the qualified safety reviewer or a mold assessor (source: spec CL-01.SAF; X-06). Chemical exposure or splash: emergency response first, then the incident form (section 20); first-aid references only from the reviewed SDS (source: 29 section 8.2 item 7). An unsafe animal or an aggressive occupant: leave the area and escalate, and call emergency services if anyone is in danger (source: spec CL-01.SAF; BRF-013). A cleaner working alone: check-in and escalation arrangement TBD (source: 02 G-065). Contacts: `<owner decision: emergency contact>` and `<owner decision: escalation order>` (Q-31-05).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].

*Standard block copied verbatim from 31 section 8.5 (PROPOSED wording). HUMAN REVIEW: attorney licensed in KY and/or IN for the fault and liability sentence; insurance broker for any insurer-notification step added later.*

- CL-01 examples to report: a slip or fall; a chemical splash or exposure; a cut or needle-stick from hidden sharps; an animal bite; breakage of the customer's property; an aggressive occupant (source: spec CL-01.HAZ, CL-01.SAF; JOB-008).
- Q-31-09 (owner; qualified safety professional): height and access policy - may cleaners ever use a step stool or ladder for CL-01, and what happens to areas out of reach from the floor?
- Q-31-10 (owner; qualified mold assessor): what is the company definition of mold growth versus cleanable mildew, and where does routine bathroom cleaning end and the excluded biohazard begin?
- C-CL01-V01 (owner): add a reviewed disinfecting step with an approved product, or narrow the main-plan copy?
- Q-31-11 (owner; qualified safety professional): emergency kit contents, SDS register owner, chemical storage and transport.
- Q-31-05 (owner): emergency and escalation contacts, escalation order and after-hours coverage, including a check-in for a cleaner working alone (02 G-065).
> Governed now by [[OWN-DEC-149]]: no interval check-ins for lone work; the worker records only Arrived and Finished.
- Q-31-15 (owner): which checks ("no damage", "rooms secured as found") need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check while there are two employees?
- Q-31-02 (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish safety text?
- Q-29-10 (local authority; safety reviewer): disposal of mop water, chemical residues, sharps and biohazards in each service municipality.
- 02 G-065 (owner): the key and lockbox custody, return and rotation procedure, and the customer-preparation checklist (pets, valuables, excluded rooms, allergies and fragrance consent).

sops.title: SOP CL-02: Elite Deep Cleaning Service
sops.sourceFile: Standard Of Operations/sop Deep Cleaning CheckList.md

lines: - The client clears major toys, clothes and excessive clutter from floors and counters before the crew arrives; the fee in the same clause is under owner review (source: agreement "Clutter Clear" clause; C-CL02-10).

- The property has running water, operational electricity and functional HVAC; the clause's cancellation and deposit consequences are under attorney review (source: agreement "Water & Utilities" clause; C-CL02-02).

- PROPOSED for the preparation checklist (not yet in the agreement): empty the refrigerator or say how food is to be handled; point out or put away fragile and valuable items; record permission and limits for moving furniture and appliances; name surface sensitivities such as stone, glass coatings and leather or wood furniture; keep pets and children away from work areas (source: 04 CL-02 "customer preparation requirements", GAP; spec CL-02.INT; X-11).
- Evidence: note
- Every job re-confirms access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions (source: spec CX-005).
- HandyHub's own pre-start checks are never moved onto the customer (source: 30 section 4.1 clause 5).
*Dispatch and Start Job gates for this service (source: spec APXA-001, APXA-003; 31 section 3.1 row 3). Every item is pending review.*
- Intake complete: deep-clean scope, appliance interiors, grout, high/low areas, furniture movement limits, surface sensitivities (source: spec CL-02.INT).

- An approved estimate version covers the tasks in section 2, with each add-on shown as a separately acceptable option; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec CX-003; EST-005; APXA-003).
- Evidence: note

- Every chemical product is on an approved product list with a reviewed SDS; a chemical product without a reviewed SDS is not carried to the job, and the chlorine-based product and the acid products are not packed in the same caddy or container (source: 29 section 8.3 interim rule, PROPOSED; C-CL02-03). No product is approved yet: TBD - requires qualified safety reviewer review.

- Property profile with the approximate age if known, with "unknown" as a value; whether age triggers lead or asbestos screening for CL-02 painted surfaces and ceilings is open (source: spec BRF-003 "approximate age if known"; 31 section 5.8 "screening questions for CL-02"; Q-31-07).
- Water and power available for the steps that need them, confirmed at intake (source: job-planner playbook "water/power availability"; agreement "Water & Utilities" clause).

- Tasks that need a ladder or step stool stay blocked until an approved height and access policy exists (source: spec CL-02.SAF "ladder controls"; job-planner playbook "A missing ladder or unverified permit keeps affected tasks blocked."; C-CL02-05; Q-31-09).
- "Behind Appliances" stays held until an approved appliance-movement policy exists and the customer's permission is recorded (source: C-CL02-04; 04 CL-02 "prerequisites", GAP; Q-31-08).
- Evidence: note
- Licensed-task and permit flags: where policy marks a task as needing a licensed trade or permit, Start Job stays blocked until that prerequisite is approved (source: spec START-010).

- Before this SOP can be activated, the named reviewers approve: SDS-based chemical compatibility and sequencing (C-CL02-03); appliance movement and isolation (C-CL02-04); height access (C-CL02-05); the line between surface mildew and mold growth (X-06; Q-31-10); the ceiling-composition and painted-surface holds (31 section 10 CL-02; C-CL02-06) (source: 31 section 10 CL-02; owner facts L20).

- On arrival: confirm address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants; inspect the actual site against the briefing; capture required existing-condition photos; protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- The original "Phase 1: Chemical Dwell Time & Setup" applies chemicals; it contains no site-protection or ventilation setup, and it stays in section 12 under its holds (source: section 12).

- Product staging: the chlorine-based product and the acid products in separate caddies or containers; secondary containers carry the product identity and hazards (source: 29 section 8.3 interim rule; 29 section 8.2 item 3, PROPOSED). Staging details: TBD - requires qualified safety reviewer review.

- Ventilation adequate for the approved products, as their SDSs require. Whether the agreement's "functional HVAC systems" condition is meant as a ventilation control is an open question for the safety reviewer (source: agreement "Water & Utilities" clause; spec BRF-008).
- Appliances are unplugged or isolated per instruction before they are cleaned; the shared isolate-verify-restore module does not exist yet (source: spec CL-02.SAF; X-07; 31 section 5.8).
- Protection of floors, furniture and fixtures near chemical work: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003; START-004).
- Evidence: note

- A customer signature or acknowledgement does not clear an unresolved safety hold (source: quality-assistant playbook "A signed customer form does not clear an unresolved safety hold.").

- Evidence: note

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: existing-condition photos of the areas to be cleaned, especially damaged or stained grout, chipping paint, appliance condition and sensitive surfaces. PROPOSED for CL-02 because the agreement's "Pre-existing Damage" clause relies on prior-condition evidence; whether they are required is the START-008 configuration decision (source: X-02; C-CL02-06; spec START-008).
- Evidence: photo
- During: concealed or unexpected conditions - suspected mold growth, damaged ceilings, chipping paint, damaged cords, sharps - with photos and severity (source: spec JOB-004; UXE-006).
- After: photos mapped to areas or tasks - kitchen, appliance interiors where included, bathrooms, floors (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo

- Every photo is internal-only by default; marketing use needs separate consent (source: spec REC-002, REC-003). Avoid people, documents and valuables, including the contents of drawers, cabinets and refrigerators (source: 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- Arrival and completion updates are drafts; the worker or admin controls the send (source: spec UXE-008).

- Record the walkthrough outcome: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004). The agreement's "final walkthrough inspection" maps to this record (source: agreement "Final Payment" clause; 04 CL-02 "completion evidence").
- Evidence: note

- Held items are told in approved wording: appliances not pulled out; height tasks blocked; chemical steps held; suspected mold, chipping paint or damaged ceilings recorded and referred; add-on steps outside the approved estimate not performed. Wording TBD - owner and qualified safety reviewer (source: section 12 holds).
- Evidence: note

- Reports of missed items after the visit are recorded, linked to the job and classified (source: spec CX-007, QA-010). The agreement's callback clause is an unapproved draft (30 section 5 row 4; Q-30-07); the worker makes no re-clean, credit or payment commitment and refers the report to the owner.
- Evidence: note
- Care notes only from approved product or manufacturer data; none are approved yet (source: spec QA-008).
- Blocked work: only the approved "work blocked" message; no incident details or access codes by text or email (source: spec NTF-007, COM-002).

- What not to say: "deep structural reset", "showroom condition", "Top-to-Bottom Reset" as a promise of add-on tasks, mold-removal, sanitizing or disinfection claims, or any health or safety outcome (source: 04 CL-02 "customer-facing description"; 32 register A row 21 and register B rows 10 and 57; 32 legal row L5).
- Required QA checks answered or an exception recorded (source: spec QA-001; section 13).
- Evidence: note
- After photos mapped to areas or tasks (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup and waste handling done as approved (source: spec QA-002; sections 14 and 15).
- Tools and materials accounted for; components altered within scope restored (source: spec APXA-005).
- Appliance state recorded as section 13 requires (source: spec CL-02.QAC "appliances restored"; C-CL02-04).
- Evidence: note
- Customer exclusions respected and customer items returned (source: spec CL-02.QAC).
- Open holds, blocked tasks and punch items recorded; walkthrough outcome recorded (source: spec QA-004; APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- The job closes only when the required operational and financial steps are complete (source: spec APXA-007).
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:

*Standard block copied verbatim from 31 SOP standard section 8.5 (PROPOSED wording; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional; attorney licensed in KY and/or IN for the "right to stop work" sentence; bilingual reviewer for Spanish).*

**Service stop triggers and holds (CL-02).** Card stop guidance (spec CL-02.SAF): "test sensitive surfaces; move only approved/light items; unplug/isolate appliances per instruction; chemical compatibility; ladder controls".
| Trigger or hold | Action | Cleared by (evidence) | Source |

| Chemical product without a reviewed SDS, or a combination or order the SDS does not allow ("Bathroom Prep", "Tile Grout", "De-scaling", "Drainage") | Do not apply; keep products apart | Reviewed SDS and approved product; reviewer-recorded compatibility and order | C-CL02-03; 29 section 8.3 |

| Irritation, unusual odor or other exposure symptoms | Stop the chemical step and move away from the area; emergency first if needed (section 19); incident form (section 20) | Qualified safety reviewer | 04 section 6 row CL-02 ("stop-work on chemical incompatibility or exposure symptoms"); spec JOB-008 |

| Work area cannot be ventilated as the product SDS requires | Stop the chemical step; escalate | Qualified safety reviewer | spec BRF-008 ("ventilation/respiratory/dust controls"); 29 section 8.2 item 9 |

| An appliance would have to be pulled out, or its gas, water or electrical connection would be disturbed | Do not move it; record the task as held; escalate | Approved appliance-movement policy; licensed trade professional for any connection | C-CL02-04; spec CL-02.SAF |

| Damaged cord, plug or outlet, or water near energized equipment | Stop that task; do not handle it further; escalate | Qualified safety reviewer; licensed electrician where needed | spec START-011; X-07 |
| A task needs a ladder or step stool | Do not start the task; record it as blocked | Approved height and access policy | C-CL02-05; 02 G-005 |
| Suspected mold growth beyond surface staining | Do not disturb; record with photos; escalate | Qualified mold assessor under the company mold definition | X-06; Q-31-10 |

| Deteriorated or chipping paint; damaged or textured ceiling of unknown composition | Do not scrub, brush or vacuum it; record with photos; escalate | EPA RRP-certified renovator or accredited asbestos inspector disposition | C-CL02-06; 31 section 10 CL-02 (RISK) |
| Sensitive surface not yet tested, or reacting or damaged | Stop on that surface; record it | Surface test recorded; owner for damage | spec CL-02.SAF; C-CL02-08 |
| Oven or range on or hot, or its state unknown | Do not start the oven steps | Off and cool per the manufacturer's instructions | 04 CL-02 "hazards" |
| Sharps or biohazard found | Stop; escalate | Owner, per a policy that does not exist yet (02 G-005) | spec Cleaning section intro; START-011 |

Critical holds cannot be overridden by any role; they clear only with a recorded qualified assessment. A hold that exists because a required company policy or module is missing (height and access, chemical compatibility and SDS) cannot be released by override until that policy is approved (source: 31 section 8.3 rule 2; 31 section 8.4 rule 4).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
*Standard block copied verbatim from 31 section 8.5 (PROPOSED wording; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional).*

**CL-02 escalation routes (owner decisions pending, Q-31-05):** chemical exposure: emergency response first, then the incident form (section 20); first-aid references only from the reviewed SDS (source: 29 section 8.2 item 7). Appliance connections (gas, water, electrical) or a request to move a connected appliance: the owner, then a licensed trade professional (source: C-CL02-04). Suspected mold growth: the owner, then a qualified mold assessor or industrial hygienist (source: X-06; Q-31-10). Chipping paint or a damaged or textured ceiling of unknown composition: the owner, then an EPA RRP-certified renovator or accredited asbestos inspector (source: C-CL02-06; Q-31-07). Contacts: `<owner decision: emergency contact>` and `<owner decision: escalation order>` (Q-31-05).

- CL-02 examples to report: chemical splash, irritation or other exposure; cuts from blades, appliance edges or drain debris; slips; strain from moving furniture; damage to customer surfaces, appliances or furniture. Paint chipped during scrubbing is reported as property damage whatever the agreement's "Pre-existing Damage" clause says; that clause is under attorney review (C-CL02-06) (source: spec CL-02.HAZ; JOB-008).
- Q-31-08 (owner and relevant reviewers): is appliance pull-out offered at all, or referred out?
- Q-31-10 (owner; qualified mold assessor): the company definition of mold growth versus cleanable mildew, and the stop rule.
- Q-31-09 (owner; qualified safety professional): the height and access policy; until it exists, CL-02 height tasks stay blocked.
- Q-31-07 (owner; EPA RRP-certified renovator; accredited asbestos inspector): which property-age thresholds trigger lead and asbestos screening for CL-02 painted surfaces and ceilings?
- Q-04-15 (owner; licensed HVAC contractor): the hood and grille split between CL-02 and CL-07.
- Q-31-05 (owner): emergency and escalation contacts, escalation order and after-hours coverage for a two-person team.
- Q-31-11 (owner; qualified safety professional): emergency kit contents, SDS register owner, chemical storage and transport.
- Q-31-15 (owner): which checks (appliances restored, components back in place) need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check while there are two employees?
- Q-31-02 (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish safety text?
- Q-29-10 (local authority; safety reviewer): disposal destinations and rules for chemical residues, mop water and used blades in each service municipality.

sops.title: SOP CL-03: Move-In & Move-Out Cleaning
sops.sourceFile: Standard Of Operations/sop Move-In and Move-Out Cleaning Checklist.md

lines: - The agreement's "Condition of Property" clause requires the client to have the property vacant of furniture, personal items and heavy trash bags before the team arrives. That clause is a customer warranty flagged for attorney review (30 section 5 row 17); HandyHub's own arrival checks are never moved onto the customer (source: agreement; 30 section 4.1 clause 5).

- PROPOSED for the preparation checklist (not yet in the agreement): electricity and water left on; access method and site contact; who authorizes entry, payment and any disposal; the desired end state of the refrigerator and freezer; the landlord or lease checklist, if any; movers and contractors finished or scheduled around the visit (source: 04 CL-03 "customer preparation requirements"; spec CL-03.INT; agreement "Access Delays" clause).
- Every job re-confirms access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions (source: spec CX-005).
*Dispatch and Start Job gates for this service (source: spec APXA-001, APXA-003; 31 section 3.1 row 3). Every added item is pending review.*
Original note, kept verbatim:
*(Property must be completely vacant)*

- Vacancy is confirmed during the initial walkthrough (section 11). If furniture, trash, boxes or personal items remain, do not discard, haul or remove them, and do not move heavy items: record them with photos and escalate (section 10). Their removal is extra scope that needs a change order the customer approves before the extra work and recorded authority to discard (source: original note; spec CL-03.SAF; FIN-008; JOB-005; Do not perform 9).
- Evidence: note
- Occupied property (people living there or belongings in use): occupied move-outs are not covered; record No Start / Blocked and escalate (source: Q-04-05; spec SCH-008).
- Evidence: note
- This SOP is not active: no job uses it until competent review and owner activation (source: owner facts 2026-10-02; 31 section 2.1).
- Intake complete: the spec CL-03.INT facts listed in section 2 (source: spec CL-03.INT).
- An approved estimate version covers the tasks in section 2; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec CX-003; APXA-003).
- Evidence: note

- Utilities: electricity and water availability are confirmed before the visit, and dispatch flags them if missing (source: spec CL-03.INT "utilities/water availability"; SCH-001). If utilities are off or unsafe on arrival, record No Start / Blocked and escalate (source: SCH-008; 04 CL-03 "stop-work conditions"). Whether any work proceeds without power or water is an owner decision; the pricing file's "Utilities Off Fine" line and the agreement's "Utility Fine" clause name different triggers for a utilities charge (Q-28-07).
- Evidence: note

- Access: the access method, the site contact and the person who may authorize entry, payment and any disposal (tenant, landlord or property manager) are recorded; lockbox and door codes stay in the app's secured fields and are never written in notes or sent by text or email (source: 04 CL-03 "prerequisites", GAP; spec COM-002; 27 AUTH-009; Q-30-20).
- Evidence: note

- Chemical products: only approved products with a reviewed SDS; a chemical product without a reviewed SDS is not carried to a job (source: 29 section 8.3 interim rule, PROPOSED; 02 G-008). No product is approved yet: TBD - requires qualified safety reviewer review.

- PPE: available as selected by the qualified safety professional for the chemical and debris tasks. None is selected or stocked yet (C-CL03-02, critical), so those tasks stay blocked until it is (source: spec CL-03.TLS "PPE"; spec START-004).

- Access equipment: any part of the skylight frames, high corners, ceiling fans, hanging fixtures or track lighting that extension tools from floor level cannot reach needs the approved height and access policy and equipment. Neither exists, so tasks that need them stay blocked (source: X-12; 02 G-005; job-planner playbook "A missing ladder or unverified permit keeps affected tasks blocked.").

- Property age and screening: the build year is recorded where known, and ceiling textures and older painted surfaces are screened with the old-property screening questions; until that module exists, the holds in section 12 apply (source: 31 section 3.1 row 3; 04 section 6.2 row CL-03; Q-04-18).
- Evidence: note

- Before this SOP can be activated, the named reviewers approve the holds in section 12: initial walkthrough and existing-condition photos; sharps and chemical control; ceiling textures; height and access; fixture power-off; older paint; refrigerator and freezer end state; garbage-disposal isolation; closeout, waste destination and exit lock-up (source: 31 section 10 CL-03; owner facts L20).
- Evidence: photo

- On arrival: confirm address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants; inspect the actual site against the briefing; capture required existing-condition photos; protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo

- Initial walkthrough of every room before any cleaning: vacancy and left-behind items, unknown debris and sharps, chemicals left on site, pests, mold or moisture, damaged fixtures, ceiling textures and deteriorating paint, utilities, and pre-existing damage to walls, floors, cabinets, appliances, fixtures, windows and doors (source: spec CL-03.SAF "initial walkthrough for damage/hazards"; C-CL03-07). Findings follow section 10.
- Lighting: headlamps or work lights for dark closets, pantries and cabinets, or where power is off (source: inventory "High-Powered LED Headlamps / Work Lights").
- Ventilation adequate for the approved products (source: product SDS; 29 section 8.2).

- Wet-floor sign placement and staging of products and tools: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve (source: spec CL-03.HAZ "slips"; 29 section 7.2 item 9).

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003; START-004).
- Evidence: note

*The original procedure lines below are unchanged and in their original order; the original phase headings are demoted one level, text unchanged. Lines starting with "HOLD" or "FLAG" were added on 2026-10-03; they are pending review and never replace the step text.*

lines: *From spec CL-03.QAC: "checklist completed, cabinets/fixtures/floors as scoped, waste removed to agreed location, pre-existing damage separated from cleaning result". The worker cannot mark the job complete without answering the required checks or recording an exception (source: spec QA-001). Which checks need a second person rather than a self-check is open (Q-31-15).*
| Check | Source | Inspector | Evidence |
| Checklist completed: every step in section 12 answered, with held steps recorded as "held - not done" | spec CL-03.QAC; QA-001 | Worker | Checklist answers; hold records |
| Cabinets, fixtures and floors cleaned as scoped | spec CL-03.QAC | Worker; supervisor where policy requires (Q-31-15) | After photos mapped to rooms and areas (QA-003) |
| Waste removed to the agreed location | spec CL-03.QAC; QA-002 | Worker | Destination recorded; no destination is approved yet (Q-29-10); left-behind items removed only with recorded authority |
| Pre-existing damage separated from the cleaning result | spec CL-03.QAC; START-008 | Worker; supervisor | Existing-condition photos (section 16) compared with after photos |
| Refrigerator and freezer in the recorded end state | spec APXA-005; 31 section 10 CL-03 | Worker | Recorded end state |
| Utilities and components altered within scope restored (fixture power, garbage disposal) | spec APXA-005 | Worker | Checklist answer |

| Property secured at exit | spec CL-03.SAF; 31 section 8.4 rule 3 | Worker; supervisor review of the lock-up record (Q-31-15) | Lock-up record: time, doors and windows checked, key or lockbox handled per the secured access record |
| Baseboards as the agreement describes | agreement "Turnover Standard"; C-CL03-04 | - | Not covered by this SOP: record "not in SOP scope" until the owner decides |
- A customer signature or acknowledgement does not clear an unresolved safety hold (source: quality-assistant playbook "A signed customer form does not clear an unresolved safety hold.").
- Evidence: note
- Missing evidence is recorded as unknown, not as a pass (source: quality-assistant playbook "Missing photos are unknown evidence, not proof of defective work.").
- Evidence: note
- Clean the area, remove waste and protection, and account for tools and materials (source: spec APXA-005; QA-002).

- Restore utilities and components altered within scope: power switched off for "Fixtures" and the garbage disposal is restored as found, by the method the reviewer approves (X-07); the refrigerator and freezer are left in the recorded end state (source: spec APXA-005; section 12 holds).
- Evidence: note
- Remove all HandyHub products, bags and equipment from the property; return unused materials (source: spec APXA-005, APXA-007).
- The original "Deep Mopping" step ends by working backward out of the front door; the closeout hold before it and the exit hold after it apply (source: section 12).

- Waste streams: debris and dust from cleaning; used cloths and pads; empty product containers and product residues; sharps found on site; items left by previous occupants (source: spec CL-03.QAC "waste removed to agreed location"; 29 section 8.2 item 10; inventory "Heavy Contractor Trash Bags").

- No disposal destination or method is approved: waste goes only to the location agreed with the customer and recorded, by a method the reviewer approves for the municipality (source: spec CL-03.QAC; 31 section 3.1 row 15; Q-29-10; 02 G-157; HUMAN REVIEW: local waste authority; qualified safety professional).
- Evidence: note

- Left-behind furniture, trash, boxes and personal items are not discarded or hauled without a change order the customer approves before the extra work and recorded authority to discard; disposal items stay inactive until a waste and disposal policy exists (source: Do not perform 9; 28 section 3.5; Q-30-17).
- Evidence: note
- Sharps: not handled until the reviewer's sharps rule, container and disposal route exist (source: spec CL-03.SAF "control sharps/chemicals"; 29 section 5.2).
- Chemical residues and rinse water: per the product SDS and the municipality's rules (source: 29 section 8.2 item 10).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: existing-condition photos of every room - walls, floors, cabinets, appliances, fixtures, windows and doors - before cleaning, plus any items left behind. PROPOSED as required for CL-03, because damage separation and deposit disputes depend on them; whether they are required is the START-008 configuration decision (source: spec CL-03.SAF "photograph pre-existing issues if required"; CL-03.QAC; START-008; AT-022; 04 CL-03 "completion evidence"; C-CL03-07).
- Evidence: photo
- During: concealed or unexpected conditions (sharps, pests, mold or moisture, damaged fixtures, suspect ceiling textures or paint) with photos and severity (source: spec JOB-004; UXE-006).
- After: photos mapped to rooms and areas (source: spec QA-003); the refrigerator and freezer end state and the lock-up record where policy requires (source: section 12 holds).
- Evidence: photo, note

- Every photo is internal-only by default; sharing with a tenant, landlord or property manager is an owner decision, and marketing use needs separate consent (source: spec REC-002, REC-003; 04 CL-03 "completion evidence"). Avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work; do not photograph the contents of mail or papers left behind (source: 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- Arrival and completion updates are drafts; the worker or admin controls the send (source: spec UXE-008).
- Record the walkthrough outcome: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed; if no customer or representative is present, record it as unavailable (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note

- Held and not-covered items, told in approved wording: items left behind (not removed without a change order); the refrigerator and freezer end state; held tasks (ceiling textures, fixtures whose power could not be confirmed off, tasks that need a ladder); baseboard washing and exterior glass not covered (source: section 12 holds; section 2). Wording TBD - owner.
- Blocked work: only the approved "work blocked" message; no incident details or access codes by text or email (source: spec NTF-007, COM-002).

- Tenant, landlord or property-manager disputes about the cleaning or a deposit go to the owner (source: 04 CL-03 "responsible skill / business role", handyhub-customer-service for tenant and landlord disputes).

- What not to say: any security-deposit promise ("guarantee the return of your security deposit", "help tenants secure their security deposits"), "sterilization", "absolute", "pristine", "every square inch", "flawless" (source: C-CL03-03; agreement "Deposit Sign-off" clause; main plan section 3; 32 register A row 22 and register B rows 1 and 2).
- Evidence: note
- Care notes only from approved product data; none are approved yet (source: spec QA-008).
- Required QA checks answered or an exception recorded (source: spec QA-001; section 13).
- Evidence: note
- Existing-condition photos on file where required, and after photos mapped to rooms and areas (source: spec START-008, QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup and waste handling done as approved; waste at the agreed location (source: spec QA-002, CL-03.QAC; sections 14 and 15).
- Refrigerator and freezer in the recorded end state; utilities and components altered within scope restored (source: spec APXA-005).
- Evidence: note
- Tools and materials accounted for (source: spec APXA-005).
- Property secured and lock-up recorded (source: spec CL-03.SAF; 31 section 8.4 rule 3).
- Evidence: note
- Open holds, left-behind items and punch items recorded; walkthrough outcome recorded (source: spec QA-004; APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- The job closes only when the required operational and financial steps are complete (source: spec APXA-007).
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:

*Standard block copied verbatim from 31 SOP standard section 8.5 (PROPOSED wording; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional; attorney licensed in KY and/or IN for the "right to stop work" sentence; bilingual reviewer for Spanish).*

**Service stop triggers and holds (CL-03).** Card stop guidance (spec CL-03.SAF): "initial walkthrough for damage/hazards; photograph pre-existing issues if required; control sharps/chemicals; secure property at exit".
| Trigger or hold | Action | Cleared by (evidence) | Source |

| Property not vacant on arrival: furniture, trash, boxes or personal items remain | Do not discard, haul or remove them, and do not move heavy items; record with photos; escalate | Owner: approved change order and recorded authority to discard | Original note (section 3); Do not perform 9; Q-30-17 |
| Occupied property | No Start / Blocked; escalate | Owner (occupied move-outs are not covered) | Q-04-05; spec SCH-008 |
| Initial walkthrough or required existing-condition photos not done | Do not start cleaning | Walkthrough and photo record (START-008 configuration) | spec CL-03.SAF; C-CL03-07 |
| Sharps, biohazard, droppings or infestation | Stop the affected area; escalate | Qualified safety reviewer; owner | spec CL-03.SAF; 31 section 10 CL-03 |

| Textured, damaged or deteriorating ceiling, or deteriorating paint, of unknown composition | Do not disturb; escalate | Accredited asbestos inspector or EPA RRP-certified renovator assessment accepted by the owner | 31 section 7.2 rank 1; spec START-011; Q-31-07 |
| Suspected mold, moisture or an active leak | Do not disturb; escalate | Qualified mold assessor (company mold definition pending, Q-31-10) | Stop-work block above; 31 section 5.8 |

| Power to a fan or fixture cannot be confirmed off; damaged fixture or exposed wiring | Do not dust or damp-wipe it; escalate | Qualified safety reviewer (isolation method); licensed electrician for any electrical defect | 31 section 10 CL-03 (RISK); Do not perform 1 |
| Utilities off or unsafe on arrival | No Start / Blocked; escalate | Owner (utilities policy) | spec CL-03.INT; SCH-008 |
| Gas odor | Emergency (section 19, step 2) | Emergency services; incident report (section 20) | spec START-011, BRF-013 |

| Chemical product without a reviewed SDS, a mix the SDS does not allow, or ventilation not possible | Do not use the product; escalate | Reviewed SDS and approved product | 29 section 8.3; Do not perform 6 |
| PPE selected by the reviewer not available | The chemical or debris task stays blocked | PPE available as selected | C-CL03-02; spec START-004 |
| Task needs a ladder or other access equipment | The task stays blocked | Approved height and access policy and equipment | X-12; 02 G-005; job-planner playbook |

| Customer or site contact asks for exterior glass, floor stripping, drain clearing, removal of left-behind items or other work not in scope | Do not perform; record the request | Owner (change order or referral) | Section 2; spec JOB-005, FIN-008 |
| Refrigerator and freezer end state not recorded | Escalate before leaving; record the state left | Recorded end-state instruction | 31 section 10 CL-03; spec APXA-005 |
| Property cannot be secured at exit | Critical hold: escalate before leaving and follow the owner's recorded instruction | Owner | spec CL-03.SAF; 31 section 8.4 rule 3 |

Critical holds cannot be overridden by any role; they clear only with a recorded qualified assessment. Suspect hazardous material is a critical class, and leaving a property unsecured is treated as critical (source: 31 section 8.3 rule 2; 31 section 8.4 rule 3).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
*Standard block copied verbatim from 31 section 8.5 (PROPOSED wording; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional).*

**CL-03 escalation routes (owner decisions pending, Q-31-05):** left-behind items, an occupied property or a request to discard property go to the owner, with the attorney question on third-party property open (Q-30-17); sharps, biohazard, droppings or infestation go to the owner, then the qualified safety professional; suspect ceiling textures or deteriorating paint go to the owner, then an accredited asbestos inspector or EPA RRP-certified renovator (Q-31-07); suspected mold goes to the owner, then a qualified mold assessor (Q-31-10); utilities that are off or unsafe go to the owner; a gas odor is an emergency (step 2 above); a property that cannot be secured goes to the owner at once (critical hold). Contacts: `<owner decision: emergency contact>` and `<owner decision: escalation order>` (Q-31-05).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].

*Standard block copied verbatim from 31 section 8.5 (PROPOSED wording). HUMAN REVIEW: attorney licensed in KY and/or IN for the fault and liability sentence; insurance broker for any insurer-notification step added later.*

- CL-03 examples to report: cuts or punctures from debris or sharps, chemical exposure, slips and falls, electrical contact, damage to the property, items discarded or moved without authority, a property left unsecured (source: spec CL-03.HAZ; JOB-008).
- Q-30-17 (owner; attorney): what are the rules for third-party property, including items left behind in move-outs? Until answered, nothing is discarded (Do not perform 9).
- Q-04-05 (owner): are occupied move-outs offered, and under CL-03 or CL-02?
- C-CL03-04 (owner; attorney if the agreement is revised): add a reviewed baseboard step, or revise the agreement and the main plan?
- Q-31-05 (owner): emergency and escalation contacts, escalation order and after-hours coverage for a two-person team.

- Q-31-07 (owner; EPA RRP-certified renovator; accredited asbestos inspector): which property-age thresholds trigger lead and asbestos screening, including the CL-03 ceiling textures and painted sills and doors?
- Q-31-09 (owner; qualified safety professional): height and access policy - maximum working heights, equipment types and who may use them.
- Q-31-10 (owner; qualified mold assessor): company definition of mold growth versus cleanable mildew, and the stop rule.
- Q-31-11 (owner; qualified safety professional): emergency kit contents, SDS register owner, chemical storage and transport.
- Q-31-15 (owner): which checks (lock-up, damage separation) need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check while there are two employees?
- Q-31-02 (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish safety text?
- Q-29-10 (local authority; safety reviewer): disposal destinations and rules for bagged waste, sharps and chemical residues in each service municipality.
- 04 CL-03 "customer preparation requirements" gap (owner): how the customer's refrigerator and freezer end-state instruction is captured before the visit.

sops.title: SOP CL-04: Post-Construction & Post-Renovation Cleaning
sops.sourceFile: Standard Of Operations/sop Post-Construction Cleaning Checklist.md

lines: - The agreement requires that "All primary trades (painters, floor installers, plumbers) must be completely finished with their work in target zones before the Company begins detailed polishing" and that the client keep the site safe, with active power and running water; verify both on arrival and record any difference (source: agreement "Construction Complete" and "On-Site Safety"; spec START-007). The site-safety clause is under attorney review (see the agreement review notes).
- Evidence: note

- Missing preparation items (GAP): area release per area, access and keys, HVAC status, paint cure dates, labels that must stay, debris or dumpster location, parking, general-contractor walkthrough date, property age (source: 04 CL-04 customer preparation requirements). A PROPOSED customer checklist is sent with the appointment reminder once the owner and attorney approve the wording (source: spec NTF-004, NTF-005).

- Occupied or partly occupied property: occupants, children and pets are kept out of the active work area; the occupant and pet module is pending qualified safety review (source: spec CL-04.INT "occupancy readiness"; APXA-002; X-11; 31 section 5.8).
- A customer's or contractor's statement or signature never clears a hold (source: owner facts 2026-10-02 "acknowledgment cannot bypass critical holds"; risk-triage playbook L27).
All pending qualified review. A precondition that is not met keeps the affected tasks blocked (source: job-planner playbook "A missing ladder or unverified permit keeps affected tasks blocked.").

- Area release: each area is released for cleaning by all trades before each phase visit, and no unsafe active construction is under way in it; a written release per area is PROPOSED (source: spec CL-04.SAF; agreement "Construction Complete"; 04 CL-04 prerequisites, PROPOSED). The client's site-safety duty in the agreement ("On-Site Safety") does not replace HandyHub's own pre-start site check (source: spec START-007; risk-triage playbook "Signing a checkbox cannot bypass an unresolved structural hazard."; C-CL04-04).
- Power and water: verified safe before corded equipment or any wet step (source: spec CL-04.SAF "verify power/water safety").

- Property age and renovation history: the approximate build year or "unknown", and what the renovation disturbed, are recorded before dispatch (source: spec BRF-003 "approximate age if known"; spec CL-04.INT "dust/debris type"). Renovation dust or debris from disturbed paint in a pre-1978 or unknown-age home, or debris suspected to contain asbestos, is a hold (section 12) (source: spec START-011; risk-triage playbook "A pre-1978 painted surface is not cleared by a customer saying it looks safe."; X-13). What evidence is needed from the renovator, and whether any obligation applies to cleaning such dust, are open questions per Kentucky and Indiana municipality (04 CL-04 permit/license flags; Q-31-07).
- Evidence: note
- Dust control and respiratory protection: decided by the qualified safety professional before any dust-generating step (section 12 hold; C-CL04-03).
- Height: steps that need ladders or access equipment stay on hold until the height and access policy exists (02 G-005; C-CL04-01; 31 section 8.4).
- Chemicals: only products with a reviewed SDS are carried to the job (29 section 8.3, PROPOSED); no acid step (C-CL04-02).
- Glass: a pre-work glass inspection with photos is recorded before any blade scraping (section 12 hold; C-CL04-05).
- Evidence: note

- Before leaving: confirm job, customer, address and time; read the latest changes; verify access and parking; review scope, exclusions, hazards and safety; load critical tools, equipment and materials; confirm required documents and approvals (source: spec APXA-001).

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003). High-risk flags may require separate checkboxes or supervisor confirmation (source: spec START-004); permit, licence or qualification flags block start until approved (source: spec START-010).
- Evidence: note

- Materials readiness: missing material may block start, for example the flat mop, floor mop and bucket, bags, filters, cleaners and metal polish, which are not stocked (source: spec START-006; C-CL04-12).
- Phase visits: one visit per phase, dependent on a general-contractor walkthrough or area release (source: 04 CL-04 applicable software workflow; spec SCH-002).

- On arrival: confirm address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants; inspect the actual site against the briefing; capture the required existing-condition photos; protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo

- Pre-start site check: record any difference from the briefing, including areas not released, trades still working, and missing or unsafe power or water; material differences trigger Risk Triage or supervisor review (source: spec START-007; CL-04.SAF).
- Evidence: note
- Confirm the area release and the other section 3 preconditions before the first step in each area and at each phase visit (source: section 3; spec CL-04.SAF).
- Existing-condition photos before work, including every window or mirror to be blade-scraped (section 16) (source: spec START-008, BRF-012; X-02; C-CL04-05).
- Evidence: photo
- Protect finished surfaces and fixtures in the work area; protection methods pending review (source: spec APXA-002 "protect work area"; CL-04.QAC "residues treated without damage").
- Stage bags and the sharps container proposed in the inventory before debris is gathered; pending review (source: spec CL-04.SAF "sharps management"; CL-04.MAT "bags").

*Original procedure, verbatim and in its original order; the original phase headings are demoted one level with their text unchanged. The HOLD and FLAG lines are additions pending qualified review: a precondition hold sits directly before the step it gates, and a hold or flag that suspends, limits or flags a step sits directly after it (36 D-36-17). They never replace or reword a step.*

> HOLD (C-CL04-04) - before "HEPA Vacuuming" below and every later step in an area: the area is released for cleaning by all trades, and no unsafe active construction is under way in it; power and water are verified safe before any corded tool or wet step; sharps are managed by the reviewer's method before debris is gathered or blades are used. If an area is not released, construction is still active, or power or water is unsafe, do not start: record No Start / Blocked with evidence and escalate (spec SCH-008). The agreement's "On-Site Safety" clause does not replace this check (spec START-007). Pending qualified review. (source: spec CL-04.SAF "confirm area released for cleaning; do not work amid unsafe active construction; respiratory/dust control; sharps management; verify power/water safety"; CL-04.HAZ; START-011; 31 section 10)

lines: > HOLD (X-13) - before "HEPA Vacuuming" below and every later step that vacuums, sweeps, wipes or bags renovation dust or debris: in a pre-1978 or unknown-age home where the renovation disturbed painted surfaces or older materials, or wherever debris is suspected to contain asbestos, do not disturb the dust or debris; stop and escalate. HEPA capture does not clear suspect material. Release only by the qualified reviewer named in section 10. Pending review by an EPA RRP-certified renovator and an accredited asbestos inspector. (source: spec START-011 "suspect hazardous materials"; 04 CL-04 hazards; risk-triage playbook "A pre-1978 painted surface is not cleared by a customer saying it looks safe."; owner facts 2026-10-02 "Unknown is not safe"; 29 section 8.1)

If the condition cannot be recorded, or the manufacturer's instructions restrict blade use, do not scrape; stop and escalate. The agreement's glass-scratch waiver depends on this evidence and is under attorney review. Pending qualified review. Glass scraping carries opposite waiver logic in the DW-04 and CL-04 agreements, and which service owns construction-glass scraping is an open decision (Q-04-07). The step text is unchanged. Bulbs and fixtures out of reach from the floor fall under the height hold above. Pending qualified review. Who runs the HVAC system for the check is undefined (04 CL-04 quality checklist, GAP); no HVAC work is performed under this SOP (section 2, Do not perform item 1), and duct interiors belong to CL-07 (04 section 5.1). Never promise "zero dust" to the customer (Do not perform item 8). The step text is unchanged.
