lines: > FLAG: the procedure above has no closeout: waste destination, used blades, filters and bags, after photos mapped to areas, and the walkthrough outcome. The job is not complete until the items in sections 14 to 16 and 18 are done or an exception is recorded; those items are PROPOSED, pending review. (source: spec QA-002 to QA-004; APXA-005; 04 CL-04 completion evidence, GAP)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 3: Final Buffing, Polish & Turnover"

lines: A worker cannot mark the job complete without answering these checks or recording an exception (source: spec QA-001). Photos cannot prove hidden conditions: do not infer hazardous-material clearance or electrical safety from an image (source: quality-assistant playbook "Do not infer hidden fasteners, structural adequacy, hazardous-material clearance or electrical safety from an image.").
| Check (spec CL-04.QAC) | How it is verified (pending review) | Evidence | Inspector |

| Fine dust removed in passes | Each phase's pass is completed in each released area by the reviewed dust-control method; "zero dust film" in the "Air Check" step is not the acceptance criterion | After photos mapped to areas (spec QA-003) | Worker self-check; whether a supervisor inspects is Q-31-15 |

| Residues treated without damage | Paint, plaster and adhesive residues removed only with approved products and methods; scraped glass compared with its pre-work photos; any damage recorded and reported as an incident (spec JOB-008 "property damage") | Before and after photos of scraped glass and treated surfaces | Worker; supervisor for any damage |

| Vents/fixtures/surfaces detailed as scoped | Fixtures and hardware, cabinetry interiors, walls, metals and floors as the approved scope lists them; vents only if scoped, and no vent step exists yet (section 2); uncovered items are recorded, not improvised | After photos mapped to areas or tasks (spec QA-003) | Worker |

| Site ready for turnover | All scoped areas complete; waste removed per section 15; tools and materials accounted for; walkthrough outcome recorded (spec QA-004). A cleaning standard, not a safety or occupancy certification (risk-triage skill "never certify site safety") | Walkthrough record; cleanup photos (spec QA-002) | Worker; the customer or general-contractor representative at the walkthrough |
- Clean the work area; remove waste and any protection placed during setup; account for tools and materials; restore utilities or components altered within scope (source: spec APXA-005; QA-002).

- Emptying the HEPA vacuum and changing its filters and bags: method per the vacuum manufacturer and the qualified safety reviewer; collected dust is a waste stream (section 15). TBD - pending qualified safety review (source: spec CL-04.MAT "filters"; 29 section 8.2 control 10).
- Cleanup photos may be required for dusty work (source: spec QA-002); see section 16.
- Evidence: photo
- Cleaning is the service itself; this section covers HandyHub's own equipment, materials, protection and waste.
TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

- Waste streams from the steps: construction debris gathered in "Bulk Debris" (drywall pieces, wood shavings, sawdust); peeled films, tape remnants and stickers; used cloths and duster sleeves; used blades (sharps); HEPA filters and bags with collected dust; chemical residues and empty containers (source: original steps in section 12; spec CL-04.MAT "bags, filters"; 29 section 8.2 control 10).

- Containers, destination, haul-away and who pays: owner decision with the rules of the actual municipality. The pricing file includes "pulling construction trash" in Phase 1 but prices no disposal, and disposal items stay inactive until a waste policy exists (source: 28 sections 3.5 and 7.4; 02 G-157; Q-29-10; Q-28-15). The debris or dumpster location is a missing customer-preparation item (04 CL-04).
- Used blades are sharps, handled by the reviewer's sharps method; a sharps container is proposed in the inventory (source: spec CL-04.SAF "sharps management").

- Suspect hazardous debris (possible lead or asbestos) is not bagged, moved or removed by HandyHub; it is a stop-and-refer condition, not a disposal line (source: section 2, Do not perform; spec START-011; 28 section 3.5).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: arrival and existing-condition photos; start is blocked until they are captured or an authorized reason is recorded (source: spec START-008). Include every window or mirror to be blade-scraped, showing existing scratches, defects and debris under protective films, on which the agreement's glass clause depends, and the new finishes, fixtures and appliances in the work areas (source: 04 CL-04 completion evidence "Pre-work glass condition evidence is needed if any scratch waiver survives attorney review"; X-02; spec BRF-012).
- Evidence: photo, note

- During: unexpected conditions with photos and severity, for example suspect debris, exposed wiring or damage found (source: spec JOB-004; APXA-004); the area-release status for each phase visit (source: 04 CL-04 prerequisites, PROPOSED).
- After: photos mapped to areas or tasks (source: spec QA-003), plus cleanup photos for this dusty service (source: spec QA-002 "Cleanup photos may be required for dusty/dirty services").
- Evidence: photo
- A photo never establishes hazardous-material clearance or electrical safety (source: quality-assistant playbook).
- Privacy: internal-only by default; avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).

- Arrival and completion updates use approved templates; a blocked job, including an area that is not released or a hazardous-material hold, uses only the approved "work blocked" message, with no incident details or access codes by text or email (source: spec NTF-007, COM-002).
- Before each phase visit, confirm with the customer or general contractor which areas are released (source: 04 CL-04 prerequisites, PROPOSED; spec SCH-002).

- Do not promise "zero dust", a safe site, readiness for occupancy, air quality or scratch-free glass (source: section 2, Do not perform item 8; 31 section 3.5 rule 5; spec CL-04.QAC "site ready for turnover").
- Questions about the glass clause or about damage go to the owner; do not discuss fault or liability with the customer (source: section 20 block; agreement review notes).
- Walkthrough: record the outcome as accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Care notes come only from approved product data (source: spec QA-008).
- Explain the invoice and payment next step without unauthorized promises (source: spec APXA-006); per-phase invoicing and the net terms are under attorney review (see the agreement review notes).
Done means all of the following, recorded in the job (source: spec QA-001 to QA-004; CL-04.QAC; APXA-005 to APXA-007):
- Every section 13 check answered, or an exception recorded (QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- After photos mapped to areas or tasks (QA-003), with cleanup photos (QA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- Waste handled by the approved method (section 15); used blades, filters and bags accounted for.
- Tools and materials accounted for (APXA-005, APXA-007).
- Walkthrough outcome recorded with punch items (QA-004); open punch items stay linked to the job (QA-005).
- Evidence: note
- Each phase recorded as complete per released area; the next phase visit needs the area released again (source: 04 CL-04 prerequisites, PROPOSED).
- Evidence: note
- Unresolved issues, incidents and change requests submitted before the job is closed (APXA-007).
- Final completion is a human sign-off; the quality review only recommends readiness (source: quality-assistant playbook "Recommend readiness for human sign-off; do not set final completion").
- Evidence: note
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:
Service-specific stop triggers and holds (all pending qualified review; release roles per 31 section 8.3):

- Card guidance, verbatim: "confirm area released for cleaning; do not work amid unsafe active construction; respiratory/dust control; sharps management; verify power/water safety" (source: spec CL-04.SAF).
- Card hazards, verbatim: "fine dust, silica/wood dust, sharp debris, unfinished electrical/fixtures, ladders, chemicals" (source: spec CL-04.HAZ).

- HOLD C-CL04-04, area release and active construction: no phase visit and no step starts in an area that is not released for cleaning or where unsafe active construction is under way; record No Start / Blocked with evidence (spec SCH-008, AT-030). Release: supervisor, with the area release recorded (a written release per area is PROPOSED, 04 CL-04 prerequisites).
- Evidence: note

- HOLD C-CL04-04, power, water and electrical: power and water verified safe before corded equipment or any wet step; ELECTRICAL - REVIEW on the "Fixtures & Hardware" step; exposed or unfinished wiring, open boxes or damaged fixtures = STOP. Release: qualified safety professional; a licensed electrician for anything electrical.
- HOLD C-CL04-04, sharps: sharps management by the reviewer's method before debris is gathered or blades are used.

- HOLD C-CL04-03, dust: DUST-CONTROL METHOD PENDING SAFETY REVIEW on the dry dust pull and the sweeping step; the inventory's "Mandatory" respirator statement stays. A hold caused by a missing policy cannot be released by override (31 section 8.4).
- HOLD C-CL04-01, height: steps or parts of steps that need ladders or access equipment, and any work "Above 12 ft", stay on hold until the height and access policy exists (31 section 8.4).
- HOLD C-CL04-02, acid: no phosphoric-acid or other acid step until an SDS-based reviewed step exists; the agreement's "Chemical Use" authorization does not release this hold.

- HOLD C-CL04-05, glass: no blade scraping until a pre-work glass inspection with photos is recorded; stop if the glass condition cannot be recorded or the manufacturer's instructions restrict blade use.
- Evidence: note

- HOLD X-13, suspect lead or asbestos in renovation dust or debris: stop and escalate; do not vacuum, sweep, wipe or bag it until a qualified reviewer decides. Release: an EPA RRP-certified renovator or an accredited asbestos inspector, as the case requires, with the owner.

- Suspect hazardous material and unapproved electrical scope are critical holds that no role can override; they clear only with a recorded qualified assessment (31 section 8.3). Holds that exist because a company policy or module is missing (height and access; chemicals and SDS; the dust and respiratory module of 04 section 5.2 rule (c)) behave as critical holds until it is approved (31 section 8.4 rule 4).
- Evidence: note
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
Service roles for CL-04 (contacts and escalation order are owner decisions, Q-31-05):
- Area not released, unsafe active construction or other trades still working: supervisor, with the general contractor or the customer's representative (C-CL04-04).
- Exposed or unfinished wiring, unsafe temporary power, water near energized equipment: qualified safety professional; licensed electrician (C-CL04-04).
- Suspect lead or asbestos in renovation dust or debris: EPA RRP-certified renovator; accredited asbestos inspector (X-13).
- Dust and respiratory protection, access equipment and height, chemical products: qualified safety professional (C-CL04-03, C-CL04-01, C-CL04-02).
- Glass condition, glass damage or a waiver question: owner, with the attorney (C-CL04-05).
- Scope questions (floor scraping, vents, floor buffing, cabinet exteriors, acid treatment, work "Above 12 ft"): owner; change order before added work (C-CL04-10; spec FIN-008).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].

- For this service, report at least: glass scratched or broken during scraping; cuts from blades or sharp debris; electrical contact or shock; suspected exposure to dust or debris that may contain lead or asbestos; a chemical splash or exposure; a fall from access equipment; a slip on a wet floor; vacuum or tool failure (source: spec JOB-008 "Injury, property damage, near miss, customer conflict, tool/equipment failure and suspected hazardous-material exposure"; CL-04.HAZ).

- **Q-31-18** (HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional; owner; licensing reviewer): confirm the hazard order of 31 section 7.2, in particular whether respirable dust and silica (rank 12, led by this service) moves up, and which of this SOP's holds are critical holds under the 31 section 8.4 rule.

- **Q-31-07** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: EPA RRP-certified renovator, accredited asbestos inspector): which property-age thresholds trigger lead and asbestos screening for post-renovation cleaning, and what evidence from the renovator releases the X-13 hold?
- **Q-31-08** (owner and the relevant reviewers): is acid grout-haze removal offered at all, or referred out?
- **Q-31-09** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional): height and access policy; is work "Above 12 ft" in scope, excluded or subcontracted (02 C-CL04-01)?
- **02 C-CL04-03** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional): is dry sweeping acceptable, or are HEPA or wet methods required, and is a respiratory program needed?
- **02 C-CL04-10** (owner): floor scraping, vents, floor buffing and cabinet exteriors: keep each with a reviewed step, or exclude it? Where does the CL-04 and CL-07 boundary fall for vents?
- **Q-04-07** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: attorney): which single service scrapes construction glass, under which attorney-reviewed clause?
- **04 CL-04 quality checklist and customer preparation requirements** (owner): who runs the HVAC system for the "Air Check", and which labels must stay in place after cleaning?

- **Q-31-01** (owner): who are the competent reviewers for this SOP (qualified safety professional, EPA RRP-certified renovator, accredited asbestos inspector, licensed electrician), and how is their competence evidenced?
- **Q-31-05** (owner): emergency and escalation contacts and escalation order for a two-person team.
- **Q-31-11** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional): emergency kit contents and the SDS register owner.
- **Q-31-15** (owner): does any section 13 check need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check?
- **Q-31-02** (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish version?

sops.title: SOP CL-05: Airbnb Turnover & Vacation Rental Management
sops.sourceFile: Standard Of Operations/sop Airbnb Cleaning and Turnover Checklist.md

lines: PROPOSED from the intake fields; customer-facing wording goes through 30 and 32 (source: spec CL-05.INT; 04 CL-05 customer preparation requirements):
- checkout and check-in times for each turnover;
- the host checklist;
- linens and towels: who supplies them, par levels and whether laundry is done on site (C-CL05-12);
- amenities and restock levels, with restock items stored in the host's locked supply closet as the agreement's "Inventory Logistics" clause says (supply conflict, Q-29-13);
- the damage-report rule and the guest-property rule (C-CL05-10);
- Evidence: note
- the access and security-codes policy: the host enters codes in the app's secured fields, never by text or email (spec COM-002; 31 section 5.8 credential rule, PROPOSED);
- trash and recycling location, welcome book, thermostat and Wi-Fi preferences, and parking (04 CL-05 customer preparation requirements, GAP).
Every turnover re-confirms that access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions are still current (source: spec CX-005).
- This SOP is a draft and is not active; no job is dispatched under it until the owner records approval after competent review (source: owner facts 2026-10-02; spec HND-004; 04 section 2.4).
- Evidence: note

- Before leaving: confirm job, customer, address and time; read the latest changes; verify access and parking; review scope, exclusions, hazards and safety; load critical tools, equipment and materials; check customer-supplied items; confirm required documents and approvals (source: spec APXA-001).
- Intake complete for the property: "checkout/check-in times, host checklist, linens, amenities/restock levels, damage-report rule, access/security codes policy" (source: spec CL-05.INT).
- Evidence: note

- The host's guest-property rule (discard, hold or notify) is recorded at intake; until an owner-approved guest-property policy exists, no guest property is discarded (source: spec CL-05.SAF; 02 C-CL05-10; 02 G-005).
- Evidence: note

- Access information is available only in the app's secured fields for the service day; it is never written into notes, messages or photos (source: spec CL-05.SAF "protect access codes", COM-002; 27 AUTH-009, PROPOSED).

- Checkout has happened: the agreement makes its window conditional on "immediate property access"; if guests are still present, the worker does not enter (Do not perform, item 9) (source: agreement "Operational Timeline" clause; 31 section 10).

- Restock items: who supplies them is undecided (Q-29-13). Host-supplied items stay in the host's locked supply closet under the agreement; missing items are recorded (source: agreement "Inventory Logistics" clause; spec START-009, JOB-004).
- Evidence: note

- Same-day capacity: how many turnovers two employees can take in one day, and whether the pricing file's time caps mean elapsed time or person-hours, are owner decisions; scheduling must respect working hours and worker capability (source: spec SCH-003; 04 CL-05 labor assumptions).

- Permit, license and qualification flags: none is set for CL-05. Whether co-hosting or any other part of this service needs a license in Kentucky or Indiana is an OPEN QUESTION, and unknown applicability does not default to "no requirement" (source: spec START-010; 30 section 8 row 24; risk-triage playbook).
- Start only when the job shows Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003).
- Evidence: note

- On arrival: confirm address, work area and contact; park and access appropriately; identify pets and occupants; inspect the actual site against the briefing; capture the required existing-condition photos; protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003, START-004).
- Evidence: note
- Existing-condition evidence: the Phase 1 "Damage Scan" and "Evidence Collection" steps are the arrival record, captured in the app (source: spec START-008; 27 AUTH-034, PROPOSED).
- Evidence: note
- Host-supplied restock and linens: record what is present and what is missing (source: spec START-009, JOB-004).
- Evidence: note
- Staging of the caddy, supplies and laundry bags: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

> HOLD (C-CL05-01): before entry and before the "Damage Scan" step below - use access information only from the app's secured fields on the service day; never write down, photograph or send a door, lockbox or alarm code. Pending privacy owner review. (source: spec CL-05.SAF "protect access codes"; COM-002; 27 AUTH-009, PROPOSED)

lines: Observable checks from the spec card; the worker answers each check or records an exception (source: spec CL-05.QAC, QA-001). A worker's self-check does not replace a supervisor inspection where one is required (source: quality-assistant playbook).
| Check | Evidence | Source |
| Clean and reset per the host checklist | Checklist answered per room or area | Spec CL-05.QAC, CL-05.INT "host checklist", QA-001 |
| Linens and amenities | Beds made, towels staged and amenities restocked to the host's levels; shortages recorded | Spec CL-05.QAC, CL-05.INT "amenities/restock levels" |
| Documented damage | Damage photos and notes on the job record, internal-only by default | Spec CL-05.QAC, JOB-004, REC-002 |
| Staging standard | After photos mapped to rooms | Spec CL-05.QAC, QA-003 |
| Property locked | Lock-up confirmation recorded (hold at the end of section 12) | Spec CL-05.QAC, CL-05.SAF |
| Host notified of exceptions | Exception note logged on the job and sent through the approved channel (Q-27-16) | Spec CL-05.QAC, JOB-009 |
- Kitchen standard: undefined (C-CL05-V01); no kitchen check beyond the "Kitchen Check" step is added until the owner decides.

- The "zero stray hairs" (Phase 3) and "zero wrinkles" (Phase 4) wording in section 12 is an internal target, not a customer promise; it stays verbatim and is never repeated to hosts or guests as a guarantee (source: 31 section 3.5 rule 5).
- Clean the area, remove waste, account for tools and materials, and restore anything altered within scope (source: spec APXA-005, QA-002).
- The exit sequence is the original Phase 5 "Floor Care" step (working backward out of the front door), followed by the lock-up hold at the end of section 12.
- Soiled linens stay separate from clean linens, as the inventory file's color-coded laundry bags intend (source: inventory file).
- Physical keys or fobs used for entry go back to their recorded place (source: 27 AUTH-009, PROPOSED: physical keys are custody items with an issue and return log).
- Evidence: note

- Waste streams: household trash and recycling from the unit, used wipes and cleaning residue, and packaging; perishable guest food is not discarded while its step is held (C-CL05-10). Destination: the trash and recycling location the host provides, an intake item not yet defined (04 CL-05 customer preparation requirements); otherwise TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.
- Sharps and biohazard waste is not handled without an approved policy; disposal rules per municipality are an open question (source: 31 section 3.1; 29 section 8.2 control 10; Q-29-10).
- Hazardous waste is not handled without an approved policy (source: 31 section 3.1; 02 G-078).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: All photos are captured in the app and kept on the job record, internal-only by default; they never show access codes, guests or other people, documents or valuables not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002, COM-002; 31 section 3.5 rule 7; 27 AUTH-034, PROPOSED).
- Before: damage and extreme-mess photos from the Phase 1 damage scan (source: spec START-008; original Phase 1).
- During: sharps, biohazard, damage or urgent maintenance found, with severity (source: spec JOB-004).
- After: wide-angle completion photos of the bedroom, bathroom and kitchen (original Phase 5), mapped to the room (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo

- Delivery to the host: held until the owner and privacy owner decide the channels (Q-27-16, Q-31-12); once decided, shares go only through the app's share or message functions (source: 27 AUTH-034, PROPOSED).
- The customer is the host or property manager. Arrival and completion updates are drafts, and the worker or admin controls the send (source: spec UXE-008; agreement preamble).

- Exceptions - damage, missing or broken amenities, guest items left behind, urgent maintenance and any lock-up problem - are reported to the host through the approved channel and logged on the job (source: spec CL-05.QAC "host notified of exceptions", JOB-009; Q-27-16).
- Evidence: note
- Guest communication is a candidate exclusion for the owner to decide (source: 04 CL-05 exclusions row).
- Never send access codes, incident details or internal notes by SMS or email (source: spec COM-002).
- No promises of review outcomes, completion times or absolute results to hosts or guests (source: 31 section 3.3 entry 8; 31 section 3.5 rule 5).
- Blocked work: use only the approved "work blocked" message (source: spec NTF-007).
- Walkthrough: where the host or a representative is present, record the outcome - accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Every check in section 13 is answered or has a recorded exception (source: spec QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- The property is locked and the host is notified of exceptions (source: spec CL-05.SAF, CL-05.QAC).
- Damage is documented, and completion photos are captured in the app and mapped to rooms (source: spec CL-05.QAC, QA-003).
- Evidence: photo, note
- No guest property was discarded without policy; items left behind are recorded (source: spec CL-05.SAF).
- Evidence: note
- No access code appears in any note, photo or message (source: spec COM-002; 27 AUTH-009, PROPOSED).
- Cleanup is done and the walkthrough outcome is recorded (source: spec QA-002, QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Host-supplied restock and linens have their START-009 record (source: spec START-009).
- Evidence: note
- Closeout: unresolved issues and incident or change follow-ups are submitted; the job closes only when the required operational and financial steps are complete (source: spec APXA-006, APXA-007).
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:
Service-specific stop triggers and holds for CL-05 (pending qualified review):
- Card rule: "protect access codes; never discard guest property without policy; escalate biohazard/damage; verify lockup and urgent maintenance" (source: spec CL-05.SAF).

- HOLD (C-CL05-01): needles, sharps, blood or bodily fluids found or suspected in bedding, towels, bathrooms, drains, bins or trash - do not handle them; stop that task and escalate (section 19). Cleanup beyond policy is not performed (section 2) (source: spec CL-05.HAZ, CL-05.SAF; 31 section 10).
- HOLD (C-CL05-01): access codes are used only from the app's secured fields and are never written, photographed or sent (source: spec CL-05.SAF; COM-002; 27 AUTH-009, PROPOSED).

- HOLD (C-CL05-01): do not leave the property unlocked. If it cannot be secured, stop and escalate; this is treated as a critical hold, so an acknowledgment or a signature does not clear it (source: spec CL-05.SAF "verify lockup"; 31 section 8.4 rule 3).

- HOLD (C-CL05-01): damage or urgent maintenance found (for example an active leak or a lock that does not secure) - record it with photos and severity and escalate; do not repair it (source: spec CL-05.SAF; JOB-004).
- HOLD (C-CL05-10): no guest property, including perishable food, is discarded until the owner sets a guest-property policy (source: spec CL-05.SAF; 31 section 10).
- HOLD (Q-27-16): photo delivery by host portal or text message is held; photos stay in the app (source: 31 section 10; 27 AUTH-034, PROPOSED).
- Guests still in the unit at arrival: do not enter; record the late checkout and escalate (PROPOSED) (source: 31 section 10).
- Evidence: note
- The agreement's completion window and any late-checkout delay never override a hold or the stop-work rule (C-CL05-02) (source: 31 section 10; master section 12).

- Extreme mess or extra work beyond the standard turnover: record it with photos; extra work only after an approved change order (source: spec FIN-008, JOB-005; original Phase 1 "Evidence Collection").
- Evidence: note
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
Service-specific (pending review):

- Biohazard, damage, urgent maintenance, a lock that does not secure, a missing key or fob, or guests still present: stop the affected task and escalate; the host is told only through the approved channel (Q-27-16) (source: spec CL-05.SAF, CL-05.QAC; COM-002).
- Emergency and escalation contacts and the escalation order are owner decisions not yet made (Q-31-05) (source: 31 section 8.5).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].
Service-specific (pending review):

- A needle-stick or contact with blood or bodily fluids is reported on the incident form as an injury or exposure; first response follows the company's approved arrangements, which are not yet defined, and medical decisions belong to medical professionals (source: spec JOB-008; 31 section 8.5).
- Property damage caused during the turnover is reported as an incident; fault and liability are not discussed with the host (source: spec JOB-008; 31 section 8.5).
- Suspected exposure of an access code (seen, recorded, photographed or sent): TBD - requires privacy owner review (source: 31 section 5.8 credentials module).
- **Q-31-12** (owner; privacy owner): which channels may deliver job photos to hosts (links to Q-27-16)? Until answered, the delivery parts of "Evidence Collection" and "Final Photo Wrap" stay held.
- **Q-27-16** (owner; privacy owner; HUMAN REVIEW: attorney for agreement wording): in-app share or portal link only, or also uploads to a host's own portal or messages from a business number?
- **Q-30-17** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: attorney): what are the rules for third-party property, including guest food and items guests leave behind? The "Kitchen Check" discard stays held until then.
- **Q-29-13** (owner): does the host or HandyHub buy and store restock items?

- **Q-31-01** (owner): who are the competent reviewers for this SOP (qualified safety professional for sharps and biohazard; privacy owner for codes and photos; attorney for the guest-property policy), and how is their competence evidenced?
- **Q-31-05** (owner): what are the emergency and escalation contacts and the escalation order for a two-person team?
- **Q-31-10** (owner; qualified mold assessor): what is the company definition of mold growth versus cleanable mildew in bathrooms?
- **Q-31-02** (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish safety text?
- **31 section 10** (owner; qualified safety professional): confirm the PROPOSED rule that workers never enter while guests are present, and decide what "Luxury / Pool Property" includes.
- **02 C-CL05-12 and C-CL05-V01** (owner): which laundry model applies per host, and which kitchen tasks belong to a standard turnover?
- **04 CL-05 card** (owner): how many same-day turnovers can two employees take, and are the pricing file's time caps elapsed time or person-hours (completion-window rule, 31 section 10)?

sops.title: SOP CL-06: Hotel-Style Luxury Housekeeping
sops.sourceFile: Standard Of Operations/sop Hotel-Style Housekeeping Checklist.md

lines: From the spec card intake, pending review:
- Privacy boundaries: off-limits rooms and items, and what may be touched, moved or photographed (source: spec CL-06.INT "privacy boundaries"; CL-06.SAF).
- Laundry, wardrobe and garment-care preferences, and the garments the customer wants pressed (source: spec CL-06.INT "laundry/wardrobe preferences").
- Delicate and high-value items, and which of them workers may care for (source: spec CL-06.INT "delicate items"; CL-06.QAC "high-value items undisturbed except authorized care").
- Access, keys and alarm instructions, entered in the app's secured fields (source: spec CL-06.INT "access"; 27 AUTH-009).
- Preferred products, fragrance preference, and allergies or sensitivities of occupants and pets (source: spec CL-06.INT "preferred products"; 02 C-CL06-02).
- Every visit re-confirms access, occupants, pets, hazards and work-area conditions (source: spec CX-005).

GAP - not yet in the agreement or any reminder (owner decision; wording through 30 and 32): the agreement has no customer-preparation clause (30 section 4.2, CL-06 column, clause 5); who supplies hangers, towels, bed linens, diffusers, flowers and organization supplies is undecided (C-CL06-12); pets and occupants during work are not addressed (X-11).
Dispatch and Start Job conditions, pending review:

- Accepted plan version: the tier, the visit days and the tasks for each visit come from the accepted estimate or plan version, not from this file's tier-free steps (source: spec CL-06.INT "recurring service plan"; spec CX-004, EST-007; C-CL06-V01; APXA-001 "review scope/exclusions").

- Intake recorded and current: privacy boundaries and off-limits rooms; laundry and wardrobe preferences; delicate and high-value items and who may touch them; access; preferred products (source: spec CL-06.INT).
- Evidence: note

- A fragrance preference and an allergy or sensitivity check covering occupants and pets are on record before any scent product is used (source: 02 C-CL06-02; spec CL-06.INT "preferred products"; 04 CL-06 "customer preparation requirements").
- Evidence: note
- Every visit re-confirms access, occupants, pets, hazards and work-area conditions (source: spec CX-005).

- Keys, lockbox and alarm instructions are held only in the app's secured fields; physical keys are custody items with a per-person issue and return log; no code appears in this SOP, in notes, photos or messages (source: 27 AUTH-009 and section 4.6, PROPOSED; spec COM-002).
- Evidence: note

- Every chemical product (scent mists, polishes, leather conditioner, cleaners, diffuser refills) is approved with a reviewed SDS; a product without one is not carried to the job (source: 29 section 8.3 interim rule, PROPOSED).

- Lone work: one housekeeper works alone in a private residence (the Elite tier names a "Dedicated personal housekeeper on property"); no check-in and escalation protocol exists yet: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve. (source: pricing Elite "Inclusions" line; 04 CL-06 "stop-work conditions")
> Governed now by [[OWN-DEC-149]]: no interval check-ins for lone work; the worker records only Arrived and Finished.
- PPE selected and available; tools and products loaded and checked (source: spec START-004, START-005; APXA-001).

- Permit, license and qualification flags: CL-06 touches none of the eight licensed boundaries; consumer subscription terms, insurance for property in HandyHub's care, background checks, mail and package handling and taxability are open questions for the attorney, insurance broker, privacy owner and CPA. This is not a finding that nothing applies; an unknown determination blocks the affected line (source: 04 section 6.3 row CL-06; spec HND-005, START-010).
- Start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented; critical holds cannot be overridden (source: APXA-003; 31 section 8.3).
- Evidence: note
Pending review; methods come from the approved modules, none of which exists yet:
- Confirm the address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants (source: APXA-002).
- Inspect the actual site against the briefing and record differences (source: spec START-007).
- Evidence: note
- Review the customer's privacy boundaries, off-limits rooms, authorized items and preferences for this visit (source: spec CL-06.INT).

- Take existing-condition photos only where the service requires them, framed to leave out people, documents, mail and valuables not needed for the evidence (source: spec START-008; APXA-002; 13 section 5.2 item 5; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- Evidence: photo
- Confirm the fragrance preference and allergy record before any scent product is staged (source: 02 C-CL06-02).
- Evidence: note
- Inspect the steamer, iron, vacuum and cords before use per the manufacturer instructions (source: 31 section 3.1 row 7).
- Have the wet-floor control ready before mopping (source: 02 C-CL06-02; 29 section 5.2 `cleaning-core`).
- Complete the safety, PPE and site checks and acknowledge the SOP and hazards before starting (source: APXA-003; spec START-004).
- Evidence: note

*The original procedure follows verbatim and in its original order; its phase headings are demoted one level. The quoted HOLD and FLAG lines were added on 2026-10-03 and are pending qualified review. A HOLD placed before a step must be cleared before that step starts; a HOLD or FLAG placed after a step suspends, limits or flags it (36 D-36-17). No hold rewords, reorders or removes a step.*

> HOLD (C-CL06-01): before the garment sorting step below - the customer's privacy boundaries, off-limits rooms and the items workers may handle are on record for this visit (section 3). Collect clothing only where the customer allows. Cash, jewelry, keys, mail, documents or other personal records found among clothing are not opened, read, photographed or kept; they are handled only as the customer has authorized in writing, and valuables out of place, missing items and any damage are reported (section 19). Pending qualified review and privacy-owner review. (source: spec CL-06.INT "privacy boundaries", "delicate items"; CL-06.SAF "strict privacy; do not photograph/access personal records without need", "escalation for valuables/damage"; 31 section 10 CL-06)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Valet, Laundry & Closet Organization"

lines: - [ ] **Garment Sorting:** Collect discarded clothing items left around the room; separate dirty laundry from clothes requiring dry cleaning or pressing.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Valet, Laundry & Closet Organization"

lines: > FLAG (C-CL06-04): the step above separates dirty laundry from clothes "requiring dry cleaning or pressing", but no step washes, dries or folds laundry, hand-washes delicates or takes garments to a dry cleaner. Those tasks are sold in pricing and the main plan and are not covered (section 2); under this SOP, garments stay in the residence where the customer keeps them. Off-site custody needs insurance broker and attorney review. (source: 02 C-CL06-04; 31 section 10 CL-06; 31 SOP-029, PROPOSED)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Valet, Laundry & Closet Organization"

lines: > HOLD (C-CL06-01, C-CL06-02): before the ironing and steaming step below - (1) read each garment's care label; a garment without a clear care label, or whose label does not allow the planned ironing or steaming, is not pressed and is set aside and reported (section 17); (2) inspect the steamer or iron and its cord before use and use it only as its manufacturer instructions allow. Burn controls and the electrical load of high-wattage equipment on household circuits are pending safety review; a damaged cord or plug or a tripped circuit stops the step, with no work on electrical components (Do not perform entry 1). Pending qualified review. (source: spec CL-06.SAF "follow garment/surface care labels"; inventory "High-wattage steamer" line; 02 C-CL06-02; 31 section 10 CL-06)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Valet, Laundry & Closet Organization"

lines: - [ ] **Ironing & Steaming:** Iron or steam requested shirts, suits, or delicate dresses to remove all wrinkles.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Valet, Laundry & Closet Organization"

lines: > FLAG: outcome wording - "to remove all wrinkles" in the step above is kept verbatim but is not a promise. What may be done to a garment is limited by its care label; a garment that cannot be pressed further within its label is reported, not forced. Owner review of the wording (Q-31-16). (source: 31 section 3.5 rule 5; spec CL-06.SAF)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Valet, Laundry & Closet Organization"

lines: - [ ] **Uniform Hanging:** Hang clothing items uniformly inside the wardrobe (all hangers facing the same direction, items spaced evenly).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Valet, Laundry & Closet Organization"

lines: - [ ] **Shoe Presentation:** Align shoes neatly on the closet floor or shoe racks, grouped by style and color, facing forward.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Valet, Laundry & Closet Organization"

lines: > FLAG (C-CL06-V01): tier scope undefined - pricing reserves closet organization and garment steaming for the Gold tier and above, while the steps of this phase make no tier distinction and the agreement gives the same scope to every tier. The tasks of each visit come from the accepted plan version (section 3); the per-tier task list is an owner decision (Q-28-21), and agreement wording changes only after attorney review. (source: 02 C-CL06-V01)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Valet, Laundry & Closet Organization"

lines: > HOLD (C-CL06-02): before the hospital corners step below - lift and tuck method pending safety review. The inventory's tuck paddles, "used to slide under heavy mattresses to tuck sheets without lifting", are the PROPOSED control; any lifting limit or two-person rule comes only from the qualified safety professional (TBD). Pending qualified review. (source: spec CL-06.HAZ "ergonomic strain"; inventory "Premium Linen Sheet Straps & Tuck Paddles" line; 02 C-CL06-02)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛌 Phase 2: Luxury Bed Turndown & Linen Care"

lines: - [ ] **Hospital Corners:** Make the bed using hospitality-grade sheets, tucking the bottom edges into tight 45-degree hospital corners.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛌 Phase 2: Luxury Bed Turndown & Linen Care"

lines: - [ ] **Symmetry Check:** Pull the duvet/comforter completely straight and symmetrical on both sides; fluff sleeping and accent pillows to stand vertically.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛌 Phase 2: Luxury Bed Turndown & Linen Care"

lines: - [ ] **Towel Rolling:** Replace used bath linens with fresh, warm-dried towels folded into precise hotel squares or rolled neatly into vanity displays.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛌 Phase 2: Luxury Bed Turndown & Linen Care"

lines: > FLAG (C-CL06-04, C-CL06-12): "warm-dried" in the step above implies drying laundry, which no step covers (section 2). Where the fresh towels and bed linens come from, the customer's stock or HandyHub, is undecided (supply responsibility, C-CL06-12). (source: 02 C-CL06-04; 29 section 5.4 row CL-06)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛌 Phase 2: Luxury Bed Turndown & Linen Care"

lines: > HOLD (C-CL06-01): before the clutter step below - organize only items in areas and of kinds the customer has authorized. Do not open, read, sort or photograph mail, documents or other personal records; stacking magazines does not extend to mail or papers. Cash, jewelry and other valuables are not moved beyond written authorization (Do not perform entries 9 and 10). Pending privacy-owner review. (source: spec CL-06.SAF; CL-06.QAC "high-value items undisturbed except authorized care"; 31 section 10 CL-06)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 3: High-End Dusting & Ambiance Staging"

lines: - [ ] **Clutter Management:** Organize daily clutter: neatly bundle charging cables with ties, stack magazines chronologically, and remove empty cups/dishes.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 3: High-End Dusting & Ambiance Staging"

lines: > HOLD (C-CL06-01, C-CL06-02): before the vanity polish step below - dust and wipe delicate and high-value items (glass trays, perfume bottles, furniture finishes) only where the customer has authorized care, with a product and method suited to the surface per its care instructions; an unknown finish is left untreated and reported, and any damage is reported at once (section 19). Pending qualified review. (source: spec CL-06.SAF "follow garment/surface care labels", "escalation for valuables/damage"; CL-06.HAZ "chemical/surface damage"; CL-06.QAC)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 3: High-End Dusting & Ambiance Staging"

lines: - [ ] **Vanity Polish:** Meticulously dust and wipe delicate glass makeup trays, perfume bottles, nightstands, and dressing tables.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 3: High-End Dusting & Ambiance Staging"

lines: > HOLD (C-CL06-02): before the scent and decor step below - mist linens, use a room scent or refresh a diffuser only when the customer's fragrance preference and an allergy or sensitivity check covering occupants and pets are on record, and only with a product approved with a reviewed SDS (29 section 8.3 interim rule, PROPOSED). If the customer declined scenting or the check is missing, skip the scenting parts of the step and record why. Pending qualified review. (source: 02 C-CL06-02; spec CL-06.INT "preferred products"; 04 CL-06 "customer preparation requirements"; 31 section 10 CL-06)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 3: High-End Dusting & Ambiance Staging"

lines: - [ ] **Scent & Decor:** Refresh room reed diffusers, spray a light fabric mist over linens, and trim/water any fresh-cut flowers in vases.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 3: High-End Dusting & Ambiance Staging"

lines: > FLAG (C-CL06-V01, C-CL06-12): tier scope undefined - pricing reserves "ambient scent refreshing" for the Gold tier and above, while the step above runs on every visit; the per-tier task list is an owner decision (Q-28-21). Who supplies and pays for diffuser refills and fresh flowers is undecided (C-CL06-12). (source: 02 C-CL06-V01, C-CL06-12)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 3: High-End Dusting & Ambiance Staging"

lines: - [ ] **Immediate Trash Clear:** Empty all trash bins even if they contain minor waste; wipe the bin interior and use premium, snug-fitting liners.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧹 Phase 4: Invisible Waste & Floor Care"

lines: > FLAG: sharps - broken glass, dishes or other sharp items in bins are a hazard that the registry lists as an ASSUMPTION pending safety review; the handling method and any container are TBD by the qualified safety professional. Until then, a sharp or biohazard item found while emptying or wiping a bin stops the step above and is reported (section 10). (source: 04 CL-06 "hazards"; 29 section 5.2 `cleaning-core`)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧹 Phase 4: Invisible Waste & Floor Care"

lines: > HOLD (C-CL06-02, X-11): before the floor care step below - (1) use a cleaning product and method suited to the floor finish per its care instructions; a stone or wood floor whose care instructions are unknown is not wet-mopped until the customer confirms them; (2) keep occupants and pets off damp floors and mark the wet area until it is dry (a wet-floor sign is proposed in the inventory). Pending qualified review. (source: spec CL-06.SAF "follow garment/surface care labels"; CL-06.HAZ "chemical/surface damage"; 02 C-CL06-02; 29 section 5.2 `cleaning-core`)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧹 Phase 4: Invisible Waste & Floor Care"

lines: - [ ] **Silent Floor Care:** Use a low-noise vacuum on carpets and rugs; damp-mop hard stone or wood floors using a high-gloss microfiber pad for a streak-free sheen.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧹 Phase 4: Invisible Waste & Floor Care"

lines: > HOLD (C-CL06-01): secure closeout - after the floor care step above and before leaving the residence: return moved items to their agreed places; leave doors, windows, locks and the alarm as the customer instructed, using access details only from the app's secured fields (never written down, photographed or texted); return or log keys as custody items; confirm that high-value items were left undisturbed except for authorized care; record the closeout check. If the residence cannot be secured as instructed, escalate before leaving (section 19), unless your own safety requires you to leave. Pending qualified review and privacy-owner review. (source: spec CL-06.QAC "high-value items undisturbed except authorized care, secure closeout"; 31 section 10 CL-06; 31 section 8.4 rule 3; 27 AUTH-009; spec COM-002)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧹 Phase 4: Invisible Waste & Floor Care"

lines: Observable checks from the service card (source: spec CL-06.QAC; QA-001), with the evidence in brackets. The worker self-checks; which checks need a supervisor is an owner decision (Q-31-15).
- Consistent room standard per the customer's recorded preferences [checklist record; completion evidence per section 16; spec CL-06.QAC "consistent room standard"].
- Evidence: note

- Laundry and wardrobe tasks done per the customer's instructions and each garment's care label, with any item set aside listed [checklist record; spec CL-06.QAC "laundry/wardrobe tasks per instructions"; CL-06.SAF].
- Evidence: note
- High-value items undisturbed except authorized care [checklist confirmation; spec CL-06.QAC].
- Beds made and presented as the original "Symmetry Check" step describes [self-check; original Phase 2].
- Floors dry, or the wet area controlled, and products suited to the finish [self-check; 02 C-CL06-02].
- Secure closeout done and recorded [closeout record; spec CL-06.QAC "secure closeout"].
- Evidence: note
Cleanup for this service means the exit sequence and the crew's own equipment (source: 31 section 6.1); pending review:
- Return items moved during the visit to the places the customer agreed (source: APXA-005; spec CL-06.QAC).
- Unplug the steamer and iron, and handle and store them as their manufacturer instructions require (source: 02 C-CL06-02; 31 section 3.1 row 7).
- Leave the wet-floor control in place until the floor is dry, or tell the occupants (source: 02 C-CL06-02).
- Account for tools, equipment and remaining products; secure chemical containers for transport under the chemical program, which does not exist yet (source: APXA-005; 29 section 8.2 rows 5 and 6).
- Restore anything altered within scope (source: APXA-005).
TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

- Waste streams: household trash emptied from bins and used liners; spent flowers and cut stems; used cloths, including cloths used with the oil-based polish if that product is kept; empty product containers; any sharps or broken glass (source: original Phases 3 and 4; inventory file; 29 section 8.1).

- No CL-06 file says where household trash goes (the residence's own bins or elsewhere), although the pricing Elite line includes "daily trash disposal" (owner decision; source: pricing Elite "Inclusions" line).
- Destination and method for product residues and sharps per municipality: HUMAN REVIEW: local authority and qualified safety professional (Q-29-10). No conclusion is drawn here.
- Hazardous waste is not handled without an approved policy (source: 31 section 3.1 row 15).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: Photos are captured in the app only and are internal-only by default (source: spec REC-002; 27 AUTH-034). Frame the work area: leave out mail, documents, family photos, medication, other private items and people; never photograph children deliberately, and never photograph codes, keypads, alarm panels or account screens; valuables appear only as pre-existing-condition evidence (source: spec CL-06.SAF; 13 sections 5.2 and 5.5; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- Before: existing-condition photos only where the service requires them, for example existing damage to a garment, finish or high-value item before work (source: spec START-008; 13 section 5.5).
- Evidence: photo
- During: none by default; photos of damage, an unexpected condition or an incident when one occurs (source: spec JOB-004, JOB-008).
- Evidence: photo

- After: completion evidence mapped to rooms or tasks (source: spec QA-003). Whether that evidence is a photo framed to leave out personal items or a checklist record without photos is an OPEN QUESTION for the privacy owner (source: 04 CL-06 "completion evidence").
- Evidence: note
- Arrival and completion updates are drafts; the worker or an administrator controls the actual send according to policy (source: spec UXE-008).
- Record the walkthrough outcome when the customer is present: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note

- Report items set aside (no clear care label, care not authorized), damage and valuables concerns through the escalation path and approved wording, without improvising terms (source: spec CL-06.SAF; section 19).
- Evidence: note
- Requests outside the plan's tasks are recorded as requests and go through a change order; the worker does not agree to them (source: spec JOB-005, FIN-008).
- Evidence: note
- Skip, makeup, billing and refund questions go to the owner; those terms are under attorney review (source: APXA-006 "explain invoice/payment next step without making unauthorized promises").
- Blocked work: use only the approved "work blocked" message; never send access codes or incident details by text or email (source: spec NTF-007, COM-002).

- Do not promise results or describe the service with the absolute wording of the original steps and headings ("remove all wrinkles", "streak-free sheen", "Invisible") or the main plan's claims about daily care, resort standards or training; make no health or allergy claims about scent products (Do not perform entry 8; 31 section 3.5 rule 5).
Definition of done (source: spec QA-001 to QA-006; CL-06.QAC; APXA-005, APXA-006):
- Every section 13 check answered, or an exception recorded (QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- Items set aside, damage and valuables escalations recorded (CL-06.SAF; spec JOB-004, JOB-008).
- Evidence: note
- Completion evidence recorded within the privacy limits of section 16 (QA-003).
- Evidence: note
- Cleanup done and moved items returned (QA-002; APXA-005).
- Secure closeout recorded; keys returned or logged (CL-06.QAC; 27 AUTH-009).
- Evidence: note
- Punch items recorded with an owner and a due date (QA-005).
- Evidence: note
- Walkthrough outcome recorded when the customer is present (QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- No hold left open; any incident reported (section 20; APXA-007).
- Evidence: note
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:
Service-specific stop triggers (source: spec CL-06.SAF unless noted; PROPOSED wording pending qualified review):
- A task would need opening, reading or photographing mail, documents or other personal records: do not; escalate (CL-06.SAF "strict privacy; do not photograph/access personal records without need").
- Evidence: measurement, note

- A garment has no clear care label, or its label does not allow the planned pressing; a surface's finish or care instructions are unknown: do not treat that item; set it aside and report it (CL-06.SAF "follow garment/surface care labels").
- Evidence: note
- Valuables found out of place or missing, or damage found or caused: stop handling the item and escalate (CL-06.SAF "escalation for valuables/damage"; spec JOB-008 for damage).
- A fragrance allergy or sensitivity is reported, or the fragrance check is not on record: no scent products (02 C-CL06-02).
- Evidence: note
- No reviewed SDS for a product: do not use it (29 section 8.3).
- An electrical fault, such as a tripped circuit or a damaged cord, plug or outlet: stop using the appliance; do not work on electrical components (Do not perform entry 1; 02 C-CL06-02).
- Occupants or pets cannot be kept off a wet floor: do not mop that area until they can be (02 C-CL06-02).
- A sharp or biohazard item in a bin, linens or clutter: stop and report (04 CL-06 "hazards", ASSUMPTION).
- Evidence: note
- The residence cannot be secured as the customer instructed at closeout: escalate before leaving, unless your own safety requires you to leave (CL-06.QAC "secure closeout"; 31 section 8.4 rule 3).

Service holds (inserted in section 12). Critical holds cannot be overridden (31 section 8.3); the secure-closeout hold is treated as critical (31 section 8.4 rule 3, PROPOSED), and a hold that exists because a required module or policy is missing (chemicals and SDS; credentials and access codes; guest property and lock-up) behaves as a critical hold until that module is approved (31 section 8.4 rule 4, PROPOSED):
| Hold | Where in section 12 | Release role and evidence |

| C-CL06-01: privacy boundaries, authorized items, personal records and valuables | Before "Garment Sorting" and before "Clutter Management" | Privacy owner (rules approved); the customer's authorization recorded at intake |

| C-CL06-01, C-CL06-02: garment care labels; steamer and iron burns and electrical load | Before "Ironing & Steaming" | Owner (care-label rule); qualified safety professional (equipment, burn and electrical controls) |
| C-CL06-02: lift and tuck method | Before "Hospital Corners" | Qualified safety professional |
| C-CL06-01, C-CL06-02: delicate and high-value items; surface care | Before "Vanity Polish" | Owner; the customer's authorization recorded |
| C-CL06-02: fragrance preference and allergy check; product SDS | Before "Scent & Decor" | Qualified safety professional (SDS); the customer's preference record |
| C-CL06-02, X-11: floor finish; wet floors with occupants and pets | Before "Silent Floor Care" | Qualified safety professional; the customer's care instructions for the floor |
| C-CL06-01: secure closeout | After "Silent Floor Care", before leaving | Owner and privacy owner (closeout rule approved); a closeout record for each visit |
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
Service roles (contacts are owner decisions, Q-31-05):
- Personal records, mail, photos, keys and access codes: privacy owner.
- Valuables, and damage to garments, finishes or high-value items: owner; insurance broker for claims questions.
- Garment care or surface finish questions: owner, from the care labels and the manufacturer's care instructions.
- Chemical or fragrance reactions: emergency services first where needed, then the qualified safety professional.
- Electrical faults: stop using the appliance; a licensed electrician through the owner.
- Lone-work concerns: owner (check-in protocol TBD).
- Requests beyond the plan's tasks (washing, errands, fridge, mail and packages): owner, by change order once a reviewed step exists.
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].
**HUMAN REVIEW:** attorney licensed in KY and/or IN for the fault and liability sentence; insurance broker for any insurer-notification step added later.

Examples for this service, all reported under JOB-008 (source: spec CL-06.HAZ; 02 C-CL06-02): a steam or iron burn; a slip on a damp floor; a skin, eye or breathing reaction to a product or fragrance; damage to a garment, finish or high-value item; a missing item or valuables concern; a lost key or an access code exposed outside the app (privacy owner); equipment failure. First-response provisions depend on the vehicle safety kit, which is not yet defined (X-10).

- Q-31-05 (owner): what are the emergency and escalation contacts, the escalation order and the after-hours coverage (section 19 placeholders)? The lone-work check-in protocol in section 3 depends on the answer.
- Q-13-06 (owner): is the owner the privacy owner at launch, and who backs the owner up? The privacy owner approves the records, photo, key and closeout rules in this SOP.
- Q-30-17 (owner; attorney): which rules apply to mail and packages before "organizing mail/packages" can be offered?
- Q-28-21 (owner): which steps does each tier include, and are fridge maintenance, mail and package organizing and bed adjustments offered (C-CL06-V01, C-CL06-07)?
- Q-31-15 (owner): which quality or closeout checks need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check?
- Q-31-16 (owner; attorney): who approves replacement wording for "to remove all wrinkles", "streak-free sheen" and "Invisible" in a revised SOP version?
- Q-31-11 (owner; qualified safety professional): what goes in the emergency kit, who owns the SDS register, and how are the polishes, mists and cleaners stored and transported?
- Q-31-09 (owner; qualified safety professional): which height and access policy applies if art frames, crystals or other items above reach are dusted?
- Q-31-02 (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish version?

- Open questions recorded with C-CL06-04 in 02 (owner; insurance broker; attorney): are washing, hand-washing and dry-cleaning errands offered, and if so with which reviewed steps (care-label check, custody log)?
- Open question in 04 CL-06 "completion evidence" (privacy owner): which completion evidence is compatible with "do not photograph/access personal records without need"?

sops.title: SOP CL-07: Air Duct & Ventilation Cleaning
sops.sourceFile: Standard Of Operations/sop Air Duct and Vent Cleaning Checklist.md

lines: - No CL-07 file defines customer preparation (source: 04 CL-07 "customer preparation requirements", GAP).

- PROPOSED for the preparation checklist, wording for owner and attorney approval: clear access to all registers, returns and the air handler; filter size; occupants or pets with respiratory sensitivity; acceptance of a power interruption; items near vents moved or covered (source: 04 CL-07 "customer preparation requirements"; spec CL-07.INT).
- PROPOSED: occupants, children and pets stay out of rooms with open registers and away from equipment and hoses while work runs (source: X-11; spec CX-005; 31 section 5.8 occupants module, pending).
- Every job re-confirms access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions (source: spec CX-005).
- HandyHub's own pre-start checks are never moved onto the customer (source: 30 section 4.1 clause 5).

> HOLD (precondition; C-CL07-V03; spec CL-07.INT, CL-07.SAF): before "System Shutdown" below, confirm the intake facts ("HVAC system type, accessible registers/returns, reported concern, filter size, suspected mold/pest/contamination, equipment capability") against the site, and photograph the air-handler area where it is accessible, each accessible register and return, and any visible ductwork; do not enter an attic or crawlspace for this screen (section 2, Out of scope). If you see suspected significant mold, suspect asbestos-containing material (for example older duct wrap, tape or mastic), damaged ducts, or work that needs a licensed HVAC professional, do not start: record it and escalate (section 10). This screen is a safety hold, not the "Base Inspection" named in the pricing file, and it certifies nothing. Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛠️ Phase 1: System Isolation & Property Protection"

items.ref: precondition; C-CL07-06; X-07; spec CL-07.SAF "system off/isolation per procedure"
lines: > HOLD (precondition; C-CL07-06; X-07; spec CL-07.SAF "system off/isolation per procedure"): before "System Shutdown" below, note that the isolation method is under review by a licensed HVAC contractor or electrician: which breaker the step means (the home's main breaker or the HVAC equipment's own circuit), lockout against re-energizing, verification and restore are not yet defined. The isolation requirement stays in force; do not skip it and do not improvise another method. Do not switch off any circuit breaker until the customer has been told that power will be interrupted and has accepted it; if the customer does not accept, or anything in the home depends on uninterrupted power, do not start and escalate (section 19). Confirm before isolation how the vacuum, drill and compressor are powered, so nothing is re-energized mid-job. Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛠️ Phase 1: System Isolation & Property Protection"

lines: - [ ] **System Shutdown:** Turn off the HVAC system at the thermostat and switch off the main circuit breaker to ensure operator safety.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛠️ Phase 1: System Isolation & Property Protection"

lines: - [ ] **Containment:** Lay plastic drop cloths over all furniture, flooring, and beds directly beneath or near air vents to catch dislodged soot.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛠️ Phase 1: System Isolation & Property Protection"

lines: > FLAG (C-CL07-V01; X-11): the step above relies on drop cloths to "catch dislodged soot" that falls into rooms, and "Grille Removal" below opens every register, while the inventory stocks foam block-off plugs and magnetic vent seals for sealing registers under negative pressure, which no step uses. The containment method for "Agitation Run" and "Vacuum Extraction" is unresolved pending qualified safety review (equipment manufacturer instructions; licensed HVAC contractor for any access openings); no method is written here. Keep occupants, children and pets out of rooms with open registers while the work runs (spec CX-005; X-11). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🛠️ Phase 1: System Isolation & Property Protection"

lines: *Dispatch and Start Job gates for this service (source: spec APXA-001, APXA-003; 31 section 3.1 row 3). Every item is pending review.*
- Intake complete: "HVAC system type, accessible registers/returns, reported concern, filter size, suspected mold/pest/contamination, equipment capability" (source: spec CL-07.INT).
- Evidence: note

- Suspected mold or another hazardous condition at intake blocks a firm quote and routes the job to a site assessment first (source: estimate-assistant playbook "Missing hazardous-condition decisions block a firm quote."; 04 CL-07 "estimating method").

- An approved estimate version covers the tasks in section 2; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented. Work listed under "Out of scope" is not performed even if it was quoted (source: spec CX-003; APXA-003; 28 PRC-042, PROPOSED).
- Evidence: note
- CL-07 is not bookable until an approved agreement or scope schedule is active; the agreement file is a structure-only skeleton (source: 30 AGR-031, PROPOSED; 02 G-001).

- Licensed-task and specialist holds: where policy flags plenum access, a furnace connection, suspected mold, suspected asbestos or biocide use, Start Job stays blocked until the prerequisite is approved (source: spec START-010; 04 CL-07 "prerequisites", PROPOSED; C-CL07-07).

- Equipment capability documented: whether the negative-pressure HEPA vacuum, compressor and drill are owned or rented, and how they are powered while the HVAC system is isolated (source: spec CL-07.INT "equipment capability"; owner facts 2026-10-02 "Reported capability is not documentary proof of ... equipment"; C-CL07-06).
- Evidence: note

- The customer has been told that power will be interrupted and has accepted it; wording pending owner and attorney review (source: 04 CL-07 "prerequisites" and "customer preparation requirements"; C-CL07-06).

- Height and access: grilles and fans that need access equipment stay blocked until an approved height and access policy exists (source: spec CL-07.HAZ "ladder"; 02 G-005; X-12; 31 section 8.4 rule 4; job-planner playbook "A missing ladder or unverified permit keeps affected tasks blocked.").
- Every chemical product carried has a reviewed SDS; none is approved yet, so none is carried (source: 29 section 8.3 interim rule, PROPOSED; X-09).

- Before this SOP can be activated, the named reviewers approve: the isolation method (C-CL07-06); the "Agitation Run" step and the company mold definition (C-CL07-01; Q-31-10); the containment method (C-CL07-V01); the duct-type and tool check before agitation; the licensed-scope boundary (C-CL07-07); the filter specification (HVAC review) (source: 31 section 10 CL-07; owner facts L20).

- On arrival: confirm address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants; inspect the actual site against the briefing; capture required existing-condition photos; protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- Pre-work screen with photos before any step, and a second screen at each opened register before boot vacuuming (holds in section 12; source: C-CL07-V03; spec CL-07.SAF).
- Protection and containment: drop cloths per "Containment"; the containment method is unresolved (source: SOP "Containment"; C-CL07-V01).

- Isolate-verify-restore: "System Shutdown" isolates the system, but the isolation point, verification and restoration are not defined, and the shared isolate-verify-restore module does not exist yet (source: X-07; C-CL07-06; 31 section 5.8).
- Staging of the vacuum unit, hoses, compressor and access equipment: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003; START-004).
- Evidence: note

*The original procedure lines below are unchanged and in their original order. Lines starting with "HOLD" or "FLAG" were added on 2026-10-03; they are pending review and never replace the step text. A hold placed before a step must be satisfied before that step starts; a hold placed after a step limits or suspends the step above it.*

> HOLD (precondition; X-12; spec CL-07.HAZ "ladder"; 02 G-005): before "Grille Removal" below, grilles on ceilings, and any grille you cannot reach while standing on the floor, need access equipment under an approved height and access policy; none exists and no ladder is stocked. Until it exists, leave those grilles in place and record them as not done (section 13). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌀 Phase 2: Dismantling & Ultrasonic/Manual Washing"

lines: - [ ] **Grille Removal:** Unscrew and carefully remove all supply (output) and return (intake) vent grilles from walls and ceilings.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌀 Phase 2: Dismantling & Ultrasonic/Manual Washing"

lines: - [ ] **Deep Scrubbing:** Submerge metal grilles in warm, soapy water; scrub away grease, dust build-up, and nicotine film, then dry them completely.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌀 Phase 2: Dismantling & Ultrasonic/Manual Washing"

lines: > HOLD (precondition; spec CL-07.SAF; X-06): before "Boot Vacuuming" below, look into each opened register boot and photograph it. If you see suspected mold growth, suspect asbestos-containing material, a damaged duct or damaged duct lining, do not vacuum or disturb that opening: record it and escalate (section 10). Until the company mold definition exists, suspected mold growth is treated as a critical hold (31 section 8.4 rule 2; Q-31-10). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌀 Phase 2: Dismantling & Ultrasonic/Manual Washing"

lines: - [ ] **Boot Vacuuming:** Use a vacuum brush attachment to clean out the immediate metal "boot" connection inside the wall before deep duct entry.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌀 Phase 2: Dismantling & Ultrasonic/Manual Washing"

lines: > FLAG (C-CL07-V01): the containment method for "Agitation Run" and "Vacuum Extraction" below is unresolved - pending safety review (see the flag under "Containment"). No containment or negative-pressure method is written here.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 3: Deep Agitation & Negative Pressure Extraction"

items.ref: precondition; spec CL-07.HAZ "damage to duct lining"; 31 section 10 CL-07
lines: > HOLD (precondition; spec CL-07.HAZ "damage to duct lining"; 31 section 10 CL-07): before "Agitation Run" below, record the duct type and the condition of any duct lining at each opened register, and confirm from the brush and air-whip manufacturers' instructions that the tool suits that duct type. If the duct type is unknown, the lining is damaged or the tool is not approved for it, do not insert the tool: record the limitation (section 13) and escalate. Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 3: Deep Agitation & Negative Pressure Extraction"

lines: - [ ] **Agitation Run:** Insert flexible rotary cleaning brushes or pneumatic air whips deep into each individual duct line to break up caked-on dust and mold spores.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 3: Deep Agitation & Negative Pressure Extraction"

lines: > HOLD (C-CL07-01, critical; X-06): the step above is held pending review by a qualified safety professional and a mold assessor. It treats breaking up "mold spores" as routine work, while spec CL-07.SAF says "stop on suspected significant mold, asbestos-containing material, damaged ducts or scope requiring licensed HVAC work". Until the reviewers release the step and the company mold definition exists (Q-31-10), the step is not performed; wherever mold growth is suspected, do not agitate, vacuum or treat it - stop and escalate (section 10). Mold remediation is not performed under this SOP (section 2, Do not perform 10). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 3: Deep Agitation & Negative Pressure Extraction"

items.ref: precondition; C-CL07-07; spec CL-07.SAF "scope requiring licensed HVAC work"
lines: > HOLD (precondition; C-CL07-07; spec CL-07.SAF "scope requiring licensed HVAC work"): before "Vacuum Extraction" below, note that the step does not say how the vacuum is attached to the trunk line, and no attachment method is approved. Do not cut, patch or seal an opening in the plenum or a trunk line, and do not connect any equipment to the furnace: whether that is licensed HVAC or permit work in the job's municipality is open, and only a licensed HVAC professional does it if the licensing review allows it (Do not perform 11; HUMAN REVIEW: licensing authority for the municipality, licensed HVAC contractor). If extraction needs either, stop and escalate. Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 3: Deep Agitation & Negative Pressure Extraction"

lines: - [ ] **Vacuum Extraction:** Run a heavy-duty negative pressure truck-mounted or portable HEPA vacuum system attached to the trunk line to suck out all loose debris.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 3: Deep Agitation & Negative Pressure Extraction"

lines: > HOLD (C-CL07-03, critical): no fogging, misting or spraying of any sanitizer, disinfectant or biocide follows the step above. The pricing file sells antimicrobial fogging "after vacuuming", but fogging is not covered by this SOP and is not performable until a specific product with label directions for duct use and its SDS are approved, with occupant, pet and re-entry controls set by the reviewer (31 section 10 CL-07; 29 section 8.2 item 9; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional; state pesticide regulator). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 3: Deep Agitation & Negative Pressure Extraction"

items.ref: precondition; spec CL-07.HAZ "electrical/mechanical equipment"; X-07; X-12
lines: > HOLD (precondition; spec CL-07.HAZ "electrical/mechanical equipment"; X-07; X-12): before "Exhaust Systems" below, confirm that the range-hood fan and the bathroom extractor fan are off and isolated so they cannot start while hands or tools are in them; whether "System Shutdown" covers them depends on the isolation method under review (C-CL07-06). If isolation cannot be confirmed, do not put hands or tools into the fan; escalate. A ceiling-mounted fan you cannot reach while standing on the floor needs access equipment under the height and access policy, which does not exist yet: leave it and record it as not done (section 13). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 3: Deep Agitation & Negative Pressure Extraction"

lines: - [ ] **Exhaust Systems:** Meticulously scrape caked grease from kitchen range hood exhaust fan blades; vacuum dust out of bathroom extractor fans.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 3: Deep Agitation & Negative Pressure Extraction"

lines: > FLAG (C-CL07-05; X-23; C-CL07-04): the step above covers residential kitchen range-hood fan blades and bathroom extractor fans only. Commercial kitchen exhaust (hoods, fan paths and ducts) is not covered (C-CL07-05; X-23), and dryer-vent lines are not covered (C-CL07-04). Under the PROPOSED boundary, range-hood filters belong to CL-02 and hood fans and ducts to CL-07 (04 section 5; Q-04-15). The step names no chemical; any degreaser must be an approved product with a reviewed SDS (29 section 8.3). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 3: Deep Agitation & Negative Pressure Extraction"

items.ref: precondition; spec CL-07.QAC "filter installed if included"; spec CL-07.INT "filter size"
lines: > HOLD (precondition; spec CL-07.QAC "filter installed if included"; spec CL-07.INT "filter size"): before "Filter Removal" below, confirm that filter replacement is included in the approved estimate and that the replacement filter is on site and matches the size recorded at intake. If not, leave the existing filter in place, record it as a limitation (section 13) and tell the customer (section 17). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔄 Phase 4: Filtration Swap & Air Verification"

lines: - [ ] **Filter Removal:** Pull out the old, clogged HVAC air filter and seal it immediately in a plastic bag to prevent dust release.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔄 Phase 4: Filtration Swap & Air Verification"

lines: - [ ] **New Filter Install:** Verify the correct dimensions and directional airflow arrow, then slide in a brand-new, high-MERV-rated air filter.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔄 Phase 4: Filtration Swap & Air Verification"

items.ref: 31 section 10 CL-07; HUMAN REVIEW: licensed HVAC contractor
lines: > FLAG (31 section 10 CL-07; HUMAN REVIEW: licensed HVAC contractor): "high-MERV-rated air filter" in the step above is not a selection rule. The filter's rating must suit this system as the HVAC equipment manufacturer specifies (system compatibility, HVAC review); no rating is set here. A customer-supplied filter needs a START-009 record (section 8). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔄 Phase 4: Filtration Swap & Air Verification"

items.ref: precondition; C-CL07-08; spec CL-07.QAC "system restored"; spec APXA-005
lines: > HOLD (precondition; C-CL07-08; spec CL-07.QAC "system restored"; spec APXA-005): before "System Test" below, reinstall and secure every grille removed in "Grille Removal" in its original location, and count the grilles against the number removed; a loose ceiling grille is a falling-object risk. A grille or fastener that cannot be secured is recorded and escalated, and the test does not run until it is resolved. Confirm that no tool, hose, rod or whip remains in the ductwork, the air handler or a fan, and that everyone is clear of them, before power is restored; power is restored only by the isolation method under review (C-CL07-06; X-07). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔄 Phase 4: Filtration Swap & Air Verification"

lines: - [ ] **System Test:** Restore power, run the system on "Fan Only" mode for 5 minutes, and verify that zero residual dust particles blow out into the clean property.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔄 Phase 4: Filtration Swap & Air Verification"

lines: > FLAG (31 section 10 CL-07; C-CL07-02): "verify that zero residual dust particles blow out into the clean property" in the step above is not measurable. It is not a pass criterion and is never said to the customer; record what was observed and document limitations instead (spec CL-07.QAC; section 13). FLAG: UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions: the "5 minutes" run time and the "Fan Only" test come from no HVAC equipment manufacturer instruction (31 section 3.5 rule 3; HUMAN REVIEW: licensed HVAC contractor). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔄 Phase 4: Filtration Swap & Air Verification"
