lines: *From spec CL-07.QAC. The worker cannot mark the job complete without answering the required checks or recording an exception (source: spec QA-001). Which checks need a second person rather than a self-check is open (Q-31-15).*
| Check | Source | Inspector | Evidence |

| Registers and accessible duct scope completed as approved: each register recorded as done, held or not done, with the reason | spec CL-07.QAC "registers/accessible duct scope completed" | Worker; supervisor where policy requires (Q-31-15) | After photos mapped to registers and areas (QA-003) |
| Every removed grille reinstalled, secured and counted against the number removed | C-CL07-08; spec CL-07.QAC "system restored" | Worker | Count recorded; after photos |
| Debris controlled | spec CL-07.QAC "debris controlled" | Worker | Cleanup photos (QA-002); method per the containment decision (C-CL07-V01) |

| Filter installed if included, in the size recorded at intake, with the airflow direction the step names | spec CL-07.QAC "filter installed if included"; SOP "New Filter Install" | Worker | Photo of the installed filter, or "not included" / "not replaced" recorded |

| System restored: power restored by the reviewed isolation method and the thermostat returned to the customer's setting | spec CL-07.QAC "system restored"; APXA-005 | Worker; supervisor where policy requires | Checklist answer; until the isolation method exists, "method pending review" is recorded (C-CL07-06) |

| Limitations and unresolved conditions documented: held steps, grilles or fans not reached, suspected conditions found, filter not replaced | spec CL-07.QAC "limitations and unresolved conditions documented" | Worker | Notes and photos (JOB-004) |
| "Fan Only" run: what was observed, not a measurement | SOP "System Test" (flagged); 31 section 10 CL-07 | Worker | Observation note; no air-quality value is recorded or claimed |
- A customer signature or acknowledgement does not clear an unresolved safety hold (source: quality-assistant playbook "A signed customer form does not clear an unresolved safety hold.").
- Evidence: note
- Missing evidence is recorded as unknown, not as a pass (source: quality-assistant playbook).
- Evidence: note
- Clean the area, remove waste, drop cloths and any containment, and account for tools and materials, including rods, whips, hoses and any plugs or seals used (source: spec APXA-005; QA-002).
- Restore utilities and components altered within scope (source: spec APXA-005), with power restored only by the isolation method under review (C-CL07-06).
- Return unused materials (source: spec APXA-007).

- Waste streams: debris collected by the HEPA vacuum; used filters, bagged as "Filter Removal" states; grease scraped from range-hood fan blades; used drop cloths; grille wash water (source: section 12; 29 section 8.2 item 10 "used filters").

- No disposal method or destination is approved: contain each stream and dispose of it only by the method the reviewer approves for the municipality (source: 31 section 3.1 row 15; Q-29-10; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional; local authority).
- If suspected mold or suspect asbestos-containing material was found, its debris is not handled under this SOP until a qualified reviewer decides (source: spec CL-07.SAF; section 10).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: existing-condition photos of the work areas, registers, grilles, any visible ductwork and the accessible air-handler area, including the pre-work screens in section 12 (source: spec APXA-002 "capture required existing-condition photos"; START-008; C-CL07-V03).
- Evidence: photo
- During: concealed or unexpected conditions - suspected mold, suspect material, damaged ducts or lining - with photos and severity (source: spec JOB-004; UXE-006).

- After: photos mapped to registers and areas, the reinstalled grilles and the installed filter (source: spec QA-003; 04 CL-07 "completion evidence"). An inspection camera is used only if the owner approves it (source: 04 CL-07 "completion evidence", PROPOSED).
- Evidence: photo

- Every photo is internal-only by default; marketing use needs separate consent (source: spec REC-002, REC-003). Avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- Arrival and completion updates are drafts; the worker or admin controls the send (source: spec UXE-008).

- Before "System Shutdown", the customer is told that power will be interrupted, in approved wording (source: C-CL07-06; 04 CL-07 "customer preparation requirements"; wording TBD - owner and attorney).
- Record the walkthrough outcome: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Care notes only from approved product or manufacturer data; none are approved yet (source: spec QA-008).

- Limitations, told in approved wording: held steps, grilles or fans not reached, suspected conditions found and referred, filter not replaced (source: spec CL-07.QAC; section 12 holds). Wording TBD - owner and qualified safety reviewer.
- Blocked work: only the approved "work blocked" message; no incident details or access codes by text or email (source: spec NTF-007, COM-002).

- What not to say: "Clean Air, Lower Energy Bills", "breathe pure, clean air", "Removing allergens, mold spores, and pet dander", "kill lingering mold spores", "eco-friendly", "zero residual dust particles", or any air-quality, health, energy-saving or mold-removal outcome (source: spec CL-07.SAF; C-CL07-01; C-CL07-02; C-CL07-03; 32 register A row 26 and register B rows 8, 9 and 60).
- Required QA checks answered or an exception recorded (source: spec QA-001; section 13).
- Evidence: note
- After photos mapped to registers and areas (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Every removed grille reinstalled, secured and counted (source: C-CL07-08; spec CL-07.QAC).
- Filter status recorded: installed as included, not included, or not replaced with the reason (source: spec CL-07.QAC "filter installed if included").
- Evidence: note
- System restored, or the restore status recorded under the C-CL07-06 hold (source: spec CL-07.QAC "system restored"; APXA-005).
- Evidence: note
- Cleanup and waste handling done as approved; tools and materials accounted for (source: spec QA-002; APXA-005; sections 14 and 15).
- Limitations, open holds and punch items recorded; walkthrough outcome recorded (source: spec CL-07.QAC; QA-004; APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- The job closes only when the required operational and financial steps are complete (source: spec APXA-007).
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:

*Standard block copied verbatim from 31 SOP standard section 8.5 (PROPOSED wording; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional; attorney licensed in KY and/or IN for the "right to stop work" sentence; bilingual reviewer for Spanish).*

**Service stop triggers and holds (CL-07).** Card stop guidance (spec CL-07.SAF): "system off/isolation per procedure; do not make unsupported indoor-air-quality claims; stop on suspected significant mold, asbestos-containing material, damaged ducts or scope requiring licensed HVAC work".
| Trigger or hold | Action | Cleared by (evidence) | Source |

| Suspected significant mold; until the company mold definition exists, any suspected mold growth in ducts, boots, registers or the air handler | Do not agitate, vacuum or disturb it; stop the affected work; photos; escalate | Qualified mold assessor and qualified safety professional (critical hold) | spec CL-07.SAF; C-CL07-01; 31 section 8.4 rule 2 |

| Suspect asbestos-containing material, for example duct wrap, tape or mastic | Do not disturb; stop; escalate | Accredited asbestos inspector (critical hold) | spec CL-07.SAF; 31 section 8.3 rule 2 |

| Damaged ducts or duct lining; duct type unknown or not approved for the brush or air whip | Do not insert tools; record; escalate | Qualified safety reviewer; licensed HVAC contractor for duct damage | spec CL-07.SAF, CL-07.HAZ; 31 section 10 CL-07 |

| Scope requiring licensed HVAC work: plenum or trunk-line openings, furnace connection, work on HVAC equipment beyond section 12 | Do not perform; record the request; refer | Licensing review; licensed HVAC contractor (critical class) | spec CL-07.SAF; C-CL07-07; 31 section 8.3 rule 2 |

| Isolation not confirmed, or power cannot be interrupted safely (the customer has not accepted, or something depends on uninterrupted power) | Do not start, or stop the affected step; escalate | Licensed HVAC contractor or electrician (method); owner | spec CL-07.SAF "system off/isolation per procedure"; C-CL07-06; X-07 |
| Containment cannot be set up as the reviewer requires | Do not agitate or extract | Qualified safety professional | C-CL07-V01; spec CL-07.QAC "debris controlled" |
| Grilles or fans that need access equipment | Leave them in place; record as not done | Approved height and access policy | spec CL-07.HAZ "ladder"; X-12; 02 G-005 |

| A request for fogging, dryer-vent cleaning or commercial kitchen exhaust work | Do not perform; record; refer to the owner | Owner, after SOP, licensing and SDS review | C-CL07-03; C-CL07-04; C-CL07-05; 28 PRC-042 |
| A chemical product without a reviewed SDS | Do not use | Reviewed SDS and approved product | 29 section 8.3 |
| Gas odor | Emergency (section 19, step 2) | Emergency services; incident report (section 20) | 31 section 8.5; 04 CL-07 "hazards" |

Critical holds cannot be overridden by any role; they clear only with a recorded qualified assessment. Suspect hazardous material and unapproved HVAC scope are critical classes, and suspected mold growth is treated as critical until the company mold definition exists (source: 31 section 8.3 rule 2 and section 8.4 rule 2).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
*Standard block copied verbatim from 31 section 8.5 (PROPOSED wording; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional).*

**CL-07 escalation routes (owner decisions pending, Q-31-05):** suspected significant mold goes to the owner, then a qualified mold assessor; suspect asbestos-containing material to an accredited asbestos inspector; licensed HVAC scope, damaged ducts or HVAC equipment concerns to a licensed HVAC contractor; isolation or electrical concerns to a licensed electrician or HVAC contractor; a gas odor is an emergency (step 2) (source: 04 CL-07 "permit/license flags" HUMAN REVIEW list; C-CL07-01; C-CL07-06; C-CL07-07). Contacts: `<owner decision: emergency contact>` and `<owner decision: escalation order>` (Q-31-05).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].

*Standard block copied verbatim from 31 section 8.5 (PROPOSED wording). HUMAN REVIEW: attorney licensed in KY and/or IN for the fault and liability sentence; insurance broker for any insurer-notification step added later.*

- CL-07 examples to report: cuts from duct or grille edges; eye or face injury from compressed-air whips or debris; a fall from access equipment; exposure to dust or a suspected hazardous material; damage to ducts, duct lining, grilles, HVAC equipment or customer property; harm caused by the power interruption (source: spec CL-07.HAZ; C-CL07-06; JOB-008).
- Q-31-08 (owner and relevant reviewers): is biocide fogging offered at all, or referred out?

- Q-30-14 (owner; licensed HVAC contractor; attorney): is CL-07 offered at launch? What is in scope versus licensed HVAC work, what is charged if work stops at the inspection, and are filters, dryer vents, fogging and commercial hoods offered?
- Q-31-10 (owner; qualified mold assessor): what is the company definition of mold growth versus cleanable mildew, and the stop rule? It decides when the "Agitation Run" hold can be released.
- Q-31-09 (owner; qualified safety professional): the height and access policy that releases ceiling grilles and ceiling-mounted fans.
- Q-31-07 (owner; accredited asbestos inspector; EPA RRP-certified renovator): which property-age thresholds trigger asbestos screening for duct wrap, tape or mastic?
- Q-04-15 (owner; licensed HVAC contractor): is the hood and grille split between CL-02 and CL-07 confirmed, and are commercial hoods excluded?
- Q-31-05 (owner): emergency and escalation contacts, escalation order and after-hours coverage for a two-person team.
- Q-31-15 (owner): which checks (grille count, system restore, isolation) need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check?
- Q-31-02 (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish safety text?
- Q-29-10 (local authority; safety reviewer): disposal destinations and rules for extracted debris and used filters in each service municipality.

sops.title: SOP DW-01: Professional Patching, Repair & Handyman Services

lines: PROPOSED for owner approval; customer-facing wording goes through 30 and 32.

- The customer clears furniture, fragile decorations and hanging art away from the target wall or ceiling zone before the technician arrives, as the agreement's "Work Workspace" clause asks; the clause's distance is unapproved draft text (source: agreement "Work Workspace" clause). This preparation does not replace HandyHub's own pre-start checks (source: 30 section 4.1 row 5).
- Occupants, children and pets are kept away from the work area and its dust (source: spec CX-005, BRF-005; X-11).

- The customer states the cause of the damage, whether any leak is active or repaired, who supplies paint, and anything known about the home's age or earlier testing (source: spec DW-01.INT; spec BRF-003).
- Client-supplied paint is on site when the approved estimate relies on it (source: pricing file paint lines; spec START-009).

- Preparation instructions go out with the appointment confirmation and reminder (source: spec NTF-004, NTF-005); every job re-confirms access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions (source: spec CX-005).
- This SOP is not active: no job uses it until competent review and owner activation (source: owner facts 2026-10-02; 31 section 2.1).

- An approved estimate version exists, with scope, exclusions and paint, primer and texture responsibility stated; the worker acknowledges the current approved scope and exclusions (source: spec CX-003, START-003; spec DW-01.INT "paint responsibility").

- Intake complete: the spec DW-01.INT facts listed in section 2. A missing cause of damage or active-leak status blocks a ready-to-start packet (source: spec DW-01.INT; job-planner playbook "Stop planning a ready-to-start packet if required scope or hazard decisions are missing").
- Leak or water source confirmed resolved before any work on water damage; HOLD at the start of section 12 (source: spec DW-01.SAF "confirm leak/source resolved").

- Property age recorded as an approximate build year or "unknown". Build year unknown or pre-1978: HOLD for RRP review before cutting, scoring or sanding painted surfaces (HOLDs in section 12). This is a conservative screening hold pending the qualified reviewers, not a legal conclusion (source: 31 section 10; spec BRF-003 "approximate age if known"; X-13; Q-31-07).
- Evidence: note
- Suspected mold, suspect hazardous material or extensive concealed damage reported before the visit: do not start; escalate (source: spec DW-01.SAF; 31 section 8.4 rule 2).
- Evidence: note

- Ceiling or other overhead work only under an approved height and access policy; none exists, so those tasks stay blocked (source: spec DW-01.HAZ "ladder for ceilings"; 02 G-005; X-12; 31 section 8.4 rule 4; Q-31-09).

- Critical tools and materials marked loaded, or an exception recorded; a missing critical item blocks the affected tasks. The stud and utility scanner, framing square, backing, LED light and ready-mix compound that the steps use are not in the inventory file today (source: spec START-005, START-006, APXA-001; C-DW01-11; job-planner playbook "A missing ladder or unverified permit keeps affected tasks blocked").
- Evidence: note
- Client-supplied paint, if the approved estimate relies on it: on site, with its condition, product and quantity recorded before use (source: spec START-009; 29 section 9.1, PROPOSED).
- Evidence: note
- Chemical products (setting and ready-mix compounds, primer-sealer) are carried only with a reviewed SDS (source: 29 section 8.3, PROPOSED interim rule; spec BRF-008).

- Permit, licence or qualification flags: applicability for DW-01, including EPA RRP and local registration, is unknown and is not treated as "no permit" (source: spec START-010; risk-triage playbook "unknown applicability must not default to no permit"; 04 permit/license flags row).

- Before leaving: confirm the correct job, customer, address and time; read the latest changes; review scope and exclusions; review hazards and safety; load critical tools, equipment and materials; check customer-supplied items; confirm required documents and approvals (source: spec APXA-001).

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; confirm materials, models and colors; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003, START-004). Critical holds are never cleared by override (source: 31 section 8.3).
- Evidence: note

- On arrival: confirm the address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants; inspect the actual site against the briefing and record differences; material differences trigger Risk Triage or supervisor review (source: spec APXA-002, START-007).
- Evidence: note
- Capture the existing-condition photos of the damaged area and its surroundings, including any water staining (source: spec APXA-002, START-008; section 16).
- Evidence: photo

- Protect the work area: "Drop Cloths" in section 12 is the original protection step; dust isolation beyond it is set by the qualified safety reviewer (source: spec APXA-002 "protect work area"; spec DW-01.SAF "isolate dust").
- Keep children and pets out of the work area (source: X-11; spec CX-005).
- Identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003, START-004).
- Evidence: note
- The original setup phase, "Phase 1: Site Protection & Damage Evaluation", stays in section 12, verbatim and in order (source: 31 section 9.2 step 6).

*Original procedure, verbatim and in its original order; the five original phase headings are demoted one level. Lines starting with HOLD or FLAG were added on 2026-10-03 as separate lines next to the affected steps: a hold that must be met first sits directly before the step it gates; a flag, or a hold that limits a step, sits directly after the step it refers to (36 D-36-17). They are pending qualified review and change no original step. Figures in the original steps (sizes, depths, grit, times) are kept verbatim and still need confirmation against manufacturer instructions in competent review; the set time is flagged below because 31 section 10 lists it (31 section 3.5 rule 3). Throughout the procedure the Appendix A "During work" rules apply: follow this SOP and the manufacturer instructions, keep protection and containment in place, document concealed conditions, stop and escalate unsafe or unapproved conditions, record progress and materials, and get change approval before added work (spec APXA-004).*

> HOLD (C-DW01-01): before "Drop Cloths" below and every later step, confirm that any leak or water source behind the damage is resolved, and record the cause of damage and the active-leak status. A leak that is active or not confirmed resolved: do not start; STOP and escalate (sections 10 and 19). Cleared by: TBD - qualified safety professional. Pending qualified review. (source: spec DW-01.SAF "confirm leak/source resolved"; spec DW-01.INT "cause of damage, active leak status")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Site Protection & Damage Evaluation"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW01-01, X-06): before "Drop Cloths" below, check the damaged area for wet material or suspected mold growth without disturbing it; the moisture check method is TBD by the qualified reviewer. Wet material or suspected mold: do not start; STOP and escalate. Until the company mold definition exists, suspected mold is a critical hold (Q-31-10). Cleared by: TBD - qualified mold assessor. Pending qualified review. (source: spec DW-01.HAZ "possible mold/moisture"; spec DW-01.SAF "stop on mold"; 31 section 8.4 rule 2)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Site Protection & Damage Evaluation"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW01-01, X-12): ceiling or other overhead patch: do not start "Drop Cloths" below or any later step overhead while no approved height and access policy and no reviewed overhead procedure exist; the task stays blocked. Cleared by: TBD - qualified safety professional, after the policy is approved. Pending qualified review. (source: spec DW-01.HAZ "ladder for ceilings"; 02 G-005; 31 section 8.4 rule 4)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Site Protection & Damage Evaluation"

lines: - [ ] **Drop Cloths:** Lay canvas drop cloths directly under the repair area. Tape lightweight plastic sheeting below the wall zone if working on painted or wallpapered surfaces.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Site Protection & Damage Evaluation"

lines: - [ ] **Structural Scan:** Use a stud finder to locate the nearest wood/metal studs on either side of the hole. Scan for hidden electrical wires or copper plumbing pipes behind the gypsum core.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Site Protection & Damage Evaluation"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW01-11): the step above relies on a stud finder that the inventory file does not list; whether a device detects wiring or pipes comes from its manufacturer documentation. The label "Structural Scan" describes a stud and service scan, not a structural assessment. Pending qualified review. (source: 02 C-DW01-11; inventory file)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Site Protection & Damage Evaluation"

lines: - [ ] **Squaring the Patch:** Use a framing square and a pencil to draw a perfect rectangle around the damage. Avoid erratic shapes to ensure clean replacement joints.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Site Protection & Damage Evaluation"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW01-01): do not start "Clean Cut" below until the scan in "Structural Scan" above has covered the drawn rectangle and the surrounding wall where backing screws will be driven, and has found no wiring, pipe or other service there. A service in that area or an uncertain scan result: STOP and escalate; moving or repairing wiring or plumbing is licensed-trade work (section 2, Do not perform). Cleared by: TBD - qualified safety professional. Pending qualified review. (source: spec DW-01.SAF "scan before cutting"; spec DW-01.HAZ "hidden utilities"; spec START-011)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔨 Phase 2: Surgical Extraction & Framing Backing"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW01-01, X-13): before "Clean Cut" below, record the approximate build year or "unknown". Build year unknown or pre-1978: do not cut, score or sand painted drywall, plaster, compound or texture until a qualified person records a disposition (HOLD for RRP review); suspect material is not disturbed. This is a conservative screening hold, not a legal conclusion. Cleared by: TBD - EPA RRP-certified renovator; accredited asbestos inspector for suspect asbestos. Pending qualified review. (source: 31 section 10 and section 7.2 rank 2; spec DW-01.SAF "suspect hazardous material"; Q-31-07)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔨 Phase 2: Surgical Extraction & Framing Backing"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW01-01): before "Clean Cut" below, isolate dust from the rest of the property. Whether the drop cloths and plastic sheeting of "Drop Cloths" are enough, how dust is isolated, whether the stocked HEPA vacuum is used and which PPE applies (no respirator class is named here) are set by the qualified safety professional (section 6). Cleared by: TBD - qualified safety professional. Pending qualified review. (source: spec DW-01.SAF "isolate dust"; spec DW-01.HAZ "silica/dust"; spec DW-01.TLS "PPE")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔨 Phase 2: Surgical Extraction & Framing Backing"

lines: - [ ] **Clean Cut:** Cut out the drawn rectangle cleanly using a drywall hand saw or utility knife. Keep the saw blade vertical at a 90-degree angle to avoid crumbling the surrounding drywall plaster.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔨 Phase 2: Surgical Extraction & Framing Backing"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW01-01, X-06): after the step above and before "Stud Clearing", inspect the opened cavity without disturbing it further. Extensive concealed damage, wet or deteriorated material, suspected mold, damaged framing, or a service in or behind the opening: STOP, photograph and record it with its severity (spec JOB-004) and escalate. Continue only after the hold is cleared and, where scope or price changes, an approved change order exists (spec FIN-008, JOB-005). Cleared by: TBD - qualified safety professional; structural engineer for framing concerns; qualified mold assessor for suspected mold. Pending qualified review. (source: spec DW-01.SAF "stop on mold/suspect hazardous material or extensive concealed damage"; 31 section 8.3)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔨 Phase 2: Surgical Extraction & Framing Backing"

lines: - [ ] **Stud Clearing:** If a stud is present, cut the drywall back exactly to the center line of the stud to leave a ledge for the new piece.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔨 Phase 2: Surgical Extraction & Framing Backing"

lines: - [ ] **Wood Backing Insertion:** If no stud is reachable, cut a piece of 1x3 lumber or plywood slat 4 inches longer than the hole. Insert it inside the cavity and secure it tightly from the outside using 1-1/4 inch drywall screws through the existing wall.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔨 Phase 2: Surgical Extraction & Framing Backing"

lines: - [ ] **Sizing the Insert:** Measure the cut opening and deduct 1/8 inch from the width and height. Cut a matching thickness replacement panel (1/2" or 5/8") from a fresh sheet.
- Evidence: measurement
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🎨 Phase 3: Hanging & Structural Bridging"

lines: - [ ] **Screw Fastening:** Screw the patch panel tightly into the wood backing or stud. Counter-sink the screws slightly (1/32 inch) to form a shallow dimple without breaking the paper facing.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🎨 Phase 3: Hanging & Structural Bridging"

lines: - [ ] **Beveling Edges:** Use a utility knife to score a slight V-groove bevel along the seams where the old and new drywall meet (improves compound penetration).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🎨 Phase 3: Hanging & Structural Bridging"

lines: - [ ] **Mesh Tape Application:** Apply high-strength self-adhesive fiberglass mesh tape centered directly over all joint seams without overlapping or wrinkling.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧽 Phase 4: Hot-Mud Taping & Feathering Layers"

lines: - [ ] **First Coat (Setting Mud):** Mix a batch of fast-drying setting compound (Sheetrock 20 or 45). Use a 6-inch taping knife to firmly press the hot-mud through the mesh, completely filling the V-groove. Skim flat.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧽 Phase 4: Hot-Mud Taping & Feathering Layers"

lines: > FLAG: the step above mixes a chemical product. Mix and use it only as the product label and SDS direct; the product names are kept verbatim and are not an approved product list, and a product without a reviewed SDS is not carried to a job (PROPOSED interim rule). No mixing ratio is added here. Pending qualified review. (source: 31 section 3.5 rules 3 and 8; 29 section 8.3)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧽 Phase 4: Hot-Mud Taping & Feathering Layers"

lines: - [ ] **Second Coat (Feather Coat):** Once the hot-mud is solid (approx. 30 mins), scrape off minor ridges with your knife blade. Switch to a 10-inch or 12-inch knife and apply a thin layer of lightweight ready-mix mud, feathering the edges 4 inches outward past the original seam.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧽 Phase 4: Hot-Mud Taping & Feathering Layers"

lines: > FLAG: UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions. The "approx. 30 mins" set time in the step above is given for two different setting compounds; set, dry and recoat times come only from the product manufacturer's instructions. The step stays unchanged until a qualified reviewer replaces the figure. (source: 31 section 10; 02 G-044)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧽 Phase 4: Hot-Mud Taping & Feathering Layers"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW01-05, X-26): "The Invisible Finish" in the heading above is an outcome term with no defined finish level. Quality is checked against the spec wording "flat/feathered finish appropriate to scope" (spec DW-01.QAC; section 13). Heading kept verbatim; owner and attorney review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Micro-Sanding & Priming (The Invisible Finish)"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW01-01, X-13): before "Dust-Controlled Sanding" below, the build-year disposition recorded before "Clean Cut" must also cover sanding into the existing painted wall at the feathered boundaries; without it, do not sand. Dust isolation and any PPE as set by the qualified safety professional (section 6). Cleared by: TBD - EPA RRP-certified renovator. Pending qualified review. (source: 31 section 10; spec DW-01.HAZ "silica/dust")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Micro-Sanding & Priming (The Invisible Finish)"

lines: - [ ] **Dust-Controlled Sanding:** Use a fine-grit (220-grit) sanding sponge to gently smooth the dry edges. Meticulously blend the feathered boundaries into the texture of the original wall.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Micro-Sanding & Priming (The Invisible Finish)"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW01-04): blending the feathered edges into the existing texture in the step above is not a texture-matching procedure. Texture matching, which the agreement promises, is not covered by this SOP (section 2). Pending owner decision.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Micro-Sanding & Priming (The Invisible Finish)"

lines: - [ ] **Flashlight Inspection:** Hold a high-powered LED light flat against the wall profile. Check for minor shadow hollows, pinholes, or tool lines. Touch up with spot معجون if needed.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Micro-Sanding & Priming (The Invisible Finish)"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW01-13): the last sentence of the step above contains a word in Arabic, kept verbatim. Proposed English gloss for owner and bilingual-reviewer confirmation: "joint compound" (02 C-DW01-13). This is not a translation; Spanish text comes only through the translation workflow (section 22).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Micro-Sanding & Priming (The Invisible Finish)"

lines: - [ ] **Dry Wiping:** Wipe down the repair zone with a clean, dry microfiber cloth to remove chalky powder.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Micro-Sanding & Priming (The Invisible Finish)"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW01-11): dry wiping in the step above is the only dust-removal step, and no step uses the stocked cordless HEPA vacuum. The cleanup method for sanding dust and the use of the vacuum are set by the qualified safety professional (section 14). (source: spec DW-01.QAC "dust cleaned"; inventory file)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Micro-Sanding & Priming (The Invisible Finish)"

lines: - [ ] **Sealing Primer:** Apply a uniform coat of high-quality drywall primer-sealer. *Crucial:* Never allow painters to apply final paint over raw compound without primer; it will absorb differently and leave a flashing silhouette blotch.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Micro-Sanding & Priming (The Invisible Finish)"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW01-07): the step above primes every patch, while the spec says "primer if included" (spec DW-01.MAT, DW-01.QAC) and the pricing file sells primer inside an add-on. Whether primer is included is an owner decision (Q-28-21); the step and its quality rationale stay unchanged. Apply the primer only as the product label and SDS direct. (source: 02 C-DW01-07; 31 section 3.5 rule 8)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Micro-Sanding & Priming (The Invisible Finish)"

lines: | Check (spec DW-01.QAC) | Evidence (draft) | Inspector |

| Stable patch | Insert fastened into backing or stud ("Screw Fastening"); the method for checking that the patch is firm is TBD; photos do not prove hidden fastening or framing condition (quality playbook) | Worker self-check or supervisor: TBD (Q-31-15) |
| Flat/feathered finish appropriate to scope | "Flashlight Inspection" in section 12; the finish level is undefined (X-26) | TBD (Q-31-15) |
| Texture match within agreed tolerance | Not covered: no texture step and no agreed tolerance exist (C-DW01-04; section 2) | TBD (Q-31-15) |
| Primed if included | "Sealing Primer" in section 12; inclusion per the approved estimate (C-DW01-07) | TBD (Q-31-15) |
| Dust cleaned | Section 14 complete; today only "Dry Wiping" removes dust (C-DW01-11) | TBD (Q-31-15) |
- The job cannot be marked complete until each required check is answered or an exception is recorded (source: spec QA-001, AT-039).
- Evidence: note

- A failed check becomes a punch item or an escalation; a worker's self-check does not replace a required supervisor inspection (source: quality playbook "Prevent a worker's self-check from replacing required supervisor inspection").

- Photos alone do not prove hidden fasteners, structural adequacy or hazardous-material clearance (source: quality playbook "Do not infer hidden fasteners, structural adequacy, hazardous-material clearance or electrical safety from an image").
- A customer acknowledgement does not clear a safety hold (source: quality playbook "A signed customer form does not clear an unresolved safety hold").
- Evidence: note

- Clean the work area, including sanding dust and debris (source: spec QA-002; spec DW-01.QAC "dust cleaned"). The cleanup method beyond "Dry Wiping", including use of the stocked HEPA vacuum, is pending safety review (C-DW01-11).
- Remove drop cloths, masking film and any other protection or containment (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005).
- Account for tools and materials; return unused materials (source: spec APXA-005, APXA-007).
- Cleanup photos where they are required for this dusty service (source: spec QA-002).
- Evidence: photo
TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

- Known streams for that review: drywall offcuts and removed damaged material; sanding dust; used sponges, blades and mesh tape; compound residue and primer containers; any water-damaged or suspect material, which is not handled until its hold is cleared. No waste destination is defined (source: section 12; 31 section 3.1 row 15; 02 G-078).
- Suspect hazardous-material waste is not handled without an approved policy (source: 31 section 3.1 row 15; spec START-011).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: arrival and existing-condition photos of the damaged area, including visible staining, and of the protection setup (source: spec START-008, APXA-002, BRF-012; 04 completion evidence row, PROPOSED).
- Evidence: photo
- During: the opened cavity after "Clean Cut", before the backing or the insert goes in; any concealed condition, with its severity (source: spec JOB-004; 04 completion evidence row, PROPOSED).
- After: a photo per patch, mapped to its work area (source: spec QA-003); cleanup photos where required (source: spec QA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- Photos are internal-only by default and avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- The required photo set, and whether Start Job is blocked without the "before" photos: TBD - owner (source: spec START-008).
- Arrival and completion updates use approved templates only; until approved they are drafts (source: 31 section 3.1 row 17).

- Before work: confirm the scope with the customer only as needed, including whether primer, paint and texture are included; record extra requests instead of accepting them outside the change process (source: spec APXA-003, JOB-005, FIN-008).
- Evidence: note
- If work is blocked (active leak, suspected mold, suspect hazardous material, concealed damage), use only the approved "work blocked" message (source: spec NTF-007; 31 section 8.5).
- At the walkthrough, record the outcome: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- Explain the invoice and payment next step without making unauthorized promises (source: spec APXA-006).

- Do not promise an invisible or flawless result, completion in one visit, a texture match or durability, and do not discuss fault; refer such questions to the owner (source: Do-not-perform entry 8; 31 section 8.5; C-DW01-05).
- Care notes, such as drying before painting, come only from approved product data (source: spec QA-008; quality playbook "Prepare handoff instructions from approved product data").
- Every required check in section 13 is answered with evidence, or an exception is recorded (source: spec QA-001, AT-039).
- Evidence: note
- After photos are captured and mapped to each patch area (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup is done, protection removed, and tools and materials accounted for (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005).
- The property is left secured (source: 31 section 3.1 row 18).
- Punch items and the walkthrough outcome are recorded (source: spec QA-004, QA-005, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- No HOLD in section 12 is left open; unresolved issues, incidents and change follow-ups are submitted before the job closes (source: 31 section 8.3; spec APXA-007, JOB-012).
- Close only when the required operational and financial steps are complete (source: spec APXA-007).
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:

DW-01 stop triggers (spec DW-01.SAF first: "confirm leak/source resolved; scan before cutting; isolate dust; stop on mold/suspect hazardous material or extensive concealed damage"; then the register holds; all pending qualified review):
- The leak or water source is active or not confirmed resolved: do not start, cut, patch or close the wall (source: spec DW-01.SAF; C-DW01-01).
- The scan has not been done, has found a service in the cut path, or gives an uncertain result: do not cut (source: spec DW-01.SAF "scan before cutting"; spec DW-01.HAZ "hidden utilities").
- Dust cannot be isolated: do not cut or sand (source: spec DW-01.SAF "isolate dust").

- Suspected mold, suspect hazardous material or extensive concealed damage: stop. Suspected mold is treated as a critical hold until the company mold definition exists (source: spec DW-01.SAF; 31 section 8.4 rule 2; X-06; Q-31-10).
- Build year unknown or pre-1978 with no recorded disposition: do not cut, score or sand painted surfaces (source: 31 section 10; X-13).
- Ceiling or overhead work without an approved height and access policy: the task stays blocked (source: 31 section 3.3 entry 5 and section 8.4 rule 4; 02 G-005; X-12).
- Structural, electrical or plumbing work turns out to be needed: stop (section 2, Do not perform).
- Client-supplied paint missing, damaged or unidentified when the approved estimate relies on it: the affected task is blocked (source: spec START-009; spec JOB-004 "missing customer-supplied item").
- Every HOLD in section 12 names who clears it; critical holds clear only with a recorded qualified assessment, never by override or customer request (source: 31 section 8.3).
- Evidence: note
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
DW-01 routes (contacts and escalation order are owner decisions, Q-31-05):

- An active or unconfirmed leak, wet material or suspected mold: stop before any further work on the affected patch and escalate; suspected mold is released only with a recorded assessment by a qualified mold assessor (source: 31 section 8.4 rule 2; X-06; Q-31-10).
- A service in the cut path, or wiring or plumbing in the opening: stop; the office refers the work to a licensed trade (section 2, Do not perform).

- Build year unknown or pre-1978 with no recorded disposition, or suspect material: stop and escalate; release needs a disposition recorded by an EPA RRP-certified renovator, or by an accredited asbestos inspector for suspect asbestos (source: 31 section 10; X-13; Q-31-07).
- Extensive concealed damage or damaged framing: stop; structural concerns go to a structural engineer before any work continues (source: spec DW-01.SAF; 31 section 8.3).
- Ceiling work that would need access equipment: stop; it waits for the approved height and access policy (X-12; Q-31-09).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].

- DW-01 examples: a cut injury from a knife or saw, a strike on hidden wiring or pipes, a fall from access equipment, exposure to dust from suspect material, and damage to customer finishes or belongings (source: spec JOB-008; spec DW-01.HAZ).

- Q-31-07 (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: EPA RRP-certified renovator, accredited asbestos inspector): which property-age threshold triggers lead and asbestos screening when DW-01 cuts or sands painted drywall, plaster or texture, and does HandyHub hold or plan EPA RRP certification (X-13)?
- Q-31-10 (owner; qualified mold assessor): the company definition of mold growth versus cleanable mildew, and the stop rule for water-damaged drywall (X-06).
- Q-31-09 (owner; qualified safety professional): the height and access policy that ceiling patches depend on (X-12).
- Q-31-01 (owner): who are the competent reviewers for this SOP, and how is their competence evidenced?
- Q-31-05 (owner): emergency and escalation contacts and order for sections 19 and 20.
- Q-31-15 (owner): which section 13 checks need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check while there are two employees?
- Q-31-16 (owner; attorney): who approves replacement wording for the promissory intro and the Phase 5 heading (C-DW01-05)?
- Q-31-02 (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer who confirms the gloss of the Arabic word and reviews the Spanish version (C-DW01-13)?
- Q-27-15 (qualified safety professional; licensing reviewer): which HOLDs in section 12 are critical holds?
- Q-28-21 (owner): is primer, and painting with client-supplied paint, included in the price or sold as an add-on (C-DW01-07)?
- OPEN QUESTION (C-DW01-04; owner, attorney): is texture matching part of DW-01, and to what agreed tolerance?

- OPEN QUESTION (C-DW01-08; owner with the qualified safety professional): the largest patch and the overhead work one technician may handle alone, and whether large panel patches get a reviewed procedure.

sops.title: SOP DW-02: Texture Matching & Popcorn Ceiling Removal

lines: - The agreement makes the client "completely remove all electronics, personal items, clothes, and furniture from the target rooms before the crew arrives", while the "Total Masking" step has the crew "Remove all furniture from the zone." Verify the room is empty on arrival and record any exception; who moves furniture, and at what price, is an owner decision (source: agreement "Total Room Evacuation"; C-DW02-14; spec START-007).
- Evidence: note

- PROPOSED customer checklist, sent with the appointment reminder once the owner and attorney approve the wording: rooms emptied; occupants and pets plan; HVAC shutdown consent and its scope; access for a multi-visit job; disclose the build year, any prior testing and whether the ceiling was painted (source: 04 DW-02 customer preparation requirements, GAP; spec NTF-004, NTF-005; DW-02.INT).

- Occupied home: occupants, children and pets are kept out of the contained area; the occupant and pet module is pending qualified safety review (source: spec DW-02.INT "occupied status"; APXA-002; X-11; 31 section 5.8).
- HVAC off in an occupied home: no temperature limit or duration is set here; the plan is pending owner, attorney (consent wording) and qualified safety review (source: C-DW02-V01).

- A customer's statement or signature never clears a hold, and a customer-provided test log counts only once the owner and an accredited asbestos inspector define what record releases work (source: risk-triage playbook "Unknown popcorn-ceiling material is not cleared by wet scraping."; owner facts 2026-10-02 "acknowledgment cannot bypass critical holds"; Q-30-18).
- Evidence: note

> HOLD (C-DW02-03, X-13) - before the first step below ("Asbestos Verification") and before any step that wets, scrapes, sands or tapes over the ceiling texture, including sealing ceiling vents in "HVAC Isolation": build year unknown = HOLD; untested texture = HOLD at any property age until a qualified reviewer sets the screening rule (04 DW-02 prerequisites, PROPOSED); painted texture in a pre-1978 or unknown-age home = HOLD for EPA RRP review. Do not disturb the ceiling; stop and escalate. Wet methods do not clear suspect material ("Unknown popcorn-ceiling material is not cleared by wet scraping"). Release only by the qualified reviewer named in section 10. Pending qualified review. (source: spec DW-02.SAF, DW-02.HAZ, DW-02.INT; 31 section 10; risk-triage playbook; owner facts 2026-10-02 "Unknown is not safe")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: High-Risk Containment Setup"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW02-02) - before the first step below: no HandyHub worker collects, cuts or sends samples of the texture; the testing role is undefined. The record that releases work (who sampled, which lab, which result) is not yet defined by the owner with an accredited asbestos inspector, so a test log alone does not release the ceiling (04 DW-02 status; Q-30-18). Positive or inconclusive result = BLOCKED: release only on documented clearance from a qualified asbestos professional accepted by the owner; never on the basis of encapsulation in place (related C-DW02-01: the agreement's resumption clause is under attorney review). Pending qualified review. (source: 31 section 10; spec DW-02.SAF, START-010)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: High-Risk Containment Setup"

lines: - [ ] **Asbestos Verification:** Confirm if the home was built before 1980. If yes, stop work and verify asbestos testing logs before disturbing the ceiling matrix.
- Evidence: note
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: High-Risk Containment Setup"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW02-03): UNSOURCED threshold - reviewer to confirm (not a manufacturer value). The "1980" build year in the step above has no cited source. The existing stop stays in force until a qualified reviewer replaces it; the holds above add the unknown-year, untested-texture and painted-texture cases and do not relax it. The step text is unchanged. HUMAN REVIEW: accredited asbestos inspector; EPA RRP-certified renovator (Q-31-07). (source: 31 section 10; 36 section 3.4 rule 8)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: High-Risk Containment Setup"

lines: > HOLD (X-12, C-DW02-12) - before "HVAC Isolation" below and every later step that needs a ladder, platform or staging rather than a pole tool from the floor, for example sealing ceiling vents, hanging the wall curtains, the Phase 3 hand work, priming and texture spraying, and any ceiling above the height the pricing file surcharges: access only with equipment and methods approved under a height and access policy, which does not exist yet (02 G-005); the inventory lists no access equipment beyond the scraper poles. Until the policy exists those steps stay on hold (31 section 8.4). Pending qualified review. (source: spec DW-02.TLS "access equipment", DW-02.HAZ "falls", DW-02.SAF "height controls")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: High-Risk Containment Setup"

lines: - [ ] **HVAC Isolation:** Turn off the home's heating/cooling system entirely and seal all air intake/output vents tightly with plastic film and painters tape.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: High-Risk Containment Setup"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW02-V01, X-07): the step above is limited by the signed consent. The agreement's "HVAC Shutdown Consent" covers "the scraping and sanding phases", while the step turns the system off "entirely" and no step restores it, including through the drying waits in Phase 4. Confirm the HVAC state against the signed consent at each phase change and record any exception (spec START-007, JOB-009). How long the HVAC may stay off, who restores it and when, and an occupant and worker temperature plan are pending owner, attorney (consent wording) and qualified safety review; no limit is set here (related X-27). No company isolate-verify-restore module exists yet (X-07; 31 section 5.8). Unsealing the vents and restoring the HVAC belong to closeout (section 14). Pending qualified review. (source: agreement "HVAC Shutdown Consent"; 02 C-DW02-V01; 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: High-Risk Containment Setup"

lines: - [ ] **Total Masking:** Remove all furniture from the zone. Line the entire floor with thick heavy plastic sheeting (6 mil thickness). Run a continuous 3-mil plastic curtain along all walls, overlapping the floor sheets by 12 inches to form a complete static dust envelope.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: High-Risk Containment Setup"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW02-14): VERIFY CLIENT PREP / record exception. The agreement makes the client remove "all electronics, personal items, clothes, and furniture" before the crew arrives, while the step above has the crew "Remove all furniture from the zone." Until the owner decides who moves furniture and at what price, verify on arrival that the rooms are empty as the agreement requires and record any exception (spec START-007). The step text is unchanged. (source: agreement "Total Room Evacuation"; 02 C-DW02-14)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: High-Risk Containment Setup"

lines: All pending qualified review. A precondition that is not met keeps the affected tasks blocked (source: job-planner playbook "A missing ladder or unverified permit keeps affected tasks blocked.").

- On-site assessment before a firm quote; no firm quote until the hazardous-material disposition (asbestos result and the lead or painted-texture decision) is recorded (source: 04 DW-02 estimating method, PROPOSED; estimate-assistant playbook "Missing hazardous-condition decisions block a firm quote.").
- Evidence: note

- Screening recorded before dispatch: approximate build year or "unknown" (spec BRF-003 "approximate age if known"), prior testing and who performed it, texture type and whether the texture is painted (spec DW-02.INT). Unknown is not safe: an unknown build year is a hold (source: owner facts 2026-10-02; 31 SOP-022, PROPOSED).
- Evidence: note

- The record that releases work (who sampled, which lab, which result) is not yet defined by the owner with an accredited asbestos inspector, and no HandyHub sampling takes place (source: 04 DW-02 status; Q-30-18; C-DW02-02). The result is stored as a START-010 prerequisite and an SCH-001 readiness flag (source: 04 DW-02 prerequisites, PROPOSED).
- Evidence: note

- Permit, licence or qualification flags: where admin policy marks the job, Start Job is blocked until the prerequisite is approved (source: spec START-010). Abatement, notification and disposal requirements after a positive result, and whether EPA RRP applies to painted texture, are OPEN QUESTIONS per Kentucky and Indiana municipality; unknown applicability must not default to "no permit" (source: 04 DW-02 permit/license flags; risk-triage playbook).
- Signed HVAC shutdown consent on file; its scope is "during the scraping and sanding phases" (source: agreement "HVAC Shutdown Consent"; C-DW02-V01).
- Customer preparation as agreed: rooms emptied before the crew arrives, verified on arrival (source: agreement "Total Room Evacuation"; C-DW02-14).

- Fixture isolation method, respiratory protection and dust-control decision, and height and access policy approved by the qualified reviewers; until they exist, the steps they gate stay on hold (source: section 12 holds; 31 section 8.4).

- Before leaving: confirm job, customer, address and time; read the latest changes; review scope, exclusions, hazards and safety; load critical tools, equipment and materials; confirm required documents and approvals (source: spec APXA-001).

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; confirm materials; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003). High-risk flags may require separate checkboxes or supervisor confirmation (source: spec START-004).
- Evidence: note
- Materials readiness: missing material may block start, for example primer, disposal bags, setting compound or mesh tape, which are not stocked (source: spec START-006; C-DW02-12).

- Multi-visit planning: the drying wait between skim passes ("Allow 12–24 hours to dry") means return visits; the job planner plans them and keeps the HVAC state within the signed consent across visits (source: original step "Drying & Ridge Scraping"; 04 DW-02 labor assumptions; job-planner playbook "drying/cure waits"; C-DW02-V01).

- On arrival: confirm address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants; inspect the actual site against the briefing; capture the required existing-condition photos; protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo

- Pre-start site check: record any difference from the briefing, including rooms not emptied as agreed; material differences trigger Risk Triage or supervisor review (source: spec START-007; C-DW02-14).
- Evidence: note
- Confirm that the hazardous-material disposition and the other section 3 preconditions are recorded before any setup step touches the ceiling (source: section 3; spec START-010).
- Evidence: note
- Existing-condition photos before any work: the whole ceiling, existing cracks, fixtures and vents (source: spec START-008, BRF-012; X-02; section 16).
- Evidence: photo

- Containment: the "HVAC Isolation" and "Total Masking" steps in section 12; keep protection and containment in place during work (source: spec APXA-004 "keep protection/containment"; DW-02.SAF "isolate area; control dust").

- PROPOSED, pending review: record the HVAC state before switching it off, so that it can be restored at closeout (source: spec APXA-005 "restore utilities/components altered within scope"; 31 section 5.8 isolate-verify-restore module; C-DW02-09).
- Evidence: note
- Fixture isolation and protection only by the approved method (section 12 hold; C-DW02-04).

*Original procedure, verbatim and in its original order; the original phase headings are demoted one level with their text unchanged. The HOLD and FLAG lines are additions pending qualified review: a precondition hold sits directly before the step it gates, and a hold or flag that suspends, limits or flags a step sits directly after it (36 D-36-17). They never replace or reword a step.*

> HOLD (C-DW02-04) - before "Misting Protocol" below and any wetting of the ceiling: the ceiling light fixtures and circuits in the work zone are electrically isolated and protected by a method approved in qualified safety review; no electrical work beyond the approved scope, and no fixture removal without a licensed electrician. If isolation cannot be confirmed, or water reaches a fixture or electrical box, stop and escalate. Pending qualified review. (source: spec DW-02.SAF "de-energize/protect fixtures as needed", DW-02.HAZ "electrical fixtures, water exposure"; 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 💧 Phase 2: Hydraulic Softening & Scraping"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW02-05) - before "Misting Protocol" below and every later step that scrapes, mixes, sands or sprays: respiratory protection, other PPE and the dust-control plan must be decided by a qualified safety professional; none is selected here and none is stocked. Until that decision exists these steps stay on hold (31 section 8.4). The containment envelope and the HEPA-connected sander are engineering controls; they do not replace the reviewer's decision and do not clear suspect material. Pending qualified review. (source: spec DW-02.TLS "PPE/respiratory equipment per plan"; original intro "hazardous dust protocol"; risk-triage playbook "do not invent respirator selection, fit-test clearance"; 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 💧 Phase 2: Hydraulic Softening & Scraping"

lines: - [ ] **Misting Protocol:** Fill a clean garden pump sprayer with warm water mixed with 2 tablespoons of liquid dish soap (helps break surface tension). Lightly mist a 5x5 foot test section. *Do not over-saturate; excess water will degrade the underlying drywall core paper.*
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 💧 Phase 2: Hydraulic Softening & Scraping"

lines: > FLAG: UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions. "2 tablespoons of liquid dish soap" in the step above has no product-label source; any wetting agent and its mixing come only from the approved product label and SDS (29 section 8.2 control 8). The step text is unchanged. (source: 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 💧 Phase 2: Hydraulic Softening & Scraping"

lines: - [ ] **Soak Window:** Allow the water to absorb into the acoustic texture for 15 minutes.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 💧 Phase 2: Hydraulic Softening & Scraping"

lines: > FLAG: UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions. The "15 minutes" soak time in the step above has no source. The step text is unchanged. (source: 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 💧 Phase 2: Hydraulic Softening & Scraping"

lines: - [ ] **Slicing Scraping:** Use a 10-inch or 12-inch floor scraper or specialty ceiling blade mounted on an extension pole. Hold the blade at a shallow 15-degree angle. Fluidly slice away the wet popcorn slurry, allowing it to drop onto the plastic. Keep the blade flat to avoid gouging the paper facing.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 💧 Phase 2: Hydraulic Softening & Scraping"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW02-07): the heading above says "Structural Re-Taping & Structural Repairs", but structural repair is outside this SOP (section 2, Do not perform). Under this draft the steps below are limited to drywall tape and fastener defects, pending review; the agreement disclaims "structural ceiling joist cracks", and no price line or change order covers repairs. The heading is kept verbatim. (source: 31 section 10; 02 C-DW02-07)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🩹 Phase 3: Structural Re-Taping & Structural Repairs"

lines: - [ ] **Exposing Defects:** Meticulously inspect the newly bared ceiling drywall. Locate split joint tapes, loose rusted nails, or structural framing sagging.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🩹 Phase 3: Structural Re-Taping & Structural Repairs"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW02-07) - before "Fastener Tightening" below: if the inspection above finds structural framing sagging or framing movement, STOP - do not fasten, tape or skim over it; photograph it, record it (spec JOB-004) and escalate for supervisor or structural engineer review. A loose or "bouncy" area that may be framing movement is treated the same way until it is reviewed. Repairs beyond the approved scope need an approved change order before work proceeds (spec FIN-008). Pending qualified review. (source: 02 C-DW02-07; 31 section 10; spec START-011)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🩹 Phase 3: Structural Re-Taping & Structural Repairs"

lines: - [ ] **Fastener Tightening:** Drive new 1-1/4 inch drywall screws into any loose or bouncy ceiling joist sectors. Punch down any popping old nails.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🩹 Phase 3: Structural Re-Taping & Structural Repairs"

lines: - [ ] **Seam Re-Tape:** Strip away any peeling old paper tape. Apply fresh fiberglass mesh tape over cracked seams and apply a structural coat of setting compound.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🩹 Phase 3: Structural Re-Taping & Structural Repairs"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW02-13, X-26): TIER-DEPENDENT STEPS - owner to confirm. Pricing Tier 1 includes a "single coat skim" and Tier 2 "two to three" passes, while the steps below apply two passes to every ceiling. "Level 5" has no shared definition; the finish target comes from the approved estimate (spec DW-02.INT "finish target"; DW-02.QAC "smooth/texture finish meets target"). "This eliminates any minor structural waves in the ceiling joists." is an outcome statement, not a structural assessment. Steps unchanged. (source: 31 section 10; 02 C-DW02-13, X-26)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🍳 Phase 4: Skim Coating to Level 5 Finish"

lines: - [ ] **First Skim Pass:** Mix lightweight joint compound slightly thin (pancake batter consistency). Use an 18-inch or 24-inch skimming blade or a large trowel to pull a uniform layer across the entire ceiling plane.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🍳 Phase 4: Skim Coating to Level 5 Finish"

lines: - [ ] **Drying & Ridge Scraping:** Allow 12–24 hours to dry. Use a wide taping knife held at a 45-degree angle to scrape down all tracking lines and ridges.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🍳 Phase 4: Skim Coating to Level 5 Finish"

lines: - [ ] **Second Skim Pass:** Apply a second, ultra-thin coat of compound perpendicular (90 degrees opposite) to the direction of the first pass. This eliminates any minor structural waves in the ceiling joists.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🍳 Phase 4: Skim Coating to Level 5 Finish"

lines: - [ ] **Dustless Sanding:** Connect a specialized drywall pole-sander to a HEPA dust-extraction vacuum. Sand the entire ceiling plane with 150-grit or 220-grit mesh paper until completely flat.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 5: Sanding & Artisanal Texture Spraying (Optional)"

lines: - [ ] **The Level 5 Choice:** If the client ordered a smooth modern finish, check with light, wipe dust, and apply primer.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 5: Sanding & Artisanal Texture Spraying (Optional)"

lines: - [ ] **Texture Spray Application:** If matching a wall profile (e.g., Orange Peel/Knockdown), fill a mechanical compressor hopper gun with texture compound. Adjust air pressure to match the speckle size exactly. Spray in consistent overlapping circular sweeps.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 5: Sanding & Artisanal Texture Spraying (Optional)"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW02-15): the step above sprays an Orange Peel or Knockdown texture on the ceiling, chosen to match "a wall profile"; texturing the walls themselves and Skip-Trowel have no step (section 2, Out of scope). "match the speckle size exactly" is not an acceptance criterion: the check is "smooth/texture finish meets target" against the finish target in the approved estimate (spec DW-02.QAC). The compressor and hopper gun are set up only per their manufacturers' instructions; no pressure is set here. The step text is unchanged. (source: 02 C-DW02-15; spec DW-02.QAC)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 5: Sanding & Artisanal Texture Spraying (Optional)"

lines: - [ ] **Knockdown Execution:** For knockdown textures, wait 10–15 minutes for the sprayed droplets to partially harden, then gently glide a wide rubber wipe blade flat across the peaks to flatten them uniformly.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 5: Sanding & Artisanal Texture Spraying (Optional)"

lines: > FLAG: UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions. The "10–15 minutes" wait in the step above has no source; the texture product's own instructions govern. The step text is unchanged. (source: 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 5: Sanding & Artisanal Texture Spraying (Optional)"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW02-09): the procedure above ends at texture; no step removes the containment, cleans up, handles the debris, unseals the vents or restores the HVAC. The job is not complete until the closeout items in sections 14 to 16 and 18 are done or an exception is recorded (spec QA-002, APXA-005). The closeout items are PROPOSED, pending review. (source: 02 C-DW02-09; 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 5: Sanding & Artisanal Texture Spraying (Optional)"

lines: A worker cannot mark the job complete without answering these checks or recording an exception (source: spec QA-001). Photos cannot prove hidden conditions: do not infer hazardous-material clearance, structural adequacy or electrical safety from an image (source: quality-assistant playbook).
| Check (spec DW-02.QAC) | How it is verified (pending review) | Evidence | Inspector |

| Approved texture removed/matched | Texture removed from the whole approved area; where texture is sprayed, compared with the finish target in the approved estimate. "exactly" and "perfectly" are not acceptance criteria (C-DW02-15) | After photos per room or area (spec QA-003) | Worker self-check; whether a supervisor inspects is Q-31-15 |

| Substrate not damaged beyond repair scope | Gouges, paper-facing damage and concealed defects found after scraping are recorded; repairs beyond the approved scope only by change order (spec FIN-008; C-DW02-07) | Photos of each repaired area (04 DW-02 completion evidence, PROPOSED) | Worker; supervisor for anything structural |

| Smooth/texture finish meets target | Smooth path: the original "check with light" before priming; texture path: compared with the target. The finish level is the one in the approved estimate; "Level 5" has no shared definition yet (X-26), and the number of skim passes is tier-dependent (C-DW02-13) | Finish photos taken at the light check (04 DW-02, PROPOSED) | Worker; whether a supervisor inspects is Q-31-15 |

| Containment cleanup documented | Containment removed and the area cleaned; vents unsealed and the HVAC restored as altered within scope (spec QA-002, APXA-005; C-DW02-09) | Cleanup photos (spec QA-002 "Cleanup photos may be required for dusty/dirty services") | Worker |
- Containment removal sequence and HEPA cleanup method: TBD - pending qualified safety review (source: 02 C-DW02-09; spec QA-002).

- Clean the area; remove waste and protection; account for tools and materials; restore utilities or components altered within scope: unseal the vents and restore the HVAC altered in "HVAC Isolation" (source: spec APXA-005; C-DW02-09). Who restores the HVAC and when, between phases or at the end, is pending owner, attorney and safety review (C-DW02-V01).
- Cleanup photos may be required for dusty work (source: spec QA-002); see section 16.
- Evidence: photo

- The agreement's "Final Walkthrough" clause makes final payment due before the containment is removed; completion includes containment removal (spec QA-002 "Completion includes cleanup, debris/waste handling and removal of protection/containment as appropriate."), and the clause is under attorney review (see the agreement review notes).
TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

- Waste from the steps: scraped texture slurry, used plastic sheeting and tape, collected sanding dust, compound and texture residues and empty containers (source: original steps in section 12; spec QA-002 "debris/waste handling"; DW-02.MAT "disposal bags").

- Containers, destination and who pays: owner decision with the local rules of the actual municipality (source: 31 section 3.1, waste row; 29 Q-29-10). The pricing file calls the work "disposal intensive" but prices no disposal (28 section 8).

- Suspect or positive material is not bagged, moved or removed by HandyHub; disposal after a positive result is part of the open abatement and permit question (source: section 2, Do not perform; spec START-011; 04 DW-02 permit/license flags).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: arrival and existing-condition photos; start is blocked until they are captured or an authorized reason is recorded (source: spec START-008). Include the ceiling texture before any wetting, existing cracks (the agreement's "Pre-existing Cracks" clause depends on this evidence), fixtures, vents and the HVAC state (source: 04 DW-02 completion evidence, PROPOSED; X-02; spec BRF-012).
- Evidence: photo, note

- During: containment in place; concealed conditions found after scraping, recorded with photos and severity (source: spec APXA-004; JOB-004); repaired areas (source: 04 DW-02 completion evidence, PROPOSED).
- Evidence: note
- After: photos mapped to rooms or areas (source: spec QA-003): the finished ceiling, containment removed and the area cleaned (source: spec QA-002), vents unsealed.
- Evidence: photo

- The hazardous-material result is a document record, not a photo; a photo of the texture never establishes clearance (source: quality-assistant playbook "Do not infer hidden fasteners, structural adequacy, hazardous-material clearance or electrical safety from an image.").
- Evidence: photo, note
- Privacy: internal-only by default; avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).

- Arrival and completion updates use approved templates; a blocked job, including a hazardous-material hold, uses only the approved "work blocked" message, with no incident details or access codes by text or email (source: spec NTF-007, COM-002).

- Do not tell the customer whether the ceiling contains asbestos or lead, and make no health, air-quality or safety statement; refer questions to the owner (source: C-DW02-10; 31 section 3.5 rule 5; section 2, Do not perform item 8).
- HVAC: tell the customer when the HVAC is switched off and when it is restored, within the signed consent and in approved wording (source: agreement "HVAC Shutdown Consent"; C-DW02-V01).
- Walkthrough: record the outcome as accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Care and handoff notes come only from approved product data (source: spec QA-008; quality-assistant playbook "Prepare handoff instructions from approved product data").
- Do not promise a "flawless" finish, a perfect texture match, crack-free results or a warranty (source: section 2, Do not perform item 8; C-DW02-15).
- Explain the invoice and payment next step without unauthorized promises (source: spec APXA-006); the agreement's payment timing is under attorney review (see the agreement review notes).
Done means all of the following, recorded in the job (source: spec QA-001 to QA-004; DW-02.QAC; APXA-005 to APXA-007):
- Every section 13 check answered, or an exception recorded (QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- After photos mapped to rooms or areas (QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Containment removed and cleanup done, with containment cleanup documented (QA-002; DW-02.QAC "containment cleanup documented").
- Evidence: note
- Waste handled by the approved method (section 15).
- Vents unsealed and the HVAC restored as altered within scope (APXA-005; C-DW02-09).
- Tools and materials accounted for (APXA-005, APXA-007).
- Walkthrough outcome recorded, with punch items (QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Unresolved issues, incidents and change requests submitted before the job is closed (APXA-007).
- Final completion is a human sign-off; the quality review only recommends readiness (source: quality-assistant playbook "Recommend readiness for human sign-off; do not set final completion").
- Evidence: note
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:
Service-specific stop triggers and holds (all pending qualified review; release roles per 31 section 8.3):

- Card guidance, verbatim: "do not disturb suspect hazardous material without required evaluation/testing/authorization; isolate area; control dust; de-energize/protect fixtures as needed; height controls" (source: spec DW-02.SAF).

- HOLD C-DW02-03, screening before the first step: build year unknown = HOLD; untested texture = HOLD at any property age until a qualified reviewer sets the screening rule (04 DW-02 prerequisites, PROPOSED); painted texture in a pre-1978 or unknown-age home = HOLD for EPA RRP review. The original "1980" stop stays in force until a qualified reviewer replaces it. Release: an accredited asbestos inspector or an EPA RRP-certified renovator, as the case requires, with the owner.

- HOLD C-DW02-02, positive or inconclusive result = BLOCKED: release only on documented clearance from a qualified asbestos professional accepted by the owner; no HandyHub sampling; never resume because the material was encapsulated in place (related C-DW02-01; the agreement's resumption clause is under attorney review).
- Evidence: note

- HOLD C-DW02-04, fixtures: no wetting until the ceiling fixtures and circuits in the work zone are isolated and protected by an approved method; if isolation cannot be confirmed, or water reaches a fixture or electrical box, stop. Release: qualified safety professional; licensed electrician for any fixture removal.

- HOLD C-DW02-05, dust and respiratory protection: the scraping, mixing, sanding and spraying steps stay on hold until the qualified safety professional's respiratory and dust-control decision exists; a hold caused by a missing policy cannot be released by override (31 section 8.4).
- HOLD X-12, access: steps that need ladders, platforms or staging stay on hold until the height and access policy exists (31 section 8.4).

- STOP C-DW02-07, structure: structural framing sagging or framing movement found after scraping = STOP, photograph, record (spec JOB-004), supervisor or engineer review; no fastening, taping or skimming over it.
- Evidence: note

- HOLD C-DW02-V01, HVAC: the HVAC state must match the signed consent at each phase change, and any exception is recorded; heat or cold for occupants and workers while the HVAC is off is a stop trigger under the "unsafe heat or cold" line of the block above.
- Evidence: note
- Suspect hazardous material, a structural concern and unapproved electrical scope are critical holds that no role can override; they clear only with a recorded qualified assessment (31 section 8.3).
- Evidence: note
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
Service roles for DW-02 (contacts and escalation order are owner decisions, Q-31-05):
- Suspect asbestos, test results and sampling questions: accredited asbestos inspector (C-DW02-02, C-DW02-03).
- Painted texture in an older or unknown-age home: EPA RRP-certified renovator (C-DW02-03).
- Ceiling fixtures and circuits: licensed electrician (C-DW02-04).
- Sagging framing or framing movement: supervisor, then structural engineer (C-DW02-07).
- Dust, respiratory protection, access equipment, and heat or cold while the HVAC is off: qualified safety professional (C-DW02-05, X-12, C-DW02-V01).
- HVAC consent scope, testing and resumption terms: owner, with the attorney (C-DW02-V01; agreement review notes).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].

- For this service, report at least: suspected exposure to texture dust or debris before a hazardous-material disposition was recorded, water reaching a fixture or an electrical shock, a fall from access equipment, a slip on wet sheeting, a containment failure, and compressor or hopper-gun failure (source: spec JOB-008 "suspected hazardous-material exposure", "tool/equipment failure"; DW-02.HAZ).

- **Q-31-07** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: EPA RRP-certified renovator, accredited asbestos inspector): which property-age thresholds trigger lead and asbestos screening for DW-02, what replaces the unsourced "1980" threshold, and does HandyHub hold or plan EPA RRP certification?

- **Q-30-18** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: accredited asbestos inspector, EPA RRP-certified renovator, attorney): who collects samples of suspect texture, which lab, what record releases work, and where is lead-safe work information acknowledged?

- **Q-31-01** (owner): who are the competent reviewers for this SOP (qualified safety professional, asbestos inspector, RRP renovator, licensed electrician, structural engineer), and how is their competence evidenced?
- **Q-31-05** (owner): emergency and escalation contacts and escalation order for a two-person team.
- **Q-31-09** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional): height and access policy for hand work at the ceiling and for high ceilings.
- **Q-31-10** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified mold assessor): company definition of mold growth and the stop rule, for moisture or mold uncovered after scraping.
- **Q-31-11** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional): emergency kit contents and the SDS register owner.
- **Q-31-15** (owner): do the finish and texture checks need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check?
- **Q-31-16** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: attorney): who approves replacement wording for the promissory intro line?
- **Q-31-02** (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish version?

- **02 C-DW02-V01** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: attorney, qualified safety reviewer): should the HVAC stay off for the whole job, which needs revised consent, or be restored between scraping and sanding as the consent implies? Who restores it, when, and for how long may it stay off in an occupied home?
- **02 C-DW02-14** (owner): who moves furniture, the client or the crew, and at what price?
- **02 C-DW02-13** (owner): Tier 1 with one skim pass or two?
- **04 DW-02 card, exclusions** (owner): is wall texture matching, including Skip-Trowel, part of DW-02?

- **04 DW-02 card, permit/license flags** (HUMAN REVIEW: accredited asbestos inspector, attorney, applicable Kentucky and Indiana environmental agencies): abatement, notification and disposal requirements after a positive result, decided per state and municipality.

sops.title: SOP DW-03: Residential Remodeling & Home Additions

lines: - Agreement duties, quoted for reference only and under attorney review: keep utilities connected ("uninterrupted electrical power" and "clean running water") and "seal personal adjacent spaces" (source: agreement "Active Utilities Mandatory" and "Dust Containment" clauses; 30 section 5 rows 31 and 59).

- PROPOSED customer checklist, sent with the appointment confirmation and reminder once the owner and attorney approve the wording: clear the work area and access path; plan for occupants, children and pets; disclose known leaks, moisture, utilities in the walls, the build year and any prior testing (source: 04 DW-03 customer preparation requirements; spec NTF-004, NTF-005; CX-005).
