- On arrival, identify pets and occupants and keep them away from active work, lifts, stilts, cutting and sanding; the occupant and pet module is pending qualified safety review (source: spec APXA-002; X-11; 31 section 5.8).

- A customer's preparation or statement never replaces HandyHub's own pre-start checks, including the old-property screening and the inspection-before-concealment hold (source: 30 section 4.1 clause 5; risk-triage playbook "A pre-1978 painted surface is not cleared by a customer saying it looks safe.").
All pending qualified review. A precondition that is not met keeps the affected tasks blocked (source: job-planner playbook "A missing ladder or unverified permit keeps affected tasks blocked.").

- Site assessment and takeoff before a firm quote; photos alone cannot establish hidden conditions or load-bearing adequacy (source: estimate-assistant playbook "Photos alone cannot establish hidden condition or load-bearing adequacy."; 04 DW-03 estimating method, PROPOSED).

- C-DW03-01 precondition block (HOLD before Phase 1 in section 12): approved plans and scope on file; permit determination recorded by a reviewer, not assumed; headers, load-bearing and addition framing on HOLD for a structural engineer or building official; plumbing, electrical and HVAC relocations by licensed trades only (source: 31 section 10 DW-03; spec DW-03.INT, DW-03.SAF).
- Evidence: note

- Permit, licence or qualification flags: where admin policy marks the job, Start Job is blocked until the prerequisite is approved (source: spec START-010; AT-024). Whether a permit is needed for framing, basement finishing, additions or headers, and who obtains it, is an OPEN QUESTION per Kentucky and Indiana municipality; unknown applicability must not default to "no permit" (source: 04 DW-03 permit/license flags; risk-triage playbook).

- C-DW03-02 old-property screening (HOLD before Phase 1 and before "The Old-to-New Merge"): the approximate build year is captured at intake, with "unknown" as a value; in a pre-1978 or unknown-age home, painted surfaces, old plaster and other suspect materials are not disturbed until a qualified person records a disposition, and the plaster disposition is recorded before any tie-in (source: 31 sections 7.2 and 10; spec BRF-003 "approximate age if known"; 04 DW-03 prerequisites, PROPOSED; X-13). The age trigger is a conservative hold until the EPA RRP-certified renovator and the accredited asbestos inspector confirm the rule (Q-31-07).
- Evidence: note

- Access and lifting (HOLD before Phase 1 for ladders, and before "Hanging Sequence" for stilts, the panel lift and team lifting): controls approved by a qualified safety professional; until they exist the affected steps stay on hold (source: 31 section 10 DW-03; spec DW-03.SAF "lifting/team controls"; 31 section 8.4 rule 4; X-12; C-DW03-08).

- Utilities and power: the agreement assumes "uninterrupted electrical power" and "clean running water". If utilities are disconnected, no generator is used until the owner decides the utilities policy and a qualified safety professional approves generator use and placement (carbon monoxide) (source: agreement "Active Utilities Mandatory" clause; C-DW03-V01; 30 section 5 row 59).

- Before leaving: confirm job, customer, address and time; read the latest changes; review scope, exclusions, hazards and safety; load critical tools, equipment and materials; check customer-supplied items and rentals; confirm required documents and approvals (source: spec APXA-001). The briefing shows the approved estimate, the permit/license/inspection dependency status, change orders and drawings (source: spec BRF-011).

- Before starting: confirm scope with the customer only as needed; do not accept material extra work outside the change process; complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; confirm materials; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003). High-risk flags may require separate checkboxes or supervisor confirmation (source: spec START-004).
- Evidence: note
- Materials readiness: missing material may block start (source: spec START-006); several items the steps use are not stocked yet (C-DW03-10; see the inventory's proposed additions).

- On arrival: confirm address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants; inspect the actual site against the briefing; capture the required existing-condition photos; protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- Pre-start site check: record any difference from the briefing; material differences trigger Risk Triage or supervisor review (source: spec START-007).
- Evidence: note

- Protection and containment: protect floors and adjacent areas and keep protection and containment in place during work (source: spec APXA-002 "protect work area", APXA-004 "keep protection/containment"); the containment standard, including the curtains the agreement promises, is an owner and safety-reviewer decision (C-DW03-03).

- Utilities: confirm that power and water are available as the agreement assumes; no generator without approval (section 3; C-DW03-V01). Isolation of any utility in the work area follows the company isolate-verify-restore module once it is approved (X-07; 31 section 5.8); no utility work is done under this SOP.
- Equipment staging: the panel lift and stilts are set up and inspected only per their manufacturers and only after the access and lifting holds are released (C-DW03-08).
- Pre-start evidence: existing-condition photos, including every wall or ceiling the new work ties into (source: spec START-008, BRF-012; 04 DW-03 completion evidence, PROPOSED).
- Evidence: photo

*Original procedure, verbatim and in its original order; the five original phase headings are demoted one level. The HOLD and FLAG lines are additions pending qualified review: a precondition hold sits directly before the step it gates, and a hold or flag that suspends, limits or flags a step sits directly after it (36 D-36-17). They never replace or reword a step.*

> HOLD (C-DW03-01) - preconditions, before the first step below ("Plumb Line Layout") and before any framing: approved plans and scope on file; permit determination recorded by a reviewer, not assumed; headers, load-bearing and addition framing = HOLD for a structural engineer or building official; plumbing, electrical and HVAC relocations by licensed trades only. Do not start framing until these are recorded for this job (spec START-010). Release only by the named reviewer, with evidence (31 section 8.3). Pending qualified review. (source: 31 section 10 DW-03; spec DW-03.INT, DW-03.SAF)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Structural Framing & Layout Verification"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW03-02) - before the first step below and before any step that cuts, drills, sands or removes existing finishes: in a pre-1978 or unknown-age home, painted surfaces, old plaster and other suspect materials are not disturbed; stop and escalate. No HandyHub sampling; release only on a recorded disposition by an EPA RRP-certified renovator or an accredited asbestos inspector accepted by the owner. Pending qualified review. (source: 31 sections 7.2 and 10; spec START-011; owner facts 2026-10-02, EPA RRP and asbestos sources; X-13)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Structural Framing & Layout Verification"

lines: > HOLD (X-12) - before the first step below: snapping ceiling lines and fastening top plates is work at height. Ladders and other access equipment are used only under the approved height and access policy, which does not exist yet (02 G-005); until it exists this work stays on hold (31 section 8.4 rule 4). Pending qualified review. (source: spec DW-03.HAZ "falls", DW-03.TLS "access equipment"; section 2, Do not perform item 5)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Structural Framing & Layout Verification"

lines: - [ ] **Plumb Line Layout:** Snap blue chalk lines on the floor and ceiling to map new partitions. Use a laser level to verify that new vertical stud tracking is perfectly plumb.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Structural Framing & Layout Verification"

lines: - [ ] **Fastening Tracks:** Secure top and bottom plates using structural wood screws (for wood joists) or concrete anchors (for basement floor slabs). Space studs precisely at 16 inches on-center.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Structural Framing & Layout Verification"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW03-01): UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions. "Space studs precisely at 16 inches on-center" in the step above has no source; stud spacing, plate fasteners and anchors come only from the approved plans, any listed assembly, the board and fastener manufacturers and any applicable code requirement confirmed by the building official (31 section 10 DW-03: "manufacturer, listed assembly and code govern"). The "structural wood screws" and "concrete anchors" stay on the structural HOLD above; anchor type, size and embedment are never estimated (risk-triage playbook "do not invent ... anchor load ratings"). The step text above is unchanged. HUMAN REVIEW: structural engineer or building official.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Structural Framing & Layout Verification"

lines: - [ ] **Fire-Blocking & Blocking:** Install solid wood blocking sections behind target zones where heavy items will be mounted later (e.g., TV wall mounts, kitchen cabinets, bathroom vanities).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Structural Framing & Layout Verification"

lines: > FLAG (G-059): the step above is titled "Fire-Blocking & Blocking" but describes only backing for later mounted items; fireblocking is not addressed and is not performed under this step until the building official's requirements are recorded for the job. The step states no load capacity for the items mounted later. The step text above is unchanged. HUMAN REVIEW: building official.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Structural Framing & Layout Verification"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW03-04): no insulation step exists between Phase 1 and Phase 2, although pricing sells the "Insulation Install" add-on and the agreement offers "insulation [ ]". Insulation is not installed under this SOP (section 2, Out of scope); if the owner adds it, a reviewed step, materials, PPE and any required inspection before cover come first. Pending owner decision.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Structural Framing & Layout Verification"

lines: - [ ] **Board Allocation Map:**
- **Standard Zones:** 1/2-inch lightweight drywall sheets.
- **Bathrooms / Wet Kitchens:** Moisture-resistant Greenboard or Purpleboard.
- **Garage Ceilings / Boiler Rooms:** 5/8-inch Fire-Rated Type X sheets.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📦 Phase 2: Technical Panel Selection & Hanging"

lines: > FLAG (spec DW-03.SAF "use correct board/system"): the board types in the step above are a default map, not a specification. The board and system for each area come from the approved plans, the board manufacturer and any listed fire-rated assembly; fire separation for garage ceilings and boiler rooms, and the suitability of moisture-resistant board in wet areas, including behind tile (the main plan's claim, 02 C-DW03-09), are questions for the building official and the board manufacturer (04 DW-03 permit/license flags). If the board on site does not match the approved plans, stop (spec START-011 "any material mismatch"). The step text above is unchanged. HUMAN REVIEW: building official.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📦 Phase 2: Technical Panel Selection & Hanging"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW03-01) - inspection before concealment, before the step below ("Hanging Sequence") and before any board covers framing, plumbing, electrical, HVAC or other work: required inspections signed off with photos before concealment; do not conceal unapproved utility work (spec DW-03.SAF). A failed or incomplete inspection is a critical hold that no role can override (31 section 8.3 rule 2). Which inspections apply, and who arranges them, is recorded for the job by a reviewer (04 DW-03 permit/license flags, OPEN QUESTION). Pending qualified review. (source: 31 section 10 DW-03; spec DW-03.SAF, DW-03.QAC "penetrations/interfaces documented, inspection prerequisites satisfied")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📦 Phase 2: Technical Panel Selection & Hanging"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW03-08) - before the step below and every later step that uses stilts, the panel lift, ladders or team lifting: controls for stilts, the panel lift and team lifting must be approved by a qualified safety professional and in place. None is defined yet, and no height, load or team size is set here; until they exist those steps stay on hold (31 section 8.4 rule 4). Pending qualified review. (source: 31 section 10 DW-03; spec DW-03.HAZ "heavy panels, lifts", "falls"; DW-03.SAF "lifting/team controls"; X-12)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📦 Phase 2: Technical Panel Selection & Hanging"

lines: - [ ] **Hanging Sequence:** Always hang ceiling panels first, then push wall panels tightly up against the ceiling line. Stagger all vertical wall seams—never allow four corners to meet at a single point (prevents settling stress cracks).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📦 Phase 2: Technical Panel Selection & Hanging"

lines: > FLAG (31 section 3.5 rule 5): "(prevents settling stress cracks)" in the step above is a working rationale, not a promise to the customer; no crack-free outcome is offered (section 2, Do not perform item 8). The step text above is unchanged.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📦 Phase 2: Technical Panel Selection & Hanging"

lines: - [ ] **Fastener Pattern:** Drive screws 8 inches apart along all perimeter edges and 12 inches apart along center interior studs. Keep screws at least 3/8 inch away from the edge of the panel. Ensure heads are recessed without piercing the paper face.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📦 Phase 2: Technical Panel Selection & Hanging"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW03-01): UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions. "8 inches apart", "12 inches apart" and "at least 3/8 inch away from the edge" in the step above have no source; fastener type, length and spacing come only from the board manufacturer and, for a fire-rated assembly, the listed assembly (31 section 10 DW-03; spec DW-03.SAF "use correct board/system"). The step text above is unchanged. HUMAN REVIEW: qualified reviewer; building official for fire-rated assemblies.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📦 Phase 2: Technical Panel Selection & Hanging"

lines: - [ ] **First Stage (Bedding):** Fill all tapered factory joints with multi-purpose joint compound. Embed premium paper joint tape directly into the wet mud using a 6-inch knife, squeezing out trapped air and excess compound.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧽 Phase 3: Premium Multi-Stage Taping & Mudding"

lines: - [ ] **Corner Bead Application:** Install metal or heavy composite plastic corner beads on all exposed external wall corners. Fasten with a crimper tool or screws, then apply a heavy coat of mud to blend the bead edge into the wall profile.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧽 Phase 3: Premium Multi-Stage Taping & Mudding"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW03-V02): the bead material differs across files: the step above allows "metal or heavy composite plastic" beads, while the agreement specifies "metal corner beads" only. Use the material on the approved estimate; a substitution that affects specification or customer expectation needs approval (spec JOB-007). The step text above is unchanged. Pending owner decision.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧽 Phase 3: Premium Multi-Stage Taping & Mudding"

lines: - [ ] **Fastener Filling:** Apply a clean single pass of mud over all recessed screw dimples throughout the boards.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧽 Phase 3: Premium Multi-Stage Taping & Mudding"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW03-02) - before the step below ("The Old-to-New Merge"): the tie-in to horsehair plaster or another old finish is held until the build year and the plaster and paint disposition are recorded for the job; in a pre-1978 or unknown-age home, stop and escalate. Release only on a recorded disposition by an EPA RRP-certified renovator or an accredited asbestos inspector accepted by the owner. Pending qualified review. (source: 31 section 10 DW-03; 04 DW-03 prerequisites "plaster disposition recorded before demolition or tie-ins", PROPOSED)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🩹 Phase 4: Blending & Skimming Transitions"

lines: - [ ] **The Old-to-New Merge:** Where new drywall connects to thick old horsehair plaster, use a wide 12-inch or 14-inch knife to feather the mud layer out at least 18 inches into the old wall area to create a gradual, invisible slope.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🩹 Phase 4: Blending & Skimming Transitions"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW03-11): the step above feathers "at least 18 inches", while the agreement commits to "up to 18 inches"; the owner decides one commitment for the agreement, this SOP and the quality check. "invisible" is an outcome word, not a promise to the customer (31 section 3.5 rule 5). The step text above is unchanged. HUMAN REVIEW: owner; attorney (agreement wording).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🩹 Phase 4: Blending & Skimming Transitions"

lines: - [ ] **Second Fill Coat:** Apply a wider coat of topping compound over all joint seams, widening the patch to 8–10 inches.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🩹 Phase 4: Blending & Skimming Transitions"

lines: - [ ] **Third Finish Coat:** Apply an ultra-thin tight coat of lightweight mud to fill micro-pinholes and sand tracks.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🩹 Phase 4: Blending & Skimming Transitions"

lines: - [ ] **Edge Sanding:** Sand all joints using a fine 180-grit sponge, taking extreme care not to scuff or fray the raw paper facing of the drywall sheets.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Final Sanding & Inspection Protocol"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW03-15): the agreement's final draw falls due on "final mechanical sanding", while the step above sands by hand with a sponge; the sanding method is not changed here, and the payment trigger is for the owner and the attorney. Dust controls for sanding are pending qualified safety review (sections 6, 9 and 11). The step text above is unchanged.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Final Sanding & Inspection Protocol"

lines: - [ ] **The Light Test:** Place a commercial halogen work light close to the wall angle. Meticulously inspect every junction for trowel marks, craters, or uneven ridges. Spot-apply compound to corrections.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Final Sanding & Inspection Protocol"

lines: - [ ] **Site Cleanup:** Vacuum up all fine sanding debris, damp-wipe window frames, and sweep clean before painter turnover.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Final Sanding & Inspection Protocol"

lines: A worker cannot mark the job complete without answering these checks or recording an exception (source: spec QA-001). Photos cannot prove hidden conditions: do not infer hidden fasteners, structural adequacy or hazardous-material clearance from an image (source: quality-assistant playbook).
| Check (spec DW-03.QAC) | How it is verified (pending review) | Evidence | Inspector |

| Walls/ceilings straight within project tolerance | Against the tolerance recorded on the approved plans or estimate; no DW-03 file states a tolerance value (04 DW-03 quality checklist, GAP). The "Plumb Line Layout" and "The Light Test" steps support the check | Layout and light-test photos per area (04 DW-03 completion evidence, PROPOSED) | Worker self-check; whether a supervisor must inspect is Q-31-15 |

| Correct materials | Board type per area, fasteners, tape, compound and bead material match the approved estimate and plans; substitutions only with approval (spec JOB-007; C-DW03-V02) | Material record against the estimate (spec BRF-010 "loaded/verified status") | Worker |

| Fastener/tape/finish quality | "The Light Test" step: trowel marks, craters or ridges corrected; finish level per the approved estimate, with finish-level criteria pending (X-26) | After photos per area (spec QA-003) | Worker; a supervisor where required (Q-31-15) |

| Penetrations/interfaces documented | Every penetration and utility interface photographed before concealment | Pre-concealment photos mapped to areas (04 DW-03 completion evidence, PROPOSED) | Worker |

| Inspection prerequisites satisfied | Inspection sign-off recorded before the "Hanging Sequence" step (HOLD C-DW03-01) | Inspection record with photos | The reviewer named in the hold; the customer walkthrough is not an inspection (spec QA-004) |
| Tie-in feathering (agreement and SOP) | Feathering at tie-ins per the one commitment the owner decides (C-DW03-11) | Tie-in photos before and after (spec BRF-012, QA-003) | Worker |
- Remove protection and containment; clean the area; remove waste; account for tools and materials; restore utilities or components altered within scope (source: spec APXA-005; QA-002).

- The original "Site Cleanup" step (section 12) vacuums sanding debris, damp-wipes window frames and sweeps; the vacuum's dust class and the cleanup method are pending qualified safety review (source: original step; 29 section 5.2 kit `dust-control`).
- Cleanup photos may be required for dusty work (source: spec QA-002); see section 16.
- Evidence: photo
- Trade cleanup stays inside the DW-03 job; post-construction cleaning (CL-04) covers detail and final cleaning of areas released by all trades (source: 02 section 5.2, PROPOSED boundary).
TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.
- Waste from the steps: board offcuts, empty compound containers, used tape, sanding dust and debris, used protection (source: original steps; spec QA-002 "debris/waste handling").
- Demolition debris: no demolition under this SOP; the pricing file's "packing out debris to dump trailers" has no reviewed disposal method (C-DW03-02).
- Containers, destination and who pays: an owner decision with the local rules of the actual municipality (source: 31 section 3.1, waste row; 29 section 8.2 control 10; Q-29-10).
- Suspect hazardous material is not bagged, moved or removed (source: section 2, Do not perform; spec START-011).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: arrival and existing-condition photos, including every wall or ceiling the new work ties into; start is blocked until they are captured or an authorized reason is recorded (source: spec START-008, BRF-012).
- Evidence: photo, note

- During: before concealment, photos of framing, blocking, penetrations and utility interfaces and of the inspection record (source: spec DW-03.QAC "penetrations/interfaces documented, inspection prerequisites satisfied"; 04 DW-03 completion evidence, PROPOSED); concealed conditions with photos and severity (source: spec APXA-004; JOB-004).
- Evidence: photo, note
- After: photos mapped to work areas or tasks (source: spec QA-003): finished walls and ceilings, tie-ins, corner beads and cleanup (source: 04 DW-03 completion evidence, PROPOSED; spec QA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- Privacy: internal-only by default; avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).

- Arrival and completion updates use approved templates; a blocked job uses only the approved "work blocked" message, with no incident details or access codes by text or email (source: spec NTF-007, COM-002).

- Waiting for plans, a permit determination, an inspection or a hazardous-material disposition is explained only in approved wording; the worker does not decide or tell the customer whether a permit applies (section 3; 04 DW-03 permit/license flags).

- Concealed damage, moisture, suspect materials or utility conflicts found when walls are opened: stop and escalate first (section 19); the customer is then told in approved wording, and any added work needs a change order (source: spec JOB-004, JOB-005, FIN-008).
- Walkthrough: record the outcome as accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Care notes come only from approved product data (source: spec QA-008; quality-assistant playbook "Prepare handoff instructions from approved product data").
- Do not promise flatness, crack-free joints, mold prevention, code compliance or a warranty (source: section 2, Do not perform item 8; C-DW03-09).
- Explain the invoice and payment next step without unauthorized promises; the agreement's draw schedule is under owner and attorney review (source: spec APXA-006; C-DW03-06).
Done means all of the following, recorded in the job (source: spec QA-001 to QA-004; DW-03.QAC; APXA-005 to APXA-007):
- Every section 13 check answered, or an exception recorded (QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- Inspection prerequisites satisfied and pre-concealment photos recorded (DW-03.QAC).
- Evidence: note
- After photos mapped to areas or tasks (QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Protection and containment removed and cleanup done (QA-002; APXA-005).
- Tools and materials accounted for; rentals returned (APXA-005, APXA-007).
- Walkthrough outcome recorded, with punch items (QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Unresolved issues, incidents and change requests submitted before the job is closed (APXA-007).
- Each progress invoice is tied to a verified milestone; the agreement's draw triggers are under review (source: 04 DW-03 completion evidence, PROPOSED; spec FIN-003, QA-006; C-DW03-15).
- Final completion is a human sign-off; the quality review only recommends readiness (source: quality-assistant playbook "Recommend readiness for human sign-off; do not set final completion").
- Evidence: note
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:
Service-specific stop triggers and holds (all pending qualified review; release roles per 31 section 8.3):

- Card guidance, verbatim: "verify approved plans/permit dependencies; do not conceal unapproved utility work; use correct board/system; lifting/team controls; inspections before concealment where required" (source: spec DW-03.SAF).

- HOLD C-DW03-01, preconditions before Phase 1: approved plans and scope on file; permit determination recorded by a reviewer, not assumed; headers, load-bearing and addition framing on hold for a structural engineer or building official; plumbing, electrical and HVAC relocations by licensed trades only. A structural concern and unapproved electrical, plumbing, gas or HVAC scope are critical holds that no role can override (31 section 8.3).
- Evidence: note

- HOLD C-DW03-01, inspection before concealment, before "Hanging Sequence": required inspections signed off with photos before any board covers framing, utilities or other work; a failed or incomplete inspection is a critical hold (31 section 8.3 rule 2).

- HOLD C-DW03-02, old-property screening, before Phase 1 and before "The Old-to-New Merge": pre-1978 or unknown-age painted surfaces, suspect materials, horsehair plaster and demolition are not disturbed; release only on a recorded disposition by a qualified person accepted by the owner (31 sections 8.3 and 10).
- Evidence: note

- HOLD X-12, access before Phase 1, and HOLD C-DW03-08, stilts, panel lift and team lifting before "Hanging Sequence": these stay on hold until a qualified safety professional approves the controls; a hold caused by a missing policy cannot be released by override (31 section 8.4 rule 4).
- Suspected mold growth or an active leak: stop; treated as critical until the company mold definition exists (31 section 8.4 rule 2; Q-31-10; X-06).

- Board or system on site that does not match the approved plans, including fire-rated or moisture-resistant assemblies: stop and escalate (spec DW-03.SAF "use correct board/system"; START-011 "any material mismatch").
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
Service roles for DW-03 (contacts and escalation order are owner decisions, Q-31-05):
- Headers, load-bearing walls, additions or any structural doubt: structural engineer or building official (C-DW03-01).
- Permit determinations and inspections before concealment: the reviewer named for the job, with the local building department (C-DW03-01).
- Utilities in the work area or needing relocation: licensed electrician, plumber or HVAC professional (C-DW03-01; X-07).
- Old painted surfaces, horsehair plaster, suspect materials or demolition: EPA RRP-certified renovator; accredited asbestos inspector (C-DW03-02).
- Mold or moisture: qualified mold assessor or industrial hygienist (X-06; Q-31-10).
- Stilts, panel lift, ladders, team lifting, dust and generator use: qualified safety professional (C-DW03-08; C-DW03-V01).
- Scope, price and draw questions: owner (C-DW03-05, C-DW03-06).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].

- For this service, report at least a fall from stilts or a ladder, a dropped panel or a lift failure, a cut or power-tool injury, dust or suspected hazardous-material exposure, and damage to a concealed utility (source: spec JOB-008; DW-03.HAZ "heavy panels, lifts, dust, falls", "electrical/plumbing/HVAC interfaces").

- **Q-31-07** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: EPA RRP-certified renovator, accredited asbestos inspector): which property-age thresholds trigger lead and asbestos screening for tie-ins, cuts into existing finishes and demolition, and does HandyHub hold or plan EPA RRP certification?

- **04 DW-03 card, active/inactive status** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: structural engineer or building official, attorney): does DW-03 include load-bearing walls, headers and true additions, or only non-structural partitions and drywall? Who determines and obtains permits, and who verifies inspections before concealment?

- **Q-31-09** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional): height and access policy: are stilts and the panel lift allowed, with what training and qualification tags, and which ladders are used for ceiling work?

- **Q-31-01** (owner): who are the competent reviewers for this SOP (qualified safety professional, structural engineer or building official, licensed trades, accredited asbestos inspector, EPA RRP-certified renovator), and how is their competence evidenced?
- **Q-31-18** (qualified safety professional; owner): which of this SOP's holds are critical holds under the 31 section 8.4 rule?
- **Q-31-05** (owner): emergency and escalation contacts and escalation order for a two-person team.
- **Q-31-10** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified mold assessor): company definition of mold growth and the stop rule for walls opened in a remodel.
- **Q-31-11** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional): emergency kit contents and the SDS register owner.
- **Q-31-15** (owner): do the inspection-prerequisite and tolerance checks need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check?
- **Q-31-02** (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish version?
- **02 C-DW03-04** (owner): is insulation in DW-03 scope? If it is, a reviewed step, materials, PPE and any required inspection before cover come first.
- **02 C-DW03-03** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional, attorney): which containment standard applies to sanding and demolition dust?
- **02 C-DW03-11** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: attorney): feathering at tie-ins: "up to" or "at least" the stated width?
- **02 C-DW03-V02** (owner): which corner-bead materials are offered, and how is the choice recorded on the estimate?

sops.title: SOP DW-04: High-Volume Residential New Construction

lines: - The customer is the general contractor or developer. For every job, confirm that access, hazards and work-area conditions are still current (source: spec CX-005; 04 DW-04 customer preparation requirements).

- Contractor preparation named in the draft agreement and pricing (unapproved text; HUMAN REVIEW: attorney): an enclosed structure with active, safe heating ("Drying Temperature Clause"); rough-in inspections passed and signed off before hanging ("Pre-requisite Trades Sign-off"); production areas free of delivery, framing and other trades' obstructions ("Standby Crew Fee"); a complete board count where the contractor supplies board (pricing "GC Material Discrepancy Surcharge") (source: the clauses as quoted; 04 DW-04 customer preparation requirements).
- Evidence: note
- Delivery staging locations agreed with the general contractor before delivery (source: spec DW-04.INT "delivery staging"; original "Load Calculation" step).
- A site contact, site access and the site's emergency arrangements are recorded (source: spec BRF-002, BRF-013; 02 G-060, GAP).
- Evidence: note

- Other trades, site visitors and anyone else on site are kept out of active work areas such as lift operation, cutting and sanding; the coordination method with the general contractor is TBD (source: X-11; 02 G-060).
- No site-readiness checklist or evidence capture for these items exists yet (GAP) (source: 04 DW-04 customer preparation requirements; spec START-007).

- Service status: DW-04 is not bookable until the HND-004 approvals and the owner's go/no-go on builder subcontract work (general contractor terms, capacity with two employees, insurance documentation, scaffold and stilt policy, fire- and sound-assembly verification) (source: 04 DW-04 active/inactive status; spec HND-004; owner facts 2026-10-02).
- Intake complete from the builder: builder plans, unit/room schedule, board types/thicknesses, fire/sound assemblies, delivery staging, inspections, finish level (source: spec DW-04.INT).

- An accepted estimate version and an attorney-approved agreement version for the project; the current agreement file is a draft template, not for signature (source: spec CX-003; 30 D-30-14, PROPOSED; agreement status callout).

- HOLD (DW-04.SAF; critical): every inspection required before cover is recorded as passed, with evidence, for each area before any board covers a cavity (section 12, after "Inspection Check") (source: spec DW-04.SAF "coordinate inspections; ... do not cover incomplete/failed inspections"; START-010; 31 section 8.3 rule 2).
- Evidence: note

- HOLD (C-DW04-02): the assembly schedule from the builder plans is verified before hanging (section 12, before the Phase 2 steps) (source: spec DW-04.SAF "verify assembly specifications"; 31 section 10).

- The "Climate Verification" precondition in section 12 (sealed envelope; the stated internal temperature held for the stated period before mud application) is met and recorded before any mud work; it is not relaxed by the pricing file's winter surcharge (C-DW04-04). The method and record of the temperature evidence are PROPOSED for owner and quality review; no threshold beyond the original step is set here (source: original SOP Phase 1; 02 C-DW04-04; spec START-007).
- Evidence: note

- Site readiness confirmed at the pre-start site check against what the draft agreement asks of the general contractor: an enclosed and heated structure, rough-in inspections passed and signed off, production areas free of delivery, framing and other trades' obstructions, and a complete board delivery where the contractor supplies board (source: agreement "Pre-requisite Trades Sign-off", "Drying Temperature Clause", "Standby Crew Fee"; pricing "GC Material Discrepancy Surcharge"; spec START-007). A contractor's commitment never replaces HandyHub's own checks (source: 30 section 4.1 row 5).
- Evidence: note

- HOLD (C-DW04-01): no scaffold, stilt or other elevated work position until an approved height and access policy exists; panel lifts only with an equipment qualification and a pre-use inspection (section 12). Until the policy is approved, this hold cannot be released by override (source: spec DW-04.TLS, DW-04.SAF; 02 G-005; 31 section 8.4 rule 4).

- Critical tools and materials loaded and matched to the job. Several items the steps use are not yet in the inventory and are proposed there: panel lifts, collated screw strips, paper tape, joint compound, long-reach sanders, Class M extractors, pole sanders and the LED scanning bar (source: spec START-005, START-006; C-DW04-08).
- Builder-supplied board: count, type and visible condition recorded before hanging (source: spec START-009; 29 section 9.1).
- Evidence: note
- Equipment qualification tags recorded for scheduling and checked before start (source: spec SCH-003, START-010; DW-04.SAF "equipment qualification").
- Evidence: note

- Site safety arrangements with the general contractor (site orientation, emergency arrangements, coordination with other trades) recorded before work: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve. (source: 02 G-060 "no multi-employer site-safety coordination with the GC")
- Evidence: note

- Weather and site conditions suitable at start; thresholds are set by the qualified safety professional, none here; if unsuitable, record No Start / Blocked (source: spec START-011 "severe weather", SCH-008; X-27).
- Evidence: note

- Appendix A checks before leaving and before starting: correct job and address, latest changes, scope and exclusions, hazards, critical tools and materials loaded, customer-supplied items, approvals confirmed; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-001, APXA-003).
- Evidence: note

- On arrival: confirm the address, unit or lot, work area and site contact; park and access as the site allows; identify other trades and anyone else on site; inspect the site against the briefing (source: spec APXA-002).
- Site orientation and emergency arrangements with the general contractor before work: TBD (source: 02 G-060).
- Confirm the delivery staging locations agreed with the general contractor (source: spec DW-04.INT "delivery staging"; original "Load Calculation" step).

- Existing-condition photos before work, including windows, glass and finished surfaces next to the work areas, because the agreement's glass clause relies on documented pre-existing scratches (source: spec START-008, APXA-002; X-02).
- Evidence: photo, note
- Inspection evidence for each area checked before hanging (section 12 hold) (source: spec START-010).
- Envelope and temperature checked and recorded before mud work (section 12 hold) (source: original "Climate Verification" step; C-DW04-04).
- Evidence: note
- Pre-use inspection of panel lifts and powered equipment per the manufacturer's instructions (section 12 hold) (source: spec DW-04.SAF "equipment qualification").
- Dust extraction connected to the sanders before Phase 4 starts, as "Power Sander Deployment" requires (source: original Phase 4).
- Protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).
- Work areas kept clear of anyone who is not part of the crew (source: X-11).

All original procedure lines appear below verbatim and in their original order; the five original phase headings are demoted one level. Added lines start with `HOLD` or `FLAG` inside a quote block and are pending qualified review.

> HOLD (C-DW04-01): applies to every step below. No step is performed from a scaffold, on stilts or from any other elevated work position unless an approved height and access policy allows it. None exists yet (02 G-005; Q-31-09), so this hold cannot be released by override (31 section 8.4 rule 4). If a step cannot be done without working at height, stop and escalate (section 19). Pending qualified review. (source: spec DW-04.TLS "scaffolds/stilts only under approved policy"; DW-04.HAZ "falls, scaffold/stilt risk"; 31 section 10)
- [ ] **Load Calculation:** Coordinate with suppliers to deliver pre-calculated sheet counts directly into designated rooms via crane/boom truck, eliminating manual hauling times.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Bulk Material Logistics & Staging"

lines: > HOLD (DW-04.SAF "safe staging/handling"): during the delivery in the step above, HandyHub workers stay clear of the supplier's crane or boom-truck lifting operation, which the supplier controls (RISK). Staging locations, stack placement in rooms and the way sheets are moved follow controls set by the qualified safety professional with the general contractor; no load, distance or stack height is set here. Stop and escalate if a delivery, a stack or a lift is unsafe. Pending qualified review. (source: spec DW-04.HAZ "material handling"; DW-04.SAF "safe staging/handling"; 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Bulk Material Logistics & Staging"

lines: - [ ] **Climate Verification:** Ensure the building envelope is fully sealed (windows and doors installed). Internal building temperature must be maintained above 50°F (10°C) for 48 hours prior to mud application to prevent freeze-cracking.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Bulk Material Logistics & Staging"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW04-04): the precondition in the step above stays in force as written and is not relaxed by pricing: the pricing file's "Winter Heat Surcharge" for sites without temporary heat is never a reason to apply mud where the step above is not met. If the envelope is not sealed, or the temperature condition is not met or cannot be shown, do not start mud work; record No Start / Blocked for that work and escalate (section 19). Record the temperature evidence before mud application (PROPOSED; the measurement method and the record are set by the owner and the quality reviewer, and no new threshold or device is set here). The draft agreement also asks the contractor to keep the heat through the sanding phase; whether this SOP adopts that is a reviewer decision. Pending qualified review. (source: spec START-007, SCH-008; 02 C-DW04-04; 31 section 10; agreement "Drying Temperature Clause")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Bulk Material Logistics & Staging"

lines: - [ ] **Inspection Check:** Verify that electrical, plumbing, and HVAC rough-ins have passed municipal building code inspections before covering any wall frame cavity.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Bulk Material Logistics & Staging"

lines: > HOLD (DW-04.SAF; critical): do not cover incomplete or failed inspections. Before the hanging steps of Phase 2 below, every inspection required before cover for the area is recorded as passed, with evidence: the electrical, plumbing and HVAC rough-ins named in the step above and any other pre-cover inspection that the builder's schedule or the local authority requires (no list is concluded here; HUMAN REVIEW: building official). If an inspection is incomplete or failed, or its evidence is missing, do not hang board over that area; record No Start / Blocked for it and escalate (section 19). This is a critical hold: no role can override it, and it clears only on recorded evidence that the inspection passed (31 section 8.3 rule 2). The contractor's sign-off commitment in the draft agreement ("Pre-requisite Trades Sign-off") does not replace this check. Pending qualified review. (source: spec DW-04.SAF "coordinate inspections; ... do not cover incomplete/failed inspections"; DW-04.INT "inspections"; START-010; 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Bulk Material Logistics & Staging"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW04-02): before "Adhesive Layering" and every hanging step below: verify the assembly schedule from the builder plans for each unit or room before hanging: board types and thicknesses, fire- and sound-rated assemblies, and the fastening that the listed assembly and the board manufacturer require. If the plans or the schedule are missing, or the specified board or assembly does not match the site, do not hang; stop and escalate (section 19). Pending qualified review. HUMAN REVIEW: building official; manufacturer listed-assembly documentation. (source: spec DW-04.INT "builder plans, unit/room schedule, board types/thicknesses, fire/sound assemblies"; DW-04.SAF "verify assembly specifications"; 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔨 Phase 2: Rapid Production Hanging Line"

lines: - [ ] **Adhesive Layering:** Apply structural drywall adhesive beads in continuous zig-zag patterns along all center wood/metal framing studs right before hanging (reduces required screw counts by 30% and prevents future nail pops).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔨 Phase 2: Rapid Production Hanging Line"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW04-02): UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions. The screw-count reduction in the step above ("reduces required screw counts by 30%") has no source. Fastener type, spacing and count follow the board manufacturer's instructions and the listed fire- or sound-rated assembly in the builder plans, never this figure, and adhesive is used only where those allow it. "prevents future nail pops" is an outcome claim and is not repeated to the general contractor or anyone else. The step text above is unchanged. HUMAN REVIEW: building official; manufacturer listed-assembly documentation; design professional.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔨 Phase 2: Rapid Production Hanging Line"

lines: > HOLD (C-DW04-01): before "Panel Lifter System" below: mechanical panel lifts are operated only by a worker who holds the equipment qualification the owner sets, after a pre-use inspection per the manufacturer's instructions; both are pending review. Using the lifts for high ceilings is part of the pending height and access review, and handling the heavy sheets follows the qualified safety professional's controls. If any of these is missing, do not use the lift; stop and escalate (section 19). Pending qualified review. (source: spec DW-04.TLS "panel lifts/carts"; DW-04.SAF "equipment qualification"; DW-04.HAZ "material handling, falls"; 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔨 Phase 2: Rapid Production Hanging Line"

lines: - [ ] **Panel Lifter System:** Utilize mechanical panel lifts (drywall jacks) to hold heavy 12-foot or 14-foot sheets flat against high ceilings, maximizing installation speed.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔨 Phase 2: Rapid Production Hanging Line"

lines: - [ ] **Fastener Automation:** Use automated auto-feed drywall screw guns with collated screw strips to fasten boards at high velocity, ensuring consistent recess depths.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🔨 Phase 2: Rapid Production Hanging Line"

lines: - [ ] **The Bazooka Run:** Utilize an automatic mechanical taper (Bazooka) to simultaneously feed, coat, and apply paper tape over all flat and internal corner joints in a single rapid pass.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧽 Phase 3: Automated Mechanical Taping & Boxing"

lines: - [ ] **Mechanical Boxing Lines:** Run a 7-inch mechanical flat box to apply the first bed coat over joints, followed immediately by mechanical corner finishers (flushers) for internal lines.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧽 Phase 3: Automated Mechanical Taping & Boxing"

lines: - [ ] **The Secondary Box Pass:** After 12 hours of drying, run a 10-inch or 12-inch mechanical flat box to distribute the secondary feathering coat over all seams at production speed.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧽 Phase 3: Automated Mechanical Taping & Boxing"

lines: > FLAG (04 DW-04 "SOP reference" row): UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions. "After 12 hours of drying" in the step above has no source; drying time depends on the compound and on site temperature and humidity, and comes from the compound manufacturer's instructions. The stated wait is never shortened on site and stays in force as written until a qualified reviewer replaces it; if the coat is not dry, the next pass waits. The step text above is unchanged. (source: 31 section 3.5 rule 3)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧽 Phase 3: Automated Mechanical Taping & Boxing"

lines: - [ ] **Power Sander Deployment:** Equip crew members with long-reach rotary drywall sanders (e.g., Festool Planex or Mirka Leros) linked directly to industrial M-class HEPA dust extractors.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 4: Industrial Mechanical Sanding"

lines: - [ ] **Unified Grit Sequence:** Sand all production walls uniformly using 150-grit mesh discs, moving fluidly down rows without pausing to prevent circular groove marks.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 4: Industrial Mechanical Sanding"

lines: - [ ] **Bead Buffing:** Use manual pole sanders to sand metal corner beads, exposing the clean metal edge line cleanly for sharp lines.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌬️ Phase 4: Industrial Mechanical Sanding"

lines: - [ ] **Flashing Verification:** Inspect all walls using a 10,000-lumen LED scanning bar held parallel to the wall to catch "joint flashing" (shadow differences between paper and mud).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Commercial QA Audit & Sign-Off"

lines: - [ ] **Punch-List Resolution:** Form a rapid-response team of 2 finishers to circle the building, resolving minor imperfections marked by inspectors within 2 hours.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Commercial QA Audit & Sign-Off"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW04-05): capacity unverified - owner decision. The step above forms "a rapid-response team of 2 finishers" and sets a response "within 2 hours". HandyHub starts with two employees (owner facts 2026-10-02), so a separate team is not available, and the response time is a service-level commitment the owner has not approved; it is not stated to the general contractor or anyone else. Punch items are recorded with owner, due date and completion evidence (spec QA-005). The step text above is unchanged. HUMAN REVIEW: owner.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Commercial QA Audit & Sign-Off"

lines: - [ ] **Turnover Protocol:** Issue an official, clean, paint-ready handover certificate to the general contractor to release milestone payment draws.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Commercial QA Audit & Sign-Off"

lines: > FLAG (C-DW04-12): certification and payment wording - owner and attorney review. "Issue an official, clean, paint-ready handover certificate" in the step above implies a certification authority that no file establishes, and tying it "to release milestone payment draws" makes it a payment document under the draft agreement. Its name, wording and effect are decided by the owner and the attorney before this SOP is activated; until then the handover is recorded as the walkthrough outcome and the completion evidence (spec QA-004, QA-006). The step text above is unchanged. HUMAN REVIEW: attorney licensed in KY/IN; owner.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Commercial QA Audit & Sign-Off"

lines: > FLAG (31 section 10; 02 G-060; C-DW04-01): no step in this SOP installs corner bead, cuts openings for electrical boxes or lights with the router, or works from scaffolds or stilts, although the spec card, the inventory or the main plan names them. items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Commercial QA Audit & Sign-Off"

lines: > Spec card DW-04.QAC (verbatim): "correct board/assembly placement, fastening/finish quality, corners/openings, production checklist, punch under lighting, clean handoff"
- Correct board and assembly placement against the verified assembly schedule from the builder plans (source: spec DW-04.QAC "correct board/assembly placement"; C-DW04-02).

- Fastening per the board manufacturer and the listed assembly, not the unsourced screw-count reduction (section 12 flag); finish quality to the finish level stated in the approved scope (source: spec DW-04.QAC "fastening/finish quality"; DW-04.INT "finish level"). A shared definition of finish levels does not exist yet (source: 04 DW-04 quality checklist row, GAP).
- Corners and openings checked (source: spec DW-04.QAC "corners/openings"; original "Bead Buffing" step).

- A production checklist per unit or room, recorded as the work proceeds; its format is TBD by the owner and the quality reviewer (source: spec DW-04.QAC "production checklist"; 04 DW-04 completion evidence, PROPOSED).
- Evidence: note

- Punch under lighting: the "Flashing Verification" step under the scanning bar; punch items recorded with owner, due date and completion evidence (source: spec DW-04.QAC "punch under lighting"; QA-005).
- Evidence: note
- Clean handoff: cleanup complete (section 14) and a handover note, including that glass was not cleaned where that applies (source: spec DW-04.QAC "clean handoff"; 04 DW-04 exclusions, PROPOSED).

- Each check is answered, or an exception recorded, before completion (source: spec QA-001). Whether a supervisor, not only the worker, inspects any check is an owner decision (Q-31-15); a worker's self-check does not replace a required supervisor inspection (source: quality-assistant playbook).
- Evidence: note
- Remove debris, offcuts and protection, and leave a clean handoff for the next trade (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005; DW-04.QAC "clean handoff").
- Account for tools and materials; return unused materials, and record what happens to leftover builder-supplied board (source: spec APXA-005, APXA-007; 29 section 9.1).
- Evidence: note
- Restore anything altered within scope (source: spec APXA-005).

- Waste streams from the steps: board offcuts, empty compound containers, tape and packaging, sanding dust collected by the extractors, and adhesive tubes (source: original Phases 2 to 4; inventory file).

- Destination, containers and who removes the waste on a builder site, for example whether the general contractor's site containers may be used: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve. (source: spec QA-002 "debris/waste handling"; 02 G-060, G-078; Q-29-10)
- Adhesive tubes and compound residue: handling per the product SDS (source: 29 section 8.2 row 10).
- Hazardous waste is not handled without an approved policy (source: 31 section 3.1, section 15 minimum content).
- Whether disposal is charged is an owner pricing decision (source: 28 Q-28-15).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: each unit or room as found, including windows, glass and finished surfaces next to the work area, and the staged board, with the START-009 record where the contractor supplied it (source: spec START-008, START-009, APXA-002; X-02).
- Evidence: note

- During: inspection evidence for each area before it is covered; the temperature evidence before mud work (PROPOSED, C-DW04-04); any concealed condition, damage or site difference found (source: spec START-010, JOB-004; 04 DW-04 completion evidence, PROPOSED).
- After: each unit or room after the final pass and after punch work, mapped to the unit or room (source: spec QA-003; 04 DW-04 completion evidence "photos per unit/room (QA-003)").
- Evidence: photo

- Photos are internal by default; marketing use needs separate consent; avoid people, documents and other trades' property not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002, REC-003; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- The customer is the general contractor or developer; arrival and completion updates use approved templates only (source: 31 section 3.1, section 17 minimum content; spec NTF-007, UXE-008).
- Walkthrough outcome recorded with the contractor's representative: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- Care or cure notes come only from approved product data (source: spec QA-008).

- Do not promise speed, results, finish quality, a punch response time or code compliance, and do not repeat unapproved main-plan claims such as "flawless, paint-ready accuracy" or "a perfect wall template" (C-DW04-12, C-DW04-05) (source: section 2, Do not perform entry 8; 04 DW-04 customer-facing description).
- Do not issue any certificate or sign-off document beyond the wording the owner and the attorney approve (section 12 flag; C-DW04-12).
- Evidence: note
- Report delays and blocked work in the app with evidence; tell the contractor only what the approved "work blocked" message says (source: spec JOB-004, SCH-008, NTF-007).
- Evidence: note
- Explain the invoice and payment next step without making unauthorized promises (source: spec APXA-006).
- Every section 13 check answered, or an exception recorded (source: spec QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- Production checklist complete for each unit or room (source: spec DW-04.QAC "production checklist").
- Inspection evidence recorded for every covered area (source: spec START-010; DW-04.SAF).
- Evidence: note
- After photos mapped to each unit or room (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup and waste handling complete; tools and materials accounted for (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005).
- Walkthrough outcome and punch items recorded with owner, due date and evidence (source: spec QA-004, QA-005, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- No hold or stop-work item left unresolved (source: 31 section 8.3).

- An invoice for a unit block follows verified completion of that block (source: agreement "Invoices will be submitted upon completion of individual unit blocks"; spec FIN-003, QA-006; 04 DW-04 completion evidence, PROPOSED).
- Unresolved issues, incidents and change follow-ups submitted; the job closes only when the required operational and financial steps are complete (source: spec APXA-007).
This SOP words its general stop-work rule differently from [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]; its own text, verbatim:
> **Stop-work rule (all HandyHub services).** You have the right to stop work. For any condition below, stop the affected work and escalate before continuing (source: spec START-011, JOB-004):
> - an unsafe condition for you, the customer, occupants, pets or the public;
> - concealed damage, substrate failure, moisture or an active leak;
> - suspect hazardous material, such as possible asbestos, lead paint or mold; do not disturb it;
> - electrical, plumbing, gas, HVAC or structural work that is not in the approved scope or needs a licensed trade;
> - an aggressive occupant or animal;
> - severe weather or unsafe heat or cold (source: spec BRF-008);
> - any material mismatch between the site and the briefing, approved scope, materials, access or approvals.

> Do not continue through an unsafe or restricted condition to keep the schedule (source: master section 12). A customer request, a checkbox or a signature does not clear a safety hold (source: owner facts 2026-10-02; risk-triage playbook L27). In an emergency, move people away and call emergency services first (source: spec BRF-013; risk-triage playbook L7). Then use Stop Work / Report Hazard in the app (source: spec UXE-004) and follow section 19.
> Spec card DW-04.SAF (verbatim): "coordinate inspections; verify assembly specifications; safe staging/handling; equipment qualification; do not cover incomplete/failed inspections"
Service holds and stop triggers (pending qualified review):
- HOLD (DW-04.SAF; critical): do not cover incomplete or failed inspections; no override; it clears only on recorded evidence that the inspection passed (sections 3 and 12).
- Evidence: note
- HOLD (C-DW04-02): the assembly specifications from the builder plans are verified before hanging; stop if the plans, the schedule or the board do not match the site (section 12).
- HOLD (C-DW04-01): no scaffold, stilt or elevated work position without an approved height and access policy; panel lifts only with an equipment qualification and a pre-use inspection (section 12).
- HOLD (C-DW04-04): the "Climate Verification" precondition is kept as written and is not relaxed by pricing; if it is not met or cannot be shown, no mud work (section 12).
- Safe staging and handling: stop if a delivery, a stack or a lift is unsafe; stay clear of supplier lifting operations (source: spec DW-04.SAF "safe staging/handling"; 31 section 10).
- Equipment without the required qualification, or that fails its pre-use inspection: do not operate it (source: spec DW-04.SAF "equipment qualification").
- Incomplete framing or utilities found in the work area (source: spec DW-04.HAZ "incomplete framing/utilities").
- An unsafe condition from temporary heating units or from other trades' work (source: agreement "Drying Temperature Clause"; 04 DW-04 hazards; spec START-011).
- Severe weather or unsafe heat or cold (source: spec BRF-008; X-27).
- Anyone who is not part of the crew enters an active lift, cutting or sanding area (source: X-11).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
Service-specific routing (contacts are owner decisions, Q-31-05):

- Inspection incomplete, failed or without evidence: record No Start / Blocked for the affected areas and escalate to the owner, who takes it up with the general contractor; no board is hung there (source: section 12 hold; spec DW-04.SAF, SCH-008).

- Assembly specification missing or not matching the site: to the owner, who obtains the specification through the general contractor; assembly questions go to the building official or the design professional, and no conclusion is drawn here (source: section 12 hold; C-DW04-02).
- Unsafe delivery, staging or lifting by a supplier: stop, stay clear and escalate to the owner and the general contractor's site contact (source: spec DW-04.SAF "safe staging/handling").
- Temperature precondition not met: no mud work; escalate to the owner, who takes it up with the general contractor (source: section 12 hold; C-DW04-04).
- Any request to work from scaffolds, on stilts or at height: to the owner; not performed until the policy exists (source: C-DW04-01; Q-31-09).

- Hazards created by other trades or by temporary heating units: to the general contractor's site contact and the owner; no conclusion about site-safety duties is drawn here (source: 04 DW-04 hazards; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional (multi-employer site)).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].
- **Q-31-09** (owner; qualified safety professional): height and access policy: maximum working heights, equipment types, and who may use lifts, scaffolds and stilts?

- **04 DW-04 card, active/inactive status** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: attorney, insurance broker, qualified safety professional): go or no-go on builder subcontract work at launch, given the general contractor terms, the capacity of two employees, insurance documentation, the scaffold and stilt policy and assembly verification.

- **04 DW-04 card, permit/license flags** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: building official): who verifies fire- and sound-rated assembly specifications and keeps inspection evidence before cover, and which pre-cover inspections apply in each municipality?
- **Q-30-04** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: attorney): which customer types are offered at launch, and does this SOP cover commercial projects at all (C-DW04-09, X-23)?
- **Q-31-01** (owner): who are the competent reviewers (qualified safety professional; building official for assemblies and inspections), and how is their competence evidenced?
- **Q-31-05** (owner): emergency and escalation contacts, including the general contractor's site contact, and after-hours coverage for a two-person team.
- **Q-31-15** (owner): which section 13 checks need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check?
- **Q-31-16** (owner; attorney): who approves replacement wording for the promissory original lines (the punch response time, the handover certificate)?
- **Q-31-18** (qualified safety professional; owner): which DW-04 holds are critical holds under the 31 section 8.4 rule? The inspection hold is critical under 31 section 8.3 rule 2.
- **Q-31-02** (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish version?

sops.title: SOP HI-01: Precision Picture Hanging & Art Installation

lines: - The customer tells HandyHub about known hidden wall utilities and specialized wall substrates, such as historic plaster or soft brick (source: agreement "Substrate Disclaimer" clause). This disclosure does not replace HandyHub's own hidden-service check in section 12 (source: 30 section 4.1 row 5).

- Items and any customer-supplied hardware on site; exact placement decided, or the customer available to approve the layout before drilling (source: spec HI-01.INT; agreement "Final Placement Approval" clause).
- Work area cleared; occupants, children and pets kept away from the work area (source: spec CX-005, BRF-005; X-11).
- Items to protect and existing damage pointed out before work (source: spec BRF-005 "items to protect"; START-008).
- Customer-facing wording of this checklist: TBD - owner, with attorney review where it becomes agreement text (source: 30 section 4.1 row 5).
- Approved estimate version and scope, with exclusions reviewed before leaving (source: spec APXA-001, START-003, CX-003).

- Intake complete for every item (the spec HI-01.INT fields in section 2). A missing weight, substrate, placement or access fact blocks a ready-to-start packet (source: spec HI-01.INT; job-planner playbook "Stop planning a ready-to-start packet if required scope or hazard decisions are missing").
- The substrate is one this SOP covers; otherwise the job is blocked for an on-site assessment (source: spec HI-01.SAF "verify substrate"; C-HI01-05).

- Property age recorded if known. The HI-01 intake has no property-age prompt, and the screening rule for older painted finishes and plaster is an open question (source: spec BRF-003 "approximate age if known"; X-13; Q-31-07).
- Evidence: note
- Hazards, controls, PPE and stop-work conditions acknowledged before start (source: spec START-004, APXA-003).
- Evidence: note

- Critical tools and materials loaded, including the hidden-service detection tool and hardware suited to the substrate; a missing critical item blocks the affected tasks (source: spec APXA-001, START-005, START-006; job-planner playbook "A missing ladder or unverified permit keeps affected tasks blocked").
- Customer-supplied artwork and hardware on site, with condition, model and quantity recorded before installation (source: spec START-009, HI-01.INT).
- Evidence: note
- A second person scheduled when an item needs a two-person lift (source: spec HI-01.SAF; job-planner playbook "Do not treat the two-person team as two independent crews when the job needs both").
- Ladder work only under an approved height/access policy, which does not exist yet; until it does, tasks that need a ladder stay blocked (source: 02 G-005; X-12; 31 section 8.4 rule 4; Q-31-09).

- Permit, licence or qualification flags: applicability for HI-01 is unknown and is not treated as "no permit" (source: spec START-010; risk-triage playbook "unknown applicability must not default to no permit").
- Start only when the job is Ready or an authorized exception is documented; critical holds are never released by override (source: spec APXA-003; 31 section 8.3).
- Evidence: note
- On arrival: confirm the address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants; inspect the actual site against the briefing and record differences (source: spec APXA-002, START-007).
- Evidence: note
- Capture the required existing-condition photos of each wall area and item (source: spec APXA-002, START-008; section 16).
- Evidence: photo
- Protect the floor and wall at each work area (source: spec HI-01.SAF "protect floor/wall"; APXA-002 "protect work area").
- Identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; confirm materials and models; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003).
- Evidence: note

- Stage the layout for the customer's approval before any hole is drilled (GATE in section 12) (source: agreement "Final Placement Approval" clause; spec HI-01.QAC "customer-approved placement"; C-HI01-04).

*Original procedure, verbatim and in original order; the two original "Problem Option" headings are demoted one level. Lines starting with HOLD, GATE or FLAG were added on 2026-10-03 as separate lines next to the affected steps (a hold that must be met first sits before the step it gates). They are pending qualified review and change no original step.*

> HOLD (C-HI01-01): before any hole or fastener goes into the wall in this option (the monkey-hook path of "Weight Audit" and the pilot hole of "Anchor Driving"), check each marked position for hidden electrical, plumbing or other services with the stocked scanner, used per its manufacturer instructions. Whether the stocked scanner detects wiring or pipes is not stated (section 7); where its manufacturer instructions do not cover them, a scan that finds nothing does not clear the risk, which counts as uncertain. If hidden-service risk or the wall condition is uncertain, STOP and escalate (sections 10 and 19). Cleared by: TBD - qualified safety professional. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-01.SAF "stop if hidden-service risk or wall condition is uncertain"; 31 section 10; owner facts 2026-10-02 "Unknown is not safe")

lines: - [ ] **Weight Audit:** Weigh the artwork. If under 10 lbs, execute using heavy-duty monkey hooks. If 10–50 lbs, utilize professional self-drilling zinc toggle anchors.

Hardware capacity for the item weight and this substrate comes from the hardware manufacturer's rating recorded for the job; no rating is added here, and the maximum accepted weight is an open owner question. Cleared by: TBD - qualified safety professional. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-01.SAF "confirm fastener capacity"; 31 section 10)
