- The worker cannot mark the job complete without answering each required check or recording an exception (source: spec QA-001).
- Evidence: note

- Photos alone do not prove hidden fasteners or anchor capacity (source: quality playbook "Do not infer hidden fasteners, structural adequacy, hazardous-material clearance or electrical safety from an image").
- A customer acknowledgement does not clear a safety hold (source: quality playbook "A signed customer form does not clear an unresolved safety hold").
- Evidence: note
- Clean the work area, including drilling dust and debris (source: spec QA-002; HI-01.HAZ "drilling dust").
- Remove floor and wall protection (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005).
- Account for tools and materials; return unused materials (source: spec APXA-005, APXA-007).
- Cleanup photos where required (source: spec QA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

- Known streams for that review: drilling dust and debris (spec HI-01.HAZ); packaging, leftover parts and the customer's old hardware, whose disposition is recorded (29 section 9.1 step 5); any lead-containing hardware waste if lead sleeves are used (31 section 10). No waste destination is defined (source: 31 section 3.1 row 15; 02 G-078).
- Evidence: note

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: arrival and existing-condition photos of each wall area and item, including visible damage, where the service is configured to require them; start is blocked until they are captured or an authorized reason is recorded (source: spec START-008, APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo, note
- During: the approved layout before the first hole (GATE in section 12); any concealed condition, with severity (source: 02 C-HI01-04; spec JOB-004).
- After: a photo per item or wall, mapped to its work area (source: spec QA-003); cleanup photos where required (source: spec QA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- Photos are internal by default; avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- Confirm the placement with the customer before drilling and record the approval (source: spec HI-01.QAC; agreement "Final Placement Approval" clause).
- Evidence: note
- At the walkthrough, record the outcome: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- Explain the invoice and payment next step without making unauthorized promises (source: spec APXA-006).
- If work is blocked, use only the approved "work blocked" message (source: spec NTF-007; 31 section 8.5).

- Do not promise load capacity, perfect alignment or that an item will never move, and do not discuss fault with the customer; refer such questions to the owner (source: 31 section 3.3 entry 8 and section 8.5; C-HI01-02, C-HI01-V01).
- Care notes only from approved product data (source: spec QA-008; quality playbook).
- Every required check in section 13 answered or an exception recorded (source: spec QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- After photos captured and mapped to work areas (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup done, protection removed, tools and materials accounted for (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005).
- Punch items and the walkthrough outcome recorded (source: spec QA-004, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- No HOLD in section 12 left open; unresolved issues, incidents and change follow-ups submitted (source: 31 section 8.3; spec APXA-007).
- Close only when the required operational and financial steps are complete (source: spec APXA-007).
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:

Service-specific stop triggers (source: spec HI-01.SAF "verify substrate; confirm fastener capacity; two-person lift when required; protect floor/wall; stop if hidden-service risk or wall condition is uncertain"):
- Hidden-service risk or the wall condition is uncertain: stop (source: spec HI-01.SAF; C-HI01-01).
- The substrate cannot be verified or is not one this SOP covers: stop and request an on-site assessment (source: spec HI-01.SAF "verify substrate"; C-HI01-05).

- Fastener capacity cannot be confirmed from the hardware manufacturer's rating for the item weight and substrate, or the item is heavier than the SOP's own bands: stop and escalate (source: spec HI-01.SAF "confirm fastener capacity"; C-HI01-02).
- A two-person lift is required and the second person is not available: stop the lift (source: spec HI-01.SAF).
- Floor and wall cannot be protected: do not start the affected task (source: spec HI-01.SAF "protect floor/wall").
- Fireplace-mantel install without the on-site assessment of heat and gas-appliance proximity: do not start (source: 31 section 10).
- A ladder is needed and no approved height/access policy exists: the task stays blocked (source: 31 section 3.3 entry 5; 02 G-005).
- Every HOLD in section 12 names who clears it; critical holds clear only with a recorded qualified assessment, never by override or customer request (source: 31 section 8.3).
- Evidence: note
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].

- For this service the path above applies before any further work on the affected item when: hidden-service risk is uncertain; an item exceeds the SOP's bands or has no recorded rating; the substrate is not covered; a fireplace mantel has not been assessed; or older finishes may contain lead paint or asbestos (source: sections 10 and 12).
- Contacts and escalation order: `<owner decision: escalation order>` (Q-31-05).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].
- For this service, report among others: a dropped or falling item, a drill strike on a hidden service, and damage to customer artwork, glass or walls (source: spec JOB-008; HI-01.HAZ).
- Q-31-01 (owner): who are the competent reviewers for this SOP, and how is their competence evidenced?

- Q-31-07 (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: EPA RRP-certified renovator, accredited asbestos inspector): which property-age threshold triggers lead and asbestos screening when drilling or patching older painted plaster, and does HandyHub hold or plan EPA RRP certification (X-13)?
- Q-31-09 (owner; qualified safety professional): height and access policy for ladder work above mantels and on high walls.
- Q-31-08 (owner and the relevant reviewers): is fireplace mounting offered at all? HI-01 is named.
- Q-31-05 (owner): emergency and escalation contacts and order for sections 19 and 20.
- Q-31-15 (owner): which section 13 checks need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check while there are two employees?
- Q-27-15 (qualified safety professional; licensing reviewer): which HOLDs in section 12 are critical holds.
- OPEN QUESTION (C-HI01-02; owner with qualified safety professional): maximum accepted item weight for HI-01, and above what weight a two-person lift is mandatory.
- OPEN QUESTION (C-HI01-05; owner): which substrates are in scope beyond standard drywall and solid brick or concrete.
- OPEN QUESTION (04 exclusions row; owner): ceiling-hung items, picture lights, wall repair, old-hole patching and gallery-wall layout.

sops.title: SOP HI-02: Deep-Clean Barbecue & Grill Maintenance

lines: - The customer grants access to the main gas line safety shut-off valve or propane tank regulator before work begins (source: agreement "Gas Isolation" clause).

- PROPOSED for the preparation checklist (not yet in the agreement): grill turned off and cool before arrival (the cool-down period is set by safety review, not here); work area clear; water and power access; pets and children kept away from the work area; make and model information ready (source: 04 HI-02 "customer preparation requirements"; spec HI-02.INT; X-11).
- Every job re-confirms access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions (source: spec CX-005).
- HandyHub's own pre-start checks are never moved onto the customer (source: 30 section 4.1 clause 5).
*Dispatch and Start Job gates for this service (source: spec APXA-001, APXA-003; 31 section 3.1 row 3). Every item is pending review.*
- Intake complete: grill fuel type, make/model, condition, location, access to water/power, customer expectations, corrosion/damage (source: spec HI-02.INT).
- An approved estimate version covers the tasks in section 2; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec CX-003; APXA-003).
- Evidence: note
- The grill manufacturer's instructions for the specific unit are available (source: spec section 17 card note "manufacturer instructions"; 04 HI-02 "prerequisites").

- Every cleaning product is on an approved product list with a reviewed SDS; a chemical product without a reviewed SDS is not carried to the job (source: 29 section 8.3 interim rule, PROPOSED; X-09). No product is approved yet: TBD - requires qualified safety reviewer review.
- The customer has granted access to the main gas shut-off valve or propane tank regulator (source: agreement "Gas Isolation" clause).
- The unit is cool and off before any work starts (source: spec HI-02.SAF "confirm unit is cool/off"; hold in section 12).

- Licensed-task and permit flags: where policy marks a task as needing a licensed trade or permit, Start Job stays blocked until that prerequisite is approved (source: spec START-010; 04 HI-02 "permit/license flags").

- Before this SOP can be activated, the named reviewers approve: the fuel-restore and leak-verification decision and method (C-HI02-03); the port-clearing method (C-HI02-04); the rinse, dry and residue-check method (C-HI02-02); the scald controls (section 12) (source: 31 section 10 HI-02; owner facts L20).

- On arrival: confirm address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants; inspect the actual site against the briefing; capture required existing-condition photos; protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- Protect surrounding surfaces with protective coverings and absorbents; types TBD (source: spec HI-02.MAT).

- Isolate-verify-restore: "System Tear-down" closes the propane tank or gas line valves, but verification and restoration are not defined, and the shared isolate-verify-restore module does not exist yet (source: X-07; C-HI02-03; 31 section 5.8).
- Ventilation adequate for the approved products (source: spec HI-02.SAF "ventilate").
- Staging of the soak bin, heat source and products: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003; START-004).
- Evidence: note

*The original procedure lines below are unchanged and in their original order. Lines starting with "HOLD" or "FLAG" were added on 2026-10-03; they are pending review and never replace the step text. No burn-off, ignition or flame test is part of this procedure (source: 31 section 10 HI-02; X-10).*

> HOLD (precondition; spec HI-02.SAF; 02 G-047): before "System Tear-down", confirm the unit is cool and off ("confirm unit is cool/off"). No cool-down period is set here (TBD - requires qualified safety reviewer review). If the unit is hot or on, or its state cannot be confirmed, do not start; escalate (section 19).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Detailing Execution"

items.ref: precondition; C-HI02-08, X-02; pending the START-008 configuration
lines: > HOLD (precondition; C-HI02-08, X-02; pending the START-008 configuration): before "System Tear-down", record the unit's existing condition with photos and notes: cookbox, grates, flavorizer bars, heat shields, burners and any part that looks rusted through, cracked or decayed. If a damaged burner, valve, hose or regulator, a gas odor or a suspected leak is found, do not start; follow section 10.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Detailing Execution"

lines: > HOLD (precondition; X-07; spec HI-02.SAF): before "System Tear-down", have the grill manufacturer's instructions for this unit; fuel and power are isolated only as they describe ("isolate fuel/power per manufacturer"). Never disconnect, loosen or modify a gas line, hose, regulator, valve or fitting (section 2, Do not perform 9-11). Whether closing a fixed natural-gas supply valve is licensed work in the municipality is an open licensing question (04 HI-02 "permit/license flags"; HUMAN REVIEW: municipal licensing authority, licensed gas fitter or plumber). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Detailing Execution"

lines: - [ ] **System Tear-down:** Turn off the propane tank or gas line valves. Dismantle all internal grates, flavorizer bars, heat shields, and grease trays.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Detailing Execution"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI02-05): disassembly is limited to the parts named in the step above until the disassembly boundary is decided; the agreement's "Full system tear-down" does not extend it. Grease-tray contents are not cleaned or disposed of under this SOP (section 2, Out of scope; section 15). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Detailing Execution"

items.ref: scald control; precondition; spec HI-02.HAZ "hot surfaces"; 31 section 10 HI-02
lines: > HOLD (scald control; precondition; spec HI-02.HAZ "hot surfaces"; 31 section 10 HI-02): before "The Chemical Bath", a qualified safety reviewer approves the heat source, the handling and draining of hot water and the PPE for the "boiling water solution", and the degreaser is an approved product used only as its label and SDS allow (section 8). Until then the step below is not performed. Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Detailing Execution"

lines: - [ ] **The Chemical Bath:** Submerge all removed grates and shields into a heavy plastic utility bin filled with a boiling water solution mixed with non-toxic, carbon-stripping eco-degreaser. Let soak for 30 minutes.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Detailing Execution"

lines: > FLAG: UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions: the soak time ("30 minutes") and the "boiling water solution" in the step above come from no product label or SDS (31 section 3.5 rule 3). The "non-toxic" wording is unverified and is not repeated to the customer (C-HI02-01).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Detailing Execution"

lines: - [ ] **Cookbox Scraping:** Use a heavy-duty plastic putty scraper and a wire block brush to manually scrape caked carbon crust off the interior walls of the cookbox down to raw aluminum/metal.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Detailing Execution"

lines: > FLAG (C-HI02-07): the step above names a plastic putty scraper, while the inventory stocks carbon-steel scrapers; spec HI-02.TLS asks for "non-damaging detailing tools". Use the scraper the step names. Whether scraping "down to raw aluminum/metal" suits this cookbox's finish depends on the grill manufacturer's care instructions (RISK, unverified). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Detailing Execution"

lines: - [ ] **Burner Tube Purging:** Wire-brush the outside of stainless steel burner tubes. Use a small drill bit or paperclip to clear out single clogged gas vent ports to ensure a uniform flame pattern.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Detailing Execution"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI02-04): in the step above, clearing gas vent ports with "a small drill bit or paperclip" is held pending review of the grill manufacturer's instructions; a drill bit may enlarge or alter ports (RISK, unverified). Until a reviewer records the manufacturer's method, ports are not cleared; note clogged ports for the supervisor and the customer (section 17). "To ensure a uniform flame pattern" is not a promise to the customer. Whether burner-port clearing is offered at all is open (Q-31-08). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Detailing Execution"

lines: > HOLD (precondition; C-HI02-02; spec HI-02.QAC "surfaces clean/dry"): before "Exterior Polishing" ("Reassemble all components"), rinse, dry and check for residue every soaked or chemically cleaned part as the approved product label directs. The label method is not available yet because no product is approved: TBD - requires qualified safety reviewer review. Do not reassemble a part that has not passed this check. Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Detailing Execution"

lines: - [ ] **Exterior Polishing:** Reassemble all components. Spray the exterior hood and shelves with specialized stainless steel polish, buffing along the grain line with a fresh microfiber cloth.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Detailing Execution"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI02-03; X-07): the step above reassembles the grill, but no step restores the fuel supply or checks for leaks. Do not reopen the valves closed in "System Tear-down" and do not light the grill until a reviewer writes the restore and leak-verification method (HUMAN REVIEW: qualified gas appliance technician or licensed gas professional; grill manufacturer instructions). A leak or damaged gas part means: shut off, tag out of service, tell the customer, escalate. A supervisor, not the worker alone, verifies the result (quality-assistant playbook). Until then the fuel supply stays off and the customer is told so in approved wording (section 17). Whether HandyHub restores fuel at all is an open question (C-HI02-03). Pending review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Detailing Execution"

lines: *From spec HI-02.QAC. The worker cannot mark the job complete without answering the required checks or recording an exception (source: spec QA-001). Which checks need a second person rather than a self-check is open (Q-31-15).*
| Check | Source | Inspector | Evidence |
| Components reassembled correctly | spec HI-02.QAC | Worker; supervisor where policy requires (Q-31-15) | After photos mapped to components (QA-003) |
| Burner ports unobstructed where in scope | spec HI-02.QAC | Worker | Port clearing is on hold (C-HI02-04): record "held - not cleared" and note clogged ports |

| No leaks or loose parts introduced | spec HI-02.QAC | Supervisor, not the worker alone (quality-assistant playbook) | Result of the reviewer-approved verification (C-HI02-03); until it exists: "not inspected - held", fuel left off, customer told |

| Surfaces clean and dry; no chemical residue on parts that touch food | spec HI-02.QAC; agreement "food-surface safe post-rinsing" | Worker; method by the reviewer | Checklist answer per the approved label method (C-HI02-02) |
| No loose wire bristles left on cooking grates (PROPOSED, RISK) | 02 G-047 | Worker | Checklist answer; method TBD - requires quality and safety review |
| Area restored | spec HI-02.QAC; QA-002 | Worker | Cleanup photo where required (QA-002) |
- A customer signature or acknowledgement does not clear an unresolved safety hold (source: quality-assistant playbook "A signed customer form does not clear an unresolved safety hold.").
- Evidence: note
- Missing evidence is recorded as unknown, not as a pass (source: quality-assistant playbook).
- Evidence: note
- Clean the area, remove waste and protection, and account for tools and materials (source: spec APXA-005; QA-002; HI-02.QAC "area restored").

- Restore utilities and components altered within scope (source: spec APXA-005), except the fuel supply, which stays off under the C-HI02-03 hold until the approved method exists; the customer is told (section 17).
- Return unused materials (source: spec APXA-007).

- Waste streams: degreaser wastewater from the soak bin; grease and carbon scrapings; used cloths, pads and absorbents; empty product containers (source: spec HI-02.SAF "control chemicals/waste"; 04 HI-02 "permit/license flags"; 29 section 8.2 item 10).

- No disposal method or destination is approved: contain chemicals, wastewater and grease, and dispose of them only by the method the reviewer approves for the municipality (source: 31 section 3.1 row 15; Q-29-10; HUMAN REVIEW: local sewer or stormwater utility; qualified safety professional).
- Cloths used with the stainless protective oil: disposal rule pending the reviewer's SDS classification (source: 29 sections 8.1 and 8.2 item 10).
- Grease-tray contents: not covered (section 2).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: existing-condition photos of the cookbox, grates, flavorizer bars, heat shields and burners before disassembly. PROPOSED for HI-02 because the agreement's "Pre-existing Defects" clause relies on them; whether they are required is the START-008 configuration decision (source: C-HI02-08; X-02; spec START-008; 04 HI-02 "completion evidence").
- Evidence: photo

- During: concealed or unexpected conditions, for example a rusted-through burner tube or a cracked part, with photos and severity (source: spec JOB-004; UXE-006; agreement "Pre-existing Defects" examples).
- After: photos mapped to components - cookbox, grates, burners, exterior (source: spec QA-003; 04 HI-02 "completion evidence").
- Evidence: photo

- Every photo is internal-only by default; marketing use needs separate consent (source: spec REC-002, REC-003). Avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- Arrival and completion updates are drafts; the worker or admin controls the send (source: spec UXE-008).
- Record the walkthrough outcome: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Care notes only from approved product or manufacturer data; none are approved yet (source: spec QA-008).

- Held items, told in approved wording: ports not cleared (C-HI02-04); fuel supply left off and why (C-HI02-03); defects found, such as rusted-through burner tubes, cracked flavorizer bars or decayed heat shields, are recorded and reported, and repair is not offered (Do not perform 10; section 2, Out of scope) (source: section 12 holds; agreement "Pre-existing Defects" examples). The worker gives no gas-restore or relighting instructions (source: 31 section 3.5 rule 4). Wording TBD - owner and qualified safety reviewer.
- Evidence: note
- Blocked work: only the approved "work blocked" message; no incident details or access codes by text or email (source: spec NTF-007, COM-002).

- What not to say: "non-toxic", "eco-safe", "sanitizes", "safe, consistent gas flow", "showroom condition", "Factory Shine", or any lifespan, health or safety outcome (source: C-HI02-01; C-HI02-V02; C-HI02-04; main plan section 2; 32 register A row 2 and register B rows 27, 28, 43, 44).
- Required QA checks answered or an exception recorded (source: spec QA-001; section 13).
- Evidence: note
- After photos mapped to components (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup and waste handling done as approved (source: spec QA-002; sections 14 and 15).
- Tools and materials accounted for (source: spec APXA-005).

- Fuel status recorded: either the reviewer-approved restore and leak-verification result with supervisor verification, or "fuel left off - customer told" under the C-HI02-03 hold (source: C-HI02-03; APXA-005).
- Evidence: note
- Open holds, defects and punch items recorded; walkthrough outcome recorded (source: spec QA-004; APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- The job closes only when the required operational and financial steps are complete (source: spec APXA-007).
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:

*Standard block copied verbatim from 31 SOP standard section 8.5 (PROPOSED wording; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional; attorney licensed in KY and/or IN for the "right to stop work" sentence; bilingual reviewer for Spanish).*

**Service stop triggers and holds (HI-02).** Card stop guidance (spec HI-02.SAF): "confirm unit is cool/off; isolate fuel/power per manufacturer; avoid modifying gas components beyond scope; ventilate; control chemicals/waste".
| Trigger or hold | Action | Cleared by (evidence) | Source |
| Unit hot or on, or its state cannot be confirmed | Do not start; escalate | Unit confirmed cool and off | spec HI-02.SAF |

| Grill manufacturer's instructions for this unit not available | Do not start "System Tear-down"; escalate | Instructions for the unit obtained and recorded | spec HI-02.SAF "isolate fuel/power per manufacturer"; X-07 |

| Gas odor, suspected leak, or a damaged burner, valve, hose or regulator | Gas odor: emergency (section 19, step 2). Leak or damaged gas part: shut off, tag out of service, tell the customer, escalate | Qualified gas appliance technician or licensed gas professional; supervisor verification | C-HI02-03; 31 section 10 HI-02; 04 HI-02 "stop-work conditions" |
| Customer asks for gas-component repair or disconnection | Do not perform; record the request; refer | Owner (referral) | Do not perform 9-11 |

| Scald control for "The Chemical Bath" ("boiling water solution") | Held: the step is not performed | Qualified safety reviewer approves the heat source, the handling and draining of hot water and the PPE; degreaser approved with a reviewed SDS | 31 section 10 HI-02; spec HI-02.HAZ "hot surfaces" |
| Port clearing in "Burner Tube Purging" | Held: ports are not cleared | Manufacturer method recorded by a reviewer | C-HI02-04 |
| Rinse, dry and residue check before reassembly | Held: parts are not reassembled until checked | Approved product label method | C-HI02-02 |
| Fuel restore and leak verification after reassembly | Held: the fuel supply stays off and the customer is told | Reviewer-written method; supervisor verification | C-HI02-03 |
| Chemical product without a reviewed SDS, or a mix the SDS does not allow | Do not use | Reviewed SDS and approved product | 29 section 8.3; X-09 |
| Work area cannot be ventilated as the product SDS requires | Stop the chemical step; escalate | Qualified safety reviewer | spec HI-02.SAF "ventilate" |
| Chemicals, wastewater or grease cannot be contained | Stop; escalate | Approved disposal method | spec HI-02.SAF "control chemicals/waste"; Q-29-10 |
| Fire, smoke or flare-up | Emergency (section 19, step 2) | Emergency services; incident report (section 20) | spec HI-02.HAZ; X-10 |
Critical holds cannot be overridden by any role; they clear only with a recorded qualified assessment. Unapproved gas scope is a critical class (source: 31 section 8.3 rule 2).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
*Standard block copied verbatim from 31 section 8.5 (PROPOSED wording; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional).*

**HI-02 escalation routes (owner decisions pending, Q-31-05):** a gas leak, a damaged gas part or a gas-component request goes to the owner, then to a qualified gas appliance technician or licensed gas professional (source: C-HI02-03; 04 HI-02 "responsible skill / business role"). Chemical exposure: emergency response first, then the incident form (section 20); first-aid references only from the reviewed SDS (source: 29 section 8.2 item 7). Contacts: `<owner decision: emergency contact>` and `<owner decision: escalation order>` (Q-31-05).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].

*Standard block copied verbatim from 31 section 8.5 (PROPOSED wording). HUMAN REVIEW: attorney licensed in KY and/or IN for the fault and liability sentence; insurance broker for any insurer-notification step added later.*
- HI-02 examples to report: burns or scalds, cuts, chemical exposure, a fire or flare-up, a gas leak, damage to the customer's grill or property (source: spec HI-02.HAZ; JOB-008).
- Q-31-08 (owner and relevant reviewers): is burner-port clearing offered at all, or referred out?
- C-HI02-03 open question (02 register): does HandyHub restore the fuel supply at all, or leave it off for the customer?
- Q-31-05 (owner): emergency and escalation contacts, escalation order and after-hours coverage for a two-person team.
- Q-31-11 (owner; qualified safety professional): emergency kit contents, SDS register owner, chemical storage and transport.
- Q-31-15 (owner): which checks (fuel status, reassembly) need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check while there are two employees?
- Q-31-02 (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish safety text?
- Q-29-10 (local authority; safety reviewer): disposal destinations and rules for degreaser wastewater, grease and carbon in each service municipality.

sops.title: SOP HI-03: Driveway Pressure Washing & Surface Restoration

lines: From the agreement and the spec, pending review:
- Vehicles removed from the driveway before crew arrival (source: agreement "Vehicle Clearing"; the distance is under attorney and safety review).
- Access to an outdoor spigot (source: agreement "Water Access Mandatory").
- Every job re-confirms access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions (source: spec CX-005).
- Nearby doors, windows and landscaping and any drainage concerns are captured at intake (source: spec HI-03.INT).

GAP - not yet in the agreement or any reminder (owner decision; wording through 30 and 32): windows and doors closed; pets and children kept indoors; outdoor items moved; sprinkler heads and landscape lights identified; drainage issues and HOA rules disclosed (source: 04 HI-03 "customer preparation requirements"; X-11).
Dispatch and Start Job conditions, pending review:
- Approved estimate version with the selected surfaces, areas and stain treatments, each option separately identifiable (source: spec CX-003, EST-005; APXA-001 "review scope/exclusions").
- Intake recorded: surface type and condition, area, drainage, nearby doors, windows and landscaping, stain types, water source and weather (source: spec HI-03.INT).
- Evidence: note

- Surface confirmed as concrete; any other surface, any coating and any damaged substrate are routed to on-site assessment before a firm scope (source: 04 HI-03 "estimating method"; spec HI-03.SAF; C-HI03-08).
- Every chemical product approved with a reviewed SDS; a product without one is not carried to the job (source: 29 section 8.3 interim rule, PROPOSED; C-HI03-02).

- Runoff and wash-water handling decided for the job's municipality; unknown does not mean allowed (source: 04 HI-03 "prerequisites" and "permit/license flags"; risk-triage playbook step 4). HUMAN REVIEW: local authority; no conclusion is drawn here.
- An unrestricted outdoor spigot is available; frozen or unavailable water means No Start / Blocked, not a forced start (source: agreement "Water Access Mandatory"; spec SCH-008).

- Weather acceptable under the weather and heat module, which does not exist yet; severe weather is a stop condition (source: X-27; spec HI-03.INT "weather", START-011). TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.
- Vehicles moved as the agreement requires; the distance it states is under attorney and safety review (source: agreement "Vehicle Clearing"; agreement review notes).
- PPE selected and available; tools, barriers and protection loaded (source: spec START-004, START-005; APXA-001).
- The worker holds the pressure-washing qualification tag once it is defined (source: spec SCH-003, PROPOSED; Q-04-13).
- Permit, license and qualification flags for this line determined; `unknown` blocks Start for the affected line (source: 04 section 6.1; spec START-010).
- Start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented; critical holds cannot be overridden (source: APXA-003; 31 section 8.3).
- Evidence: note
Pending review; methods come from the approved modules, none of which exists yet:
- Confirm the address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants (source: APXA-002).
- Inspect the actual site against the briefing and record differences (source: spec START-007).
- Evidence: note
- Photograph existing cracks, etching, stains and adjacent property before work (source: spec START-008; APXA-002; X-02).
- Set up barriers and keep people and pets out of the wash zone (source: spec HI-03.TLS "barriers", HI-03.SAF "exclude people/pets").
- Protect electrical fixtures, outlets, openings and landscaping (source: spec HI-03.SAF).
- Set up rinse-water and runoff controls as needed (source: spec HI-03.MAT; HI-03.SAF "manage runoff").

- Connect to the customer's spigot as agreed; whether backflow protection is needed is an open question (source: agreement "Water Access Mandatory"; 04 HI-03 "permit/license flags"; HUMAN REVIEW: water utility or plumbing inspector).
- Place and refuel the gas washer only under a reviewed fuel and exhaust rule: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve. (source: 04 HI-03 "hazards")
- Inspect the equipment before use per the manufacturer instructions (source: 31 section 3.1 row 7).
- Test an inconspicuous area and record the result before full washing (source: spec HI-03.SAF; 04 HI-03 "completion evidence").
- Evidence: note
- Complete the safety, PPE and site checks and acknowledge the SOP and hazards before starting (source: APXA-003; spec START-004).
- Evidence: note

*The original procedure follows verbatim and in its original order; its option headings are demoted one level. The quoted HOLD and FLAG lines were added on 2026-10-03 and are pending qualified review. A HOLD placed before a step must be cleared before that step starts; a HOLD or FLAG placed after a step suspends, limits or flags it (36 D-36-17). No hold rewords, reorders or removes a step.*

> FLAG (X-06): the mold wording in this option is kept verbatim. The stop-work rule in section 10 lists possible mold; which exterior growth this option may treat is decided by the qualified reviewer once the company definition that separates cleanable mildew, algae and staining from suspected mold growth exists (Q-31-10). Until then the stop-work rule is not relaxed. (source: 31 section 5.8)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Removing Deep Organic Moss & Black Mold Spores"

lines: - [ ] **Chemical Pre-Treat:** Mix a specialized sodium hypochlorite solution (soft-wash mix) with a foaming surfactant inside a pump sprayer. Apply a generous wet coat over dark mold areas.

lines: - [ ] **Dwell Period:** Allow the solution to dwell for 15 minutes to liquefy microscopic mold roots deep inside concrete pores. Keep the surface damp.

lines: - [ ] **Rotary Surface Cleaning:** Hook up a 20-inch circular flat surface cleaning deck to a 3,000 PSI gas pressure washer. Glide the deck across the concrete in slow, overlapping parallel rows to prevent streak lines.

lines: Observable checks from the service card (source: spec HI-03.QAC; QA-001), with the evidence in brackets. The worker self-checks; which checks need a supervisor is an owner decision (Q-31-15).
- Uniform cleaning without etching or striping [after photos per area, spec QA-003].
- Stain treatment documented: stain type, product used and result [stain-treatment record].
- Evidence: note
- Runoff controlled [runoff-control note, spec QA-002].
- Adjacent property protected: plants, fixtures, openings and vehicles [after photos compared with the arrival photos, spec START-008].
- Evidence: photo

- Site rinsed, and hazards created by the work cleared or recorded. This is an observable check, not a safety certification (source: spec HI-03.QAC "site safe and rinsed"; risk-triage SKILL "never certify site safety").
- Evidence: note
Source: spec QA-002; APXA-005; pending review:
- Remove barriers, coverings and protection.
- Clean the work area; keep used absorbent and poultice for the reviewed waste route (section 15).
- Account for tools, equipment and remaining materials; secure chemical containers for transport under the chemical program, which does not exist yet (source: 29 section 8.2 rows 5 and 6).
- Restore anything altered within scope, such as the customer's water connection (source: APXA-005).
TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

- Waste streams: wash water and runoff that may carry hypochlorite, surfactant, degreaser and oil residue; used absorbent and poultice; empty chemical containers (source: 29 section 8.2 row 10; spec HI-03.MAT).

- Destination and method per municipality: HUMAN REVIEW: local authority and qualified safety professional (Q-29-10; 31 section 5.8 waste, runoff and disposal module). No conclusion is drawn here on discharge or disposal rules.
- Hazardous waste is not handled without an approved policy (source: 31 section 3.1 row 15).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: Photos are internal-only by default and avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- Before: arrival and existing-condition photos of the work area, existing cracks, etching and stains, and adjacent property (source: spec START-008; APXA-002; X-02).
- Evidence: photo
- During: the test-area result and the stain treatment applied (source: spec HI-03.SAF, HI-03.QAC; 04 HI-03 "completion evidence", PROPOSED).
- After: after photos mapped to each area (source: spec QA-003) and the runoff-control and cleanup note (source: spec QA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- Arrival and completion updates are drafts; the worker or an administrator controls the actual send according to policy (source: spec UXE-008).
- Record the walkthrough outcome: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Care notes come only from approved product data (source: spec QA-008).
- Blocked work: use only the approved "work blocked" message (source: spec NTF-007).

- Do not tell the customer that every stain will come out (agreement "Stain Limitations"), that products are "eco-safe" or harmless (C-HI03-V02), that the surface is safe or that mold is killed (X-06; Do not perform entry 8), and do not offer the bio-shield until it is approved (C-HI03-05).
Definition of done (source: spec QA-001 to QA-006; HI-03.QAC; APXA-005, APXA-006):
- Every section 13 check answered, or an exception recorded (QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- After photos mapped to areas (QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup done and protection removed (QA-002).
- The customer's water connection and anything else altered within scope restored (APXA-005).
- Punch items recorded with an owner and a due date (QA-005).
- Evidence: note
- Walkthrough outcome recorded (QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- No hold left open; any incident reported (section 20; APXA-007).
- Evidence: note
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:
Service-specific stop triggers (source: spec HI-03.SAF unless noted; PROPOSED wording pending qualified review):
- People or pets enter the wash zone: stop washing until they are clear (X-11).
- The test on an inconspicuous area shows etching, striping or other damage: stop and escalate (HI-03.SAF "test inconspicuous area"; HI-03.QAC "without etching/striping").
- The pressure is not confirmed as appropriate for the surface: do not start washing (HI-03.SAF "use surface-appropriate pressure"; C-HI03-08).
- Electrical fixtures, outlets, openings or landscaping cannot be protected: do not wash toward them; stop and escalate (HI-03.SAF "protect electrical/openings/landscape").
- Runoff cannot be managed: stop (HI-03.SAF "manage runoff").
- Damaged substrate: stop, record (JOB-004) and escalate (HI-03.SAF "stop for damaged substrate").
- Evidence: note
- Water frozen or unavailable, or severe weather: record No Start / Blocked instead of starting (spec SCH-008, START-011; agreement "Water Access Mandatory").
- Evidence: note

Service holds (inserted in section 12). Critical holds cannot be overridden (31 section 8.3); a hold that exists because a required module or policy is missing (pressure washing, chemicals and SDS, weather) behaves as a critical hold until that module is approved (31 section 8.4 rule 4, PROPOSED):
| Hold | Where in section 12 | Release role and evidence |

| C-HI03-01: test area, exclusion zone, PPE and protection of fixtures, outlets and openings before washing; turbo-nozzle method suspended | Before the rotary and turbo-nozzle steps; after the turbo-nozzle step | Qualified safety professional: reviewed method from the washer and nozzle manufacturer instructions, recorded approval |

| C-HI03-02: SDS, PPE, landscape protection, final rinse and runoff control for the chemical program | Before the chemical pre-treat and absorbent lift steps; after the last step of each option | Qualified safety professional (SDS and PPE); local authority for discharge rules |
| X-08 pressure-washing module; X-11 occupants and pets; X-27 weather module | In the holds before the washing steps | Qualified safety professional, once the modules are approved |
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
Service roles (contacts are owner decisions, Q-31-05):
- Safety holds in sections 10 and 12: qualified safety professional.
- Scope questions (perimeter detailing, bio-shield, other surfaces, old oil stains): owner.
- Runoff and disposal rules: local authority, through the legal-compliance lens; no conclusion is drawn here.
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].
**HUMAN REVIEW:** attorney licensed in KY and/or IN for the fault and liability sentence; insurance broker for any insurer-notification step added later.

Examples for this service, all reported under JOB-008 (source: spec HI-03.HAZ): an injection injury or near miss; a chemical splash or exposure; etched or damaged surfaces; plant or vehicle damage; equipment failure. First-response provisions depend on the vehicle safety kit, which is not yet defined (X-10).
- Q-31-11 (owner; qualified safety professional): what goes in the emergency kit, who owns the SDS register, and how are the chemicals stored and transported?
- Q-31-10 (owner; qualified mold assessor): what is the company definition of mold growth versus cleanable mildew, and the stop rule (Option A wording, X-06)?
- Q-31-05 (owner): who are the emergency and escalation contacts and in what order (section 19 placeholders)?
- Q-31-15 (owner): which quality or safety checks need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check?
- Q-31-02 (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish version?
- Q-04-13 (owner; qualified safety professional): which qualification tags release pressure washing and chemical cleaning?
- Q-29-10 (local authority; safety reviewer): where may wash water and chemical residue go in each service municipality?
- Q-28-21 (owner; agreement text through 30): is the bio-shield included or an add-on?

- Open questions recorded with C-HI03-03 and C-HI03-08 in 02 (owner; safety reviewer): is perimeter detailing offered, and which surfaces are in scope? Rust-line treatment ("Not covered" in 31 section 10) needs the same scope decision.

sops.title: SOP HI-04: Professional TV Wall Mounting & Wire Hiding

lines: PROPOSED for owner approval; customer-facing wording goes through 30 and 32.
- The TV, the mount (where the customer supplies it) and their model and weight documents are on site (source: 04 HI-04 "customer preparation requirements"; spec HI-04.INT).
- The mounting height and location are decided and the outlet location is known (source: 04 HI-04; spec HI-04.INT "desired height", "outlet/low-voltage situation").
- Furniture is cleared from the work area; children and pets are kept away from the work area and the lift (source: 04 HI-04; spec CX-005; X-11).
- Option B: the customer supplies functional HDMI cables of sufficient length (source: agreement "Hardware Sufficiency" clause, itself under attorney review).
- Every job re-confirms access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions (source: spec CX-005).
- This SOP is not active: no job uses it until competent review and owner activation (source: owner facts 2026-10-02; 31 section 2.1).
- An approved estimate version exists for the job; Option B is performed only when it is an itemized line of that version (source: spec CX-003, EST-005; agreement "Component Clause").
- Intake recorded: TV size, weight and model; mount model; wall and substrate; stud layout; desired height; cable plan; outlet and low-voltage situation (source: spec HI-04.INT).
- Evidence: note

- Customer-supplied TV and mount: visible condition, model and quantity recorded before installation; a missing or rejected item blocks the affected task (source: spec START-009, JOB-004; 29 section 9.1, PROPOSED).
- Evidence: note
- TV and mount ratings checked against the manufacturer documentation before any drilling (source: spec HI-04.SAF "verify mount/TV ratings"; section 12 hold, C-HI04-01).
- The wall is drywall over wood studs; any other substrate stops the job for an on-site assessment (source: original Option A heading; 02 C-HI04-07).

- A second person is scheduled when the lift needs one; the threshold is TBD by the owner and the qualified safety reviewer (source: spec HI-04.SAF "two-person lift when needed", spec HI-04.TLS "lift help"; 02 C-HI04-01).

- Option B: the low-voltage permission status for the municipality is recorded before start; unknown does not mean that no permit is needed (source: spec HI-04.MAT "if permitted", START-010; 04 HI-04 permit and license flags; handyhub-risk-triage playbook "unknown applicability must not default to no permit").
- Evidence: note
- Property-age screening before cutting older wall finishes is not part of the HI-04 intake (02 G-049); until it exists, suspected hazardous material means stop (source: spec START-011; Q-31-07).
- Ladder work only under an approved height and access policy, which does not exist yet (source: 02 G-005; X-12).

- Before leaving: confirm the correct job, customer, address and time; read the latest changes; review scope and exclusions; review hazards and safety; load critical tools, equipment and materials; check customer-supplied items; confirm required documents and approvals (source: spec APXA-001).

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; confirm materials and models; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003, START-004).
- Evidence: note

- On arrival: confirm the address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants; inspect the actual site against the briefing; capture the required existing-condition photos; protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- Confirm that the site matches the briefing, or record the differences; material differences trigger Risk Triage or supervisor review (source: spec START-007).
- Evidence: note
- Existing-condition photos of the wall area and of the customer's TV and mount, with the START-009 record (source: spec START-008, START-009).
- Evidence: photo, note
- Protect the floor and furnishings below the work area, for example with a drop cloth (source: spec HI-04.HAZ "wall damage"; spec APXA-002 "protect work area"; 29 section 7.3).
- Keep children and pets out of the work area and the lift path (source: X-11; spec CX-005).
- Ladder set-up only under an approved height and access policy: TBD (source: 02 G-005; X-12).
- Safety, PPE and site checks complete and the SOP hazards acknowledged before starting (source: spec APXA-003, START-004).
- Evidence: note

*Original procedure, verbatim and in its original order. HOLD and FLAG lines are added drafts pending qualified review (31 section 10). A hold placed before a step must be satisfied before that step starts; a hold or flag placed after a step limits or flags "the step above" (36 D-36-17).*
- [ ] **Center Locating:** Run a deep-scanning stud finder to locate both edges of the wood stud. Mark the exact center column line with a pencil.

Release: section 10. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-04.SAF "verify mount/TV ratings; use structural attachment per instructions"; spec START-009)

Whether the stocked scanner detects wiring or pipes is not stated (section 7); where its manufacturer instructions do not cover them, a scan that finds nothing does not clear the risk and counts as uncertain. If anything is uncertain, STOP and escalate. Release: section 10. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-04.HAZ "drilling into hidden utilities"; spec HI-04.SAF "stop on uncertain substrate/utilities"; spec START-011; inventory file; 02 C-HI04-02; owner facts 2026-10-02 "Unknown is not safe")

lines: - [ ] **Pilot Hole Boring:** Use a bubble level to align the metal TV wall bracket template flat against the wall. Bore 2.5-inch deep pilot holes directly into the center of the studs using a wood drill bit.

lines: > FLAG: UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions. "Bore 2.5-inch deep pilot holes" in the step above is not taken from a mount or fastener instruction; those instructions govern hole depth and bit size. Do not lift or hang the TV under this SOP until the owner confirms the hang is in scope and a reviewer writes that step from the mount manufacturer's instructions; no step is invented here. lines: - [ ] **Cutout Mapping:** Trace the outline of a plastic low-voltage entry box directly below the TV bracket and another box 12 inches above the floor level.

lines: > HOLD (C-HI04-02): before "Drywall Cutout" below, run a hidden-service check of both traced openings with the stocked scanner per its manufacturer instructions, and record the result; any uncertainty = STOP and escalate. Where those instructions do not cover wiring or pipes, a scan that finds nothing does not clear the risk and counts as uncertain (section 7). Release: section 10. Pending qualified review. lines: - [ ] **Drywall Cutout:** Use a drywall hand saw to carefully cut out both rectangles, ensuring no stud interference.

lines: - [ ] **Conduit Fish Tape Run:** Drop a flexible fiberglass fish tape down through the top wall cavity cutout until it exits the bottom opening. Secure HDMI and media cables to the tape and pull them cleanly up behind the drywall.

lines: > HOLD (C-HI04-08): during the step above, if the fish tape meets blocking, insulation or any pipe or vent, STOP - do not bore or cut; record the condition (JOB-004) and escalate. Release: section 10. Pending qualified and building-official review. (source: 02 C-HI04-08; 31 section 10)

- Photos are internal-only by default and avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- The required photo set, and whether Start Job is blocked without it: TBD - owner (source: spec START-008).
- Arrival and completion updates use approved templates only; until approved they are drafts (source: 31 section 3.1).
- Before drilling, confirm the marked height and position with the customer (section 12 hold, C-HI04-V01).
- Run a TV function test only with the customer's authorization, and record the result (source: spec HI-04.QAC).
- Evidence: note
- Walkthrough: record accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- Blocked work: use only the approved "work blocked" message; never send incident details or access codes by text or email (source: spec NTF-007, COM-002).

- A request for line-voltage work, for example an outlet or power routed in the wall, is not performed; it is referred to a licensed electrician. Customer wording: TBD - licensed electrician and attorney (source: 02 C-HI04-06).

- Do not repeat the agreement's "Structural Guarantee", the main plan's "absolute structural safety" or "completely wireless appearance", or any load, safety or code-compliance promise (source: C-HI04-01, C-HI04-06; Do-not-perform entry 8).
- Explain the invoice and payment next step without unauthorized promises (source: spec APXA-006).
- Every section 13 check is answered with evidence, or an exception is recorded (source: spec QA-001, AT-039).
- Evidence: note
- After photos are captured and mapped to the work (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup is done, protection removed, and tools and materials accounted for (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005).
- The property is left secured (source: 31 section 3.1).
- The walkthrough outcome is recorded (source: spec QA-004, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- No hold from sections 10 and 12 is open, and unresolved issues, incidents and change requests are submitted before the job closes (source: spec APXA-007, JOB-012).
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:
HI-04 stop triggers (spec HI-04.SAF first, then the register holds; all pending qualified review):
- The mount or TV ratings are not verified, or the TV exceeds the mount rating (source: spec HI-04.SAF "verify mount/TV ratings"; C-HI04-01).
- The attachment cannot follow the mount instructions (source: spec HI-04.SAF "use structural attachment per instructions").
- The work would need line-voltage electrical work (source: spec HI-04.SAF "do not perform unlicensed line-voltage work"; C-HI04-06).
- The lift needs two people and only one is available (source: spec HI-04.SAF "two-person lift when needed").
- The substrate or hidden utilities are uncertain (source: spec HI-04.SAF "stop on uncertain substrate/utilities"; C-HI04-02).
- The fish tape meets blocking, insulation or any pipe or vent: do not bore or cut (source: 31 section 10; C-HI04-08).
- The wall is masonry, plaster or lath, or metal stud, or the mount is at a fireplace: not covered; stop and request an on-site assessment (source: 02 C-HI04-07).
- The customer-supplied TV, mount or cables are missing, damaged or without model information (source: spec START-009; spec JOB-004 "missing customer-supplied item").
- Option B: the low-voltage permission status is not recorded (source: spec START-010; spec HI-04.MAT "if permitted").

- Every hold is released only by a named role with recorded evidence (source: 31 section 8.3 rule 1; risk-triage playbook L17). Critical holds clear only with a recorded qualified assessment and are never overridden (source: 31 section 8.3 rule 2); which holds below are critical is pending (Q-27-15).
- Evidence: note
Service holds (inserted in section 12). Release roles are PROPOSED from the reviewers named in the 02 register rows; all are TBD - requires qualified safety reviewer review:
| Hold | Where in section 12 | Release role and evidence (PROPOSED) |
| C-HI04-01: TV and mount ratings | Before "Pilot Hole Boring" | Qualified safety professional; TV and mount model, weight and rated capacity recorded from the manufacturer documentation |
| C-HI04-V01: customer confirms the marked height and position | Before "Pilot Hole Boring" | The customer's acknowledgement and photo recorded; release role TBD - owner |
| C-HI04-09: hidden services before drilling | Before "Pilot Hole Boring" | Qualified safety professional; scan result recorded, and a recorded assessment wherever the result is uncertain |
| C-HI04-01: no TV lift or hang under this SOP | After "Lag Bolt Driving" | Owner scope decision, then a hang step written by a qualified reviewer from the mount manufacturer's instructions |
| C-HI04-02: hidden services before the cutouts | Before "Drywall Cutout" | Qualified safety professional; scan result recorded, and a recorded assessment wherever the result is uncertain |

| C-HI04-08: obstruction in the cable path | After "Conduit Fish Tape Run" | Qualified safety professional, with the local building official before any boring or cutting through blocking is considered |
| C-HI04-06: low-voltage cables only | After "Conduit Fish Tape Run" | Not released under this SOP; line-voltage work is referred to a licensed electrician |
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
HI-04 routes (contacts are owner decisions, Q-31-05):
- Line-voltage request or exposed wiring: stop that task; the office refers it to a licensed electrician (C-HI04-06).
- Blocking, fire blocking, a pipe or a vent in the cable path: stop; the owner obtains review by the local building official before any boring or cutting is considered (C-HI04-08).
- Fireplace, masonry or another uncovered substrate: stop; on-site assessment; licensed gas professional where a gas appliance is present (C-HI04-07).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].

- HI-04 examples: a TV or mount that drops or falls, damage to the wall or to the customer's property, contact with hidden wiring or pipes, and a ladder incident (source: spec JOB-008; spec HI-04.HAZ).
- **Q-31-08** (owner and relevant reviewers): is fireplace mounting for HI-04 offered at all, or referred out?

- C-HI04-01 condition in 02 (owner): does HI-04 include attaching and hanging the TV, or only mounting the bracket (agreement "Component Clause")? If it does, a reviewer writes the hang step from the mount manufacturer's instructions, with the two-person threshold set by the owner and the qualified safety professional; if not, it becomes a customer-visible exclusion.
- C-HI04-06 in 02 (licensed electrician and attorney): which customer requests count as line-voltage work, and how is any exclusion worded?

- Related: **Q-31-05** (owner) emergency and escalation contacts for sections 19 and 20; **Q-31-07** (owner, EPA RRP-certified renovator, accredited asbestos inspector) property-age thresholds for lead and asbestos screening before cutouts; **Q-31-09** (owner and qualified safety professional) the height and access policy; **Q-31-15** (owner) which QA checks need a supervisor rather than a self-check.

sops.title: SOP HI-05: Door Hardware & Smart Lock Installation

lines: PROPOSED from the intake fields; customer-facing wording goes through 30 and 32 (source: 04 HI-05 customer preparation requirements; spec HI-05.INT):
- the compatible lock is on site;
- the customer or an authorized representative is present with their own phone and account;
- a Wi-Fi bridge is available if the lock model needs one;
- all existing keys are available;
- the customer has decided what happens to the old hardware.
Every job re-confirms that access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions are still current (source: spec CX-005).
- This SOP is a draft and is not active; no job is dispatched under it until the owner records approval after competent review (source: owner facts 2026-10-02; spec HND-004; 04 section 2.4).
- Evidence: note

- Before leaving: confirm job, customer, address and time; review scope, exclusions, hazards and safety; load critical tools and materials; check customer-supplied items; confirm required documents and approvals (source: spec APXA-001).
- Intake complete: door material/thickness, existing bore/backset, lock model, handing, strike alignment, Wi-Fi/app needs, customer account/privacy (source: spec HI-05.INT).

- The lock supplier is recorded on the estimate (customer, HandyHub stock or job purchase; Q-29-14). A customer-supplied lock gets a record of visible condition, model and quantity before installation (source: spec START-009; 29 section 9.1).
- Evidence: note

- For Option B, the customer or an authorized representative is present to create and own the app account and all codes; the absent-customer case (for example a remote rental host) is an OPEN QUESTION (source: 04 HI-05 prerequisites, PROPOSED; C-HI05-01).
- The requester's authority to change the locks is confirmed; how it is verified is an OPEN QUESTION for the attorney (source: 04 HI-05 prerequisites; 31 section 10).

- Permit, license and qualification flags: none is set for HI-05. Whether locksmith or security-hardware licensing applies in each Kentucky and Indiana municipality is an OPEN QUESTION, and unknown applicability does not default to "no permit". Start Job stays blocked where admin policy marks a requirement (source: spec START-010; 04 HI-05 permit/license flags; risk-triage playbook).
- A door suspected to be fire-rated or an egress door is not started without review (source: 31 section 10; OPEN QUESTION).

- Old-property screening for painted doors and frames (property age, older paint) is pending (source: 31 section 5.8; 04 HI-05 hazards). Until it is resolved, Do not perform entry 3 (section 2) applies before any chiseling, filing or boring of a painted door or frame in a home built before 1978 or of unknown build year; a customer statement does not clear it (source: owner facts 2026-10-02 "Unknown is not safe"; risk-triage playbook "A pre-1978 painted surface is not cleared by a customer saying it looks safe").
- Start only when the job shows Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003).
- Evidence: note

- On arrival: confirm address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants; inspect the actual site against the briefing; capture the required existing-condition photos; protect the work area (source: spec APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; confirm materials and models; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003, START-004).
- Evidence: note
- Customer-supplied lock: record visible condition, model and quantity (source: spec START-009).
- Evidence: note
- Door and floor protection and staging details: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

*Original procedure text below is unchanged and in its original order. HOLD and FLAG lines are added review items pending qualified review; they never replace or reword a step (source: 31 section 9.2; 36 section 3.4).*
- [ ] **Drag Inspection:** Close the door and manually turn the lock thumb-turn. Identify if the deadbolt rubs against the top, bottom, or back of the strike plate cavity.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Adjusting Misaligned Deadbolts & Strike Plates"

lines: - [ ] **Chisel Recess Modification:** Unscrew the metal strike plate from the door frame. Use a sharp 1/2-inch wood chisel to chip away wood fibers to widen the cavity recess in the direction of the bolt drag.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Adjusting Misaligned Deadbolts & Strike Plates"

lines: - [ ] **Screw Reinforcement:** Reinstall the strike plate using heavy 3-inch wood screws driven deep into the structural jack studs (this stabilizes the loose frame and prevents future settling misalignment).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Adjusting Misaligned Deadbolts & Strike Plates"

lines: > FLAG (C-HI05-05): outcome claim in the step above - "this stabilizes the loose frame and prevents future settling misalignment" - is unverified and conflicts with the agreement's "Structural Frame Waiver". Do not repeat it to customers. Do not diagnose foundation settling; record visible frame movement (spec JOB-004) and escalate (section 10). Owner and attorney review. (source: 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Adjusting Misaligned Deadbolts & Strike Plates"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI05-02): before leaving after the steps above, check with the door closed that it latches and locks and that the deadbolt moves smoothly, including manual operation; do not leave the property unsecured - if the door cannot be locked, stop and escalate (section 19). Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-05.SAF, HI-05.QAC; 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Adjusting Misaligned Deadbolts & Strike Plates"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI05-02): before the old lock is removed and before the step below, confirm compatibility - door thickness, bore/backset, handing and lock model - against the lock manufacturer's instructions; on any mismatch, do not remove the old lock; stop and escalate. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-05.INT; 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Setting Up Smart Wi-Fi Keyless Access Locks"

lines: > FLAG (C-HI05-07): no step covers removing the old lock or recording what happens to old keys and hardware; not covered - pending review (section 2).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Setting Up Smart Wi-Fi Keyless Access Locks"

lines: - [ ] **Hardware Assembly:** Mount the smart lock exterior keypad and interior motorized deadbolt unit uniformly, ensuring the wires clear the latch spindle paths without pinching.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Setting Up Smart Wi-Fi Keyless Access Locks"

lines: - [ ] **Motor Calibration:** Run the smart lock's automatic calibration loop. The lock will shoot the deadbolt out multiple times to confirm zero friction or electronic motor drag.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Setting Up Smart Wi-Fi Keyless Access Locks"

lines: - [ ] **Network Pairing:** Pair the lock to the home Wi-Fi hub, configure temporary guest access pin codes, and test remote lock/unlock commands via the client's smartphone.

Until then the credential rule applies (31 section 5.8, PROPOSED): the customer creates and owns the app account and enters the Wi-Fi password and all master and guest codes on their own device; the worker may point to the manufacturer's setup steps; codes and passwords are never recorded, photographed or sent. (source: spec HI-05.SAF, HI-05.QAC, COM-002; owner facts 2026-10-02)

If the lock fails, stop and escalate (section 19); the contingency is an OPEN QUESTION for the owner. An acknowledgment does not clear this hold. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-05.SAF, HI-05.QAC; 31 section 10)

lines: Observable checks from the spec card; the worker answers each check or records an exception (source: spec HI-05.QAC, QA-001). A worker's self-check does not replace a supervisor inspection where one is required (source: quality-assistant playbook).
| Check | Evidence | Source |
| Smooth latch and deadbolt operation (key, thumb-turn, and keypad and app where in scope) | Function-test record | Spec HI-05.QAC; 04 HI-05 completion evidence |
| Secure attachment of the hardware | After photos that show no codes or account screens | Spec HI-05.QAC, REC-002, COM-002 |
| Door closes and locks; emergency and manual operation verified per the lock manufacturer | Function-test record (hold in section 12) | Spec HI-05.QAC, HI-05.SAF |
| Customer controls codes and accounts | Customer confirmation; no code or password value in any record | Spec HI-05.QAC, COM-002; 27 AUTH-009 (PROPOSED) |
| Old keys and hardware disposition confirmed | Disposition record (customer keeps or disposed per policy - OPEN QUESTION, C-HI05-07) | Spec HI-05.QAC |
- Clean the area, remove protection, account for tools and materials, and restore components altered within scope (source: spec APXA-005, QA-002).
- Wood chips and dust from chiseling: vacuum per the card's tool list; a vacuum is not yet in the inventory (C-HI05-10) (source: spec HI-05.TLS).
- Record what happens to packaging, leftover lock parts and old hardware (source: 29 section 9.1; spec HI-05.QAC).
- Evidence: note

- Waste streams: wood chips and dust, packaging, removed hardware, used batteries, lubricant residue. Destinations and disposal rules: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve. Battery handling per the manufacturer and the reviewer (source: 29 section 8.1).
- Hazardous waste is not handled without an approved policy (source: 31 section 3.1; 02 G-078).
- Disposition of removed hardware and old keys follows an owner policy that does not exist yet (OPEN QUESTION; C-HI05-07); record it (source: spec HI-05.QAC).
- Evidence: note

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: All photos are internal-only by default and never show keypad codes, app or account screens, or people and documents not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002, COM-002; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- Before: existing-condition photos of the door, frame and existing hardware (source: spec START-008; X-02, because the agreement disclaims prior conditions).
- Evidence: photo
- During: concealed damage, frame damage or other unexpected conditions, with severity (source: spec JOB-004).
- After: interior and exterior hardware photos mapped to the door (source: spec QA-003; 04 HI-05 completion evidence).
- Evidence: photo
- Arrival and completion updates are drafts; the worker or admin controls the send (source: spec UXE-008).
- Walkthrough: record the outcome - accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- The customer confirms they hold all codes and the account (source: spec HI-05.QAC).
- Never send codes, passwords, internal notes or incident details by SMS or email (source: spec COM-002).

- Care and warranty notes come only from an approved template; no HI-05 warranty or callback position exists yet (Q-30-07), and manufacturer-warranty handling is undefined (source: spec QA-008; 04 HI-05 warranty or callback policy).
- Do not repeat the flagged claim that the screws prevent future settling (C-HI05-05); make no security or outcome promises (source: 31 section 3.3 entry 8).
- Blocked work: use only the approved "work blocked" message (source: spec NTF-007).
- Every check in section 13 is answered or has a recorded exception (source: spec QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- The door closes and locks, emergency and manual operation are verified, and the property is secured (source: spec HI-05.SAF, HI-05.QAC).
- The customer controls all codes and accounts; no code or password appears in any record (source: spec HI-05.QAC, COM-002).
- Evidence: note
- Old keys and hardware disposition is recorded (source: spec HI-05.QAC).
- Evidence: note
- After photos are captured and mapped (QA-003); cleanup is done (QA-002); the walkthrough outcome is recorded (QA-004) (source: spec QA-002 to QA-004).
- Evidence: photo, note
- A customer-supplied lock has its START-009 record (source: spec START-009).
- Evidence: note
- Closeout: unresolved issues and incident or change follow-ups are submitted; the job closes only when the required operational and financial steps are complete (source: spec APXA-006, APXA-007).
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:
Service-specific stop triggers and holds for HI-05 (pending qualified review):
- Card rule: "protect customer credentials; have customer control personal account/password; verify emergency/manual operation; do not leave property unsecured" (source: spec HI-05.SAF).

- HOLD (C-HI05-02): do not leave the property unsecured. If the door cannot be closed and locked, or emergency and manual operation cannot be verified, stop and escalate; the contingency is an OPEN QUESTION for the owner. Treated as a critical hold: an acknowledgment or a customer signature does not clear it (source: spec HI-05.SAF; 31 section 8.4 rule 3; job-planner playbook).

- HOLD (C-HI05-02): compatibility (door thickness, bore/backset, handing, lock model) is confirmed before the old lock is removed; on a mismatch the old lock is not removed and the job is escalated. Cleared only by the authorized role with an override record (source: spec HI-05.INT, PERM-006; 31 sections 8.4 rule 5 and 10).
- Evidence: note
- HOLD (C-HI05-01): the Option B network-pairing and code step is held under the credential rule; cleared only after privacy owner and attorney review of the step (source: 31 sections 5.8 and 10).
- Stop on a door suspected to be fire-rated or an egress door; review by the building official or fire marshal (OPEN QUESTION) (source: 31 section 10; 04 HI-05 stop-work conditions, PROPOSED).
- Stop on visible frame or structural movement: record the condition (spec JOB-004) and escalate; do not diagnose (source: 04 HI-05 stop-work conditions, PROPOSED; C-HI05-05).
- Evidence: note
- Stop where the requester's authority to change the locks is unclear (source: 31 section 10; OPEN QUESTION).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
Service-specific (pending review):

- A lock that fails after the old one is removed, or a door that cannot be locked: stop and escalate; minimal stabilization only if a policy allows it (source: spec JOB-006). The contingency and the stabilization policy are owner decisions not yet made (OPEN QUESTION; 02 G-005).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].
Service-specific: suspected exposure of a customer code or password (seen, recorded, photographed or sent): TBD - requires privacy owner review (source: 31 section 5.8 credentials module).

- **Q-31-01** (owner): who are the competent reviewers for this SOP (qualified safety professional; privacy owner and attorney for credential handling; building official or fire marshal for rated or egress doors), and how is their competence evidenced?
- **31 section 10** (owner): what is the contingency if a new lock fails after the old one is removed, and who approves leaving the site?
- **04 HI-05 card** (attorney): how is the requester's authority to change locks verified (owner, tenant, landlord, rental host)?
- **04 HI-05 card** (privacy owner; attorney): how are Wi-Fi/app credentials and codes handled when the customer cannot be present, for example a remote rental host (C-HI05-01)?

- **04 HI-05 card** (legal-compliance-administrator; attorney; municipal licensing office): does locksmith or security-hardware licensing apply in the Kentucky and Indiana municipalities served? No conclusion is drawn here.
- **31 section 10** (building official or fire marshal; owner): will HandyHub work on fire-rated or egress doors at all?
- **04 HI-05 card** (EPA RRP-certified renovator): does the RRP rule apply to chiseling, filing or boring pre-1978 painted doors and frames? No conclusion is drawn here.

sops.title: SOP HI-06: Gutter Maintenance & Leaf Protection

lines: - For every job, confirm that access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions are current (source: spec CX-005).

- PROPOSED, pending owner review (source: 04 HI-06 card, customer preparation row): access to all sides of the house; vehicles and items moved from beneath the eaves; pets indoors (X-11); access to an outdoor water spigot; known leaks, sags and underground drains disclosed; roof warranty information before guard installation.
- Occupants, children and pets stay outside the exclusion zone during the work (source: spec HI-06.SAF "maintain exclusion zone"; X-11).

- HOLD (C-HI06-01): no part of this SOP is performed until an approved height/access and fall-protection policy exists and this SOP passes competent review; until then elevated work is blocked. Cleared only by recorded approval of the qualified safety professional and the owner (source: spec HI-06.SAF "beyond approved height/access policy"; 02 G-005; 31 section 7.2 rank 3).
- Evidence: note
- Intake complete: building height/roofline, gutter type/length, downspouts, access, ground conditions, known leaks/sagging, guard product (source: spec HI-06.INT).
- Approved estimate version and scope; Option B only when guards are in the accepted scope (source: spec CX-003; 04 HI-06 card, prerequisites row).
- Ladder-work qualification tag for every worker on site, as the height/access policy will define it (source: spec SCH-003, START-010; 04 HI-06 card, prerequisites row).

- Weather and ground suitable at start; thresholds are set by the qualified safety professional, none here; if unsuitable, record No Start / Blocked (source: spec HI-06.SAF "weather/ground check", SCH-008; X-27).
- Evidence: note

- Property age (year built, or unknown) recorded before any wire-wheel work on painted gutters or fascia. Until a qualified reviewer sets the screening threshold (Q-31-07), an older or unknown-age painted surface is not abraded and is escalated (source: spec BRF-003 "approximate age if known"; 31 sections 5.8 and 7.2 rank 2).
- Evidence: note

- Appendix A checks before leaving and before starting: correct job and address, latest changes, scope and exclusions, hazards, critical tools and materials loaded, approvals confirmed; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-001, APXA-003).
- Evidence: note
- On arrival: confirm the address, work area and site contact; park and access appropriately; identify pets and occupants; inspect the site against the briefing (source: spec APXA-002).
- Weather and ground check before any ladder is raised; if unsuitable, record No Start / Blocked (source: spec HI-06.SAF "weather/ground check"; SCH-008).
- Evidence: note

> HOLD (C-HI06-01): before any ladder is raised, look for overhead power lines and service drops near the work area. If a line is near where the ladder or the work will be, do not raise the ladder: stop and escalate. The clearance distance is set only by the qualified safety professional; none is set here. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-06.HAZ "overhead power", HI-06.SAF "stop near unsafe power lines"; 31 sections 7.2 rank 4 and 10)

- Ladder setup per the approved height/access policy and the ladder manufacturer's instructions: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve. (source: spec HI-06.SAF "ladder setup"; risk-triage playbook: no invented ladder setup tolerances)
- Exclusion zone below the work area, kept clear of occupants, children and pets (source: spec HI-06.SAF "maintain exclusion zone"; X-11).
- Existing-condition photos before work: sags, leaks, fascia, roof edge and downspouts (source: spec APXA-002, START-008; X-02).
- Evidence: photo
- Protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).

All original procedure lines appear below verbatim and in their original order; the two original "Problem Option" headings are demoted one level. Added lines start with `HOLD` or `FLAG` inside a quote block and are pending qualified review.

> HOLD (C-HI06-01): whole-SOP hold. Every step below is done at gutter or roof-edge height, and no approved height/access, fall-protection, ladder, power-line or weather control exists yet. Do not perform any step below until the approved height/access policy exists and this SOP passes competent review. Cleared only by recorded approval of the qualified safety professional and the owner. (source: spec HI-06.HAZ, HI-06.SAF; 31 section 10; owner facts 2026-10-02 "Unknown is not safe")

> HOLD (C-HI06-01): before any ladder is raised for the steps below, complete the section 11 checks: weather and ground, overhead power lines (no clearance distance is set here), ladder setup per the approved policy, and the exclusion zone. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-06.SAF; 31 section 10)
- [ ] **Manual Clearance:** Scoop out packed leaves from the gutter lines, then flush the downspouts with a high-volume water line to clear subterranean blockages.

If the fascia is rotted or its condition is uncertain, do not drive fasteners: stop, record the condition (JOB-004) and escalate for a change order or referral; fascia carpentry is outside the catalog (X-05).
