lines: > Spec card HI-06.QAC (verbatim): "debris removed, flow verified, leaks/sags addressed only in approved scope, guards secure/aligned, site cleaned"
- Debris removed from gutters and downspouts (source: spec HI-06.QAC "debris removed").

- Flow verified after cleaning and after any re-pitching; method and acceptance values come from the gutter manufacturer or a qualified reviewer (none set here); the result is recorded (source: spec HI-06.QAC "flow verified"; C-HI06-V01; QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- Leaks and sags addressed only within the approved scope; anything more is recorded as a customer request or change order (source: spec HI-06.QAC; FIN-008; JOB-005).
- Evidence: note
- Guards secure and aligned along each run (source: spec HI-06.QAC "guards secure/aligned").
- Site cleaned (source: spec HI-06.QAC "site cleaned"; QA-002).

- Each check is answered, or an exception recorded, before completion (source: spec QA-001). Whether a supervisor, not only the worker, inspects any check is an owner decision (Q-31-15); a worker's self-check does not replace a required supervisor inspection (source: quality-assistant playbook).
- Evidence: note
- Remove debris, protection and exclusion-zone markers, and restore the site (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005).
- Lower and remove access equipment per the approved policy (source: spec HI-06.SAF "ladder setup"; APXA-005).
- Account for tools and materials; return unused materials (source: spec APXA-005, APXA-007).
- Restore components altered within scope (source: spec APXA-005).
- Gutter debris is bagged (source: spec HI-06.MAT "bags"); disposal destination: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve. (Q-29-10)
- Used sealant tubes, rags and scraped caulk: handling per the product SDS; destination TBD (source: 29 section 8.2 control 10; X-09).
- Screen offcuts, removed fasteners and hardware: destination TBD (source: spec QA-002 "debris/waste handling").
- Hazardous waste is not handled without an approved policy (source: 31 section 3.1, section 15 minimum content).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: existing-condition photos of sags, leaks, fascia condition, roof edge and downspouts, tagged to each run (source: spec START-008, APXA-002; 04 HI-06 card, completion evidence, PROPOSED; X-02).
- Evidence: photo
- During: the fascia behind each sagging section before fastening (C-HI06-04); any concealed condition found (source: spec JOB-004).
- After: each run after cleaning or guard installation, guard fastening and alignment, and evidence of the flow check (source: spec QA-003; HI-06.QAC).
- Photos are internal by default; marketing use needs separate consent; avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002, REC-003; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- Arrival and completion updates use approved templates only (source: 31 section 3.1, section 17 minimum content; spec NTF-007).
- Walkthrough outcome recorded: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- Care or maintenance notes only from approved product data and templates (source: spec QA-008).

- Do not promise results, permanence or warranties, and do not repeat unapproved main-plan claims such as "permanently" (C-HI06-02) or "Seamless" (C-HI06-07) (source: section 2, Do not perform entry 8; 32 claims registers).
- When work is blocked, tell the customer only what the approved "work blocked" message says (source: spec NTF-007).
- Explain the invoice and payment next step without making unauthorized promises (source: spec APXA-006).
- Every section 13 check answered, or an exception recorded (source: spec QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- After photos mapped to each run or task (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup and waste handling complete; tools and materials accounted for (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005).
- Walkthrough outcome and any punch items recorded (source: spec QA-004, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- No hold or stop-work item left unresolved (source: 31 section 8.3).
- Unresolved issues, incidents and change follow-ups submitted; the job closes only when the required operational and financial steps are complete (source: spec APXA-007).
This SOP words its general stop-work rule differently from [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]; its own text, verbatim:
> **Stop-work rule (all HandyHub services).** You have the right to stop work. For any condition below, stop the affected work and escalate before continuing (source: spec START-011, JOB-004):
> - an unsafe condition for you, the customer, occupants, pets or the public;
> - concealed damage, substrate failure, moisture or an active leak;
> - suspect hazardous material, such as possible asbestos, lead paint or mold; do not disturb it;
> - electrical, plumbing, gas, HVAC or structural work that is not in the approved scope or needs a licensed trade;
> - an aggressive occupant or animal;
> - severe weather or unsafe heat or cold (source: spec BRF-008);
> - any material mismatch between the site and the briefing, approved scope, materials, access or approvals.

> Do not continue through an unsafe or restricted condition to keep the schedule (source: master section 12). A customer request, a checkbox or a signature does not clear a safety hold (source: owner facts 2026-10-02; risk-triage playbook L27). In an emergency, move people away and call emergency services first (source: spec BRF-013; risk-triage playbook L7). Then use Stop Work / Report Hazard in the app (source: spec UXE-004) and follow section 19.
> Spec card HI-06.SAF (verbatim): "weather/ground check; ladder setup; maintain exclusion zone; stop near unsafe power lines/roof conditions or beyond approved height/access policy"
Service holds and stop triggers (pending qualified review):
- HOLD (C-HI06-01): whole-SOP hold until the approved height/access policy exists and this SOP passes competent review (sections 3 and 12).
- Stop near unsafe power lines or roof conditions, or beyond the approved height/access policy (source: spec HI-06.SAF).

- Stop for unsuitable weather or ground; do not raise a ladder on unstable or slippery ground (source: spec HI-06.SAF "weather/ground check"; HI-06.HAZ "unstable ladders", "wet/slippery surfaces"; X-27).
- Stop when anyone enters the exclusion zone (source: spec HI-06.SAF "maintain exclusion zone"; X-11).

- Rotted or uncertain fascia behind a sagging section: do not drive fasteners; stop, record and escalate for a change order or referral (source: agreement "Fascia Board Decay" clause; C-HI06-04; FIN-008; X-05).
- Evidence: note
- A downspout's underground drain backs up while flushing: stop flushing and escalate (source: 31 section 10; RISK, unverified).
- A painted surface of older or unknown age: do not abrade it; escalate (source: section 3; 31 section 7.2 rank 2).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
Service-specific routing (contacts are owner decisions, Q-31-05):
- Overhead power-line concerns: to the owner, who consults the electric utility (no conclusion drawn here) (source: 31 section 7.2 rank 4; 04 HI-06 card, permit/license flags).
- Rotted fascia: to the owner for a change order or referral; fascia carpentry is outside the catalog (source: agreement "Fascia Board Decay" clause; X-05; Q-30-15).
- Roof or shingle damage: to the owner for referral to a roofing professional (source: 04 section 5.9).

- Suspect lead paint on older painted surfaces: to the owner for review by an EPA RRP-certified renovator; applicability is not concluded (source: 04 HI-06 card, permit/license flags; 31 section 7.2 rank 2).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].
- Q-31-09 — Height and access policy: maximum working heights, equipment types and the second-person rule for ladder work. Owner; qualified safety professional.
- Q-31-08 — Is roof-edge guard installation (the "Roofline Slide" step) offered at all, or referred out? Owner; relevant reviewers (roofing professional).
- Q-31-07 — Which property-age threshold triggers lead screening before wire-wheel work on painted gutters or fascia? Owner; EPA RRP-certified renovator.
- Q-31-05 — Emergency and escalation contacts, escalation order and after-hours coverage for a two-person team. Owner.
- Q-31-15 — Which section 13 checks need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check? Owner.
- Q-31-01 — Who are the competent reviewers (qualified safety professional, roofing and carpentry reviewers) and how is their competence evidenced? Owner.
- Q-31-02 — Who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish version? Owner.

sops.title: SOP HI-07: Attic Insulation Upgrades

lines: - PROPOSED customer checklist, sent with the appointment reminder once the owner and attorney approve the wording: clear path and space under the hatch; pets and occupants plan; disclose known leaks, pests, wiring and existing insulation (source: 04 HI-07 customer preparation requirements; spec NTF-005 "customer-preparation checklist"; CX-005).
- The crew, not the customer, protects the floor under the hatch (original "Site Masking" step); whether the hatch room is wrapped as the agreement says is an owner decision (C-HI07-08).
- On arrival, identify pets and occupants and keep them away from the active work area; the occupant and pet module is pending qualified safety review (source: spec APXA-002; X-11; 31 section 5.8).

- A customer's preparation or statement never replaces HandyHub's own pre-work inspection (source: 30 section 4.1 clause 5 "never moves HandyHub's own pre-start checks onto the customer"; risk-triage playbook "Signing a checkbox cannot bypass an unresolved structural hazard.").
All pending qualified review. A precondition that is not met keeps the affected tasks blocked (source: job-planner playbook "A missing ladder or unverified permit keeps affected tasks blocked.").

- On-site assessment before a firm quote: missing hazardous-condition decisions block a firm quote, and photos alone cannot establish hidden conditions (source: estimate-assistant playbook; 04 HI-07 estimating method, PROPOSED).

- The approved estimate records the product, the target coverage and depth, and the counts of eave bays and recessed lights; the fixed depth in section 12 is not the target (source: spec HI-07.QAC "target coverage/depth per approved plan"; 04 HI-07 prerequisites; C-HI07-06).
- Evidence: note

- Pre-work inspection gate (C-HI07-01): pre-inspect moisture/electrical/combustion concerns; stop on mold, active leak or unsafe wiring; unknown or suspect existing insulation, for example vermiculite, is not disturbed (source: spec HI-07.SAF; 31 section 10). Release only by a recorded qualified assessment (31 section 8.3).
- Evidence: note

- Attic controls (C-HI07-02): attic travel, fall-through, heat-stress, low-clearance and respiratory controls approved by a qualified safety professional; until they exist the attic steps stay on hold (source: spec HI-07.HAZ, HI-07.SAF; 31 sections 8.4 and 10).

- Combustion concerns found at the inspection (flues, vents, gas appliances): stop and refer to an HVAC or gas professional; clearances come only from manufacturer data or that professional and are never estimated (source: spec HI-07.SAF; 31 section 10; risk-triage playbook "Use manufacturer/SDS guidance").

- Permit, licence or qualification flags: where admin policy marks the job, Start Job is blocked until the prerequisite is approved (source: spec START-010). Whether retrofit insulation needs a permit or inspection is an OPEN QUESTION per Kentucky and Indiana municipality, and unknown applicability must not default to "no permit" (source: 04 HI-07 permit/license flags; risk-triage playbook).

- Before leaving: confirm job, customer, address and time; read the latest changes; review scope, exclusions, hazards and safety; load critical tools, equipment and materials; check rentals (the blower may be rented); confirm required documents and approvals (source: spec APXA-001).

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; confirm materials; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003). High-risk flags may require separate checkboxes or supervisor confirmation (source: spec START-004).
- Evidence: note
- Materials readiness: missing material may block start, for example an approved fixture-protection material, which is not stocked (source: spec START-006; C-HI07-V01).

- On arrival: confirm address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants; inspect the actual site against the briefing; capture the required existing-condition photos; protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- Pre-start site check: record any difference from the briefing; material differences trigger Risk Triage or supervisor review (source: spec START-007).
- Evidence: note

- Protection: the original "Site Masking" step (section 12) covers the floor under the hatch; keep protection and containment in place during work (source: spec APXA-004 "keep protection/containment"; containment standard C-HI07-08).

- Blower staging: outside, per the original step ("into the commercial blowing machine hopper outside"); set-up and pre-use check per the blower manufacturer (source: original step; 31 section 3.1, tools row "pre-use inspection per manufacturer").
- Pre-start evidence: existing-condition photos before start (source: spec START-008; section 16).
- Evidence: photo

*Original procedure, verbatim and in its original order. The HOLD and FLAG lines are additions pending qualified review: a precondition hold sits directly before the step it gates, and a hold or flag that suspends, limits or flags a step sits directly after it (36 D-36-17). They never replace or reword a step.*

> HOLD (C-HI07-01) - pre-work inspection gate, before the first step below ("Site Masking") and before any work in the attic: pre-inspect moisture/electrical/combustion concerns and record what is found with photos (spec HI-07.SAF; JOB-004). Stop on mold, active leak or unsafe wiring (spec HI-07.SAF). Release only by a recorded qualified assessment (31 section 8.3). Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-07.SAF; 31 section 10)

lines: > HOLD (C-HI07-01) - before the first step below: unknown or suspect existing insulation, for example vermiculite: do not disturb; stop; escalate. No HandyHub sampling; release only on documented clearance from a qualified asbestos professional accepted by the owner (31 section 7.2). Pending qualified review. (source: 31 section 10; spec START-011; owner facts 2026-10-02, EPA asbestos source)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Execution Flow"

lines: - [ ] **Site Masking:** Cover the entire floor hallway directly beneath the attic hatch entry with plastic drops to trap loose blown fibers.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Execution Flow"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI07-02) - before the step below ("Soffit Ventilation Baffle Placement") and every later attic step ("Fixtures Isolation", "Pneumatic Blow-In Application"): attic travel and fall-through, heat-stress, low-clearance and respiratory and skin protection controls must be approved by a qualified safety professional and in place. None is defined yet, and no temperature limit or respirator type is set here; until they exist the attic steps stay on hold (31 section 8.4). Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-07.HAZ, HI-07.SAF, HI-07.TLS; 31 section 10; X-12, X-27)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Execution Flow"

lines: - [ ] **Soffit Ventilation Baffle Placement:** Crawl into the low attic perimeter edges. Install plastic or styrofoam insulation baffles (rafter vents) directly into every single joist bay near the soffit vents. *Crucial: This ensures fresh airflow is not blocked by loose insulation, which causes roof ice dams.*
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Execution Flow"

lines: - [ ] **Fixtures Isolation:** Build protective fire-rated drywall boxes around the top of hot recessed can lights to isolate them from loose insulation elements.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Execution Flow"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI07-03): the step above is held. Do not build or install fixture protection until a licensed electrician approves the method, materials and clearances from the fixture manufacturer's instructions and applicable requirements. This hold also limits the blow-in step below: if a fixture's type or rating is unknown, or it is damaged or not approved, stop, keep insulation out of the clearance zone and escalate; do not cover unsafe fixtures/vents (spec HI-07.SAF). Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-07.SAF, HI-07.MAT "approved light/penetration protection materials"; spec section 17 intro; 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Execution Flow"

lines: - [ ] **Pneumatic Blow-In Application:** Feed premium fiberglass or cellulose insulation bags into the commercial blowing machine hopper outside. The attic technician will direct the hose uniformly, filling the floor joists to a depth of 16–20 inches to hit the regional code target (R-49 to R-60 value).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Execution Flow"

lines: > FLAG (C-HI07-06, C-HI07-05): UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions. "to a depth of 16–20 inches to hit the regional code target (R-49 to R-60 value)": the depth comes from the approved estimate and the selected product's coverage chart (spec HI-07.QAC "target coverage/depth per approved plan"), and the code-target wording is an unverified regulatory claim until local requirements are verified for each Kentucky and Indiana municipality. The step text above is unchanged. HUMAN REVIEW: owner; local building official; attorney.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 📋 Standard Operational Execution Flow"

lines: A worker cannot mark the job complete without answering these checks or recording an exception (source: spec QA-001). Photos cannot prove hidden conditions: do not infer hazardous-material clearance or electrical safety from an image (source: quality-assistant playbook).
| Check (spec HI-07.QAC) | How it is verified (pending review) | Evidence | Inspector |

| Target coverage/depth per approved plan | Measured at the depth markers against the depth and product in the approved estimate, not the fixed range in section 12 (C-HI07-06) | Depth-marker photos per area; product and bag-count record (04 HI-07 completion evidence, PROPOSED) | Worker self-check; whether a supervisor must inspect is Q-31-15 |
| Vents clear | Baffles in place at the eaves; soffit ventilation maintained (spec HI-07.SAF) | Baffle photos per eave run (04 HI-07, PROPOSED) | Worker |

| Fixtures protected as required | Only by a method a licensed electrician approved; unknown fixtures kept clear (C-HI07-03 hold) | Fixture-protection photos (04 HI-07, PROPOSED) | Worker; licensed electrician where the approved method requires it |
| Access/weatherstripping restored | Hatch closed and restored; weatherstripping restoration has no step yet (section 2, Out of scope) | Hatch photo (04 HI-07, PROPOSED) | Worker |

| No insulation contamination in living space | Living space checked after protection is removed (spec QA-002) | Living-space photos (04 HI-07, PROPOSED) | Worker; the customer walkthrough (spec QA-004) is not a safety inspection |
- Remove the protection installed in the "Site Masking" step and check the living space for insulation contamination (source: spec QA-002; HI-07.QAC "no insulation contamination in living space").
- Clean the area; remove waste and protection; account for tools and materials; restore utilities or components altered within scope (source: spec APXA-005).
- Cleanup photos may be required for dusty work (source: spec QA-002); see section 16.
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup method and vacuum dust class: TBD - pending qualified safety review (source: spec HI-07.TLS "vacuum").
TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.
- Waste from the steps: empty insulation bags and used plastic sheeting (source: original steps "Site Masking" and "Pneumatic Blow-In Application"; spec QA-002 "debris/waste handling").
- Containers, destination and who pays: owner decision with the local rules of the actual municipality (source: 31 section 3.1, waste row; 29 section 8.2 control 10).
- Suspect hazardous material is not bagged, moved or removed (source: section 2, Do not perform; spec START-011).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: arrival and existing-condition photos; start is blocked until they are captured or an authorized reason is recorded (source: spec START-008). Include what the pre-work inspection finds: moisture, wiring or fixture concerns, combustion concerns and existing insulation (source: spec HI-07.SAF; JOB-004).
- Evidence: photo, note
- During: concealed conditions recorded with photos and severity (source: spec APXA-004; JOB-004); baffle and depth-marker placement (source: 04 HI-07 completion evidence, PROPOSED).
- Evidence: note

- After: photos mapped to work areas or tasks (source: spec QA-003): depth markers per area, baffles per eave run, fixture protection, hatch and weatherstripping restored, living space clean (source: 04 HI-07 completion evidence, PROPOSED); cleanup photos where required (source: spec QA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- Privacy: internal-only by default; avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).

- Arrival and completion updates use approved templates; a blocked job uses only the approved "work blocked" message, with no incident details or access codes by text or email (source: spec NTF-007, COM-002).

- Rot, water stains, active leaks, mold, wiring or combustion concerns: stop and escalate first (section 19); the customer is then told in approved wording. The agreement's notify-only clause is under attorney review (source: spec HI-07.SAF; C-HI07-01).
- Walkthrough: record the outcome as accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Care and handoff notes come only from approved product data (source: spec QA-008; quality-assistant playbook "Prepare handoff instructions from approved product data").
- Do not state that the work meets a code, reaches an R-value standard or will lower energy bills, and make no warranty statement (source: section 2, Do not perform item 8; C-HI07-05).
- Explain the invoice and payment next step without unauthorized promises (source: spec APXA-006).
Done means all of the following, recorded in the job (source: spec QA-001 to QA-004; HI-07.QAC; APXA-005 to APXA-007):
- Every section 13 check answered, or an exception recorded (QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- After photos mapped to areas or tasks (QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Protection removed and cleanup done, with no insulation contamination in the living space (QA-002; HI-07.QAC).
- Hatch and access restored (HI-07.QAC).
- Tools and materials accounted for; rentals returned (APXA-005, APXA-007).
- Walkthrough outcome recorded, with punch items (QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Unresolved issues, incidents and change requests submitted before the job is closed (APXA-007).
- Final completion is a human sign-off; the quality review only recommends readiness (source: quality-assistant playbook "Recommend readiness for human sign-off; do not set final completion").
- Evidence: note
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:
Service-specific stop triggers and holds (all pending qualified review; release roles per 31 section 8.3):

- Card guidance, verbatim: "pre-inspect moisture/electrical/combustion concerns; do not cover unsafe fixtures/vents; maintain soffit ventilation; use respiratory/skin protection; stop on mold, active leak or unsafe wiring" (source: spec HI-07.SAF).

- HOLD C-HI07-01, pre-work inspection gate before the first step: release only by a recorded qualified assessment. Suspect hazardous material and unapproved electrical, gas or HVAC scope are critical holds that no role can override (31 section 8.3); suspected mold is treated as critical until the company mold definition exists (31 section 8.4; Q-31-10).
- Evidence: note

- HOLD C-HI07-01, unknown or suspect existing insulation (for example vermiculite): do not disturb; release only on documented clearance from a qualified asbestos professional accepted by the owner (31 section 7.2).
- Evidence: note

- HOLD C-HI07-02, attic travel, heat, fall-through, low-clearance and respiratory controls: the attic steps stay on hold until a qualified safety professional approves the controls; a hold caused by a missing policy cannot be released by override (31 section 8.4).

- HOLD C-HI07-03, fixture protection: the "Fixtures Isolation" step is held until a licensed electrician approves the method; if a fixture's type or rating is unknown, stop and keep insulation out of the clearance zone.
- Combustion concern (flue, vent or gas appliance): stop and refer to an HVAC or gas professional (spec HI-07.HAZ "combustion/ventilation issues").
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
Service roles for HI-07 (contacts and escalation order are owner decisions, Q-31-05):
- Wiring, junction boxes or recessed fixtures: licensed electrician (C-HI07-03).
- Flues, vents or gas appliances: HVAC or gas professional (spec HI-07.HAZ).
- Unknown or suspect existing insulation: accredited asbestos inspector (C-HI07-01).
- Mold: qualified mold assessor or industrial hygienist (X-06; Q-31-10).
- Heat, falls, low clearance and respiratory protection: qualified safety professional (C-HI07-02).
- Roof leaks or rafter rot: owner, for the referral decision (Q-30-15).
- Code, permit or R-value questions: owner, with the local building official (C-HI07-05).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].

- For this service, report at least a fall or step-through of the ceiling, heat illness, insulation or dust exposure, and blower or hose failure (source: spec JOB-008; HI-07.HAZ "heat stress", "falls through ceiling", "dust/fibers").

- **Q-31-07** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: EPA RRP-certified renovator, accredited asbestos inspector): which property-age thresholds trigger lead and asbestos screening for attic work, and does HandyHub hold or plan EPA RRP certification?
- **Q-31-08** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: licensed electrician): is fixture boxing offered at all, or referred out?

- **Q-31-01** (owner): who are the competent reviewers for this SOP (qualified safety professional, licensed electrician, HVAC or gas professional, asbestos inspector), and how is their competence evidenced?
- **Q-31-05** (owner): emergency and escalation contacts and escalation order for attic work by a two-person team.
- **Q-31-09** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional): height and access policy for the hatch ladder and joist travel.
- **Q-31-10** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified mold assessor): company definition of mold growth and the stop rule.
- **Q-31-11** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional): emergency kit contents and the SDS register owner.
- **Q-31-15** (owner): do the depth and fixture-protection checks need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check?
- **Q-31-02** (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish version?

- **02 C-HI07-05** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: local building official, attorney): which R-value target, if any, applies per Kentucky and Indiana municipality, and should this SOP name any code target at all?
- **02 C-HI07-08** (owner): which containment standard is intended: floor protection (this SOP) or a full hatch-room wrap (agreement)?
- **02 C-HI07-V01** (owner; HUMAN REVIEW: licensed electrician, local building official): is top-plate penetration sealing in scope at all?
- **02 C-HI07-12** (owner): which baffle materials are approved?

sops.title: SOP HI-08: Closet & Shelving System Installation

lines: - The customer clears all clothes, boxes and personal items out of the closet before the technician arrives (source: agreement "Closet Clearance" clause); the appointment confirmation and reminder carry this as the preparation checklist (source: spec NTF-004, NTF-005).
- The customer-supplied kit is on site, complete, with its manufacturer instructions (source: spec START-009; 29 section 9.1).
- Obstructions such as closet lights or outlets are identified at intake; HandyHub does not move them (source: spec HI-08.INT "obstructions"; Do not perform 10).
- Every job re-confirms access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions (source: spec CX-005).

- The approved estimate version states the system model and who supplies it, the layout and dimensions, the desired heights, the wall or substrate, obstructions and the customer's expected load (source: spec HI-08.INT "wall/substrate, dimensions/layout, load expectation, system model, obstructions, desired heights"; CX-003).
- The substrate is drywall over a hollow cavity (Option A) or wood framing studs (Option B); any other substrate is a stop condition (section 10) (source: 31 section 10 HI-08).

- The system and anchor manufacturer's instructions, rated load and spacing are available for the job. If they are unknown, fastening does not start (source: spec HI-08.SAF "confirm load path/fastener rating ... follow manufacturer spacing"; C-HI08-03).

- The customer-supplied kit is on site; its visible condition, model and quantity are recorded, and missing or defective parts are recorded as an unexpected condition (source: spec START-009, JOB-004).
- Evidence: note
- Critical tools are loaded or an exception is recorded, including a scanner able to locate studs and utilities (source: spec START-005; HI-08.SAF; inventory file, proposed additions).
- Evidence: note

- The closet is cleared by the customer (source: agreement "Closet Clearance" clause). If it is not, record the access issue with evidence and escalate; the worker does not quote or apply any fee (source: spec SCH-008, JOB-004, JOB-005).

- The approximate build year is recorded ("unknown" is a valid value) so that older painted or textured walls are screened before drilling; the property-age thresholds are an open question (source: spec BRF-003 "approximate age if known"; 04 HI-08 hazards; Q-31-07).
- Evidence: note
- Occupants, children and pets are identified and kept out of the work area (source: spec APXA-002 "identify pets/occupants", CX-005; X-11).
- Work at height happens only under an approved height and access policy, which does not exist yet (source: 02 G-005; X-12).
- Start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003).
- Evidence: note

- On arrival: confirm the address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants; inspect the site against the briefing; capture the required existing-condition photos; protect the work area; identify the utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; confirm materials and models against the approved scope; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003).
- Evidence: note
- Confirm the layout, dimensions and desired heights against the approved scope before "Laser Level Baseline"; a changed layout needs a change order (source: spec HI-08.INT; JOB-005; FIN-008).
- Check the customer-supplied kit against its manufacturer instructions and the START-009 record (source: spec START-009; 29 section 9.1).
- Evidence: note
- Record the system and anchor manufacturer's rated load and spacing and the customer's expected load in the job record before any drilling (source: spec HI-08.SAF; C-HI08-03).
- Evidence: note

Original procedure text is kept verbatim and in its original order. Lines that start with HOLD or FLAG are added draft controls pending qualified review (source: 31 section 10 HI-08). A HOLD placed before a step must be cleared before that step starts; a HOLD or FLAG placed after a step limits or flags the step above it.
- [ ] **Laser Level Baseline:** Project a horizontal green laser line along the target back wall at the exact height required for the main support track.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Securing Wire Track Systems into Drywall Hollows"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI08-02): before "Top Track Drilling" below, scan the drilling and fastening path for wiring, pipes, gas lines and other hidden services with a scanner able to locate them, used per its manufacturer instructions, and record the result. The listed magnetic stud finder is not shown to locate wiring or pipes (section 7; C-HI08-10); a scan with a device whose ability to detect them is not established does not clear the path and counts as inconclusive. If a service is detected, the result is inconclusive or the cavity cannot be cleared, STOP and escalate (section 19). Release: section 10. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-08.HAZ "drilling hidden utilities"; HI-08.SAF "locate studs/utilities"; owner facts 2026-10-02 "Unknown is not safe")

lines: > HOLD (C-HI08-03): before "Top Track Drilling" below, confirm that the wall is drywall over a hollow cavity; metal studs, plaster, masonry and tile are not covered: STOP and escalate. Confirm the toggle anchor and track system manufacturer's rated load and spacing and record them with the customer's expected load; if either is unknown, or the expected load exceeds the rating, STOP. Release: section 10. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-08.SAF "confirm load path/fastener rating ... follow manufacturer spacing; do not overload wall/substrate"; 31 section 10 HI-08)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Securing Wire Track Systems into Drywall Hollows"

lines: - [ ] **Top Track Drilling:** Align the metal top track, mark the pre-bored holes, and drill 1/2-inch holes through the drywall.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Securing Wire Track Systems into Drywall Hollows"

lines: - [ ] **Toggle Bolt Fastening:** Push heavy-duty metal toggle anchors through the track holes, thread them into the drywall cavity until the spring-wings flip open, and drive the bolts tight using an impact driver.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Securing Wire Track Systems into Drywall Hollows"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI08-03): the step above is limited by the anchor manufacturer's instructions: tighten per the anchor manufacturer instructions and at the spacing recorded for the job - pending review. "drive the bolts tight using an impact driver" sets no torque and does not override those instructions. (source: 02 C-HI08-03; spec section 17 "Service-card defaults never override a site-specific hazard, manufacturer instruction")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Securing Wire Track Systems into Drywall Hollows"

lines: - [ ] **Standard Hanging:** Hang the vertical shelf standards into the top track, verify perfect square alignment, and clip wire shelf brackets into place.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Securing Wire Track Systems into Drywall Hollows"

lines: - [ ] **Stud Mapping:** Locate all vertical wood framing studs using a deep-scanning sensor; trace their center columns along the wall line.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Anchor Locking into Natural Wood Framing Studs"

lines: > FLAG (C-HI08-10): the step above names a "deep-scanning sensor", while the inventory lists a "Magnetic Stud Finder with Center Target Laser"; which scanner is standard is an open question. Mapping studs is not the hidden-service check, which follows below. If the framing found is not wood, for example metal studs, STOP: Option B does not cover it. (source: inventory file; 31 section 10 HI-08)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Anchor Locking into Natural Wood Framing Studs"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI08-02): before "Direct Wood Driving" below, scan the fastening path along each traced stud center for wiring, pipes, gas lines and other hidden services with a scanner able to locate them, used per its manufacturer instructions, and record the result. The listed magnetic stud finder is not shown to locate wiring or pipes (section 7; C-HI08-10); a scan with a device whose ability to detect them is not established does not clear the path and counts as inconclusive. If a service is detected, the result is inconclusive or the path cannot be cleared, STOP and escalate (section 19). Release: section 10. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-08.HAZ "drilling hidden utilities"; HI-08.SAF "locate studs/utilities"; owner facts 2026-10-02 "Unknown is not safe")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Anchor Locking into Natural Wood Framing Studs"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI08-03): before "Direct Wood Driving" below, confirm the track system and fastener manufacturer's rated load and spacing and record them with the customer's expected load; if either is unknown, or the expected load exceeds the rating, STOP. Release: section 10. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-08.SAF "confirm load path/fastener rating ... follow manufacturer spacing; do not overload wall/substrate")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Anchor Locking into Natural Wood Framing Studs"

lines: - [ ] **Direct Wood Driving:** Screw the main support tracks and vertical shelf standard lines directly into the centers of the wood studs using 2.5-inch structural wood screws without plastic anchors. This guarantees maximum load limits for heavy clothing arrays or garage storage boxes.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Anchor Locking into Natural Wood Framing Studs"

lines: > FLAG: outcome claim - owner and attorney review (C-HI08-01). The sentence "This guarantees maximum load limits for heavy clothing arrays or garage storage boxes." in the step above is kept verbatim; it is not an approved claim and sets no load limit. Load limits come only from the manufacturer's ratings recorded for the job (spec HI-08.SAF "do not overload wall/substrate"); never repeat the claim to a customer (Do not perform 8). (source: 31 section 10 HI-08; 02 C-HI08-01)

- The worker cannot mark the job complete without answering these checks or recording an exception (source: spec QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- Photos cannot prove hidden fastener or load adequacy; a missing mounting verification needs inspection, not approval (source: quality-assistant playbook; 04 HI-08 completion evidence).
- Vacuum drilling dust and remove debris and packaging from the work area (source: spec HI-08.QAC "area clean", QA-002).
- Remove protection, account for tools and materials, and restore components altered within scope (source: spec APXA-005).
- Return unused materials and record leftover customer-supplied parts (source: spec APXA-007; 29 section 9.1).
- Evidence: note
- Expected waste from the current steps: drilling dust, kit packaging, leftover hardware and, if cutting is authorized, wire or track offcuts (source: section 12; inventory file).
- Destination, who removes the waste and any charge: TBD — owner decision; no waste policy exists (source: 31 section 3.1; 02 G-078).
- Removal or disposal of existing shelving is not covered (section 2).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: arrival and existing-condition photos of the wall and closet, and the customer-supplied kit's condition and model (source: spec START-008, START-009, APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- During: fastener locations before shelves or components cover them (source: 04 HI-08 completion evidence, PROPOSED; quality-assistant playbook).
- After: the level check, the installed components and the cleaned area, each tagged to its work area or task (source: spec QA-003; 04 HI-08 completion evidence).
- Photos are internal-only by default and avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- Arrival and completion updates are drafts; the worker or admin controls the send (source: spec UXE-008).
- Record the walkthrough outcome: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Care notes: give the customer the system and anchor manufacturer's rated load limits and care instructions from approved product data (source: spec QA-008; 02 C-HI08-01).
- Describe the method actually used, Option A (toggle anchors in drywall hollows) or Option B (screws into wood studs); the website copy that mixes them is flagged (source: C-HI08-11).
- Never state or "certify" a load capacity, and never repeat the "guarantee" or "certification" wording of the SOP, pricing file or main plan (source: Do not perform 8; C-HI08-01).
- Blocked work: tell the customer only what the approved "work blocked" message says (source: spec NTF-007, COM-002).
- Price or scope changes, including any fee, are not agreed on site without a recorded change order (source: spec JOB-005, FIN-008).
- All section 13 checks answered or an exception recorded (source: spec QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- After photos captured and mapped to tasks (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup done, protection removed, tools and materials accounted for (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005).
- Manufacturer rating, spacing and the customer's expected load recorded; care notes with the rated limits given (source: spec HI-08.SAF, QA-008).
- Evidence: note
- Customer-supplied kit leftovers and any missing parts recorded (source: spec START-009; 29 section 9.1).
- Evidence: note
- Walkthrough outcome recorded (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Unresolved issues, incidents and change follow-ups submitted before the job is closed (source: spec APXA-007).
- The worker recommends completion for human sign-off; a customer signature does not clear an unresolved safety hold (source: quality-assistant playbook).
- Evidence: note
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:
**HI-08 stop triggers (draft, pending qualified review).** In addition, stop the affected work and escalate (section 19) when:

- a utility or other hidden service is detected in the drilling or fastening path, the scan is inconclusive, or the cavity cannot be cleared (source: spec HI-08.HAZ; HI-08.SAF "locate studs/utilities"; C-HI08-02);

- the system or anchor manufacturer's rated load or spacing is unknown, or the customer's expected load exceeds it (source: spec HI-08.SAF "confirm load path/fastener rating ... follow manufacturer spacing; do not overload wall/substrate"; C-HI08-03);
- the substrate is not drywall over a hollow cavity (Option A) or wood framing studs (Option B), for example metal studs, plaster, masonry or tile (source: 31 section 10 HI-08);
- closet lights, outlets or other electrical items are in the way of the layout (source: Do not perform 10; spec START-011);
- suspect hazardous material is found, or the build-year or surface screening is not cleared, before drilling older painted or textured walls (source: spec START-011; 04 HI-08 hazards);
- the customer-supplied kit is missing parts, damaged or not the approved model (source: spec START-009, JOB-004);
- the work needs a ladder or step stool and no approved height and access policy exists (source: spec HI-08.HAZ; 02 G-005; X-12);
- occupants or pets cannot be kept clear of the work area (source: X-11).

Release role and release evidence for each trigger: `<reviewer decision: release role and evidence>` (31 section 8.3). Which of these triggers are critical holds that no role can override is pending (Q-31-18).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
- HI-08 roles and contacts: `<owner decision: escalation order and contacts>` (Q-31-05).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].

- From the register, C-HI08-05 (owner): are layout design and wooden or custom shelving launch scope? If yes, SOP sections and inventory items are drafted for review; if no, they are marked not offered.

- From the register, C-HI08-03 (owner; qualified safety professional; experienced lead installer): adopt a decision rule between Option A and Option B (studs where available; anchors only within the manufacturer's rating and spacing)?
- From the register, C-HI08-10 (owner; lead installer): which scanner is standard for stud and utility detection?
- Q-31-01 (owner): who are the competent reviewers for this SOP, and how is their competence evidenced?
- Q-31-07 (owner; EPA RRP-certified renovator; accredited asbestos inspector): which property-age thresholds trigger lead and asbestos screening before drilling older painted or textured walls?
- Q-31-09 (owner; qualified safety professional): the height and access policy that ladder or step-stool work depends on (X-12).
- Q-31-11 (owner; qualified safety professional): emergency kit contents (X-10).
- Q-31-05 (owner): emergency and escalation contacts and their order for sections 19 and 20.
- Q-31-15 (owner): which section 13 checks need a supervisor rather than a self-check.
- Q-31-16 (owner; attorney): who approves replacement wording for the flagged "guarantees" sentence in a revised SOP version.
- Q-31-18 (qualified safety professional; owner): which HI-08 holds are critical holds under 31 section 8.4.
- Q-31-02 (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish version.
- Q-36-08 (31 owner; owner; qualified safety professional): accept the placement of precondition holds before the step they gate, as used in section 12 of this file.

sops.title: SOP HI-09: Custom Trim & Architectural Molding Installation

lines: - PROPOSED checklist for review, sent with the appointment confirmation and reminder: move furniture and wall decor away from the work walls; plan access and pets; name items to protect; state any noise or dust sensitivity (source: 04 HI-09 "customer preparation requirements", PROPOSED; spec BRF-005, NTF-004, NTF-005). Who moves furniture is an owner decision; the agreement has no preparation clause (30 section 4.2, clause 5).

- Paint or stain responsibility is agreed before the visit; final paint coats are not part of this service unless a separate painting agreement covers them (source: spec HI-09.INT "paint/stain responsibility"; agreement "Prep vs Painting" clause).
- Every job re-confirms access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions (source: spec CX-005).

- The approved estimate version states the trim type and profile, the material and who supplies it, the finish state, room dimensions, wall and ceiling condition, corner geometry and who paints or stains (source: spec HI-09.INT "room dimensions, profile/material, finish state, wall/ceiling condition, corner geometry, paint/stain responsibility"; CX-003).

- Trim stock and the critical materials are on site and match the approved profile and quantity, or an exception is recorded (source: spec START-006; HI-09.MAT "trim/molding, fasteners, adhesive/caulk as specified, filler, shims"). If the customer supplies the stock, its visible condition, profile and quantity are recorded before installation (source: spec START-009; 29 section 9.1).
- Evidence: note

- Critical tools are loaded or an exception is recorded, including the approved fastening system and a scanner able to locate framing and hidden wiring and pipes (source: spec START-005; HI-09.TLS; HI-09.SAF "scan fastening paths"; inventory file, proposed additions).
- Evidence: note

- The guard, PPE and dust-collection selection for cutting and nailing is recorded by the qualified safety professional; until then cutting and nailing stay on hold (source: spec HI-09.SAF "guarded tool use; eye/hearing protection; dust collection"; C-HI09-01).
- Evidence: note

- The approximate build year is recorded ("unknown" is a valid value). If the work would remove, cut or sand existing painted trim or other painted surfaces in a home built before 1978 or of unknown build year, that work is held until a qualified person records a disposition (source: spec BRF-003 "approximate age if known"; 31 section 10 HI-09; X-13; Q-31-07).
- Evidence: note

- Outlets, switches or other electrical devices inside the planned trim or wainscot layout are identified at intake; HandyHub does not extend boxes or move devices (source: 04 HI-09 "stop-work conditions", PROPOSED; Do not perform 9).
- Occupants, children and pets are identified and kept out of the work area (source: spec APXA-002 "identify pets/occupants", CX-005; X-11).
- Ceiling-height or other ladder work happens only under an approved height and access policy, which does not exist yet (source: 02 G-005; X-12).
- Start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003).
- Evidence: note

- On arrival: confirm the address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants; inspect the site against the briefing; capture the required existing-condition photos; protect the work area; identify the utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; confirm materials and models against the approved scope; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003).
- Evidence: note
- Protect floors, furniture and finished surfaces in and next to the work area before cutting or fastening (source: spec HI-09.HAZ "finish damage"; APXA-002 "protect work area").

- Set up the miter saw on its stand with the guarding and dust collection selected under section 6, per the saw manufacturer's instructions (source: inventory file "Mounted on a rolling stand platform"; spec HI-09.SAF "guarded tool use ... dust collection").
- Confirm the trim profile, room dimensions, corner geometry and layout against the approved scope before any cut; a changed scope needs a change order (source: spec HI-09.INT; JOB-005; FIN-008).

- Record wall and ceiling conditions such as dips, waves and out-of-square corners in the existing-condition photos before work (source: spec HI-09.INT "wall/ceiling condition"; START-008; agreement section "Craftsmanship Standards & Room Anomalies").
- Evidence: photo, note

Original procedure text is kept verbatim and in its original order. Lines that start with HOLD or FLAG are added draft controls pending qualified review (source: 31 section 10 HI-09). A HOLD placed before a step must be cleared before that step starts; a HOLD or FLAG placed after a step limits or flags the step above it.

> HOLD (X-13): no step below removes, cuts or sands existing painted trim or other existing painted surfaces; removal of existing trim is not covered (section 2). If a job would require that in a home built before 1978 or of unknown build year, STOP before that work: it stays on hold until a qualified person records a disposition, and a customer statement does not clear it. Whether the EPA RRP rule applies is not concluded here (Q-31-07). Release: section 10. Pending review by an EPA RRP-certified renovator. (source: 31 section 10 HI-09; risk-triage playbook "A pre-1978 painted surface is not cleared by a customer saying it looks safe")

> HOLD (C-HI09-01): before "Compound Cut Calculation" below, and before any other saw cut, the miter saw is used only with guarded tool use, eye and hearing protection and dust collection, as the spec card requires, and per the saw manufacturer's instructions. The guard, PPE and dust-collection selection is pending the qualified safety professional; until it is recorded, cutting stays on hold. Release: section 10. (source: spec HI-09.SAF "guarded tool use; eye/hearing protection; dust collection"; HI-09.HAZ "saw/nailer injury, dust")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Installing Crown Molding on Wavy Ceilings"

lines: - [ ] **Compound Cut Calculation:** Set your dual-compound miter saw table angle and bevel tilt exactly to the wood's profile specification (standard is 31.6-degree miter and 33.9-degree bevel). Cut inside/outside corners upside-down and backward.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Installing Crown Molding on Wavy Ceilings"

lines: > FLAG: UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions. The settings "standard is 31.6-degree miter and 33.9-degree bevel" in the step above are kept verbatim and are not verified for any molding profile or corner. HYPOTHESIS for review: fixed compound settings suit only one molding spring angle and corner angle, and cutting corners "upside-down and backward" is usually an alternative to compound settings, not an addition to them. An experienced finish carpenter confirms the method and the settings from the molding profile, the measured corner geometry and the saw manufacturer's instructions. (source: 31 section 10 HI-09; 04 HI-09 "SOP reference"; spec HI-09.INT "corner geometry")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Installing Crown Molding on Wavy Ceilings"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI09-01; X-12): before "The Shimming Fix" below and the other ceiling-height steps of Option A, a ladder or other access equipment is used only under the approved height and access policy, which does not exist yet (02 G-005); until it does, ceiling-height work is held. No ladder type or setup rule is set here. Release: section 10. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-09.HAZ "ladder"; HI-09.SAF "ladder controls"; 31 section 8.4 rule 4, PROPOSED)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Installing Crown Molding on Wavy Ceilings"

lines: - [ ] **The Shimming Fix:** If the residential ceiling dips or waves, do not force the crown molding flat—it will warp the joint line. Slide thin wooden wedges (shims) behind the molding back edge to bridge hollow gaps.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Installing Crown Molding on Wavy Ceilings"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI09-01): before "Pneumatic Brad Driving" below, scan every nailing path in the ceiling and wall framing for wiring, pipes and other hidden services with a scanner able to locate them, used per its manufacturer instructions, and record the result. If a service is detected or the result is inconclusive, STOP and escalate (section 19). Release: section 10. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-09.SAF "scan fastening paths"; HI-09.HAZ "hidden wiring/pipes")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Installing Crown Molding on Wavy Ceilings"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI09-01): before "Pneumatic Brad Driving" below, the nailer is used only per its manufacturer's instructions, with guarded tool use and the eye and hearing protection that the qualified safety professional selects; until that selection is recorded, nailing stays on hold. Release: section 10. (source: spec HI-09.SAF "guarded tool use; eye/hearing protection"; HI-09.HAZ "saw/nailer injury")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Installing Crown Molding on Wavy Ceilings"

lines: - [ ] **Pneumatic Brad Driving:** Fire 2-inch brad nails through the trim molding straight into solid wood ceiling plates and wall studs.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Installing Crown Molding on Wavy Ceilings"

lines: > FLAG (C-HI09-05): the step above names a pneumatic brad nailer, while the inventory lists a cordless brad nailer and no compressor or brad nails. Which fastening system is standard is an owner decision; use only the approved system and its manufacturer's fastener specification. (source: inventory file; spec HI-09.TLS "nailer/compressor or approved fastening system")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Installing Crown Molding on Wavy Ceilings"

lines: - [ ] **Finishing Touch:** Trim off protruding shims with a sharp utility knife, apply premium paintable latex caulk along the ceiling edge line to hide gaps, and fill brad holes with wood putty.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Installing Crown Molding on Wavy Ceilings"

lines: - [ ] **Grid Layout Blueprinting:** Snap vertical and horizontal chalk lines on the wall to grid out perfectly symmetrical wainscoting box patterns based on room dimensions.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Installing Wainscoting Box Panels on Flat Walls"

lines: > FLAG: if the grid in the step above reaches an outlet, switch or other electrical device, do not extend the box or move the device: STOP and escalate (Do not perform 9; section 10). Pending qualified review. (source: 31 section 10 HI-09; 04 HI-09 "stop-work conditions", PROPOSED; 02 G-054)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Installing Wainscoting Box Panels on Flat Walls"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI09-01): before "Adhesive Layering" below, scan the pin-nailing paths along the chalk-line grid for wiring, pipes and other hidden services with a scanner able to locate them, used per its manufacturer instructions, and record the result; the panel pieces are pinned in "Fastener Setting" right after the adhesive is applied. If a service is detected or the result is inconclusive, STOP and escalate (section 19). Release: section 10. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-09.SAF "scan fastening paths"; HI-09.HAZ "hidden wiring/pipes")

| Surface ready for the agreed finish, with the painting hand-off recorded where painting follows | spec HI-09.QAC "surface ready for agreed finish"; HI-09.INT "paint/stain responsibility" | Finish-readiness photo; hand-off note | TBD - self or supervisor (Q-31-15) |
