- The worker cannot mark the job complete without answering these checks or recording an exception (source: spec QA-001).
- Evidence: note

- Photos cannot prove that hidden fasteners hold or that a scan was clear; missing evidence needs inspection, not approval (source: quality-assistant playbook "Do not infer hidden fasteners, structural adequacy, hazardous-material clearance or electrical safety from an image").
- Collect trim offcuts and shim trimmings, and vacuum sawdust from the work area (source: spec QA-002; HI-09.SAF "dust collection").
- Remove protection, account for tools and materials, and restore components altered within scope (source: spec APXA-005).
- Return unused materials and record leftover stock (source: spec APXA-007).
- Evidence: note
- Expected waste from the current steps: trim offcuts, shim trimmings, sawdust, empty caulk and adhesive tubes and packaging (source: section 12; inventory file).
- Destination, who removes the waste and any charge: TBD — owner decision; no waste policy exists (source: 31 section 3.1; 02 G-078).
- Empty or partly used chemical containers are handled per the product SDS once the reviewer has summarized it (source: 29 section 8.2, control 10).
- Removal or disposal of existing trim is not covered (section 2).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: arrival and existing-condition photos of the walls, ceilings and corners where trim goes, including dips and out-of-square conditions, and of nearby finishes (source: spec START-008, APXA-002; 04 HI-09 "completion evidence", PROPOSED).
- Evidence: photo
- During: joints and corners before caulking and filling cover them (source: 04 HI-09 "completion evidence", PROPOSED; quality-assistant playbook).

- After: joint and corner close-ups, caulk and fill completion per room, a finish-readiness photo for the painting hand-off and the cleaned area, each tagged to its work area or task (source: spec QA-003; 04 HI-09 "completion evidence", PROPOSED).
- Photos are internal-only by default and avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- Arrival and completion updates are drafts; the worker or admin controls the send (source: spec UXE-008).
- Record the walkthrough outcome: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note

- Painting hand-off: tell the customer that the trim is filled and caulked per the approved scope and ready for painting, and that final paint coats are not part of this service unless a separate painting agreement covers them (source: agreement "Prep vs Painting" clause; 04 HI-09 exclusions).
- Care notes come only from approved product data, for example the caulk or adhesive label; none is written here (source: spec QA-008).

- Describe the method actually used: in Option A the crown is shimmed, brad-nailed into framing, caulked and filled; in Option B the panel molding is fixed with construction adhesive and pinned along a chalk-line grid. The website copy that says trim pieces are brad-nailed "onto framing lines" is flagged in the register (source: section 12; C-HI09-V01).

- Never promise "flawless", "seamless" or gap-free joints, and never repeat that wording from the main plan or the agreement; the finish standard is "tight joints appropriate to finish level" (source: Do not perform 8; C-HI09-04; spec HI-09.QAC).
- Blocked work: tell the customer only what the approved "work blocked" message says (source: spec NTF-007, COM-002).
- Price or scope changes, including baseboards, casings, sanding or trim removal, are not agreed on site without a recorded change order (source: spec JOB-005, FIN-008).
- All section 13 checks answered or an exception recorded (source: spec QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- After photos captured and mapped to tasks (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup done, protection removed, tools and materials accounted for (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005).
- Scan results recorded for every fastening path (source: spec HI-09.SAF; C-HI09-01).
- Evidence: note

- Painting hand-off note recorded where painting follows, stating that the trim is filled and caulked per scope and that paint coats are not part of this service (source: 04 HI-09 "completion evidence", PROPOSED; agreement "Prep vs Painting" clause).
- Evidence: note
- Walkthrough outcome recorded (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Unresolved issues, incidents and change follow-ups submitted before the job is closed (source: spec APXA-007).
- The worker recommends completion for human sign-off; a customer signature does not clear an unresolved safety hold (source: quality-assistant playbook).
- Evidence: note
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:
**HI-09 stop triggers (draft, pending qualified review).** In addition, stop the affected work and escalate (section 19) when:
- wiring, pipes or another hidden service is detected in a fastening path, or the scan is inconclusive (source: spec HI-09.HAZ "hidden wiring/pipes"; HI-09.SAF "scan fastening paths"; C-HI09-01);

- a saw or nailer guard is missing or damaged, a tool malfunctions, or the PPE and dust collection selected by the reviewer are not available (source: spec HI-09.SAF "guarded tool use; eye/hearing protection; dust collection"; JOB-008);
- the work needs a ladder or other access equipment and no approved height and access policy exists (source: spec HI-09.HAZ "ladder"; HI-09.SAF "ladder controls"; 02 G-005; X-12);

- the work would remove, cut or sand existing painted trim or other painted surfaces and the build year is before 1978 or unknown, or suspect material is found (source: 31 section 10 HI-09; X-13; spec START-011);
- an outlet or switch box would need extension, or an electrical device would need moving, to fit the trim or wainscot layout (source: 04 HI-09 "stop-work conditions", PROPOSED; Do not perform 9);
- the job requires baseboards, door or window casings, sanding or removal of existing trim that the approved scope does not include (source: section 2; spec JOB-010);
- the trim stock on site does not match the approved profile, material or quantity (source: spec START-006, JOB-004);
- occupants or pets cannot be kept clear of the work area (source: X-11).

Release role and release evidence for each trigger: `<reviewer decision: release role and evidence>` (31 section 8.3). Which of these triggers are critical holds that no role can override is pending (Q-31-18).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
- HI-09 roles and contacts: `<owner decision: escalation order and contacts>` (Q-31-05).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].

- Q-31-07 (owner; EPA RRP-certified renovator; accredited asbestos inspector): which property-age thresholds trigger lead and asbestos screening for HI-09, and does HandyHub hold or plan EPA RRP certification if removing, cutting or sanding existing painted trim is ever offered (X-13)?

- From the register, C-HI09-02 (owner; experienced finish carpenter; attorney): are baseboards and door/window casings offered? If yes, SOP sections are drafted for competent review; if no, they are marked not offered in pricing and the agreement.
- From the register, C-HI09-05 (owner; lead carpenter): which fastening system is standard, pneumatic or cordless? The step wording is aligned only through a new SOP version after that decision.
- From the register, C-HI09-06 (owner; qualified safety professional): is sanding in scope? If yes, a step with dust controls and the older-coating screen is drafted for review.
- From the register, C-HI09-V01 (owner; experienced finish carpenter): does wainscot attachment need a fastener or framing rule in addition to the construction adhesive?

- HYPOTHESIS for the experienced finish carpenter (31 section 10 HI-09): confirm or replace the crown cutting method and the flagged saw settings in "Compound Cut Calculation"; any change to the original step text is made as a new SOP version (36 section 5.6 item 34).
- Owner; licensed electrician: are outlet or switch box extensions and device moves in wainscot or baseboard zones always referred out, and to whom (02 G-054; 04 HI-09 permit/license flags)?
- Q-31-01 (owner): who are the competent reviewers for this SOP, and how is their competence evidenced?
- Q-31-09 (owner; qualified safety professional): the height and access policy that ceiling-height crown work depends on, including the maximum ceiling height for ladder work (X-12).
- Q-31-11 (owner; qualified safety professional): emergency kit contents (X-10).
- Q-31-05 (owner): emergency and escalation contacts and their order for sections 19 and 20.
- Q-31-15 (owner): which section 13 checks need a supervisor rather than a self-check.
- Q-31-18 (qualified safety professional; owner): which HI-09 holds are critical holds under 31 section 8.4.
- Q-31-02 (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish version.
- Q-36-08 (31 owner; owner; qualified safety professional): accept the placement of precondition holds before the step they gate, as used in section 12 of this file.

sops.title: SOP HI-10: Structural Fence Maintenance & Structural Repairs

lines: - For every job, confirm that access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions are current (source: spec CX-005).

- PROPOSED, pending owner review (source: 04 HI-10 customer preparation row): pets secured; yard and gate access; fence line cleared; private buried lines disclosed; neighbor notice on shared lines; people and pets kept clear of braces and wet concrete during the cure.
- A customer's disclosure of buried lines never replaces the utility-locate hold in section 3 (source: 30 section 4.1 row 5 "never moves HandyHub's own pre-start checks onto the customer").
- Occupants, children and pets stay away from the work area, open holes, wet concrete and braces (source: spec CX-005; X-11).

- HOLD (C-HI10-01): no digging, augering or ground-driven anchor work until utility-locate status and property authorization are recorded for this job. Who requests locates, the lead time and the form of evidence are owner decisions taken with the local authority's and utility-locate guidance for each Kentucky and Indiana municipality; no rule is concluded here (Q-31-08). Until the owner's utility-locate policy is approved, this hold cannot be released by override (31 section 8.4 rule 4). (source: spec HI-10.SAF "utility-location/permit policy before digging"; 02 G-005; 31 section 10)
- Evidence: note

- Property authorization recorded before any work: the customer's authority to have this fence line repaired (the agreement relies on the client's representation of "legal ownership or neighbor approval"); stop on any boundary uncertainty (source: spec HI-10.SAF "verify scope/property authorization"; agreement "Boundary Disclaimer").
- Evidence: note
- Intake complete: fence type/material, damaged posts/rails/pickets/gate, property-line assumptions, underground utility concerns, soil/access (source: spec HI-10.INT).
- Approved estimate version and scope; a site assessment before a firm quote for digging or structural work (source: spec CX-003; 04 HI-10 estimating method; 28 section 5.3).

- Permit, zoning or HOA status recorded where the owner's policy marks the job as needing it; unknown applicability does not default to "no permit" (source: spec START-010, HND-005; 04 HI-10 permit/license flags; risk-triage playbook "unknown applicability must not default to no permit"; HUMAN REVIEW: local permit office).
- Evidence: note
- Critical items loaded: bracing lumber and stakes and the post level, which are not yet in the inventory and are proposed there (source: spec START-005, START-006; C-HI10-V01).

- Weather and ground suitable at start; thresholds are set by the qualified safety professional, none here; if unsuitable, record No Start / Blocked (source: spec START-011 "severe weather", SCH-008; X-27).
- Evidence: note

- Appendix A checks before leaving and before starting: correct job and address, latest changes, scope and exclusions, hazards, critical tools and materials loaded, approvals confirmed; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-001, APXA-003).
- Evidence: note
- On arrival: confirm the address, work area and site contact; park and access appropriately; identify pets and occupants; inspect the site against the briefing (source: spec APXA-002).

- Confirm on site that the work area is the recorded fence line on the existing footprint, and that utility-locate status and property authorization are recorded before any digging (section 3 hold) (source: spec HI-10.SAF; APXA-002 "identify utilities/emergency constraints relevant to task").
- Evidence: note
- Existing-condition photos before work: the fence line, each damaged post, rail and gate, and the locate record (source: spec START-008, APXA-002; 04 HI-10 completion evidence, PROPOSED).
- Evidence: photo, note
- Weather and ground check before work; if unsuitable, record No Start / Blocked (source: spec START-011 "severe weather", SCH-008; X-27).
- Evidence: note
- Work area kept clear of occupants, children and pets, including the area a leaning section could fall into (source: X-11; spec HI-10.HAZ "collapse/unstable sections").
- Bracing lumber, stakes and the post level staged before any excavation or rail removal (section 12 holds) (source: spec HI-10.SAF "brace unstable sections"; C-HI10-V01).
- Protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).

All original procedure lines appear below verbatim and in their original order; the two original "Problem Option" headings are demoted one level. Added lines start with `HOLD` or `FLAG` inside a quote block and are pending qualified review.

> HOLD (HI-10.SAF): applies to every step below. Stop and escalate on major structural or boundary uncertainty: the work area is not the recorded fence line on the existing footprint, ownership or authorization is disputed or unclear, or a section cannot be braced (section 19). Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-10.SAF "verify scope/property authorization", "stop for major structural/boundary uncertainty"; agreement "Boundary Disclaimer"; 31 section 10)

> HOLD (C-HI10-01): before Option A below ("Slurry Excavation") and before any other digging, augering or ground-driven anchor work: do not dig until utility-locate status and property authorization are recorded for this job (section 3). This hold cannot be released by override until the owner's utility-locate policy is approved (31 section 8.4 rule 4). Who requests locates, the lead time and the evidence are owner decisions with the local authority's and utility-locate guidance (Q-31-08); no rule is concluded here. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-10.SAF "utility-location/permit policy before digging"; HI-10.HAZ "underground utilities"; 31 sections 7.2 rank 8 and 10)

> HOLD (C-HI10-05): before the "Slurry Excavation" step below: brace or support the leaning section so that it cannot fall or shift while its post is excavated, and keep people and pets out of the area it could fall into. If it cannot be braced, stop and escalate. The order of "Slurry Excavation" and "Plumb Bracing" is under competent review (bracing before disturbance). Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-10.SAF "brace unstable sections"; HI-10.HAZ "collapse/unstable sections"; 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Stabilizing Leaning Posts (Concrete Collar Reinforcement)"

lines: - [ ] **Slurry Excavation:** Dig out a 24-inch deep cone-shaped trench around the base of the leaning wood fence post using a trenching spade, leaving the post undisturbed.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Stabilizing Leaning Posts (Concrete Collar Reinforcement)"

lines: > FLAG (C-HI10-02): UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions. "24-inch deep" in the step above has no source. No vault file states a frost depth for any municipality, so whether this depth reaches "below regional frost lines" (agreement) or "below the frost line" (main plan) is unknown; the depth comes from the reviewed method, the product instructions and any local requirement, verified separately for each Kentucky and Indiana municipality. The trenching spade is not in the inventory (C-HI10-V01). The step text above is unchanged. HUMAN REVIEW: licensed trade professional (structural); local building official.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Stabilizing Leaning Posts (Concrete Collar Reinforcement)"

lines: - [ ] **Plumb Bracing:** Push the leaning fence section back into a true vertical plumb line using a post level. Secure temporary structural wood 2x4 kick-braces to the post to hold it locked in place.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Stabilizing Leaning Posts (Concrete Collar Reinforcement)"

lines: > FLAG (C-HI10-05): SEQUENCE UNDER REVIEW - the step above moves the section to plumb before the kick-braces are secured. Until competent review sets the order, the section stays braced or supported throughout (hold above); if it shifts, stop. Bracing lumber and the post level are not in the inventory and are critical items (C-HI10-V01). The step text above is unchanged. Pending qualified review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Stabilizing Leaning Posts (Concrete Collar Reinforcement)"

lines: - [ ] **Concrete Pouring:** Pour fast-setting concrete dry mix straight into the open trench around the post base. Pour 1–2 gallons of plain water directly over the dry powder. Use a metal digging bar to stab the mix to eliminate hidden air pockets. Let cure for 4 hours before removing temporary braces.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Stabilizing Leaning Posts (Concrete Collar Reinforcement)"

lines: > FLAG (31 section 10): UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions. "1–2 gallons of plain water" and "cure for 4 hours" in the step above have no source; the water amount, the method of wetting the mix in place and the cure time come only from the concrete product's instructions (spec section 17: "Service-card defaults never override a site-specific hazard, manufacturer instruction, permit/licensing requirement, or approved change order."). The cure wait before the braces are removed is never shortened on site: it stays in force as written until a qualified reviewer replaces it. Dust and skin and eye contact controls for dry and wet mix come from the product SDS (sections 6 and 9). The step text above is unchanged. HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional; licensed trade professional (structural).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Stabilizing Leaning Posts (Concrete Collar Reinforcement)"

lines: > HOLD (X-11): during the cure wait in the step above, the filled hole, wet concrete and braces stay in the yard. Keep occupants, children and pets away from them; protection means, for example covers or caution tape, are chosen by the qualified safety professional, and the customer receives the cure and no-load note from the product instructions (spec QA-008). Whether the crew waits on site or returns to remove the braces is an owner decision (04 HI-10 labor assumptions). Pending qualified review. (source: 29 section 7.3 HI-10 row; spec QA-008)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Stabilizing Leaning Posts (Concrete Collar Reinforcement)"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI10-05): before the "Rail Extraction" step below: brace or support the section so that removing a rail cannot let the section or its pickets fall, and keep people and pets out of the area it could fall into. If it cannot be braced, stop and escalate. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-10.SAF "brace unstable sections"; HI-10.HAZ "collapse/unstable sections"; 31 section 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Replacing Broken Rails & Sagging Gates"

lines: - [ ] **Rail Extraction:** Back out rusted fasteners and pull down broken horizontal 2x4 rails.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Replacing Broken Rails & Sagging Gates"

lines: - [ ] **New Rail Setting:** Measure and cut fresh pressure-treated 2x4 rails. Secure them between posts using heavy galvanized steel fence brackets and outdoor polymer exterior screws.
- Evidence: measurement
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Replacing Broken Rails & Sagging Gates"

lines: - [ ] **Gate Re-Squaring:** Screw a heavy steel anti-sag gate cable kit diagonally across the back framework of the gate. Tighten the central turnbuckle link until the gate lifts and closes smoothly without dragging the ground latch.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Replacing Broken Rails & Sagging Gates"

lines: > FLAG (C-HI10-06, C-HI10-07): no step in this SOP covers picket replacement, post replacement, steel post splints or other ground-driven anchors, the gas auger, or gate hinge, latch and drop-rod replacement, although pricing, the agreement, the inventory or the main plan offer them. They are not performed under this SOP (section 2, Out of scope). Pending owner decision and competent review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Replacing Broken Rails & Sagging Gates"

lines: > Spec card HI-10.QAC (verbatim): "stable posts/rails, aligned replacement pieces, gate functions, fasteners appropriate, site/backfill clean and safe"

- Posts and rails stable (source: spec HI-10.QAC "stable posts/rails"). When the braces may come off follows the cure wait in section 12, which stays in force until a qualified reviewer replaces it; the stability check method is TBD by the reviewer, and no load test is set here.
- Replacement pieces aligned with the existing fence line (source: spec HI-10.QAC "aligned replacement pieces").
- Gate functions: the "Gate Re-Squaring" step's own check that the gate "lifts and closes smoothly without dragging the ground latch" (source: spec HI-10.QAC "gate functions"; section 12).
- Fasteners appropriate per the bracket and fastener manufacturers' instructions (source: spec HI-10.QAC "fasteners appropriate").
- Site and backfill clean and safe: no open hole, loose brace, cut stub or debris left unprotected or undisclosed to the customer (source: spec HI-10.QAC "site/backfill clean and safe"; X-11).

- Each check is answered, or an exception recorded, before completion (source: spec QA-001). Whether a supervisor, not only the worker, inspects any check is an owner decision (Q-31-15); a worker's self-check does not replace a required supervisor inspection (source: quality-assistant playbook).
- Evidence: note
- Backfill and leave the site clean and safe (source: spec HI-10.QAC "site/backfill clean and safe").
- Remove debris, protection and markers, and restore the site (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005).

- Temporary braces come off only after the cure wait in section 12. If the crew leaves before then, the braces and the area stay protected and the customer has the cure and no-load note (source: section 12 holds; spec QA-008).
- Account for tools and materials; return unused materials (source: spec APXA-005, APXA-007).

- Excavated soil: backfilled or removed within the approved scope; destination for surplus soil: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve. (source: spec HI-10.QAC "site/backfill clean and safe"; QA-002; Q-29-10)

- Removed rails and pickets, old fasteners, empty concrete bags and treated-wood offcuts: disposal destination and any rule for treated wood per the local authority; TBD (source: spec QA-002 "debris/waste handling"; 02 G-078; Q-29-10).
- Concrete product residue and bags: handling per the product SDS (source: 29 section 8.2 row 10).
- Hazardous waste is not handled without an approved policy (source: 31 section 3.1, section 15 minimum content).
- Whether disposal is charged is an owner pricing decision (source: 28 Q-28-15).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: the fence line and each damaged post, rail, picket and gate; the utility-locate record and marks and the authorization record before digging (source: spec START-008, APXA-002; 04 HI-10 completion evidence, PROPOSED).
- Evidence: note

- During: post plumb and bracing before the pour; the collar after the pour; any concealed condition such as rot at or below grade, or a buried object found while digging (source: spec JOB-004; 04 HI-10 completion evidence, PROPOSED).
- After: rails, gate operation, backfill and site clean, mapped to each post, section and gate (source: spec QA-003; HI-10.QAC).

- Photos are internal by default; marketing use needs separate consent; avoid people, neighbors' property not needed for the work, documents and valuables (source: spec REC-002, REC-003; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- Arrival and completion updates use approved templates only (source: 31 section 3.1, section 17 minimum content; spec NTF-007, UXE-008).

- Cure and no-load note, for example on gate use or leaning on a repaired post; its content comes only from the concrete product's instructions (source: spec QA-008; 04 HI-10 completion evidence, PROPOSED).
- Walkthrough outcome recorded: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note

- Do not promise results, permanence, wind-load performance, frost depth or code compliance, and do not repeat unapproved main-plan claims such as "like-new strength" or "below the frost line" (C-HI10-02) (source: section 2, Do not perform entry 8; 32 register B rows 39 and 40).
- Do not give an opinion on where the property line is or settle a neighbor question on site; refer it to the owner (source: agreement "Boundary Disclaimer"; spec HI-10.SAF).
- When work is blocked, tell the customer only what the approved "work blocked" message says (source: spec NTF-007).
- Explain the invoice and payment next step without making unauthorized promises (source: spec APXA-006).
- Every section 13 check answered, or an exception recorded (source: spec QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- After photos mapped to each post, section and gate (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Braces removed after the cure wait, or left protected with the customer informed (source: section 12; spec QA-008).
- Cleanup and waste handling complete; tools and materials accounted for (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005).
- Walkthrough outcome and any punch items recorded (source: spec QA-004, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- No hold or stop-work item left unresolved (source: 31 section 8.3).
- Unresolved issues, incidents and change follow-ups submitted; the job closes only when the required operational and financial steps are complete (source: spec APXA-007).
This SOP words its general stop-work rule differently from [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]; its own text, verbatim:
> **Stop-work rule (all HandyHub services).** You have the right to stop work. For any condition below, stop the affected work and escalate before continuing (source: spec START-011, JOB-004):
> - an unsafe condition for you, the customer, occupants, pets or the public;
> - concealed damage, substrate failure, moisture or an active leak;
> - suspect hazardous material, such as possible asbestos, lead paint or mold; do not disturb it;
> - electrical, plumbing, gas, HVAC or structural work that is not in the approved scope or needs a licensed trade;
> - an aggressive occupant or animal;
> - severe weather or unsafe heat or cold (source: spec BRF-008);
> - any material mismatch between the site and the briefing, approved scope, materials, access or approvals.

> Do not continue through an unsafe or restricted condition to keep the schedule (source: master section 12). A customer request, a checkbox or a signature does not clear a safety hold (source: owner facts 2026-10-02; risk-triage playbook L27). In an emergency, move people away and call emergency services first (source: spec BRF-013; risk-triage playbook L7). Then use Stop Work / Report Hazard in the app (source: spec UXE-004) and follow section 19.
> Spec card HI-10.SAF (verbatim): "verify scope/property authorization; utility-location/permit policy before digging; brace unstable sections; stop for major structural/boundary uncertainty"
Service holds and stop triggers (pending qualified review):
- HOLD (C-HI10-01): no digging, augering or ground-driven anchors until utility-locate status and property authorization are recorded (sections 3 and 12).
- Evidence: note
- HOLD (C-HI10-05): brace or support unstable sections before excavation or rail removal (section 12); if a section cannot be braced, stop (source: spec HI-10.SAF "brace unstable sections").
- Stop for major structural or boundary uncertainty (source: spec HI-10.SAF).

- A buried line, pipe, cable or other unexpected object found while digging: stop digging, keep people away and escalate; if it is damaged or leaking, treat it as an emergency (section 19) (source: spec HI-10.HAZ "underground utilities"; START-011; JOB-004).
- Non-wood or unknown fence materials: stop (source: 31 section 10).

- A post found rotted at or below grade, or another concealed condition: stop the affected work, record it with photos and escalate for a change order (source: spec JOB-004, FIN-008; 04 HI-10 estimating method).
- Evidence: note
- Severe weather or unsafe heat or cold (source: spec BRF-008; X-27).
- Anyone, including a pet, enters the work area or reaches an open hole or brace (source: X-11).
- Painted components of older or unknown age: do not cut or pry them; escalate (source: spec START-011; Q-31-07).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
Service-specific routing (contacts are owner decisions, Q-31-05):

- Contact with, or damage to, a buried line: emergency services and the utility as the situation requires, then the owner; no conclusion about notification duties is drawn here (source: section 19 step 2; 31 section 7.2 rank 8; HUMAN REVIEW: local authority and utility-locate guidance).
- Utility-locate status missing or unclear before digging: record No Start / Blocked for the digging tasks and escalate to the owner (source: section 3 hold; spec SCH-008).
- Boundary dispute or doubt about authorization: to the owner, who takes legal questions to the attorney (source: agreement "Boundary Disclaimer"; spec HI-10.SAF).

- A section that cannot be braced, or rot at or below grade: to the owner for a change order or referral; structural questions to the licensed trade professional (structural) (source: spec FIN-008, JOB-004; 31 section 10).
- Pool-barrier gate or latch questions: to the owner, who consults the local building official (no conclusion drawn here) (source: 04 HI-10 permit/license flags).
- Suspect lead paint on older painted fence components: to the owner for review by an EPA RRP-certified renovator; applicability is not concluded (source: spec START-011; Q-31-07).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].

- Q-31-08 — Locate rules (owner and local authority): who requests utility locates, how far ahead, how the result is recorded, and are private buried lines covered? Are picket replacement, post replacement, steel post splints, the gas auger and gate hardware replacement offered at all, or withdrawn? Owner; local authority and utility-locate guidance; relevant reviewers.

- 30 section 8 row 15 / C-HI10-02 — Which frost-depth and code rules apply per municipality, and does any depth statement belong in customer documents? Local building official; attorney, for Kentucky and for Indiana separately.
- 04 HI-10 card, labor assumptions — After a concrete collar, does the crew wait out the cure on site or return to remove the braces? Owner.
- Q-31-01 — Who are the competent reviewers (qualified safety professional; licensed trade professional (structural)) and how is their competence evidenced? Owner.
- Q-31-05 — Emergency and escalation contacts, escalation order and after-hours coverage for a two-person team. Owner.
- Q-31-07 — Which property-age threshold triggers lead screening before painted fence components are cut or pried? Owner; EPA RRP-certified renovator.
- Q-31-15 — Which section 13 checks need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check? Owner.
- Q-31-18 — Confirm the hazard order for dry concrete dust (rank 12) and which HI-10 holds are critical holds under the 31 section 8.4 rule. Qualified safety professional; owner.
- Q-31-02 — Who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish version? Owner.

sops.title: SOP HI-11: Structural Deck Maintenance & Deck Board Repairs

lines: - For every job, confirm that access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions are current (source: spec CX-005).

- PROPOSED, pending owner review, sent with the appointment reminder: clear furniture, grills and planters from the work area; keep occupants and pets off the deck; access under the deck; disclose deck-lighting wiring (source: 04 HI-11 customer preparation, PROPOSED; spec NTF-005).

- A customer's disclosure, for example of deck-lighting wiring, never replaces HandyHub's own pre-start checks in sections 3 and 11 (source: 30 section 4.1 row 5 "never moves HandyHub's own pre-start checks onto the customer").
- Occupants, children and pets stay off the deck area being worked and away from open board gaps and tools until the work area is released (source: spec CX-005; X-11).

- HOLD (C-HI11-03): before any board is removed or loaded, access to the work area is restricted, the support is inspected and the means to cover or barricade openings are on site (section 12) (source: spec HI-11.SAF "restrict access; inspect support before loading/removing boards"; 31 section 10).

- HOLD (X-12): fall control at a loose guard rail and at elevated deck edges and openings is pending review. The height and access module does not exist yet; until it is approved, elevated work is held and this hold cannot be released by override, and the heights at which fall controls apply are set by the qualified safety professional, none here (source: 31 sections 5.8, 7.2 rank 3, 8.4 rule 4 and 10; 02 G-005; Q-31-09; job-planner playbook "A missing ladder or unverified permit keeps affected tasks blocked.").

- Structural scope decided: no structural repair (joist sistering, ledger, hanger, footing or stair-stringer work) is in scope unless the owner approves it with a qualified structural review; the referral path is an open question (source: 04 HI-11 prerequisites, OPEN QUESTION; Q-31-08; Q-30-15).
- Intake complete: deck size/height, damaged boards/rails/stairs, framing condition, ledger/joist observations, material match, access (source: spec HI-11.INT).

- Approved estimate version and scope; a site assessment of framing condition before a firm quote, because "Photos alone cannot establish hidden condition or load-bearing adequacy." (source: spec CX-003; 04 HI-11 estimating method; estimate-assistant playbook; 28 section 5.3).

- Permit or inspection status recorded where the owner's policy marks the job as needing it; unknown applicability does not default to "no permit" (source: spec START-010, HND-005; 04 HI-11 permit/license flags; risk-triage playbook "unknown applicability must not default to no permit"; HUMAN REVIEW: local building official).
- Evidence: note

- High-risk service flag: supervisor confirmation at Start Job, PROPOSED (source: spec START-004 "High-risk service/site flags may require separate checkboxes or supervisor confirmation."; 04 HI-11 applicable software workflow, PROPOSED).

- Critical items loaded: the impact driver, reciprocating saw, drill with a long bit, hammer, rot probe and flashlight, and the access-restriction items, which are not yet in the inventory and are proposed there (source: spec START-005, START-006; C-HI11-08).
- Weather suitable at start; thresholds are set by the qualified safety professional, none here; if unsuitable, record No Start / Blocked (source: spec START-011 "severe weather", SCH-008; X-27).
- Evidence: note

- Appendix A checks before leaving and before starting: correct job and address, latest changes, scope and exclusions, hazards, critical tools and materials loaded, approvals confirmed; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-001, APXA-003).
- Evidence: note
- On arrival: confirm the address, work area and site contact; park and access appropriately; identify pets and occupants; inspect the site against the briefing (source: spec APXA-002).

- Restrict access to the work area and keep occupants, children and pets off the deck area being worked; stage the barricade, caution tape and covers for openings before any board is removed (source: spec HI-11.SAF "restrict access"; C-HI11-03; X-11).

- Existing-condition photos before work: the deck area, each board, post and rail to be worked, and the access restriction in place (source: spec START-008, APXA-002; 04 HI-11 completion evidence, PROPOSED "before photos").
- Evidence: photo
- Weather check before work; if unsuitable, record No Start / Blocked (source: spec START-011 "severe weather", SCH-008; X-27).
- Evidence: note

- Protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task, including any deck-lighting wiring the customer disclosed (source: spec APXA-002; 04 HI-11 customer preparation, PROPOSED).

All original procedure lines appear below verbatim and in their original order; the two original "Problem Option" headings are demoted one level. Added lines start with `HOLD` or `FLAG` inside a quote block and are pending qualified review.

> HOLD (HI-11.SAF): applies to every step below. Stop and escalate for any major structural, ledger or foundation issue outside the approved repair (section 19), and use fall controls as applicable: until the height and access policy is approved, work at an elevated deck edge or opening is held (section 10). Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-11.SAF "stop for major structural/ledger/foundation issues outside approved repair; use fall controls as applicable"; 31 sections 7.2 rank 3 and 10; 02 G-005)

> HOLD (C-HI11-03): before the "Screw Extraction" and "Joist Inspection" steps below: restrict access to the work area and keep occupants, children and pets away; visually inspect the support under each board before it is removed or loaded; have the means to cover or barricade openings on site, and cover or barricade every opening left by a removed board until it is closed. If the support is in doubt, do not remove or load the board: stop and escalate (section 19). The inspection is a visual screening, not a structural evaluation (section 2, Do-not-perform entry 11); how and from where it is done, and the means of covering openings, are set by the qualified safety professional. The order of the steps below, which pry the board up before the joist is inspected, is under competent review. Pending qualified review. (source: spec HI-11.SAF "restrict access; inspect support before loading/removing boards"; HI-11.HAZ "falls, unstable framing"; 31 section 10; X-11)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Replacing Rotted or Cupped Deck Floorboards"

lines: - [ ] **Screw Extraction:** Locate rusted fasteners on the rotted board. Use an impact driver with a fresh bit to back them out. If stripped, use a reciprocating saw with a metal demolition blade to slide underneath the board and slice the nail/screw shafts flush with the joist top.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Replacing Rotted or Cupped Deck Floorboards"

lines: - [ ] **Joist Inspection:** Pry up the rotted floorboard. Inspect the exposed wood joist tops below for deep rot. If spongy, sister a fresh pressure-treated 2x4 block alongside the damaged joist for structural support.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Replacing Rotted or Cupped Deck Floorboards"

lines: > HOLD (C-HI11-01): the sistering instruction in the step above is suspended pending structural review: stop, make safe (JOB-006), record (JOB-004), escalate. If a joist top is spongy or shows deep rot, do not sister, fasten to or load it: keep the opening covered or barricaded, record the condition with photos and severity, and escalate for an approved change order (FIN-008) or a referral. A structural concern is a critical hold: it clears only with a recorded qualified assessment and is never overridden (31 section 8.3 rule 2). The step text above is unchanged. Pending qualified review. HUMAN REVIEW: structural engineer or building official. (source: spec HI-11.SAF "stop for major structural/ledger/foundation issues outside approved repair"; spec FIN-008; 31 section 10; risk-triage playbook "Do not provide DIY abatement or speculative structural repair instructions.")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Replacing Rotted or Cupped Deck Floorboards"

lines: - [ ] **New Board Hanging:** Cut a fresh pressure-treated floorboard to fit the opening, leaving a uniform 1/8-inch expansion gap on the sides. Fasten tightly using 3-inch exterior polymer-coated deck screws driven flush.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Replacing Rotted or Cupped Deck Floorboards"

lines: > FLAG (31 section 3.5 rule 3): UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions. The "1/8-inch expansion gap" and the "3-inch exterior polymer-coated deck screws" in the step above have no source; board spacing and fastener type, size and placement come from the board and fastener manufacturers' instructions (spec HI-11.QAC "fasteners correct"; 02 G-044). The step text above is unchanged.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option A: Replacing Rotted or Cupped Deck Floorboards"

lines: > HOLD (X-12): before the "Boring Bolt Shafts" step below: a loose guard cannot be relied on as fall protection, so fall control at the loose guard rail is pending review; until the qualified safety professional approves a fall control under the height and access policy, do not work at an elevated edge where the guard is loose. The access restriction and support inspection of the hold before Option A apply here as well. Before drilling, look for wiring, for example deck lighting, along the post and the band joist; if any is present, stop (section 10). Pending qualified review. (source: 31 section 10 "Working at a loose guard rail: fall control pending review"; spec HI-11.SAF "use fall controls as applicable"; spec START-011; APXA-002; 04 HI-11 hazards "drilling through the band joist")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Tightening Loose Guard Handrails & Steps"

lines: - [ ] **Boring Bolt Shafts:** Drill a 1/2-inch clean hole entirely through the base of the loose vertical handrail post and the primary deck perimeter fascia band joist.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Tightening Loose Guard Handrails & Steps"

lines: - [ ] **Through-Bolt Installation:** Hammer a heavy-duty, 5-inch galvanized carriage structural bolt through both timbers.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Tightening Loose Guard Handrails & Steps"

lines: > FLAG (31 section 10): HYPOTHESIS - bolt length to be field-measured. The bolt named in the step above may be too short to leave thread for the washer and nut once it passes through both the post and the band joist; the inventory also stocks a longer bolt. Bolt length, the hole size in "Boring Bolt Shafts" and the connection method itself come from the reviewed method and the bolt manufacturer's data. Whether a single through-bolt is an acceptable guard-post connection is a question for the structural engineer or building official; no vault file states load criteria for guards (32 register B row 49, disposition "Hold"). The step text above is unchanged. HUMAN REVIEW: structural engineer or building official.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Tightening Loose Guard Handrails & Steps"

lines: - [ ] **Torque Locking:** Fit a thick washer and nut onto the protruding bolt end behind the joist. Tighten securely using a socket wrench until the wood compresses slightly, completely eliminating any sway or play in the safety handrail.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Tightening Loose Guard Handrails & Steps"

lines: > FLAG: outcome claim - owner and attorney review (31 section 10). "completely eliminating any sway or play in the safety handrail" in the step above is an absolute outcome judged by feel; guard adequacy cannot be verified by the worker or from photos. Do not repeat it to the customer (section 17). The stability check of section 13 is TBD by the reviewer, and the tightening point comes from the reviewed connection method and the bolt manufacturer's data. The step text above is unchanged. HUMAN REVIEW: structural engineer or building official; owner and attorney for the wording (Q-31-16).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Tightening Loose Guard Handrails & Steps"

lines: > FLAG (C-HI11-04): the Option B heading names "Steps", but no step in this SOP covers stair treads, stair tightening, stringers, railings or balusters, although pricing, the agreement and the main plan sell stair work. NO APPROVED PROCEDURE: not schedulable until drafted and competently reviewed (section 2, Out of scope). Offering, defining or withdrawing stair and railing work is an owner decision. Pending owner decision and competent review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🚨 Problem Option B: Tightening Loose Guard Handrails & Steps"

lines: > Spec card HI-11.QAC (verbatim): "replaced elements secure/flush, stairs/rails stable, trip hazards removed, fasteners correct, unresolved structural concerns documented"
- Replaced elements secure and flush: each new board fastened with its screws driven flush, as "New Board Hanging" states (source: spec HI-11.QAC "replaced elements secure/flush"; section 12).

- Stairs and rails stable: for Option B, the tightened post; the stability check method is TBD by the reviewer and no load test or criterion is set here; the "any sway or play" wording of "Torque Locking" is flagged (section 12). Stairs are not covered (section 2) (source: spec HI-11.QAC "stairs/rails stable"; 32 register B row 49).
- Trip hazards removed: no raised fastener, loose or uneven board, cut stub, removed fastener or debris left on the deck (source: spec HI-11.QAC "trip hazards removed").
- Fasteners correct per the board, fastener and bolt manufacturers' instructions (source: spec HI-11.QAC "fasteners correct").

- Unresolved structural concerns documented: every decay, movement or damaged connection observed is recorded with photos and severity and reported through the approved wording, without a structural conclusion (source: spec HI-11.QAC "unresolved structural concerns documented"; JOB-004; quality-assistant playbook).
- Evidence: note

- Each check is answered, or an exception recorded, before completion (source: spec QA-001). Whether a supervisor, not only the worker, inspects any check is an owner decision (Q-31-15); a worker's self-check does not replace a required supervisor inspection (source: quality-assistant playbook "Prevent a worker's self-check from replacing required supervisor inspection.").
- Evidence: note
- Remove the removed boards, fasteners, cut-offs, debris and protection, and restore the site (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005; HI-11.QAC "trip hazards removed").

- Barricades and covers come off only when no opening remains. If work pauses with an opening left, for example after a structural stop, the opening stays covered or barricaded and the customer is told through the approved wording; the make-safe policy itself does not exist yet (source: spec JOB-006, NTF-007; 31 section 5.8 make-safe module; X-11).
- Account for tools and materials; return unused materials (source: spec APXA-005, APXA-007).

- Removed boards, treated-wood offcuts and old fasteners: disposal destination and any rule for treated wood per the local authority; TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve. (source: spec QA-002 "debris/waste handling"; 02 G-078; Q-29-10)
- Removed nails and screws are collected, not left on the deck or in the yard (source: spec HI-11.HAZ "nails/splinters"; HI-11.QAC "trip hazards removed").
- Hazardous waste is not handled without an approved policy (source: 31 section 3.1, section 15 minimum content).
- Whether disposal is charged is an owner pricing decision (source: 28 Q-28-15).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: the deck area and each board, post and rail to be worked, and the access restriction in place (source: spec START-008, APXA-002; 04 HI-11 completion evidence, PROPOSED).

- During: concealed-condition photos of the exposed joists after a board is lifted, and any decay, movement or damaged connection found (source: spec JOB-004; 04 HI-11 completion evidence, PROPOSED "concealed-condition photos of exposed joists").
- Evidence: photo
- After: per replaced element, mapped to the board, post or area (source: spec QA-003; 04 HI-11 completion evidence, PROPOSED "after photos per replaced element").
- Evidence: photo

- Photos are internal by default; marketing use needs separate consent; avoid people, neighbors' property not needed for the work, documents and valuables (source: spec REC-002, REC-003; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- Arrival and completion updates use approved templates only (source: 31 section 3.1, section 17 minimum content; spec NTF-007, UXE-008).
- Walkthrough outcome recorded: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note

- Unresolved structural concerns are told to the customer as observations with a referral, in approved wording, never as a structural conclusion or a statement that the deck is safe (source: spec HI-11.QAC; 32 register B row 42 "Reword as visual observation with referral"; quality-assistant playbook).

- Do not promise results, safety, structural soundness, lifespan or code compliance, and do not repeat unapproved claims such as "Ensure Backyard Safety", "restores the safety and lifespan of your deck footprint" or the "any sway or play" wording of "Torque Locking" (source: section 2, Do-not-perform entry 8; 32 register A row 11 and register B rows 41 and 49).

- Care notes, including when new lumber may be stained, come only from approved product data and templates; staining is PT-02 work (source: spec QA-008; 04 HI-11 exclusions "staining timed by product instructions, not an invented cure period").
- When work is blocked, tell the customer only what the approved "work blocked" message says (source: spec NTF-007).
- Explain the invoice and payment next step without making unauthorized promises (source: spec APXA-006).
- Every section 13 check answered, or an exception recorded (source: spec QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- After photos mapped to each replaced element (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- No open board gap left uncovered: the access restriction comes off only when no opening remains, or stays in place with the customer informed (source: spec HI-11.SAF; section 14).
- Cleanup and waste handling complete; tools and materials accounted for (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005).
- Unresolved structural concerns documented and punch items recorded (source: spec HI-11.QAC, QA-005).
- Evidence: note
- Walkthrough outcome recorded (source: spec QA-004, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- No hold or stop-work item left unresolved (source: 31 section 8.3).
- Unresolved issues, incidents and change follow-ups submitted; the job closes only when the required operational and financial steps are complete (source: spec APXA-007).

> Spec card HI-11.SAF (verbatim): "restrict access; inspect support before loading/removing boards; stop for major structural/ledger/foundation issues outside approved repair; use fall controls as applicable"
Service holds and stop triggers (pending qualified review):
- HOLD (C-HI11-03): restrict access, inspect the support before boards are removed or loaded, and cover or barricade openings (sections 3 and 12); if the support is in doubt, stop.

- HOLD (C-HI11-01): a spongy or decayed joist: the sistering instruction is suspended; stop, make safe (JOB-006), record (JOB-004), escalate; no structural repair without an approved change order (FIN-008) and qualified structural review. A structural concern is a critical hold: it clears only with a recorded qualified assessment and is never overridden (source: 31 sections 8.3 rule 2 and 10).
- Evidence: note
- Stop for major structural, ledger or foundation issues outside the approved repair (source: spec HI-11.SAF).

- HOLD (X-12): fall control at a loose guard rail and at elevated deck edges and openings is pending review; until the height and access policy is approved, this hold cannot be released by override (source: 31 sections 8.4 rule 4 and 10).
- Wiring, for example deck lighting, found in a drilling or cutting path: stop (source: spec START-011 "unapproved electrical/plumbing/gas/structural scope"; 04 HI-11 hazards).
- A customer request for stair, railing, baluster, stringer, ledger or under-deck work: not covered; record the request and escalate (source: spec JOB-010; section 2).
- Evidence: note
- Severe weather or unsafe heat or cold (source: spec BRF-008; X-27).
- Anyone, including a pet, enters the restricted area or approaches an open board gap (source: X-11).
- Painted surfaces of older or unknown age: do not cut, pry or drill them; escalate (source: spec START-011; Q-31-07).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
Service-specific routing (contacts are owner decisions, Q-31-05):

- A spongy or decayed joist, ledger, beam or post, or framing movement: stop, make safe only as policy allows (JOB-006), record (JOB-004) and escalate to the owner for a change order or a referral; structural questions go to the structural engineer or building official (source: section 12 hold C-HI11-01; spec FIN-008; Q-30-15).
- Structural movement while people are on the deck: an emergency, step 2 above (source: 31 section 8.5 escalation block "structural movement").

- A fall-control or access question at an elevated edge, an opening or a loose guard: record No Start / Blocked for the affected tasks and escalate to the owner and the qualified safety professional (source: section 12 holds; spec SCH-008; Q-31-09).
- Wiring found in a drilling or cutting path: to the owner; a licensed electrician only if wiring work would be needed (source: spec START-011).
- Stair, railing, baluster, stringer or ledger requests: record them as customer requests and escalate to the owner (source: spec JOB-010; section 2).
- Suspect lead paint on painted deck surfaces of older or unknown age: to the owner for review by an EPA RRP-certified renovator; applicability is not concluded (source: spec START-011; Q-31-07).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].

- Q-30-15 — What is the referral path when hidden rot, ledger or foundation problems are found and no catalog service covers the repair? Owner.
- Q-31-09 — Height and access policy: the deck heights and stairs at which fall controls and access equipment apply, the equipment types, and who may use them. Owner; qualified safety professional.
- Q-31-01 — Who are the competent reviewers (qualified safety professional; structural engineer or building official) and how is their competence evidenced? Owner.
- Q-31-05 — Emergency and escalation contacts, escalation order and after-hours coverage for a two-person team. Owner.
