- Q-04-18 — Does the qualified safety professional confirm the old-property screening questions for HI-11? Qualified safety professional.
- Q-31-15 — Which section 13 checks, for example the stability of a tightened post, need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check? Owner.
- Q-31-16 — Who approves replacement wording for the "any sway or play" line once the SOP is revised? Owner; attorney.
- Q-31-18 — Which HI-11 holds are critical holds under the 31 section 8.4 rule? Qualified safety professional; owner.
- Q-31-02 — Who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish version? Owner.

sops.title: SOP PT-01: Professional Residential Interior Painting

lines: PROPOSED for owner approval; customer-facing wording goes through 30 and 32.
- The customer moves heavy home-theater setups, pianos and fine art collections before the crew arrives (source: agreement "Exclusions" clause, itself under attorney review).
- Color, sheen and product are chosen and signed off before scheduling (source: agreement "Color Confirmation Waiver"; 04 PT-01 "customer preparation requirements").
- Wall hangings, valuables and small items are removed from the work area (source: 04 PT-01 "customer preparation requirements").

- Children and pets are kept away from the work area during work and until the product label allows re-occupancy (source: 04 PT-01 "customer preparation requirements"; spec CX-005; 29 section 8.2 control 9; X-11).
- Access, parking and water availability are confirmed (source: 04 PT-01 "customer preparation requirements"; spec BRF-002).
- Customer-supplied paint is on site with its label (source: spec PT-01.INT; spec START-009).
- Every job re-confirms access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions (source: spec CX-005).

- Notice to cancel or reschedule and home entry follow the draft agreement's "24-Hour Notice" clause, which is under owner and attorney review; this SOP states no fee (source: agreement "24-Hour Notice" clause).
- [ ] **Furniture Consolidation:** Move all lightweight furniture completely out of the room. Shift heavy furniture (sofas, large tables) to the exact center of the room.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: White-Glove Room Prep & Masking"

lines: > FLAG: the step above moves and shifts furniture with no weight limit, two-person rule or list of items not to move; the draft agreement leaves heavy home-theater setups, pianos and fine art collections to the customer (Do-not-perform entry 13). Limits pending owner and qualified safety review. (source: 04 PT-01 "hazards" and "exclusions"; agreement "Exclusions" clause)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: White-Glove Room Prep & Masking"

lines: - [ ] **Plastic Encapsulation:** Wrap the centered furniture cluster tightly in 1-mil plastic masking film to protect against floating paint overspray or dust.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: White-Glove Room Prep & Masking"

lines: - [ ] **Floor Defense:** Lay clean, heavy-weight canvas drop cloths across 100% of the exposed flooring. Secure edges with delicate surface tape to prevent sliding.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: White-Glove Room Prep & Masking"

lines: - [ ] **Hardware Removal:** Unscrew and remove all electrical switch plates, outlet covers, and wall-mounted thermostat faces. Put screws in a labeled zip bag.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: White-Glove Room Prep & Masking"

lines: > HOLD (C-PT01-V01): the step above is limited to removing covers: never touch wiring, devices or thermostat controls (Do-not-perform entry 10). Whether workers may remove wall-mounted thermostat faces at all is pending the owner and a licensed electrician or HVAC professional. If a face cannot be removed without touching wiring or controls, or a plate, device or thermostat is damaged or wiring is exposed, stop, photograph and escalate (spec JOB-004). Everything removed here is refitted before completion (HOLD after "Hardware Install"). Pending qualified review. (source: 31 section 10; 02 C-PT01-V01; 04 PT-01 "permit/license flags")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: White-Glove Room Prep & Masking"

lines: - [ ] **Trim Masking:** Apply premium painter's tape along the top edge of all baseboards, window casings, and door frames. Press down firmly with a plastic putty knife to seal the edge against paint bleed.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: White-Glove Room Prep & Masking"

lines: - This SOP is not active: no job uses it until competent review and owner activation (source: owner facts 2026-10-02; 31 section 2.1).

- An approved estimate version exists for the job. Lines that no approved step covers (ceilings, trim, doors, closets, a full primer coat) are not performed under this SOP (source: spec CX-003, EST-005; section 2; C-PT01-06, C-PT01-04).
- Intake recorded: rooms and areas, colors and finish, paint brand or product if specified, wall condition, furniture and occupancy, repair scope (source: spec PT-01.INT).
- Evidence: note

- PROPOSED: the customer's color, sheen and product sign-off is recorded before the visit. The agreement's "Color Confirmation Waiver" relies on this sign-off, and no step records it today (source: agreement "Color Confirmation Waiver"; 30 section 5 row 27; spec PT-01.QAC "agreed sheen/color").
- Evidence: note

- Property age: the build year, or "unknown", is recorded. Before 1978 or unknown: the HOLD before "Pole Sanding" applies until a qualified person records the lead disposition (source: spec PT-01.SAF, PT-01.HAZ; spec BRF-003 "approximate age if known"; 31 section 10; risk-triage playbook "A pre-1978 painted surface is not cleared by a customer saying it looks safe."; C-PT01-01; X-13). Whether the EPA RRP program applies to a job and whether HandyHub holds or will obtain certification is an OPEN QUESTION (Q-31-07; HUMAN REVIEW: EPA RRP-certified renovator, attorney).
- Evidence: note

- Ventilation and occupants: the work area can be ventilated as the product instructions require, and occupants, children and pets (including users of a nursery or an allergy-sensitive room) can be kept out until the label allows re-occupancy; method TBD - qualified safety reviewer (source: spec PT-01.SAF "ventilate", "follow product instructions"; inventory "Zero-VOC Odor-Free Paints" line; X-11).
- A reviewed SDS is on file for every paint, primer, spackle, caulk and cleaner carried to the job (source: 29 section 8.3 interim rule, PROPOSED; 02 G-008).

- Ladder or other access work only under an approved height and access policy, which does not exist yet; the maximum ceiling height served is an OPEN QUESTION (Q-31-09) (source: spec PT-01.SAF "ladder controls"; 02 G-005; C-PT01-02; X-12).

- Customer-supplied paint: visible condition, product and quantity recorded before use and checked against the signed-off color and sheen; a missing or wrong product blocks the affected task (source: spec START-009, JOB-004; 29 section 9.1, PROPOSED).
- Evidence: note

- Before leaving: confirm the correct job, customer, address and time; read the latest changes; verify access and parking; review scope and exclusions; review hazards and safety; load critical tools, equipment and materials; check customer-supplied items; confirm required documents and approvals (source: spec APXA-001).

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; confirm materials, models and colors; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003, START-004).
- Evidence: note

- On arrival: confirm the address, work area and contact; park and access appropriately; identify pets and occupants; inspect the actual site against the briefing; capture the required existing-condition photos; protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- Confirm that the site matches the briefing, or record the differences; material differences trigger Risk Triage or supervisor review (source: spec START-007).
- Evidence: note
- Existing-condition photos of the walls, floors, trim, furniture and fixtures, and of the plates, covers and any thermostat before removal (source: spec START-008; section 16).
- Evidence: photo
- Ventilation set up as the product label requires, with occupants, children and pets kept out: method TBD - qualified safety reviewer (source: spec PT-01.SAF "ventilate"; X-11).
- Protection set-up is Phase 1 of section 12: furniture, film, drop cloths, cover plates and trim masking (source: original Phase 1).
- Ladder or access-equipment set-up only under an approved height and access policy: TBD (source: 02 G-005; X-12; C-PT01-02).
- Safety, PPE and site checks complete; materials, colors and sheen confirmed against the sign-off; SOP hazards acknowledged before starting (source: spec APXA-003, START-004).
- Evidence: note

*Original procedure, verbatim and in its original order. HOLD and FLAG lines are added drafts pending qualified review (31 section 10). A hold placed before a step must be satisfied before that step starts; a hold or flag placed after a step limits or flags "the step above" (36 D-36-17).*

> HOLD (PT-01.SAF; X-11): before "Defect Patching" below, and before every later step that applies spackle, primer or paint, the reviewed SDS and the product label are on hand; ventilate the work area as the product instructions require; keep occupants, children and pets out of the work area, including a nursery or an allergy-sensitive room, until the label allows re-occupancy. No SDS, or ventilation not possible as the label requires: stop and escalate. Ventilation method TBD - qualified safety reviewer. Pending qualified review. (source: spec PT-01.SAF "ventilate", "follow product instructions"; spec PT-01.HAZ "VOC/chemical exposure"; 31 section 10; 29 section 8.3 interim rule, PROPOSED)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🩹 Phase 2: Surface Restoration & Priming"

lines: - [ ] **Defect Patching:** Inspect walls under high-intensity light. Fill nail holes, dents, and cracks using professional lightweight spackle.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🩹 Phase 2: Surface Restoration & Priming"

lines: > HOLD (C-PT01-01): before "Pole Sanding" below, check the recorded build year. If the home was built before 1978, or the build year is unknown, do not sand or scrape existing coatings (the whole-wall sanding in that step included) until a qualified person records the lead disposition; a customer saying the paint looks safe does not clear this hold. If an old texture or joint compound is suspected to contain asbestos, leave it undisturbed, stop and escalate. No abatement or lead-safe work method is given here. Pending review by an EPA RRP-certified renovator and an attorney licensed in KY/IN. (source: spec PT-01.SAF "assess older coatings before aggressive disturbance"; spec PT-01.HAZ "dust/lead in older coatings"; 31 section 10; risk-triage playbook "A pre-1978 painted surface is not cleared by a customer saying it looks safe."; X-13)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🩹 Phase 2: Surface Restoration & Priming"

lines: - [ ] **Pole Sanding:** Sand patched areas and the entire wall plane using a 120-grit pole sander to remove old paint textures and nubs. Wipe down walls with a dry microfiber tack cloth to capture powder.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🩹 Phase 2: Surface Restoration & Priming"

lines: - [ ] **Spot Priming:** Apply a high-hiding latex primer over raw spackle patches to seal them and prevent "flashing" (flat dull spots in the final coat).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🩹 Phase 2: Surface Restoration & Priming"

lines: > FLAG (C-PT01-04): the step above spot-primes raw spackle patches only. The main plan promises a full "foundation primer" coat and the agreement's "Inclusions" clause names "priming": full prime coat, spot-prime only or a separate option is an owner decision (spec EST-005). A full primer coat is not covered by this SOP (section 2). Pending owner review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🩹 Phase 2: Surface Restoration & Priming"

lines: - [ ] **Brush Loading:** Dip a clean 2.5-inch or 3-inch angled sash brush exactly 1 inch into the paint bucket. Tap the inner side of the bucket to remove excess (never wipe).
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🪒 Phase 3: The Precision Edge Cut"

lines: > HOLD (C-PT01-02): before "Ceiling and Trim Cut" below, and before any other work above floor reach, use a ladder or other access equipment only under an approved height and access policy, which does not exist yet (02 G-005). Ladder type, set-up, inspection and the maximum ceiling height served are TBD - qualified safety professional and owner (Q-31-09). Without approved access equipment on site, the affected task is blocked: record No Start or Blocked and escalate (spec SCH-008). Pending qualified review. (source: spec PT-01.SAF "ladder controls"; spec PT-01.HAZ "ladders"; 31 section 10; job-planner playbook "A missing ladder or unverified permit keeps affected tasks blocked.")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🪒 Phase 3: The Precision Edge Cut"

lines: - [ ] **Ceiling and Trim Cut:** Execute a free-hand laser-straight cut-line along the ceiling boundary and taped trim lines. Maintain a continuous wet edge, working in 3-to-4 foot sections.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🪒 Phase 3: The Precision Edge Cut"

lines: > FLAG (C-PT01-06): the step above cuts in along the ceiling boundary and the taped trim; painting the ceiling, trim, baseboards, doors or closet interiors is not covered by this SOP, although pricing sells them (section 2). Pending owner and lead-painter review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🪒 Phase 3: The Precision Edge Cut"

lines: - [ ] **Feathering the Cut:** Gently brush out the thick outer edge of your cut-line to prevent a raised paint ridge from showing later.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🪒 Phase 3: The Precision Edge Cut"

lines: - [ ] **Roller Load:** Saturate a 3/8-inch or 1/2-inch lint-free microfiber roller nap uniformly in the paint tray grid.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌀 Phase 4: Rolling the Open Fields"

lines: - [ ] **The "W" Pattern:** Apply paint to the wall in a large, sweeping "W" or "N" pattern (approx. 3x3 feet) to distribute the bulk load.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌀 Phase 4: Rolling the Open Fields"

lines: - [ ] **Fill & Back-Roll:** Roll back across the "W" in vertical, overlapping ceiling-to-floor strokes to smooth out shadows. *Crucial:* Always maintain a wet edge and finish rolling an entire wall panel before stopping to prevent visible seam lines.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌀 Phase 4: Rolling the Open Fields"

lines: > FLAG (C-PT01-04): no step states the number of coats or the recoat interval. Coats follow the approved estimate (the agreement's "Inclusions" clause names a minimum number of coats); recoat and dry times follow the approved product label; no interval is set here (section 8). Pending owner review.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🌀 Phase 4: Rolling the Open Fields"

lines: - [ ] **Tape Pull:** Pull all painters tape slowly at a sharp 45-degree angle while the second coat of paint is still slightly damp to avoid tearing dry paint edges.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Reassembly, Clean-up & Quality Audit"

lines: - [ ] **Hardware Install:** Re-screw all clean electrical plates and outlet covers back onto the walls once dry.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Reassembly, Clean-up & Quality Audit"

lines: > HOLD (C-PT01-V01): the step above refits electrical plates and outlet covers only. Before completion, every item removed in "Hardware Removal", including any thermostat face, is refitted as found and the result is recorded (section 13). If an item cannot be refitted without touching wiring or controls, stop and escalate; no electrical or HVAC procedure is given here. Pending review by a qualified safety professional and a licensed electrician or HVAC professional. (source: spec APXA-005 "restore utilities/components altered within scope"; 31 section 10; 02 C-PT01-V01)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Reassembly, Clean-up & Quality Audit"

lines: - [ ] **The Flashlight Sweep:** Run an LED inspection beam flat against the wall profile to double-check for roller skips, holidays, or sagging drips. Touch up immediately.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Reassembly, Clean-up & Quality Audit"

lines: - [ ] **Site Restoration:** Gather canvas cloths, vacuum up minor debris, and move furniture back to its original layout.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Reassembly, Clean-up & Quality Audit"

lines: | Check | Source | Evidence | Inspector |

| Uniform coverage: no roller skips, holidays or sagging drips | spec PT-01.QAC "uniform coverage"; original "The Flashlight Sweep" | After photos per wall or room (spec QA-003) | TBD - self-check or supervisor (Q-31-15) |
| Clean cut lines at the ceiling boundary and along trim | spec PT-01.QAC "clean cut lines"; original "Ceiling and Trim Cut" and "Tape Pull" | Photos of the cut lines | TBD (Q-31-15) |

| Agreed sheen and color, matching the signed-off selection | spec PT-01.QAC "agreed sheen/color"; agreement "Color Confirmation Waiver" | Product label, color and sheen recorded against the sign-off | TBD (Q-31-15) |
| Repaired prep areas checked after the final coat | spec PT-01.QAC "repaired prep areas"; original "Spot Priming" ("flashing") | Photo of each repaired area | TBD (Q-31-15) |

| No overspray or drips on protected surfaces: floors, trim, fixtures, furniture | spec PT-01.QAC "no overspray/drips on protected surfaces" | Check result recorded; photos where found | TBD (Q-31-15) |
| Coats applied as the approved estimate states | agreement "Inclusions" clause; spec EST-002; C-PT01-04 | Number of coats and product recorded | TBD (Q-31-15) |

| Every plate, cover and any thermostat face removed in Phase 1 refitted as found | 02 C-PT01-V01 ("every removed device/cover reinstalled as found"); spec APXA-005 | Check result recorded; photo | TBD (Q-31-15) |
| Cleanup done and furniture back in its original layout | spec PT-01.QAC "cleanup"; spec QA-002; original "Site Restoration" | Cleanup photos where required (spec QA-002) | TBD (Q-31-15) |
- The job cannot be marked complete until each required check is answered or an exception is recorded (source: spec QA-001; AT-039).
- Evidence: note

- A failed check becomes a punch item or an escalation; open punch items stay linked to the job (source: spec QA-005). A worker's self-check does not replace a required supervisor inspection (source: handyhub-quality-assistant playbook).

- Remove protection (tape, film, drop cloths), clean the area, account for tools and materials, and restore components altered within scope, including every plate, cover and any thermostat face removed (source: spec APXA-005, QA-002; original Phase 5; section 12 HOLD after "Hardware Install").

- Sanding dust: HEPA vacuum as the spec card lists; the dust class and the cleanup method where older coatings may be involved are TBD - qualified safety professional and EPA RRP-certified renovator (source: spec PT-01.TLS "sanding/HEPA vacuum"; original "Site Restoration"; C-PT01-01).
- Brushes, rollers and trays are cleaned as the product label states; the rinse-water destination is in section 15 (source: spec PT-01.SAF "follow product instructions").
- Cleanup photos where they are required for dusty work (source: spec QA-002).
- Evidence: photo
TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

- Waste streams to classify: leftover paint and primer, rinse water from cleaning tools, used tray liners, tape, plastic film, sanding dust and spent abrasives, and empty spackle, caulk and paint containers; destination and who pays are owner decisions (source: inventory file; original steps; 02 G-061; 31 section 3.1).

- Leftover paint: whether it stays with the customer for touch-up or leaves with the crew is an owner decision; the customer note comes from approved product data (source: 04 PT-01 "completion evidence"; spec QA-008).

- Disposal destinations follow the rules of the actual municipality: TBD - local authority and safety reviewer (source: 29 Q-29-10; owner facts 2026-10-02 "Verify the actual Kentucky/Indiana municipality").
- Dust and debris from any older coating are not handled without an approved policy (source: 31 section 3.1; C-PT01-01).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: the existing condition of the walls, floors, trim, furniture and fixtures in each work area; the plates, covers and any thermostat before removal (supports the refit check, C-PT01-V01); the protection set-up (source: spec START-008, BRF-012 "floor/wall protection setup"; 04 PT-01 "completion evidence", PROPOSED).

- During: patched and spot-primed areas before painting; any concealed condition, moisture or suspect material found (source: spec JOB-004; 04 PT-01 "completion evidence"). The agreement's second payment milestone names this stage; payment terms are under attorney review.
- After: each painted wall or room, the cut lines and the refitted plates and covers, with each photo mapped to its work area (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Photos are internal-only by default and avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- The required photo set, and whether Start Job is blocked without it: TBD - owner (source: spec START-008).
- Arrival and completion updates use approved templates only; until approved they are drafts (source: 31 section 3.1).
- Before starting, confirm the color, sheen and product with the customer against the signed-off selection (source: spec APXA-003; agreement "Color Confirmation Waiver").

- A color change after application is recorded as a change request and goes through the change-order process; do not agree a price on site (source: spec JOB-005, FIN-008; agreement "Color Confirmation Waiver", under attorney review).
- Evidence: note
- Ventilation, drying and re-occupancy information comes only from the approved product label or SDS; care notes use approved templates (source: spec QA-008; 31 section 3.1).
- Walkthrough: record accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note

- Blocked work, including an older-coating hold: use only the approved "work blocked" message; make no statement about lead content, health effects or legal requirements, and refer questions to the owner (source: spec NTF-007, COM-002; Q-31-07).

- Do not repeat the opening statement in section 1 ("guarantees flawless ... absolute property protection"), the main plan's "absolutely zero mess left behind", or any Zero-VOC, health, safety or warranty promise (source: C-PT01-07; Do-not-perform entry 8).
- Explain the invoice and payment next step without unauthorized promises (source: spec APXA-006).
- Every section 13 check is answered with evidence, or an exception is recorded (source: spec QA-001, AT-039).
- Evidence: note
- After photos are captured and mapped to the work (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup is done, protection removed, furniture back in place, and tools and materials accounted for (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005; original "Site Restoration").
- Every plate, cover and any thermostat face removed is refitted as found (source: spec APXA-005; C-PT01-V01).
- The care and leftover-paint note comes from approved product data (source: spec QA-008; 04 PT-01 "completion evidence").
- The walkthrough outcome is recorded, and open punch items stay linked to the job (source: spec QA-004, QA-005, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- The property is left secured (source: 31 section 3.1).
- No hold from sections 10 and 12 is open, and unresolved issues, incidents and change requests are submitted before the job closes (source: spec APXA-007, JOB-012).
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:
PT-01 stop triggers (spec PT-01.SAF first, then the register holds; all pending qualified review):

- The work would sand or scrape existing coatings and the build year is before 1978 or unknown: stop before "Pole Sanding" until a qualified person records the lead disposition (source: spec PT-01.SAF "assess older coatings before aggressive disturbance"; C-PT01-01).
- Evidence: note
- Old texture or joint compound is suspected to contain asbestos (source: spec START-011; X-13).
- The work area cannot be ventilated as the product instructions require, or a product has no reviewed SDS (source: spec PT-01.SAF "ventilate", "follow product instructions"; 29 section 8.3).
- Contents cannot be protected (source: spec PT-01.SAF "protect contents").

- Work needs a ladder or other access equipment and no approved height and access policy or suitable equipment exists (source: spec PT-01.SAF "ladder controls"; C-PT01-02; job-planner playbook "A missing ladder or unverified permit keeps affected tasks blocked.").
- A plate, device or thermostat is damaged, wiring is exposed, or the task goes beyond removing and refitting covers (source: 31 section 10; C-PT01-V01).
- Moisture, concealed damage or suspected mold behind a patch area (source: spec JOB-004, START-011).
- Customer-supplied paint is missing or does not match the signed-off color and sheen (source: spec START-009; spec JOB-004 "missing customer-supplied item"; spec PT-01.QAC "agreed sheen/color").
- Occupants, children or pets cannot be kept out of the work area (source: X-11).

- The customer asks for ceilings, trim, doors, closets or a full primer coat that the approved estimate or this SOP does not cover: record the request; change order (source: spec JOB-005, JOB-010; C-PT01-06, C-PT01-04).
- Each hold names the role and the evidence that clear it: TBD - requires qualified safety reviewer review. Critical holds clear only with a recorded qualified assessment (source: 31 section 8.3).
- Evidence: note
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
PT-01 routes (contacts are owner decisions, Q-31-05):

- Build year before 1978 or unknown and the job needs sanding or scraping of existing coatings: stop; the owner obtains the qualified person's lead disposition before work resumes (C-PT01-01; Q-31-07).
- Suspect old texture or joint compound: stop; accredited asbestos inspector through the owner (X-13).
- Damaged device, exposed wiring or a thermostat question: stop that task; the office refers it to a licensed electrician or HVAC professional (C-PT01-V01).
- Work above reach without approved access equipment: stop that task; owner and qualified safety professional (C-PT01-02).
- A customer request for ceilings, trim, doors, closets or a full primer coat that is not on the approved estimate: record it; change order (C-PT01-06, C-PT01-04).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].

- PT-01 examples: a fall from a ladder or step, a paint or chemical spill on customer property, damage to furniture, floors or fixtures, suspected lead-dust or chemical exposure, and contact with electrical wiring (source: spec JOB-008; spec PT-01.HAZ).

- **Q-31-07** (owner; EPA RRP-certified renovator; accredited asbestos inspector): which property-age thresholds trigger lead and asbestos screening for PT-01, and does HandyHub hold or plan EPA RRP certification, or decline or refer work that disturbs existing coatings in older homes?
- **Q-31-09** (owner; qualified safety professional): the height and access policy for PT-01 - the maximum ceiling height served, which access equipment, and who may use it.

- Related: **Q-31-05** (owner) emergency and escalation contacts; **Q-31-10** (owner; qualified mold assessor) the company mold definition and stop rule; **Q-31-15** (owner) which section 13 checks need a second person; **Q-31-16** (owner; attorney) who approves replacement wording for the flagged opening statement; **Q-04-08** (owner; quality assistant) the patch size at which PT-01 repair becomes a DW-01 line; **Q-30-07** (owner; attorney) warranty and callback policy (no warranty is drafted here).

- Register questions without a Q-number, all in 02: C-PT01-V01 (owner; qualified safety professional; licensed electrician or HVAC professional) whether workers may remove thermostat faces at all; C-PT01-04 (owner) full primer coat, spot-prime only or a separate option, and the coat rule; C-PT01-06 (owner; lead painter) whether ceiling, trim, door and closet procedures are written from approved product instructions or those items are withdrawn from sale. Owner decisions recorded as gaps in 04 without a question ID: spray application ("required tools": "spraying not approved") and furniture weight limits ("exclusions").

sops.title: SOP PT-02: Outdoor Deck & Fence Staining and Sealing

lines: From the agreement, the spec and the original steps, pending review:
- Every job re-confirms access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions (source: spec CX-005).
- Wood species and age, existing coating, color and product choice, and landscaping are captured at intake (source: spec PT-02.INT).
- The customer knows that the schedule depends on weather and wood drying (source: agreement "The Midwest Weather Clause" and "Moisture Limit Guarantee"; wording under attorney review).
- After staining the homeowner receives keep-off instructions; the times come from the approved product data (source: original Phase 5 "Drying Signs"; C-PT02-V01).

GAP - not yet in the agreement or any reminder (owner decision; wording through 30 and 32): items on the deck (furniture, planters, grills) removed; pets and children kept away during chemical work and drying; nearby windows and doors closed; vehicles moved out of overspray range; water access confirmed; neighbors told about fence work; HOA color approval where it applies (source: 04 PT-02 "customer preparation requirements" and "permit/license flags"; X-11).
- [ ] **Siding & Glass Shielding:** Tape plastic film over adjacent vinyl siding, brick walls, and low window glass near the deck to protect against chemical drifts.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Property Isolation & Plant Protection"

lines: - [ ] **Landscape Saturation:** Thoroughly spray down nearby grass, bushes, and flowerbeds with plain water before applying chemicals. *Wet plants will not absorb toxic wood stripping agents.*
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Property Isolation & Plant Protection"

lines: > FLAG: unsourced claim - the sentence "Wet plants will not absorb toxic wood stripping agents." in the step above is kept verbatim but is not verified; pre-wetting stays as written, and plant protection and runoff control come from the product label, the SDS and the qualified safety professional. The SOP's own "toxic" wording stays; no "eco" claim from the main plan, the agreement or the inventory is repeated in this SOP or to customers (C-PT02-01). (source: 31 section 10 PT-02; spec PT-02.SAF "protect plants/adjacent surfaces")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Property Isolation & Plant Protection"

lines: Dispatch and Start Job conditions, pending review:

- Approved estimate version with the selected areas (deck floor, railings, steps), product and color, each option separately identifiable (source: spec CX-003, EST-005; APXA-001 "review scope/exclusions").
- Intake recorded: wood species and age, existing coating, moisture condition, area, color and product, weather forecast and landscaping (source: spec PT-02.INT).
- Evidence: note

- Soundness: rot, loose boards, protruding fasteners or other structural defects found at assessment or on arrival are routed to HI-10 or HI-11 before any coating; PT-02 does no structural work (source: 04 section 5.4 rules (a) and (d), PROPOSED; agreement "Structural Integrity"). The shared exterior-wood soundness checklist does not exist yet: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

- Existing coating and property age: the approximate build year is captured, with "unknown" as a value. Whether stripping or washing existing coatings at properties built before 1978 or of unknown age needs lead screening is an OPEN QUESTION (EPA RRP-certified renovator, Q-31-07); until it is answered, such coatings are not disturbed. Older treated lumber of unknown treatment is an OPEN QUESTION for the qualified safety professional (source: 31 SOP-022 and section 7.2 rank 2, PROPOSED; 31 section 10 PT-02; risk-triage playbook L27).

- Every chemical product (stripper, brightener, stain, brush cleaner, engine fuel) approved with a reviewed SDS; a product without one is not carried to the job (source: 29 section 8.3 interim rule, PROPOSED; X-09).

- The approved stain's product instructions are on file; application weather and temperature, moisture limit, dry and recoat times and keep-off times come from them (source: spec PT-02.SAF "verify wood dry enough per product"; C-PT02-05, C-PT02-08, C-PT02-V01).

- Weather suitable for each visit; unsuitable weather means postpone. The agreement's weather clause sets parameters that are under review against product data, and the weather and heat module does not exist yet (source: spec PT-02.SAF "postpone unsuitable weather"; agreement "The Midwest Weather Clause"; C-PT02-05; X-27).

- Two visits planned (wash day and stain day) with the drying interval between them; both employees are needed on staining day because back-brushing immediately follows the sprayer or roller (source: pricing "Minimum Trip Fee for Decks" line; original Phase 3 "Moisture Check" and Phase 4 "Mandatory Back-Brushing"; job-planner playbook "Do not treat the two-person team as two independent crews when the job needs both").
- Evidence: measurement
- Water source confirmed: HandyHub hose or the customer's spigot (source: original Phases 1 to 3; C-PT02-V02; owner decision).

- Runoff and rinse-water handling decided for the job's municipality; unknown does not mean allowed (source: 04 PT-02 "permit/license flags"; risk-triage playbook step 4). HUMAN REVIEW: local authority; no conclusion is drawn here.
- Fence work, once a procedure exists: neighbor-side permission recorded before work on the neighbor's side (source: 04 PT-02 "prerequisites", PROPOSED; HUMAN REVIEW: attorney).
- Evidence: note
- PPE selected and available; tools, moisture meter and protection loaded (source: spec START-004, START-005; APXA-001).
- Evidence: measurement
- Permit, license and qualification flags for this line determined; `unknown` blocks Start for the affected line (source: 04 section 6.1; spec START-010).
- Start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented; critical holds cannot be overridden (source: APXA-003; 31 section 8.3).
- Evidence: note
Pending review; methods come from the approved modules, none of which exists yet:
- Confirm the address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants (source: APXA-002).
- Inspect the actual site against the briefing and record differences, including the weather and the wood's condition (source: spec START-007).
- Evidence: note

- Walk the deck, railings and steps for rot, loose boards, protruding fasteners and structural defects before any chemical work; route findings to HI-10 or HI-11 (source: 04 section 5.4 rules (a) and (d), PROPOSED; agreement "Structural Integrity").
- Photograph the existing coating, the wood's condition and adjacent property before work (source: spec START-008; APXA-002; X-02).

- Protect plants and adjacent surfaces (source: spec PT-02.SAF "protect plants/adjacent surfaces"; original Phase 1). Whether exterior outlets, fixtures and equipment near the deck need covering before washing or spraying is a review item (source: 31 section 7.2 rank 4; HUMAN REVIEW: qualified safety professional).
- Keep people and pets out of the wash and spray zones (source: 02 C-PT02-09; X-08, X-11).
- Set up runoff and rinse-water controls as decided for the municipality (source: 04 PT-02 "permit/license flags"; Q-29-10).

- Place and refuel the gas washer only under a reviewed fuel and exhaust rule: TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve. (source: 29 section 7.2 item 10)
- Inspect the equipment before use per the manufacturer instructions (source: 31 section 3.1 row 7).
- Confirm the weather window for this visit against the approved product's instructions and the agreement's weather clause (source: spec PT-02.SAF; C-PT02-05).
- Complete the safety, PPE and site checks and acknowledge the SOP and hazards before starting (source: APXA-003; spec START-004).
- Evidence: note

*The original procedure follows verbatim and in its original order; its phase headings are demoted one level. The quoted HOLD and FLAG lines were added on 2026-10-03 and are pending qualified review. A HOLD placed before a step must be cleared before that step starts; a HOLD or FLAG placed after a step suspends, limits or flags it (36 D-36-17). No hold rewords, reorders or removes a step.*

> HOLD (C-PT02-05, X-27): before the stripper application step below - confirm that the weather and temperature are suitable for the work and for the approved products, per the product instructions and the agreement's weather clause; if not, postpone and record No Start / Blocked. Pending qualified review. (source: spec PT-02.SAF "postpone unsuitable weather"; spec SCH-008; 31 section 10 PT-02)

items.ref: soundness, 04 D-04-11; older coatings and treated lumber, OPEN QUESTION Q-31-07
lines: > HOLD (soundness, 04 D-04-11; older coatings and treated lumber, OPEN QUESTION Q-31-07): before the stripper application step below - walk the deck for rot, loose boards and structural defects, route any finding to HI-10 or HI-11 and do not coat over it; where the property was built before 1978 or its age is unknown, do not strip or wash an existing coating until a qualified person records a disposition; older treated lumber of unknown treatment waits for the qualified safety professional. Pending qualified review. (source: agreement "Structural Integrity"; 31 section 7.2 rank 2; 31 section 10 PT-02; risk-triage playbook L27)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧪 Phase 2: Chemical Stripping & Slurry Flushing"

lines: > HOLD (C-PT02-02, X-11): before the stripper application step below - do not pour or apply the sodium hydroxide stripper until its SDS has been reviewed and the product approved, PPE for pouring, spraying and washing it off has been selected by the qualified safety professional, the sprayer is dedicated and labeled for it (acid and caustic products never share a sprayer unless both SDSs allow it - RISK), and people and pets are out of the work area. No strength, dilution or dwell is set here. Pending qualified review. (source: spec PT-02.HAZ "chemicals"; 29 section 8.2 rows 1, 3, 4 and 8; 31 section 10 PT-02)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧪 Phase 2: Chemical Stripping & Slurry Flushing"

lines: - [ ] **Stripper Application:** Pour heavy-duty sodium hydroxide wood stripper into a plastic pump sprayer. Apply a uniform wet coat over gray, weather-beaten wood sections.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧪 Phase 2: Chemical Stripping & Slurry Flushing"

lines: - [ ] **Dwell Monitor:** Allow the chemical to sit for 15-20 minutes. *Never let the wood dry out; mist lightly with water if it begins to evaporate.*
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧪 Phase 2: Chemical Stripping & Slurry Flushing"

lines: > FLAG: UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions (product label and SDS) for the dwell time in the step above; it stays verbatim until a reviewer confirms or replaces it. (source: 31 section 3.5 rule 3; 31 section 10 PT-02)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧪 Phase 2: Chemical Stripping & Slurry Flushing"

lines: > HOLD (C-PT02-09, X-08): before the power-wash step below - confirm a pressure method appropriate for the wood from the washer manufacturer instructions and the reviewer, keep people and pets out of an exclusion zone, and wear PPE selected by the qualified safety professional; the pressure washing module does not exist yet. Pending qualified review. (source: spec PT-02.SAF "pressure appropriate"; 02 C-PT02-09; 31 section 5.8)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧪 Phase 2: Chemical Stripping & Slurry Flushing"

lines: - [ ] **Low-Pressure Power Wash:** Use a pressure washer fitted with a wide 40-degree fan nozzle. Keep the wand tip 12 inches away from the wood and sweep fluidly *with the grain*. Scrape away the liquefied gray pulp without tearing soft wood fibers.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧪 Phase 2: Chemical Stripping & Slurry Flushing"

lines: > FLAG: UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions for the nozzle angle and stand-off distance in the step above. "Low-pressure" is not tied to a stated pressure, and the listed washer's rated pressure is not confirmed as appropriate for wood (C-PT02-09). The step stays as written. (source: 31 section 3.5 rule 3; 31 section 10 PT-02)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧪 Phase 2: Chemical Stripping & Slurry Flushing"

lines: > HOLD (C-PT02-02): before the brightener step below - apply the oxalic acid brightener only with its SDS reviewed and PPE selected by the qualified safety professional (the inventory's gloves and goggles line stays mandatory), from a sprayer dedicated and labeled for the acid; never the stripper's sprayer unless both SDSs allow it (RISK). Pending qualified review. (source: inventory "Chemical-Resistant Elbow Gloves & Splash Goggles" line; 29 section 8.2 rows 3 and 4; 31 section 10 PT-02)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧴 Phase 3: Wood Brightening & Neutralization"

lines: - [ ] **pH Reset:** Spray an oxalic acid wood brightener over the freshly washed wet lumber. This instantly neutralizes the harsh alkaline stripper, kills deep mold spores, and returns the wood to its original bright blonde tone.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧴 Phase 3: Wood Brightening & Neutralization"

lines: > FLAG (X-06): "kills deep mold spores" in the step above is kept verbatim. It is an unsubstantiated antimicrobial claim and is not repeated to customers; which exterior growth this step may treat waits for the company definition that separates cleanable mildew from suspected mold growth (Q-31-10). The stop-work rule in section 10 for possible mold is not relaxed meanwhile. (source: 31 section 5.8; 04 PT-02 "permit/license flags")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧴 Phase 3: Wood Brightening & Neutralization"

lines: - [ ] **Dwell & Deep Rinse:** Let it sit for 10 minutes, then thoroughly rinse the entire deck structure and adjacent plants with a high-volume garden hose.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧴 Phase 3: Wood Brightening & Neutralization"

lines: > FLAG: UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions (product label and SDS) for the dwell time in the step above. Where the rinse water and residue may go is decided for the municipality (Q-29-10); no conclusion is drawn here. (source: 31 section 3.5 rule 3; 04 PT-02 "permit/license flags")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧴 Phase 3: Wood Brightening & Neutralization"

lines: - [ ] **Moisture Check:** Allow the wood to dry for a minimum of 48 hours. Check wood moisture levels using a digital meter—**must be below 12% to 15%** before applying oil stain.
- Evidence: measurement
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧴 Phase 3: Wood Brightening & Neutralization"

lines: > FLAG (C-PT02-08): UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions for the drying time and the moisture range in the step above. The range is ambiguous and is stated differently from the agreement's moisture clause; the limit must come from the approved product's instructions (spec PT-02.SAF "verify wood dry enough per product"). The existing check stays in force until a qualified reviewer replaces it. Record the meter reading as completion evidence; the meter is not in the inventory (proposed there). (source: 31 section 3.5 rule 3; 36 section 3.4 rule 8)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧴 Phase 3: Wood Brightening & Neutralization"

lines: > HOLD (C-PT02-05, C-PT02-02, X-27): before the perimeter cut step below - start staining only when the moisture check above has passed and is recorded, the weather and temperature suit the approved stain per its instructions and the agreement's weather clause, the stain's SDS has been reviewed, and PPE for brushing and spraying it has been selected by the qualified safety professional. Pending qualified review. (source: spec PT-02.SAF "verify wood dry enough per product", "postpone unsuitable weather"; 31 section 10 PT-02)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧳 Phase 4: Staining Application & Back-Brushing"

lines: - [ ] **Perimeter Cut:** Use a 4-inch wide thick stain brush to paint edges, vertical posts, railings, and spaces between deck boards.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧳 Phase 4: Staining Application & Back-Brushing"

lines: > HOLD (X-08, X-11): before the spray/roll step below - if the airless sprayer is used, follow the sprayer manufacturer's safety instructions, keep people and pets out of the spray zone, protect adjacent property from overspray, and confirm that conditions allow spraying without drift; the method waits for the pressure washing and airless spraying module. The step itself also names a roller. Pending qualified review. (source: original step "using a roller or airless sprayer"; 31 section 5.8; 31 section 7.2 rank 10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧳 Phase 4: Staining Application & Back-Brushing"

lines: - [ ] **Bulk Spray/Roll:** Apply the oil-based stain over flat floorboards using a roller or airless sprayer.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧳 Phase 4: Staining Application & Back-Brushing"

lines: - [ ] **Mandatory Back-Brushing:** Immediately follow the sprayer/roller with a wide stain brush, manually pushing the liquid deep into the wood pores to prevent pooling, tracking, or surface flashing blotches.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧳 Phase 4: Staining Application & Back-Brushing"

lines: > FLAG (C-PT02-04): the steps above apply oil-based stain only. Solid acrylic stain, which pricing sells as a premium, and any sealer have no approved step, product or quality check; they are not covered (section 2). (source: 31 section 10 PT-02)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧳 Phase 4: Staining Application & Back-Brushing"

lines: Observable checks from the service card (source: spec PT-02.QAC; QA-001), with the evidence in brackets. The worker self-checks; which checks need a supervisor is an owner decision (Q-31-15).

- Even preparation: stripped and brightened wood uniform, without torn or gouged fibers from washing [photos after washing; spec PT-02.QAC "even preparation"; original Phase 2 "without tearing soft wood fibers"].
- Moisture reading within the approved product's limit recorded before staining [meter reading; original Phase 3 "Moisture Check"; C-PT02-08].
- Evidence: measurement, note
- Even coating with no pooling, tracking or flashing blotches after back-brushing [after photos per area; original Phase 4 "Mandatory Back-Brushing"; spec QA-003].
- Evidence: photo

- No lap or overspray defects beyond the agreed tolerance on the wood, siding, glass, plants, vehicles or neighboring property; the tolerance itself is not defined yet (owner decision) [after photos compared with the arrival photos; spec PT-02.QAC; spec START-008].
- Evidence: photo
- Dry and cure guidance given to the customer from approved product data [care-note record; spec PT-02.QAC "dry/cure guidance provided"; spec QA-008; C-PT02-V01].
- Evidence: note
- Site protected and clean: masking removed, rags and cleaners controlled, signs placed [cleanup note; spec PT-02.QAC "site protected/clean"; spec QA-002].

- [ ] **Oily Rags Disposal:** *Safety Warning:* Submerge all oil-soaked cloths and brush cleaners in a water-filled metal bucket immediately. Air-dry flat afterward to prevent spontaneous combustion fires.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Clean-up & Drying Rules"

lines: > FLAG (C-PT02-V02): the step above stays exactly as written; it is the only fire control in any PT-02 file. Rags and brush cleaner are not in the inventory (proposed there); the brush cleaner is selected and disposed of per its SDS, and where soaked rags and used cleaner go afterwards is decided per municipality (Q-29-10). Pending qualified review. (source: 29 section 8.1; 31 section 3.1 row 15)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Clean-up & Drying Rules"

lines: - [ ] **Drying Signs:** Place "Wet Paint/Stain" signs at deck entryways. Inform the homeowner to keep foot traffic off for 24 hours and heavy furniture off for 48 hours.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Clean-up & Drying Rules"

lines: > FLAG (C-PT02-V01): UNSOURCED - verify against manufacturer instructions for the keep-off times in the step above. They differ from the inventory's barrier window and the agreement's drying-window wording; one product-sourced set of keep-off times must appear in this SOP, the inventory, the agreement and the customer care note (owner and estimator decide; OPEN QUESTION). The step stays as written until then. (source: 02 C-PT02-V01; 31 section 3.5 rule 3; spec QA-008)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Clean-up & Drying Rules"

lines: Source: spec QA-002; APXA-005; pending review:
- Remove masking film, tape and other protection (source: original Phase 1; spec QA-002).
- Handle oil-soaked rags and brush cleaners exactly as the original oily-rag step says (source: original Phase 5 "Oily Rags Disposal").
- Clean the work area; keep chemical residue and used materials for the reviewed waste route (section 15).

- Account for tools, equipment and remaining materials; secure chemical containers for transport under the chemical program, which does not exist yet; segregation of the caustic stripper and the acid brightener comes from the reviewer's SDS-based groups (source: 29 section 8.2 rows 5 and 6).
- Restore anything altered within scope, such as moved items or the customer's water connection (source: APXA-005).
TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

- Waste streams: rinse water and runoff that may carry stripper, brightener and stripped coating; stripped residue scraped off the wood; oil-soaked rags and used brush cleaner; empty chemical containers; used masking film (source: original Phases 2, 3 and 5; 29 section 8.2 row 10; 04 PT-02 "permit/license flags").
- The oily-rag step in the original procedure stays exactly as written; it is a fire control, not a disposal destination (source: original Phase 5; 29 section 8.1).

- Destination and method per municipality: HUMAN REVIEW: local authority and qualified safety professional (Q-29-10; 31 section 5.8 waste, runoff and disposal module). No conclusion is drawn here on discharge or disposal rules.
- Residue from existing coatings at older properties stays a hazardous-material question until the older-coating disposition is recorded (Q-31-07).
- Evidence: note
- Hazardous waste is not handled without an approved policy (source: 31 section 3.1 row 15).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: Photos are internal-only by default and avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).

- Before: arrival and existing-condition photos of the existing coating, the wood's condition (rot, splitting, loose boards) and adjacent property, plants and siding (source: spec START-008; APXA-002; 04 PT-02 "completion evidence", PROPOSED; X-02).
- Evidence: photo
- During: post-strip photos and the pre-stain moisture reading (source: 04 PT-02 "completion evidence", PROPOSED; C-PT02-08).
- Evidence: measurement
- After: after photos mapped to each area, such as deck floor, railings and steps (source: spec QA-003), and the cleanup note (source: spec QA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- Arrival and completion updates are drafts; the worker or an administrator controls the actual send according to policy (source: spec UXE-008).
- Weather or drying delays: the reschedule is recorded with its reason and the customer notification result (source: spec CX-006, SCH-007; agreement "The Midwest Weather Clause").
- Evidence: note
- Record the walkthrough outcome: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Care notes, including keep-off and recoat information, come only from approved product data (source: spec QA-008; C-PT02-V01).
- Explain the invoice and payment next step without making unauthorized promises; whether final payment may fall due before a walkthrough or cure check is an open question (source: APXA-006; X-14).
- Blocked work: use only the approved "work blocked" message (source: spec NTF-007).

- Do not describe the chemicals as eco-friendly, eco-safe, non-toxic or harmless to plants, pets or people (C-PT02-01); do not say that mold is killed (X-06); do not promise a product lifespan, waterproofing or any result (agreement "Moisture Limit Guarantee" wording under attorney review; Do not perform entry 8).
Definition of done (source: spec QA-001 to QA-006; PT-02.QAC; APXA-005, APXA-006):
- Every section 13 check answered, or an exception recorded (QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- Moisture reading recorded before staining (C-PT02-08).
- Evidence: measurement, note
- After photos mapped to areas (QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup done, protection removed, oily rags and cleaners handled as the original step says (QA-002; original Phase 5).
- Drying signs placed and the care note from approved product data given (original Phase 5; QA-008).
- Anything altered within scope restored (APXA-005).
- Punch items recorded with an owner and a due date (QA-005).
- Evidence: note
- Walkthrough outcome recorded (QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- No hold left open; any incident reported (section 20; APXA-007).
- Evidence: note
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:
Service-specific stop triggers (source: spec PT-02.SAF unless noted; PROPOSED wording pending qualified review):

- Unsuitable weather for the work or the product: postpone; record No Start / Blocked instead of starting, and stop if conditions change during work (PT-02.SAF "postpone unsuitable weather"; spec SCH-008, START-011; C-PT02-05).
- Evidence: note
- Wood not dry enough for the approved product, or no meter reading recorded: do not apply stain (PT-02.SAF "verify wood dry enough per product"; C-PT02-08).
- Plants and adjacent surfaces cannot be protected: do not apply chemicals or spray (PT-02.SAF "protect plants/adjacent surfaces").
- Pressure not confirmed as appropriate for the wood, or anyone in the wash or spray zone: do not wash or spray (PT-02.SAF "pressure appropriate"; C-PT02-09; X-08).
- Oily rags or brush cleaners cannot be controlled as the oily-rag step requires: stop (PT-02.SAF "manage oily rags").
- Rot, loose boards, protruding fasteners or other structural defects found: stop, record (JOB-004) and route to HI-10 or HI-11 (agreement "Structural Integrity"; 04 section 5.4 rule (a)).
- Evidence: note
- Existing coating at a property built before 1978 or of unknown age: do not strip, wash or sand it; escalate (Q-31-07; 31 section 7.2 rank 2).
- No reviewed SDS or no selected PPE for a chemical step: do not start that step (C-PT02-02; 29 section 8.3).

Service holds (inserted in section 12). Critical holds cannot be overridden (31 section 8.3); a hold that exists because a required module or policy is missing (pressure washing, chemicals and SDS, weather, old-property screening) behaves as a critical hold until that module is approved (31 section 8.4 rule 4, PROPOSED):
| Hold | Where in section 12 | Release role and evidence |

| C-PT02-05, X-27: weather and temperature suitable per the product instructions and the agreement's weather clause | Before "Stripper Application" and before "Perimeter Cut" | Owner or estimator from the product instructions; qualified safety professional (heat plan) |

| Soundness walk (04 D-04-11, PROPOSED; X-02) and older coatings and treated lumber (OPEN QUESTION, Q-31-07) | Before "Stripper Application" | HI-10 or HI-11 assessment for defects; EPA RRP-certified renovator and qualified safety professional for older coatings and lumber |

| C-PT02-02: SDS reviewed and PPE selected for every chemical step, including the sodium hydroxide stripper; acid and caustic products never share a sprayer unless both SDSs allow it (RISK) | Before "Stripper Application", "pH Reset" and "Perimeter Cut" | Qualified safety professional: SDS-based PPE selection and sprayer rule recorded |

| X-08, C-PT02-09: pressure washing and airless spraying module (method, exclusion zone, PPE) | Before "Low-Pressure Power Wash" and "Bulk Spray/Roll" | Qualified safety professional, once the module is approved |
| C-PT02-08: moisture limit per the approved product | After "Moisture Check" (the existing check stays in force) | Owner or estimator from the product instructions |
| C-PT02-V01: keep-off times per the approved product | After "Drying Signs" | Owner or estimator from the product instructions |
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
Service roles (contacts are owner decisions, Q-31-05):
- Chemical, pressure-washing, spraying and weather holds in sections 10 and 12: qualified safety professional.
- Older coatings and treated lumber: EPA RRP-certified renovator and qualified safety professional (Q-31-07).
- Rot or structural findings: owner, routing to HI-10 or HI-11 by change order.
- Product limits (moisture, weather, dry and keep-off times): owner or estimator from the approved product instructions.
- Scope questions (fences, under-deck work, stairs, sanding, solid acrylic stain, sealer): owner.
- Runoff and disposal rules: local authority, through the legal-compliance lens; no conclusion is drawn here.
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].
**HUMAN REVIEW:** attorney licensed in KY and/or IN for the fault and liability sentence; insurance broker for any insurer-notification step added later.

Examples for this service, all reported under JOB-008 (source: spec PT-02.HAZ): a caustic or acid splash or exposure; an injection injury or near miss from the washer or the airless sprayer; a slip on a wet or stained surface; a rag or cleaner fire; plant, siding, vehicle or neighboring-property damage from chemicals or overspray; equipment failure. First-response provisions depend on the vehicle safety kit, which is not yet defined (X-10).

- Q-31-07 (owner; EPA RRP-certified renovator; accredited asbestos inspector): which property-age threshold triggers lead screening before existing deck and fence coatings are stripped, washed or sanded, and does HandyHub hold or plan EPA RRP certification? Older treated lumber of unknown treatment needs the same answer from the qualified safety professional.
- Q-31-10 (owner; qualified mold assessor): what is the company definition of mold growth versus cleanable mildew ("kills deep mold spores" wording, X-06)?
- Q-31-11 (owner; qualified safety professional): what goes in the emergency kit, who owns the SDS register, and how are the caustic, acid and oil-based products stored and transported?
- Q-31-09 (owner; qualified safety professional): height and access policy, if fence tops or under-deck work are offered.
- Q-31-05 (owner): who are the emergency and escalation contacts and in what order (section 19 placeholders)?
- Q-31-15 (owner): which quality or safety checks need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check?
- Q-31-02 (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish version?
- Q-04-09 (owner; qualified safety professional): is washing wood without staining offered, and as a PT-02 line or a separate line?
- Q-04-13 (owner; qualified safety professional): which qualification tags release pressure washing, chemical application and airless spraying?
- Q-29-10 (local authority; safety reviewer): where may rinse water, stripped residue, oil-soaked rags and used brush cleaner go in each service municipality?
- Open questions recorded with C-PT02-04, C-PT02-06 and C-PT02-07 in 02 (owner): offer, define or withdraw solid acrylic stain, sanding, fence and under-deck staining, and sealing?
- Open questions recorded with C-PT02-08 and C-PT02-V01 in 02 (owner; estimator with manufacturer instructions): which moisture limit and keep-off times does the approved stain require?

sops.title: SOP PT-03: Brick Limewashing & Elastomeric Masonry Coatings

lines: From the agreement and the spec, pending review:
- Vehicles kept away from the building during active spray windows (source: agreement "Overspray Prevention"; the distance it states is under attorney and safety review, 30 section 5 row 91).
- Option, color or sample chosen before scheduling (source: spec PT-03.INT "product/system, color/sample"; agreement Option A and B checkboxes).
- Every job re-confirms access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions (source: spec CX-005).

GAP - not yet in the agreement or any reminder (owner decision; wording through 30 and 32): any HOA or historic-district approval; water and power access; windows and doors closed; HVAC intakes; pets and children kept indoors; outdoor furniture and items moved; plants; neighbor notice (source: 04 PT-03 "customer preparation requirements"; X-11).
Dispatch and Start Job conditions, pending review:

- Approved estimate version with the selected option (Option A limewash or Option B elastomeric coating), the elevations and areas, and any rental, each separately identifiable (source: spec CX-003, EST-005; APXA-001 "review scope/exclusions").
- Intake recorded: masonry type and condition, efflorescence and cracks, moisture source, product or system, color or sample, height and access, weather (source: spec PT-03.INT).
- Evidence: note

- Moisture-source disposition recorded by the qualified reviewer before any coating; unknown means not ready, and no moisture threshold is set here (source: spec PT-03.SAF "address active moisture cause before coating when required"; C-PT03-05). HUMAN REVIEW: qualified masonry or building-envelope professional.
- Evidence: note

- Coating system confirmed as compatible with the masonry and any existing coating or sealer, from the manufacturer's data for the named product (source: spec PT-03.SAF "confirm compatible coating system"; C-PT03-02). HUMAN REVIEW: qualified masonry or building-envelope professional; coating manufacturer technical data.

- Previously painted or sealed brick and the build year recorded at intake and screened with the old-property screening questions. The property-age threshold that triggers lead screening is an open question (Q-31-07), and a painted surface is not cleared by a customer saying it looks safe (source: 04 section 6.2 "lead (c)"; 31 section 5.8; risk-triage playbook). HUMAN REVIEW: EPA RRP-certified renovator; applicability is not concluded here.
- Evidence: note

- Every chemical product approved with a reviewed SDS: the masonry cleaner, any bleach, the efflorescence cleanser, slaked lime, the elastomeric coating, glass cleaner and any engine fuel. A product without a reviewed SDS is not carried to the job (source: 29 section 8.3 interim rule, PROPOSED; C-PT03-01).

- Access plan approved for any roof-edge, soffit, fascia, gutter or upper-story work and for any lift; no height and access policy exists yet (source: spec PT-03.SAF "weather and height controls"; C-PT03-04; X-12; Q-31-09). A rented lift also needs its rental record, inspection-out and an operator with the matching qualification tag (source: 29 section 9.2 steps 4 and 5).
- Evidence: note

- Weather acceptable under the weather and heat module, which does not exist yet, and within the application limits in the product data; severe weather is a stop condition (source: spec PT-03.INT "weather", PT-03.SAF; X-27; START-011). TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.
- Water and power for washing and spraying confirmed on site; who supplies them is an owner decision (source: 04 PT-03 "customer preparation requirements", GAP).

- Wash-water and runoff handling decided for the job's municipality; unknown does not mean allowed (source: 04 PT-03 "permit/license flags"; risk-triage playbook step 4). HUMAN REVIEW: local authority; no conclusion is drawn here.

- Whether a historic-district or HOA approval applies, and who obtains it, recorded as the customer reports it (source: 04 PT-03 "permit/license flags", OPEN QUESTION). HUMAN REVIEW: attorney licensed in KY/IN and the local authority; no conclusion is drawn here.
- Evidence: note

- PPE selected and available, including skin and eye protection for lime; tools, access equipment, masking and protection loaded; rentals checked (source: spec PT-03.SAF; START-004, START-005; APXA-001 "check customer-supplied items/rentals").
- Workers hold the qualification tags for pressure washing, airless spraying and lift use once they are defined (source: spec SCH-003, START-010; Q-04-13).
- Permit, license and qualification flags for this line determined; `unknown` blocks Start for the affected line (source: 04 section 6.1; spec START-010).
- Start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented; critical holds cannot be overridden (source: APXA-003; 31 section 8.3).
- Evidence: note
Pending review; methods come from the approved modules, none of which exists yet:
- Confirm the address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants (source: APXA-002).
- Inspect the actual site against the briefing and record differences (source: spec START-007).
- Evidence: note

- Photograph each elevation before work: existing cracks, spalling, loose mortar, efflorescence, stains and coatings, window glass, landscaping, driveways and adjacent property (source: spec START-008; APXA-002; X-02; agreement "Pre-existing Masonry Defects").
- Set up barriers and keep people and pets out of the wash and spray zones (source: X-08; X-11).

- Protect electrical fixtures, outlets, meters and openings from direct spray before washing; the original order washes before the Phase 2 masking, and that sequence is under review (source: 31 section 10 PT-03; 04 PT-03 "hazards").
- Protect landscaping, plants, driveways and vehicles before spraying: method not yet defined (C-PT03-08). TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.
- Set up rinse-water and runoff controls as decided for the municipality (source: 04 PT-03 "permit/license flags"; Q-29-10).

- Set up access equipment only under the approved access plan; for a rented lift, record the inspection-out with photos and attach the rental-yard instructions (source: C-PT03-04; 29 section 9.2 step 5).
- Evidence: note
- Inspect the pressure washer, airless sprayer, hoses and access equipment before use per the manufacturer or rental instructions (source: 31 section 3.1 row 7; spec START-005).
- Confirm the water and power supply (source: 04 PT-03 "customer preparation requirements", GAP).
- Complete the safety, PPE and site checks and acknowledge the SOP and hazards before starting (source: APXA-003; spec START-004).
- Evidence: note

*The original procedure follows verbatim and in its original order; its phase headings are demoted one level. The quoted HOLD and FLAG lines were added on 2026-10-03 and are pending qualified review. A HOLD placed before a step must be cleared before that step starts; a HOLD or FLAG placed after a step suspends, limits or flags it (36 D-36-17). No hold rewords, reorders or removes a step.*
- [ ] **Efflorescence Scrape:** Use a stiff wire brush to scrub away chalky white salt deposits (efflorescence) from old brick faces.

lines: > HOLD (C-PT03-05): the step above removes efflorescence but does not address its cause. Photograph and record where efflorescence was found (spec PT-03.QAC "defects/limitations documented"), and do not start any step of Phase 3 or Phase 4 until a qualified reviewer has recorded the moisture-source disposition. No moisture threshold is set here. Pending qualified review. (source: spec PT-03.SAF "address active moisture cause before coating when required"; PT-03.INT "efflorescence/cracks, moisture source")

lines: > HOLD (C-PT03-01): before the "Mildew Wash" step below - NO MIXING - pending SDS-based product selection. Do not mix the masonry cleaner with bleach or any other product, and do not apply it, until a named product has been selected and its SDS, and the SDS of anything it would be combined with, reviewed and approved by the qualified safety professional. Use, mix and apply only as the approved label allows; no product, ratio or dwell is set here. Plants, openings, people and pets are protected and runoff control is in place before any application. Pending qualified review. The stop-work rule in section 10 lists possible mold; which exterior growth this step may treat is decided by the qualified reviewer once the company definition that separates cleanable mildew and staining from suspected mold growth exists (Q-31-10). Until then the stop-work rule is not relaxed. (source: 31 section 5.8)

If loose or crumbling mortar or spalling brick appears, stop washing that area and follow section 10. Pending qualified review. (source: spec PT-03.HAZ "pressure wash", PT-03.INT "weather"; agreement "Pre-existing Masonry Defects"; 31 sections 5.8 and 10)

lines: - [ ] **High-Pressure Cleanse:** Power wash the entire brick envelope at 2,500-3,000 PSI to clear out deep dirt, mud splatters, and organic residue from porous masonry joints.

It stays verbatim until a qualified reviewer confirms or replaces it; no value is set here, and no pressure washer is listed in the inventory yet. (source: 31 section 3.5 rule 3; 31 section 10 PT-03)

A wind limit for spraying is an open question; no value is set here.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🪟 Phase 2: High-Volume Spray Masking"

lines: - [ ] **Total Window Wrap:** Wrap all windows, exterior light fixtures, entry doors, and utility meters completely in 3-mil masking film, securing edges tightly with high-adhesion outdoor tape.

Pending qualified review. (source: 31 section 10 PT-03; 04 PT-03 "hazards")

Ladders, lifts and fall protection are selected and approved by the qualified safety professional; no setup tolerance is set here. Pending qualified review. (source: spec PT-03.SAF "weather and height controls"; PT-03.TLS "access equipment"; 31 section 10 PT-03; Q-31-09)

lines: - [ ] **Roofline Protection:** Tuck plastic flashing underneath the first row of roof shingles to prevent spray drift from staining the roof.

lines: - [ ] **Soffit Masking:** Tape off all under-roof vinyl soffits, fascia boards, and aluminum gutters.

Not covered - pending review (section 2); open question recorded with C-PT03-07 in 02.

Pending qualified review. (source: spec PT-03.SAF "confirm compatible coating system", "address active moisture cause before coating when required")

The "instructions" named in that step are the approved limewash product's label and data sheet; mix, pre-wet and apply only as they state. Pending qualified review. (source: spec PT-03.SAF "PPE/skin/eye protection"; PT-03.HAZ "chemical/alkaline materials"; 29 section 8.2 row 8)

lines: - [ ] **Slaking Slurry Mix:** Mix authentic Italian Class-A slaked lime powder with water according to instructions until a milk-like consistency is reached.

lines: - [ ] **Saturating the Masonry:** Spray the brick wall with water right before application—*Limewash requires a wet brick canvas to bind chemically.*
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧪 Phase 3: Execution - Option A: Authentic Limewash Look"

lines: - [ ] **Masonry Brush Apply:** Use a large, thick block brush to work the limewash slurry into the brick pores using cross-hatch strokes.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧪 Phase 3: Execution - Option A: Authentic Limewash Look"

lines: > HOLD (C-PT03-03, X-08): before the "Artisanal Distressing" step below - the "light pressure washer mist" in that step falls under the same pressure-washing hold as "High-Pressure Cleanse" (method and pressure from the manufacturer instructions and the qualified safety professional; people and pets out of the zone). Until that hold is released, only the damp-sponge method named in the same step is available. Pending qualified review. (source: spec PT-03.HAZ "pressure wash"; 31 section 10 PT-03)

lines: - [ ] **Artisanal Distressing:** Wait 30 minutes for the limewash to partially set. Use a light pressure washer mist or a damp sponge to selectively wash away wash coats from edges/corners, exposing natural brick hints for an old-world look.
