lines: Source: spec QA-002; APXA-005; pending review:
- Remove masking film, tape, flashing and other protection (original "Film Strip").
- Clean the work area; keep film, tape, used blades, washout and residues for the reviewed waste route (section 15).

- Account for tools, equipment and remaining materials; secure lime, coating and chemical containers for transport under the chemical program, which does not exist yet (source: 29 section 8.2 rows 5 and 6).
- Return rented equipment with inspection-in photos and a return receipt (source: APXA-007 "return unused materials/rentals"; 29 section 9.2 step 7).
- Restore anything altered within scope (source: APXA-005).
TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

- Waste streams: wash water and runoff that may carry cleaner and bleach residue and efflorescence; lime slurry and limewash washout; elastomeric coating washout and sprayer flush; used masking film and tape; used razor blades; empty product containers (source: 29 section 8.2 row 10; original steps; 31 section 5.8 waste module).
- Destination and method per municipality: HUMAN REVIEW: local authority and qualified safety professional (Q-29-10). No conclusion is drawn here on discharge or disposal rules.
- Hazardous waste is not handled without an approved policy (source: 31 section 3.1 row 15).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: Photos are internal-only by default and avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).

- Before: each elevation, with existing cracks, spalling, loose mortar, efflorescence, stains, existing coatings, window glass, landscaping, driveways, vehicles and adjacent property (source: spec START-008; APXA-002; X-02).

- During: masking complete; any concealed condition found, such as loose mortar or a moisture source (source: spec JOB-004); the test section and the customer's sign-off once a reviewed step exists (C-PT03-07).
- Evidence: note
- After: each elevation mapped (source: spec QA-003); de-masked openings and glass; the ground and landscaping (original "Ground Audit"); the runoff and cleanup note (source: spec QA-002).
- Arrival and completion updates are drafts; the worker or an administrator controls the actual send according to policy (source: spec UXE-008).
- Report loose mortar, moisture findings and other blocked work only with the approved "work blocked" message (source: spec NTF-007; agreement "Pre-existing Masonry Defects").
- Evidence: note
- Record the walkthrough outcome: accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- Cure, care and reapplication notes come only from the approved product data (source: spec QA-008).

- Do not tell the customer that a coating is "breathable" or "waterproof", that cracks will be sealed or bridged, or that the spray zone is completely isolated (C-PT03-02, C-PT03-08; Do not perform entry 8). Do not describe the agreement's "Site Protection & Masking Warranty" heading as a warranty: no warranty terms exist, and the heading is under attorney review (30 section 5 row 6).
Definition of done (source: spec QA-001 to QA-006; PT-03.QAC; APXA-005, APXA-006):
- Every section 13 check answered, or an exception recorded (QA-001).
- Evidence: note
- After photos mapped to elevations (QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup done; masking and protection removed (QA-002).
- Rented equipment returned with inspection-in records (APXA-007; 29 section 9.2).
- Evidence: note
- Anything altered within scope restored (APXA-005).
- Punch items recorded with an owner and a due date (QA-005).
- Evidence: note
- Walkthrough outcome recorded (QA-004).
- Evidence: note
- No hold left open; any incident reported (section 20; APXA-007).
- Evidence: note
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:
Service-specific stop triggers (source: spec PT-03.SAF unless noted; PROPOSED wording pending qualified review):
- Coating system not confirmed as compatible with the masonry and any existing coating or sealer: do not coat ("confirm compatible coating system").

- An active moisture source, or efflorescence that points to one, with no recorded disposition: do not coat; stop and escalate ("address active moisture cause before coating when required"; C-PT03-05).
- Required PPE, including skin and eye protection, not available: do not handle lime or chemicals ("PPE/skin/eye protection").
- Unsuitable weather, or height or access beyond the approved policy: record No Start / Blocked or stop ("weather and height controls"; spec SCH-008, START-011).
- Evidence: note

- Loose or crumbling mortar or spalling brick found during washing: stop washing that area, photograph it, record it (JOB-004) and report it with the approved message (agreement "Pre-existing Masonry Defects"; Do not perform entry 9).
- Evidence: note
- People or pets enter the wash or spray zone, or spray drifts toward vehicles, plants or neighboring property: stop (X-11; C-PT03-08).
- Any instruction to mix the masonry cleaner with bleach before an approved product and SDS review: do not mix (C-PT03-01).
- A gas meter, regulator or vent would have to be wrapped or covered to continue: stop and escalate (Do not perform entry 10).

Service holds (inserted in section 12). Critical holds cannot be overridden (31 section 8.3); a hold that exists because a required module or policy is missing (height and access, pressure washing, chemicals and SDS, weather) behaves as a critical hold until that module is approved (31 section 8.4 rule 4, PROPOSED):
| Hold | Where in section 12 | Release role and evidence |

| C-PT03-05: efflorescence is a moisture indicator; no coating until the moisture-source disposition is recorded | After "Efflorescence Scrape"; before the first step of each option | Qualified masonry or building-envelope professional: disposition recorded |
| C-PT03-01: NO MIXING - pending SDS-based product selection | Before "Mildew Wash" | Qualified safety professional: named product, reviewed SDSs and approved label method recorded |

| C-PT03-03, X-08: pressure washing; pressure figure UNVERIFIED; washing before masking is a sequence under review | Before and after "High-Pressure Cleanse"; before "Artisanal Distressing" | Qualified safety professional: method reviewed against the masonry condition and manufacturer instructions, approval recorded; the pressure-washing module once approved |
| Gas meters, regulators and occupant exit (31 section 10 seed; X-11) | After "Total Window Wrap" | Gas utility or licensed gas professional (gas meters); qualified safety professional |

| C-PT03-04, X-12: no roof-edge or elevated work until an access plan is approved | Before "Roofline Protection" and "Soffit Masking" | Qualified safety professional: approved height and access policy and job access plan recorded |

| C-PT03-02, C-PT03-05: compatible coating system and moisture disposition before coating | Before the first step of Option A and of Option B | Qualified masonry or building-envelope professional, with the coating manufacturer data |
| PT-03.SAF lime PPE: skin and eye protection before slaking | Before "Slaking Slurry Mix" | Qualified safety professional: PPE selected and available |
| X-08, X-11: airless spraying per the sprayer manufacturer's safety instructions | Before "Airless Spray Setup" | Qualified safety professional; sprayer manufacturer instructions |
| X-17: glass condition recorded before scraping | Before "Overspray Scrape" | Qualified safety professional (scraping method) |
| X-27 weather | Inside the holds before the washing step | Qualified safety professional, once the weather and heat module is approved |
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
Service roles (contacts are owner decisions, Q-31-05):
- Safety holds in sections 10 and 12 (height and lifts, pressure washing, chemicals, lime PPE, airless spraying): qualified safety professional.
- Moisture source and coating compatibility: qualified masonry or building-envelope professional, with the coating manufacturer's technical data.
- Gas meters and regulators: the gas utility or a licensed gas professional.
- Scope questions (masonry repair, test section, landscape protection, commercial work): owner; referrals only under the owner's referral policy (Q-30-15).
- Runoff and disposal rules: local authority, through the legal-compliance lens; no conclusion is drawn here.
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].
**HUMAN REVIEW:** attorney licensed in KY and/or IN for the fault and liability sentence; insurance broker for any insurer-notification step added later.

Examples for this service, all reported under JOB-008 (source: spec PT-03.HAZ): a fall or near fall from a ladder, lift or roof edge; a pressure-washer or airless injection injury or near miss; a lime or chemical splash or exposure; overspray on vehicles, plants or neighboring property; scratched or broken glass; an equipment or rental failure. First-response provisions depend on the vehicle safety kit, which is not yet defined (X-10).
- **Q-31-09** (owner; qualified safety professional): what height and access policy applies (maximum working heights, equipment types, who may use lifts) to the roofline, soffit and two-story work?
- **Q-31-10** (owner; qualified mold assessor): what is the company definition of mold growth versus cleanable mildew, and the stop rule ("Mildew Wash", X-06)?
- **Q-31-11** (owner; qualified safety professional): what goes in the emergency kit, who owns the SDS register, and how are lime, coatings and cleaners stored and transported?

- **Q-31-07** (owner; EPA RRP-certified renovator; accredited asbestos inspector): which property-age thresholds trigger lead screening for previously painted brick, and does HandyHub hold or plan EPA RRP certification?
- **Q-31-05** (owner): who are the emergency and escalation contacts, and in what order (section 19 placeholders)?
- **Q-31-15** (owner): which quality or safety checks need a supervisor rather than the worker's self-check?
- **Q-31-02** (owner): who is the qualified bilingual reviewer for the Spanish version?
- **Q-04-13** (owner; qualified safety professional): which qualification tags release pressure washing, airless spraying, chemical cleaning and lift use?
- **Q-29-10** (local authority; safety reviewer): where may wash water, cleaner residue, lime slurry and coating washout go in each service municipality?
- **Q-30-15** (owner): what is the referral policy for masonry repair found during the work?
- Open question in 31 section 10 PT-03 (gas utility or licensed gas professional): may workers mask near gas meters and regulators at all, and how?

- Open questions recorded with C-PT03-02, C-PT03-07 and C-PT03-08 in 02 (owner; attorney; coating manufacturer data; qualified safety professional): which limewash and elastomeric products are used and what permeability claim their data supports; is the test section offered and priced, and is limewash brushed or sprayed; what wind limit applies to spraying?

sops.title: SOP PT-04: Wallpaper Removal & Surface Restoration

lines: PROPOSED for owner approval; customer-facing wording goes through 30 and 32.
- Furniture, wall hangings and window treatments are moved away from the walls to be stripped (source: 04 PT-04 "customer preparation requirements", GAP).
- Children and pets are kept away from steam, chemicals and electrical boxes during the work (source: 04 PT-04; spec CX-005; X-11).
- Ventilation is possible where oil-based primer will be used (source: 04 PT-04; inventory "Oil-Based Stain-Blocking Primer"; ventilation per SDS).
- Running water is accessible on site (source: agreement "Running Hot Water" clause).
- Access is available for more than one visit because of the drying wait (source: 04 PT-04 "customer preparation requirements").
- The customer states the build year, if known, and any known leaks, past mold or other hazards (source: spec PT-04.INT "age"; 30 section 4.1 clause 5 "disclosures the customer is asked to make").

- The agreement's breaker-permission and power clause is under attorney and licensed-electrician review; it is not relied on to clear any electrical hold (source: 30 section 5 row 84; 30 section 3.2 rule 6).
- Every job re-confirms access, occupants, pets, parking, hazards and work-area conditions (source: spec CX-005).
- [ ] **Electrical Cut:** Turn off circuit breakers for wall outlets in the active room to prevent liquid shorts.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Space Containment & Baseboard Masking"

lines: > HOLD (C-PT04-03): the step above is held. Who may switch breakers, and the isolation method, are pending licensed-electrician review; switching breakers alone is not a verified isolation. Before any wet or steam work near an outlet or switch box, the de-energized state is verified with an approved tester, by the method the licensed electrician approves; if it cannot be verified, STOP and escalate. Pending licensed-electrician and qualified safety review. (source: spec PT-04.SAF "protect/de-energize near outlets as appropriate"; 02 C-PT04-03; X-07; agreement "Active Electrical Isolation" clause, under attorney review)

lines: - [ ] **Outlet Plugging:** Stuff wall electrical boxes with plastic bag scrapers and tape them shut tightly.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Space Containment & Baseboard Masking"

lines: > HOLD (C-PT04-03): the step above is held. Nothing is placed inside an electrical box until a box-protection method is approved by a licensed electrician; no electrical procedure is written here. Pending licensed-electrician review. (source: 02 C-PT04-03; 31 section 10 PT-04)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Space Containment & Baseboard Masking"

lines: - [ ] **Floor Protection:** Lay thick plastic sheeting along the floor edges, taping it securely over baseboards to catch sticky glue droplets and liquid runoff.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🕒 Phase 1: Space Containment & Baseboard Masking"

lines: - This SOP is not active: no job uses it until competent review and owner activation (source: owner facts 2026-10-02; 31 section 2.1).

- An approved estimate version exists for the job, naming the walls, the finish level and whether any primer coat is included (source: spec CX-003, EST-005; spec PT-04.QAC "removed to agreed level", "primed if included"; C-PT04-06).
- Intake recorded: wallpaper type and layers, wall substrate, age, painted or unpainted wall, room area and desired finish (source: spec PT-04.INT).
- Evidence: note

- Property age and older coatings: in a building built before 1978 or of unknown age, or where older joint compound or a coating is suspect, no scoring, scraping, scrubbing or sanding starts until a qualified person records a disposition. "A pre-1978 painted surface is not cleared by a customer saying it looks safe." (source: spec PT-04.SAF; 02 C-PT04-04; X-13; risk-triage playbook; Q-31-07).
- Evidence: note

- Electrical isolation: no wet or steam work near an outlet or switch box until the isolation method approved by a licensed electrician is applied and the de-energized state is verified with an approved tester (source: spec PT-04.SAF "protect/de-energize near outlets as appropriate"; 02 C-PT04-03; X-07). The agreement's breaker-permission clause is under attorney and electrician review and does not replace this check.

- Steamer power: how the steamer is powered is pending licensed-electrician review; the agreement's "reachable junction box" wording is not a method (source: agreement "Active Electrical Isolation" clause; 02 C-PT04-03).
- Running water is available on site (source: agreement "Running Hot Water" clause).
- Access over more than one visit: walls dry completely after "Fresh Water Flush" before skim coating (source: original "Fresh Water Flush" step; 04 PT-04 "labor assumptions").

- Product labels and SDS for the stripper, adhesive remover, primer and compound are available and reviewed; a chemical product without a reviewed SDS is not carried to the job (source: 29 section 8.3, PROPOSED; X-09).
- Ladder work only under an approved height and access policy, which does not exist yet (source: spec PT-04.HAZ "ladder"; 02 G-005; X-12).

- Before leaving: confirm the correct job, customer, address and time; read the latest changes; review scope and exclusions; review hazards and safety; load critical tools, equipment and materials; check customer-supplied items; confirm required documents and approvals (source: spec APXA-001).

- Before starting: complete the required safety, PPE and site checks; confirm materials; acknowledge the SOP and hazards; start only when Ready or an authorized exception is documented (source: spec APXA-003, START-004).
- Evidence: note

- On arrival: confirm the address, work area and contact; identify pets and occupants; inspect the actual site against the briefing; capture the required existing-condition photos; protect the work area; identify utilities and emergency constraints relevant to the task (source: spec APXA-002).
- Evidence: photo
- Confirm that the site matches the briefing, or record the differences; material differences trigger Risk Triage or supervisor review (source: spec START-007).
- Evidence: note

- Existing-condition photos of every wall to be stripped, including damage already present, before protection or work starts; the agreement's "Damage Disclaimer" depends on this evidence (source: spec START-008; X-02).
- Evidence: photo
- Keep children and pets out of the work area (source: X-11; spec CX-005).
- Electrical isolation and box protection follow the holds in section 12, Phase 1; no wet or steam work starts until the de-energized state is verified (source: 02 C-PT04-03; X-07).
- Floor protection: the original "Floor Protection" step in section 12, Phase 1.
- The removal-method test comes before any scoring or saturation: section 12 hold before "Wall Scoring" (source: spec PT-04.SAF "test removal method"; 02 C-PT04-07).
- Ventilation set-up before any oil-based primer use, per the SDS: TBD - qualified safety reviewer (source: inventory "Oil-Based Stain-Blocking Primer"; 29 section 8.1).
- Ladder set-up only under an approved height and access policy: TBD (source: 02 G-005; X-12).
- Safety, PPE and site checks are complete and the SOP hazards acknowledged before starting (source: spec APXA-003, START-004).
- Evidence: note

*Original procedure, verbatim and in its original order. HOLD and FLAG lines are added drafts pending qualified review (31 section 10). A hold placed before a step must be satisfied before that step starts; a hold or flag placed after a step limits or flags "the step above" (36 D-36-17).*

> HOLD (C-PT04-04): before "Wall Scoring" below, and before any scraping, scrubbing or sanding in the steps that follow, confirm the build year and the wall condition. Walls in a building built before 1978 or of unknown age, or suspect older joint compound, mean no disturbance until a qualified person records a disposition; STOP and escalate. Pending review by an EPA RRP-certified renovator and an accredited asbestos inspector. (source: spec PT-04.SAF "stop on suspect hazardous coating/material"; spec PT-04.INT "age, painted/unpainted wall"; 02 C-PT04-04; X-13; risk-triage playbook "A pre-1978 painted surface is not cleared by a customer saying it looks safe.")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🪒 Phase 2: Perforation & Chemical Softening"

lines: > HOLD (C-PT04-07): before "Wall Scoring" below, run a test patch of the removal method and record the method decision (whether to score, how to apply the solution, whether steam is needed), with a photo. Pending owner and lead-technician review with the product instructions. (source: spec PT-04.SAF "test removal method"; spec PT-04.TLS "scorer only when appropriate"; 02 C-PT04-07 "test patch + method decision recorded")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🪒 Phase 2: Perforation & Chemical Softening"

lines: - [ ] **Wall Scoring:** Use an ergonomic wallpaper scoring tool (like a Paper Tiger) to roll over the wallpaper using light pressure. Make circular patterns to puncture the outer vinyl layer *without piercing the drywall paper below*.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🪒 Phase 2: Perforation & Chemical Softening"

lines: > FLAG (C-PT04-07): the step above is conditional: score only when appropriate, as the removal-method test decides; the card does not make scoring a default. Pending owner and lead-technician review. (source: spec PT-04.TLS "scorer only when appropriate"; 02 C-PT04-07)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🪒 Phase 2: Perforation & Chemical Softening"

lines: - [ ] **Enzyme Mix:** Mix a warm water batch of professional enzyme-based wallpaper stripper (e.g., DIF brand) inside a clean garden pump sprayer.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🪒 Phase 2: Perforation & Chemical Softening"

lines: - [ ] **Saturation Pass:** Spray the chemical solution generously over a 4x6 foot wall section. Allow the formula to absorb for 15 minutes to liquefy the old starched wheat paste beneath.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🪒 Phase 2: Perforation & Chemical Softening"

lines: > FLAG (C-PT04-07): "generously" in the step above is in tension with the card's "avoid excessive saturation". Apply the solution per the product label, as the removal-method test decides; water or solution reaching an electrical box is a stop condition (section 10). The dwell time in the step above stays unchanged pending a label check. The same applies to the second spray in "Glue Stripping". Pending owner and lead-technician review. (source: spec PT-04.SAF "avoid excessive saturation"; 02 C-PT04-07 "per product label; avoid excessive saturation (spec)", "Dwell times unchanged pending label check")
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🪒 Phase 2: Perforation & Chemical Softening"

lines: - [ ] **Steam Plate Apply:** If the glue is stubborn, hold a commercial wallpaper steam plate flat against the wet paper for 15-20 seconds to force moisture deep into the adhesive backing.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 💨 Phase 3: Steam Extraction & Damage-Free Scraping"

lines: - [ ] **The Gentle Slide:** Use a wide, flexible, rounded-edge putty knife. Slide the blade under the softened paper seams at a shallow 15-degree angle. Fluidly lift the sheets away in large panels. *Never force or gouge the drywall.*
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 💨 Phase 3: Steam Extraction & Damage-Free Scraping"

lines: > HOLD (C-PT04-02): if suspected mold or moisture is found behind the paper lifted in the step above, STOP work on that wall, keep people and pets away, photograph it and escalate (JOB-004). Do not clean, scrape, remove or rebuild the affected material; the agreement's "paid change order" for reconstruction does not replace this stop. Pending review by a mold assessor and the qualified safety professional. (source: spec START-011 "suspect hazardous materials"; spec JOB-004; 02 C-PT04-02; X-06; 31 section 8.5 escalation step 1; Q-31-10)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 💨 Phase 3: Steam Extraction & Damage-Free Scraping"

lines: - [ ] **Glue Stripping:** Spray the bare walls a second time with warm enzyme solution.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧼 Phase 4: Residual Glue Scraping & Wash"

lines: - [ ] **Scrubbing Grime:** Use a heavy-duty coarse abrasive sponge to scrub the walls down, pulling away sticky paste ribbons.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧼 Phase 4: Residual Glue Scraping & Wash"

lines: - [ ] **Fresh Water Flush:** Wipe down the bare walls using clean sponges and a bucket of pure warm water to remove all chemical residue. Let walls dry completely for 24 hours.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / 🧼 Phase 4: Residual Glue Scraping & Wash"

lines: - [ ] **Torn Paper Seal:** If any minor brown drywall paper tore during removal, seal it immediately with an oil-based primer to prevent compound bubbling later.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Skim Coating & Final Sanding"

lines: - [ ] **Skim Coat Finish:** Apply a thin layer of lightweight joint compound (معجون) over rough spots, indents, and seams using a 10-inch or 12-inch taping knife.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Skim Coating & Final Sanding"

lines: > FLAG (C-PT04-11): the step above contains an Arabic word, kept verbatim as a legacy artifact; it is not a translation. Worker-facing text is English, with Spanish only through the reviewed translation workflow. Pending the owner's cleanup decision with the bilingual reviewer. (source: spec BIZ-002; owner facts 2026-10-02; 36 section 5.4 item 21)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Skim Coating & Final Sanding"

lines: - [ ] **Dustless Polish:** Sand the dry compound using 220-grit sponges or a HEPA dustless sander to leave a smooth Level 4 finish ready for interior primer.
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Skim Coating & Final Sanding"

lines: > FLAG (C-PT04-04): "or a HEPA dustless sander" in the step above leaves dust capture optional; the dust-control method is pending qualified safety review, and the review may only strengthen it. The older-coating hold before "Wall Scoring" applies to sanding as well. (source: spec PT-04.SAF "control dust"; spec PT-04.TLS "sanding/HEPA vacuum"; 02 C-PT04-04)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Skim Coating & Final Sanding"

lines: > FLAG (X-26; C-PT04-06): "smooth Level 4 finish" in the step above has no shared definition or acceptance criteria yet, and the main plan's "flawless, paint-ready Level 4 finish" is not covered (section 2). Pending the owner's decision with an experienced drywall finisher. (source: 02 X-26, C-PT04-06)

lines: > HOLD (C-PT04-03): the procedure above ends without restoring what Phase 1 altered. Before completion, anything placed in or over electrical boxes is removed and any circuit switched off is restored, by the method the licensed electrician approves; no restore procedure is written here. Pending licensed-electrician review. (source: spec APXA-005 "restore utilities/components altered within scope"; 02 C-PT04-03; X-07)
items.section: From "12. Step-by-step procedure / ✨ Phase 5: Skim Coating & Final Sanding"

lines: | Check | Source | Evidence | Inspector |

| Wallpaper and adhesive removed to the agreed level | spec PT-04.QAC "wallpaper/adhesive removed to agreed level" | After photos per wall; the agreed level as recorded on the approved estimate (definition pending, X-26; C-PT04-06) | TBD - self-check or supervisor (Q-31-15) |
| Substrate repairs smooth | spec PT-04.QAC "substrate repairs smooth"; original "Dustless Polish" | Photo of the repaired areas; finish-level criteria pending (X-26) | TBD (Q-31-15) |
| Surface clean and dry, chemical residue removed | spec PT-04.QAC "surface clean/dry"; original "Fresh Water Flush" ("remove all chemical residue") | Check result recorded | TBD (Q-31-15) |

| Primed if included | spec PT-04.QAC "primed if included"; original "Torn Paper Seal" | Whether a primer coat is included is read from the approved estimate; spot seals of torn paper recorded | TBD (Q-31-15) |

| No unmanaged damage: every tear or gouge recorded with photos and either repaired within scope or raised for a change order | spec PT-04.QAC "no unmanaged damage"; original "The Gentle Slide" ("Never force or gouge the drywall."); spec FIN-008 | Tear and damage log with photos (04 PT-04 "completion evidence", PROPOSED) | TBD (Q-31-15) |
| Removal-method test recorded before scoring | spec PT-04.SAF "test removal method"; 02 C-PT04-07 | Test-patch photo and method decision | TBD (Q-31-15) |
| Electrical boxes cleared and circuits restored | spec APXA-005; 02 C-PT04-03 | Restore confirmation by the approved method | TBD - method by the licensed electrician |
- The job cannot be marked complete until each required check is answered or an exception is recorded (source: spec QA-001; AT-039).
- Evidence: note
- A failed check becomes a punch item or an escalation; a worker's self-check does not replace a required supervisor inspection (source: handyhub-quality-assistant playbook).
- Clean the area, remove protection, account for tools and materials, and restore utilities and components altered within scope (source: spec APXA-005, QA-002).

- Remove anything placed in or over electrical boxes and restore any circuit switched off, by the method the licensed electrician approves; record the restore (source: spec APXA-005; 02 C-PT04-03; X-07).
- Evidence: note

- Lift the floor sheeting and tape together with the wet paper, adhesive residue and sanding dust they hold; the dust-capture method is pending safety review (source: original "Floor Protection"; spec QA-002; spec PT-04.SAF "control dust").
- Take cleanup photos where they are required for dusty or messy work (source: spec QA-002).
- Evidence: photo
TBD — requires review by safety-liability-manager and a qualified person; owner to approve.

- Waste streams to classify: wet wallpaper; adhesive residue and wash water; joint compound scraps and sanding dust; rags and applicators wet with oil-based primer; used sheeting and tape. Destination and who pays are owner decisions (source: original steps in section 12; 31 section 3.1; 02 G-078; Q-29-10).
- Rags and applicators wet with oil-based primer are handled per the primer SDS; no method is set here (source: 29 section 8.1; X-09).
- Waste from suspect hazardous coatings or compound is not handled without an approved policy (source: 31 section 3.1; spec START-011).

stages.heading: 6. Final checks, completion photos and walkthrough

lines: - Before: every wall to be stripped, including damage already present, and the electrical boxes as found (source: spec START-008, APXA-002, APXA-005; X-02).

- During: the removal-method test and its result (section 12 hold, C-PT04-07); every tear or gouge in the drywall paper, for the damage log (source: spec PT-04.QAC "no unmanaged damage"); any suspected mold, moisture or other concealed condition (source: spec JOB-004; 02 C-PT04-02).
- Evidence: note
- After: each wall after the final step, mapped to its work area (source: spec QA-003); the restored electrical boxes (source: spec APXA-005); cleanup where required (source: spec QA-002).
- Photos are internal-only by default and avoid people, documents and valuables not needed for the work (source: spec REC-002; 31 section 3.5 rule 7).
- The required photo set, and whether Start Job is blocked without it: TBD - owner (source: spec START-008).
- Arrival and completion updates use approved templates only; until approved they are drafts (source: 31 section 3.1).

- Before work starts, confirm the agreed walls and finish level with the customer, only as needed, and record the result of the removal-method test (source: spec APXA-003; spec PT-04.QAC "removed to agreed level"; 02 C-PT04-07).
- Evidence: note

- If the glue needs another method, or tearing goes beyond minor tears, tell the customer before any added work; no price changes without a change order that the customer approves (source: spec FIN-008, JOB-005; pricing "Hourly Safe-Fallback Rate" and "Unprimed Drywall Fine" lines, under review).

- Suspected mold, a suspect older coating or an electrical problem: use only the approved "work blocked" message; never send incident details or access codes by text or email (source: spec NTF-007, COM-002).

- Do not repeat "damage-free", "flawless", "completely eradicate ... preventing future paint bubbling or peeling flaws" or any finish, safety or health promise (source: main plan section 4; 02 C-PT04-05, C-PT04-06; Do-not-perform entry 8).
- Primer and paint are applied under separate agreements; do not promise how later painting will turn out (source: agreement "Payment Due" clause).
- Walkthrough: record accepted, accepted with punch items, unavailable or disputed (source: spec QA-004, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- Explain the invoice and payment next step without unauthorized promises (source: spec APXA-006).
- Every section 13 check is answered with evidence, or an exception is recorded (source: spec QA-001, AT-039).
- Evidence: note
- After photos are captured and mapped to the work (source: spec QA-003).
- Evidence: photo
- Cleanup is done, protection removed, and tools and materials accounted for (source: spec QA-002, APXA-005).
- Anything placed in or over electrical boxes is removed and any circuit switched off is restored by the approved method (source: spec APXA-005; 02 C-PT04-03).
- The tear and damage log is complete, and every tear is repaired within scope or raised for a change order (source: spec PT-04.QAC "no unmanaged damage"; spec FIN-008).
- Evidence: note
- The property is left secured (source: 31 section 3.1).
- The walkthrough outcome is recorded (source: spec QA-004, APXA-006).
- Evidence: note
- No hold from sections 10 and 12 is open, and unresolved issues, incidents and change requests are submitted before the job closes (source: spec APXA-007, JOB-012).
The general stop-work rule is [[FACT-SVC-STOP-WORK-RULE]]. Service-specific triggers:
PT-04 stop triggers (spec PT-04.SAF first, then the register holds; all pending qualified review):

- Suspect hazardous coating or material: walls in a building built before 1978 or of unknown age with no recorded disposition, or suspect older joint compound (source: spec PT-04.SAF "stop on suspect hazardous coating/material"; 02 C-PT04-04; X-13).
- Suspected mold or moisture behind removed paper: stop, photograph, escalate (source: spec JOB-004; 02 C-PT04-02; X-06).

- Electrical isolation not approved or not verified with an approved tester, water or solution reaching an electrical box, or exposed or damaged wiring (source: spec PT-04.SAF "protect/de-energize near outlets as appropriate"; 02 C-PT04-03; X-07).
- No approved power source for the steamer (source: 02 C-PT04-03).
- The removal method has not been tested, or the test shows that it damages the substrate (source: spec PT-04.SAF "test removal method"; 02 C-PT04-07).
- Saturation beyond what the product label and the method test allow (source: spec PT-04.SAF "avoid excessive saturation"; 02 C-PT04-07).
- Dust that cannot be controlled (source: spec PT-04.SAF "control dust").

- Tearing of the drywall paper face beyond minor tears: stop, photograph and record; any added repair or price goes through a change order that the customer approves before the work; the threshold is an owner decision (source: spec JOB-004, FIN-008, JOB-005; pricing "Unprimed Drywall Fine" line, under review).
- Evidence: note
- Ladder work needed with no approved height and access policy (source: 02 G-005; X-12).
- A chemical product without a reviewed SDS or label (source: 29 section 8.3; X-09).
- Each hold names the role and the evidence that clear it: TBD - requires qualified safety reviewer review. Critical holds clear only with a recorded qualified assessment (source: 31 section 8.3).
- Evidence: note
General path: [[FACT-SVC-ESCALATION-PATH]].
PT-04 routes (contacts are owner decisions, Q-31-05):
- Electrical: the isolation cannot be verified, water reaches a box, or wiring is exposed or damaged: stop; the office refers it to a licensed electrician (02 C-PT04-03).

- Suspect older coating or compound: stop; the owner arranges assessment by an EPA RRP-certified renovator or an accredited asbestos inspector, per the owner's policy (02 C-PT04-04; Q-31-07; Q-30-18).
- Suspected mold or moisture: stop; assessment by a mold assessor; the referral path is an owner decision (02 C-PT04-02; Q-31-10).
- Tearing beyond minor tears, or a different removal method needed: stop that task; the owner or the estimator prepares a change order before any added work (spec FIN-008, JOB-005).
General path: [[FACT-SVC-INCIDENT-REPORTING]].

- PT-04 examples: a steam or hot-water burn, an electrical shock or short, a chemical splash or exposure, a slip on wet sheeting, water damage to floors or other property, and a ladder incident (source: spec JOB-008; spec PT-04.HAZ).

- **Q-31-07** (owner; EPA RRP-certified renovator; accredited asbestos inspector): which property-age thresholds trigger lead and asbestos screening for PT-04, and does HandyHub hold or plan EPA RRP certification?
- **Q-31-10** (owner; qualified mold assessor): what is the company definition of mold growth versus cleanable mildew, and what is the stop rule for staining found behind removed paper?
- C-PT04-03 in 02 (licensed electrician; owner): may workers switch breakers, which box-protection, verification and restore method applies, and how is the steamer powered?
- C-PT04-06 in 02 (owner; drywall finishing lead): spot touch-up or full skim, which acceptance criteria apply, and where does DW-01 drywall repair begin?

- Related: **Q-31-05** (owner) emergency and escalation contacts for sections 19 and 20; **Q-31-09** (owner; qualified safety professional) the height and access policy; **Q-31-15** (owner) which QA checks need a supervisor rather than a self-check; **Q-31-16** (owner; attorney) who approves replacement wording for the "damage-free" statement; **Q-31-02** (owner) the qualified bilingual reviewer.
